> विश्वासु । विक्षु । अविताऽइव । हव्यः । भुवत् । वस्तुः । ऋषूणाम् ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निं नः अस्माकं द्वेषः द्वेष्टॄन् योतवै पृथक्कर्तुं गृणीमसि गृणीमः स्तुमः । तथा अग्निं शं सुखं योश्च भयानाममिश्रणं च दातवे दातुम् । अथवा शं सुखस्य योर्मिश्रणाय च गृणीमसि । अस्मिन् पक्षे द्वेषो योतवा इत्यनेन सह समुच्चयार्थश्चशब्दः । सोऽग्निः विश्वासु सर्वासु विक्षु प्रजासु अवितेव रक्षिता राजेव ऋषूणाम् ऋषीणामस्माकं वस्तुः वासको देवः हव्यो भुवत् भवतु । अथवा सर्वासु विक्षु यजमानरूपासु प्रजासु मध्य ऋषूणामृषीणां सूक्तद्रष्टॄणामस्माकमेव हव्यो भवतु वस्तुः सर्वस्य वासको देवः ॥ ॥ १३ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

We praise Agni in order to separate from us our haters, to drive them away. So also we praise Agni to give happiness, शं (*śaṃ*), and the non-mingling, योः (*yoḥ*), with fears. Or else: we praise for the mingling of happiness, शं (*śaṃ*), and योः (*yoḥ*); in this alternative the word च (*ca*) is for combining it with "to separate the haters". May that Agni be, among all the peoples, like a protector, like a king, for us, the seers, the god who makes us dwell, to be invoked. Or else: among all the peoples in the form of sacrificers, among the seers, that is, the seers of the sūkta, for us alone, may he be to be invoked, the god who makes all dwell.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- द्वेषः (*dveṣaḥ*)—haters
- योतवै (*yotavai*)—in order to drive far away
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—Agni
- गृणीमसि (*gṛṇīmasi*)—we praise
- शं (*śaṃ*)—happiness
- योः च (*yoḥ ca*)—and the warding off of fear
- दातवे (*dātave*)—in order to bring about
- अग्निं (*agniṃ*)—we pray to Agni
- (सः (*saḥ*)—that same Agni)
- विश्वासु (*viśvāsu*)—all
- विक्षु (*vikṣu*)—among the peoples also
- अवितेव (*aviteva*)—shining like a protecting king
- ऋषूणां (*ṛṣūṇāṃ*)—for us, who are seers
- वसुः (*vasuḥ*)—as the giver of dwelling
- हव्यः (*havyaḥ*)—and as one to be worshipped
- भुवत् (*bhuvat*)—let him be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We praise Agni in order to drive far away our haters. We pray to that same Agni in order to bring about happiness for us and the warding off of fear. May that same Agni, shining like a protecting king among all the peoples, be for us, who are seers, the giver of dwelling and one to be worshipped.

### Printed p. 79

##### English translation
We praise Agni that he may keep off our enemies; we praise Agni that he may give us joy and security; he may well be worshipped as the giver of dwellings to the Rishis, he who is as it were the protector of men.

## Sūkta 72 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘ हविष्कृणुध्वम् ' इत्यष्टादशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तम् । अत्रानुक्रमणिका – हविर्द्व्यूना हर्यतः प्रागाथो हविषां स्तुतिर्वा ' इति । प्रगाथपुत्रो हर्यत ऋषिः । परं गायत्रं प्राग्वत्सप्रेः ' इति परिभाषया गायत्री छंदः ।  ‘ आग्नेयं तु ' इत्युक्तत्वादग्निर्देवता यद्वा हविषां स्तूयमानत्वात्तद्देवताकं वा । सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning हविष्कृणुध्वम् (*haviṣkṛṇudhvam*) has eighteen Ṛks and is the third sūkta. The Anukramaṇikā says here: हविर्द्व्यूना हर्यतः प्रागाथो हविषां स्तुतिर्वा (*havirdvyūnā haryataḥ prāgātho haviṣāṃ stutirvā*). The seer is Haryata, the son of Pragātha. By the rule of interpretation परं गायत्रं प्राग्वत्सप्रेः (*paraṃ gāyatraṃ prāgvatsapreḥ*) the metre is Gāyatrī. Since it is said आग्नेयं तु (*āgneyaṃ tu*), the deity is Agni; or else, because the oblations are praised, the deity is the oblations. The use of the sūkta in ritual is by the indicatory sign (liṅga).

The Kannada Anuvāda: This sūkta, हविष्कृणुध्वं (*haviṣkṛṇudhvaṃ*), is the third sūkta in the eighth anuvāka. It has eighteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Haryata, the son of Pragātha; the metre is Gāyatrī. The deity is Agni, or, since there is praise of the oblation, that praise itself is the deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: हविदूर्व्यना हर्यतः प्रागाथो हविषां स्तुतिर्वा (*havidūrvyanā haryataḥ prāgātho haviṣāṃ stutirvā*). The use in ritual is by the indicatory sign.

Sūkta—72
Maṇḍala—8 ‖ Anuvāka—8 ‖ Sūkta—72 ‖
Aṣṭaka—6 ‖ Adhyāya—5 ‖ Varga—14, 15, 16, 17 ‖
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—18 ‖
Seer—हर्यतः प्रागाथः (*haryataḥ prāgāthaḥ*) ‖
Deity—अग्निर्हवींषि वा (*agnirhavīṃṣi vā*) ‖
Metre—गायत्री (*gāyatrī*) ‖

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ह॒विष्कृ॑णुध्व॒मा ग॑मदध्व॒र्युर्व॑नते॒ पुनः॑ ।  
> वि॒द्वाँ अ॑स्य प्र॒शास॑नम् ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 80

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हविः । कृणुध्वम् । आ । गमत् । अध्वर्युः । वनते । पुनरिति ।  
> विद्वान् । अस्य । प्रऽशासनम् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्युसंबंधिनो हविष्कर्तारः यूयं हविः कृणुध्वं कुरुध्वं शीघ्रम् । यतः आ गमत् आजगामायमग्निः अतः कृणुध्वम् । अध्वर्युः पुनः वनते संभजते । किम् । सामर्थ्यादध्वरमिति गम्यते । कीदृशोऽध्वर्युः । अस्य हविषः प्रशासनं प्रदानं विद्वान् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O makers of the oblation, you who belong to the Adhvaryu, make the oblation, prepare it quickly. Because this Agni has come (आ गमत् (*ā gamat*)), therefore make it. The Adhvaryu again takes up (वनते (*vanate*), he resorts to). What does he take up? By implication, the sacrifice (the adhvara) is understood. What kind of Adhvaryu is he? One who knows the bestowal (प्रशासनं (*praśāsanaṃ*)) of this oblation.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आ गमत् (*ā gamat*)—(O givers of the oblation) Agni has come here
- हविः (*haviḥ*)—the oblation
- कृणुध्वं (*kṛṇudhvaṃ*)—offer to him
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this oblation
- प्रशासनं (*praśāsanaṃ*)—the offering
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—who knows
- अध्वर्युः (*adhvaryuḥ*)—the Adhvaryu
- पुनः (*punaḥ*)—again
- वनते (*vanate*)—performs the sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O givers of the oblation, Agni has come here. Offer the oblation to him. The Adhvaryu, who knows the offering of this oblation, again performs the sacrifice.

##### English translation
(Priests), present the oblation, for (Agni) has come; the Adhwaryu again offers (the sacrifice), well-skilled in its offerings.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि ति॒ग्मम॒भ्यं१॒॑शुं सीद॒द्धोता॑ म॒नावधि॑ ।  
> जु॒षा॒णो अ॑स्य स॒ख्यम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नि । तिग्मम् । अभि । अंशुम् । सीदत् । होता । मनौ । अधि ।  
> जुषाणः । अस्य । सख्यम् ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 81

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> होता ऋत्विक् तिग्मं तीक्ष्णम् अंशुं तमग्निं नि षीदत् निषीदति । कीदृशो होता । अस्य अग्नेः सख्यं मनावधि यजमाने जुषाणः । अधीति सप्तम्यर्थानुवादी ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Hotṛ, the priest, sits down (नि षीदत् (*ni ṣīdat*)) by the sharp (तिग्मं (*tigmaṃ*)), that is, keen, flame (अंशुं (*aṃśuṃ*)), that is, by Agni. What kind of Hotṛ? One delighting (जुषाणः (*juṣāṇaḥ*)) in the friendship of this Agni, which is established in the offerer (मनावधि (*manāvadhi*)). The word अधि (*adhi*) merely repeats the sense of the locative case.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनावधि (*manāvadhi*)—established in the offerer
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Agni
- सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)—the friendship
- जुषाणः (*juṣāṇaḥ*)—praising and rejoicing in
- होता (*hotā*)—the Hotṛ
- तिग्मं (*tigmaṃ*)—sharp
- अंशुं अभि (*aṃśuṃ abhi*)—near the flame of Agni
- नि षीदत् (*ni ṣīdat*)—sits down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Hotṛ, praising and rejoicing in the friendship of this Agni, which is established in the offerer, sits down near the flame of the keen Agni.

##### English translation
The Hotri sits down by (Agni's) hot flame, rejoicing in his friendship towards the offerer.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अं॒तरि॑च्छंति॒ तं जने॑ रु॒द्रं प॒रो म॑नी॒षया॑ ।  
> गृ॒भ्णंति॑ जि॒ह्वया॑ स॒सम् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अंतः । इच्छंति । तम् । जने । रुद्रम् । परः । मनीषया ।  
> गृभ्णंति । जिह्वया । ससम् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तं रुद्रम् । रुत् दुःखम् । तस्य द्रावयितारम् । अथवा रुत् स्तुतिः । तया गंतव्यम् । स्तुत्यमित्यर्थः । तादृशमग्निं जने यजमानार्थं मनीषया स्वप्रज्ञानेन परः परस्तात् पुरोदेशे इच्छंति स्थापयितुम् । त एव पश्चात् ससं स्वपंतमग्निं जिह्वया । जन्ये जनकशब्दः । जिह्वाप्रभवया स्तुत्या गृभ्णंति गृह्णंत्यंगुलिभिः । अत्र यास्कः - स्वप्नमेतन्मध्यमं ज्योतिरनित्यदर्शनम्।....द्वैधं सत्ता मध्यमे च स्थाने उत्तमे च । ' ( निरु. ५. ३) इति ॥
> [ xxv. 6 ]

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Rudra is that Agni. रुत् (*rut*) is sorrow, and he is the one who drives it away; or else रुत् (*rut*) is praise, and he is the one to be approached with it, that is, the one worthy of praise. Such an Agni, for the sake of the offerer among men, they desire to establish by their own insight in the forward region (परः परस्तात् पुरोदेशे (*paraḥ parastāt purodeśe*)). The same people afterwards seize Agni, who is sleeping (ससं (*sasaṃ*)), with the tongue (जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)); the word for the cause stands for what is born of it, so that it means the praise that arises from the tongue; they seize him with the fingers. Here Yāska says (Ni. 5. 3): स्वप्नमेतन्मध्यमं ज्योतिरनित्यदर्शनम्।....द्वैधं सत्ता मध्यमे च स्थाने उत्तमे च । (*svapnametanmadhyamaṃ jyotiranityadarśanam|....dvaidhaṃ sattā madhyame ca sthāne uttame ca |*) **GLOSS**

### Printed p. 82

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रुद्रं (*rudraṃ*)—the remover of sorrow
- तं (*taṃ*)—Agni
- जने (*jane*)—for the offerer
- मनीषया (*manīṣayā*)—by their own insight
- अंतःपरः (*aṃtaḥparaḥ*)—in the forward region
- इच्छंति (*icchaṃti*)—they desire to establish
- ससं (*sasaṃ*)—Agni who is asleep
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—together with the praise born of the tongue
- गृभ्णंति (*gṛbhṇaṃti*)—they seize

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

They desire to establish Agni, the remover of sorrow, in the forward region by their own insight for the sake of the offerer. They seize Agni, who is asleep, together with the praise born of the tongue.

##### English translation
For the sake of the offerer, they seek by their skill to place Rudra in the fore front; they seize him, as he sleeps, with their tongue.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> जा॒म्य॑तीतपे॒ धनु॑र्वयो॒धा अ॑रुह॒द्वन॑म् ।  
> दृ॒षदं॑ जि॒ह्वयाव॑धीत् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> जामि । अतीतपे । धनुः । वयःऽधाः । अरुहत् । वनम् ।  
> दृषदम् । जिह्वया । आ । अवधीत् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वयोधाः अन्नस्य दाताग्निर्मध्यमस्थानः जामि प्रवृद्धं सर्वमतिरिच्य वर्तमानम् । ‘ जाम्यतिरेकनाम ' (निरु. ४. २०) इति यास्कः । धनुः धन्वांतरिक्षम् अतीतपे अतितपति । अथवाग्नेर्जामि गमनशीलं धनुरतितपते स्वविरोधिनम् । स च वयोधा अन्नस्य दाताग्निः वनम् उदकम् अरुहत् आरोहति विमोकाय । तदर्थं जिह्वया ज्वालया दृषदं मेघम् अवधीत् हंति । दावाग्निपक्षे वनं तरुसमूहं हंति । जिह्वया दृषदं कठिनमपि पाषाणं भिनत्तीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Agni, the giver of food (वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*)), who dwells in the middle region, scorches (अतीतपे (*atītape*)) the bow (धनुः (*dhanuḥ*)), that is, the atmosphere, which is swollen (जामि (*jāmi*)), standing above and beyond everything. Yāska says: जाम्यतिरेकनाम (*jāmyatirekanāma*) (Ni. 4. 20) **GLOSS** Or else: the bow of Agni, which is quick-moving (जामि (*jāmi*)), scorches what is hostile to it. And that Agni, the giver of food, mounts (अरुहत् (*aruhat*)) the water (वनम् (*vanam*)) in order to release it; for that purpose he smites (अवधीत् (*avadhīt*)) the cloud (दृषदं (*dṛṣadaṃ*)) with his tongue, that is, his flame. According to the view of the forest fire, he destroys the forest, the mass of trees; with his tongue he breaks even the hard stone (दृषदं (*dṛṣadaṃ*)).

### Printed p. 83

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*)—Agni, the giver of food
- जामि (*jāmi*)—swollen, grown vast
- धनुः (*dhanuḥ*)—the atmosphere
- अतीतपे (*atītape*)—makes it burn
- वसं (*vasaṃ*)—the water
- अरुहत् (*aruhat*)—has mounted
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—with his tongue
- दृषदं (*dṛṣadaṃ*)—the cloud
- आ अवधीत् (*ā avadhīt*)—splits

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, the giver of food, makes the vastly grown atmosphere burn. He has mounted the water. With his tongue he splits the cloud.

##### English translation
(Agni), the giver of food, scorches the vast bow (of the sky); he mounts the water; he smites the cloud with his tongue.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> चर॑न्व॒त्सो रुश॑न्नि॒ह नि॑दा॒तारं॒ न विं॑दते ।  
> वेति॒ स्तोत॑व अं॒ब्य॑म् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> चरन् । वत्सः । रुशन् । इह । निऽदातारम् । न । विंदते ।  
> वेति । स्तोतवे । अंब्यम् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वत्सः । वत्सवच्चापलेन धावनाद्वत्स इत्युपचर्यते । अथवा वत्स इव संचरन् । इवशब्दो लुप्यते । रुशन श्वेतो भवन् इह अस्मिँल्लोके निदातारं निरोधकं न विंदते न लभते । किंतु स्तोतवे स्तोतुम् अंब्यं स्तोतारं स्वयं वेति कामयते । अथवात्र वैद्युतोऽग्निरुच्यते । वैद्युतोऽयं रुशंश्चरंश्चेहांतरिक्षे वत्सः सर्वदा वसन् वत्सस्थानीयो वा सन्निदातारं निरोधकं न विंदते । किंतु स्तोतुमंब्यं माध्यमिकां वाचं वेति ॥ ॥ १४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वत्सः (*vatsaḥ*) is said figuratively, because he runs about with a calf's restlessness; or else the meaning is moving about like a calf, the word इव (*iva*) being dropped. Becoming white (रुशन् (*ruśan*)), he finds (विंदते (*viṃdate*)) here, in this world, no hinderer (निदातारं (*nidātāraṃ*)); rather, to praise (स्तोतवे (*stotave*)) he himself desires (वेति (*veti*)) a praiser (अंब्यं (*aṃbyaṃ*)). Or else the fire of lightning is spoken of here: this lightning fire, shining and moving here in the atmosphere, always dwelling there as a calf or standing in the place of a calf, finds no hinderer; rather he desires the speech of the middle region in order to be praised.

### Printed p. 84

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वत्सः (*vatsaḥ*) चरन् (*caran*)—Agni, who roams like a young calf
- रुशन् (*ruśan*)—and who is shining
- इह (*iha*)—in this world
- निदातारं (*nidātāraṃ*)—one who obstructs him
- न विंदते (*na viṃdate*)—does not find
- स्तोतवे (*stotave*)—in order to praise him
- अंब्यं (*aṃbyaṃ*)—in order to obtain a praiser
- वेति (*veti*)—he desires
- अथवा वत्सः (*athavā vatsaḥ*)—or, always dwelling in the atmosphere
- चरन् (*caran*)—moving
- रुशन् (*ruśan*)—and shining, the fire of lightning
- निदातारं (*nidātāraṃ*)—one who obstructs him
- न विंदते (*na viṃdate*)—does not find
- स्तोतवे (*stotave*)—in order to praise him
- अंब्यं (*aṃbyaṃ*)—the speech of the middle region
- वेति (*veti*)—he desires

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who roams everywhere like a young calf and who is shining, does not find in this world one who obstructs him. He desires to obtain a praiser who will praise him.

##### English translation
Roaming like a calf and bright-shining, he finds here no hinderer; he seeks a chanter to praise him.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒तो न्व॑स्य॒ यन्म॒हदश्वा॑व॒द्योज॑नं बृ॒हद् ।  
> दा॒मा रथ॑स्य॒ ददृ॑शे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उतो इति । नु । अस्य । यत् । महत् । अश्वऽवत् । योजनम् । बृहत् ।  
> दामा । रथस्य । ददृशे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतो अपि च नु क्षिप्रमद्य अस्य आदित्यस्य यन्महत् माहात्म्ययुक्तम् अश्वावत् संवृद्धाश्ववत् बृहत् महत् स्थूलं योजनं दृश्यते । तदेवाह। रथस्य दामा ददृशे दृश्यते। अंतरिक्षे रथेऽश्वान्नियोजयतीत्यर्थः। तदा दुहंतीत्युत्तरत्र संबंधः ॥
> अभिष्टवे घर्मदाहे ‘ दुहंति सप्त ' इत्येषा । सूत्रितं च -- दुहंति सप्तैकां समिद्धो अग्निरश्विना' (आश्व. श्रौ. ४. ७) इति । ग्रावस्तोत्रेऽप्येषा । सूत्रितं च - ‘ दुहंति सप्तैकामधुक्षत्पिप्युषीमिषम् ' (आश्व. श्रौ. ५. १२) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And now quickly, today, the great, vast, thick yoking of this Āditya, filled with majesty and like that of fully grown horses, is seen. That is what he says: the rope of the chariot is seen (ददृशे (*dadṛśe*)); the meaning is that in the atmosphere he yokes the horses to the chariot. The connection with दुहंति (*duhaṃti*) is in the following Ṛk. This Ṛk, in the Abhiṣṭava at the heating of the Gharma, is the one beginning दुहंति सप्त (*duhaṃti sapta*). It is also given in the sūtra: दुहंति सप्तैकां समिद्धो अग्निरश्विना (*duhaṃti saptaikāṃ samiddho agniraśvinā*) (Āśv. Śrau. 4. 7). This Ṛk is also in the Grāvastotra; and it is given in the sūtra: दुहंति सप्तैकामधुक्षत्पिप्युषीमिषम् (*duhaṃti saptaikāmadhukṣatpipyuṣīmiṣam*) (Āśv. Śrau. 5. 12). **NOTE**

### Printed p. 85

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उतो (*uto*)—and
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अस्य (*asya*)—of the Āditya
- महत् (*mahat*)—possessing majesty
- अश्वावत् (*aśvāvat*)—connected with horses
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—large
- योजनं (*yojanaṃ*)—the union with the chariot takes place
- सु (*su*)—immediately
- रथस्य (*rathasya*)—of his chariot
- दामा (*dāmā*)—the course of movement
- ददृशे (*dadṛśe*)—becomes visible

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the union with the chariot takes place, a union that is possessed of the Āditya's majesty, connected with horses and large, immediately the course of movement of his chariot becomes visible.

##### English translation
As soon as the great stout harness of his horses is seen (in the sky), the traces of his chariot.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दु॒हंति॑ स॒प्तैका॒मुप॒ द्वा पंच॑ सृजतः ।  
> ती॒र्थे सिंधो॒रधि॑ स्व॒रे ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दुहंति । सप्त । एकाम् । उप । द्वा । पंच । सृजतः ।  
> तीर्थे । सिंधोः । अधि । स्वरे ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सप्त ऋत्विजः एकां घर्मं दुहंति । तेषां मध्ये द्वा द्वौ प्रतिप्रस्थातारावध्वर्यू पंच अन्यान् उप सृजतः प्रयोजयतः । के ते पंच त उच्यंते । यजमानं ब्रह्माणं होतारमाग्नीध्रं प्रस्तोतारमिति । कुत्रेति उच्यते। सिंधोः कस्याश्चित् सरस्वत्यादिप्रख्याताया नद्याः तीर्थे । यत्रायमृषिर्यजति तत्र । स्वरे अधि। स्वरतिः शब्दकर्मा । अधीति सप्तम्यर्थानुवादी । स्वरोपेते शब्दवति । यत्तीर्थमृत्विजाम् ओ श्रावय इत्यादिशब्दैः शब्दवद्भवति तस्मिन्नित्यर्थः ॥
> प्रवर्ग्येऽभिष्टवे ग्राव्णोऽभिष्टवे च  आ दशभिः' इत्येषा । सूत्रितं च - ‘ आ दशभिर्विवस्वतो दुहंति सप्तैकाम्' (आश्व. श्रौ. ४. ७ ; ५. १२) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Seven priests milk one Gharma. Among them the two, the two Pratiprasthātṛ Adhvaryus, send forth, that is, employ, the other five. Who are those five? They are named: the offerer, the Brahmā, the Hotṛ, the Āgnīdhra and the Prastotṛ. Where? On the bank (तीर्थे (*tīrthe*)) of some river (सिंधोः (*siṃdhoḥ*)), a river made famous like the Sarasvatī and the others, there where this seer performs the sacrifice. The words स्वरे अधि (*svare adhi*) mean: स्वरतिः (*svaratiḥ*) is a root of sound, and अधि (*adhi*) merely repeats the sense of the locative; so the bank that is sounding, that is, which resounds with such words of the priests as ओ श्रावय (*o śrāvaya*). The Ṛk आ दशभिः (*ā daśabhiḥ*) is used in the Pravargya, in the Abhiṣṭava, and in the Abhiṣṭava of the Grāvan. It is given in the sūtra: आ दशभिर्विवस्वतो दुहंति सप्तैकाम् (*ā daśabhirvivasvato duhaṃti saptaikām*) (Āśv. Śrau. 4. 7 ; 5. 12).

### Printed p. 86

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सिंधोः (*siṃdhoḥ*)—of the famed river
- स्वरे अधि (*svare adhi*)—resounding
- तीर्थे (*tīrthe*)—on the bank of the water
- सप्त (*sapta*)—seven priests
- एकां (*ekāṃ*)—the one Gharma
- दुहंति (*duhaṃti*)—milk
- द्वा (*dvā*)—two of them
- पंच (*paṃca*)—to the remaining five persons
- उप सृजतः (*upa sṛjataḥ*)—gives direction

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

On the bank of the resounding water of the famed river, seven priests together milk the one Gharma. Of them the two Pratiprasthātṛs give direction to the five, namely the offerer, the Brahmā, the Hotṛ, the Āgnīdhra and the Prastotṛ.

##### English translation
Seven milk one (cow), the two direct the five, on the resounding shore of the river.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Abhiṣṭaveṣṭi, at the heating of the Gharma, the Ṛk beginning दुहंति सप्त (*duhaṃti sapta*) is to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, दुहंति सप्तैकां समिद्धो अग्निरश्विना (*duhaṃti saptaikāṃ samiddho agniraśvinā*) (Ā. 4-7). And in the Grāvastotra also this Ṛk is to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, दुहंति सप्तैकामधुक्षत्पिप्युषीमिषं (*duhaṃti saptaikāmadhukṣatpipyuṣīmiṣaṃ*) (Ā. 5-12).

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ द॒शभि॑र्वि॒वस्व॑त॒ इंद्रः॒ कोश॑मचुच्यवीत् ।  
> खेद॑या त्रि॒वृता॑ दि॒वः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । दशऽभिः । विवस्वतः । इंद्रः । कोशम् । अचुच्यवीत् ।  
> खेदया । त्रिऽवृता । दिवः ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 87

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> विवस्वतः परिचरतो यजमानस्य दशभिः अंगुलीभिर्याचितः सन् इंद्रः कोशम् । मेघनामैतत् । उदकसेचकं मेघं दिवः अंतरिक्षसंबंधिनं तत्सकाशाद्वा आ अचुच्यवीत् । व्यदारयदित्यर्थः। केन साधनेनेति तदुच्यते । त्रिवृता त्रिप्रकारवर्तनवता खेदया रश्मिना । यद्वा । अत्रेंद्रशब्देनाग्निरादित्यो वा गृह्यते । खेदया त्रिवृतेति लिंगात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, entreated by the ten fingers of the offerer who is engaged in service (विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*)), split the कोशम् (*kośam*). This is a name for the cloud: the cloud that sprinkles water, belonging to heaven, the atmosphere, or from there, he split (आ अचुच्यवीत् (*ā acucyavīt*)). By what means is this said: by the ray (खेदया (*khedayā*)) of threefold turning (त्रिवृता (*trivṛtā*)). Or else: here by the word इंद्र (*iṃdra*) Agni or the Āditya is understood, because of the indicatory sign खेदया त्रिवृता (*khedayā trivṛtā*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*)—of the offerer engaged in worship
- दशभिः (*daśabhiḥ*)—also prayed to by the ten fingers
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- कोशं (*kośaṃ*)—the cloud
- त्रिवृता (*trivṛtā*)—threefold
- खेदया (*khedayā*)—by means in the form of rays
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—so as to scatter from the atmosphere
- आ अचुच्यवीत् (*ā acucyavīt*)—has split asunder

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, prayed to also by the ten fingers of the offerer who is engaged in worship, has split the cloud asunder, so that it scatters from the atmosphere, by a threefold means in the form of rays.

##### English translation
Invoked by the ten (fingers) of the worshipper, Indra has caused the cloud to fall from heaven by his three-fold ray.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Pravargya and in the Abhiṣṭaveṣṭi, and also in the Grāvābhiṣṭava, the Ṛk आ दशभिः (*ā daśabhiḥ*) is to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, आ दशभिर्विवस्वतो दुहंति सप्तैकां (*ā daśabhirvivasvato duhaṃti saptaikāṃ*) (Ā. 4-7; 5-12).

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॑ त्रि॒धातु॑रध्व॒रं जू॒र्णिरे॑ति॒ नवी॑यसी ।  
> मध्वा॒ होता॑रो अंजते ॥ ९ ॥

### Printed p. 88

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । त्रिऽधातुः । अध्वरम् । जूर्णिः । एति । नवीयसी ।  
> मध्वा । होतारः । अंजते ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयमग्निः त्रिधातुः लोहितशुक्लकृष्णभेदेन त्रिवर्णः जूर्णिः जवो वेगवान् नवीयसी नवीयस्या ज्वालया अध्वरं प्रवर्ग्यम् एति गच्छति । होतारः होमनिष्पादका अध्वर्य्वादयः मध्वा आज्यादिना परि अंजते । अथवाग्नेस्त्रिस्त्रिप्रकारा क्षिप्रा जवतरा ज्वाला पर्येति महावीरम् । तं मध्वांजत इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Agni is त्रिधातुः (*tridhātuḥ*), of three colours by the distinction of red, white and black; जूर्णिः (*jūrṇiḥ*) is swift, speedy. With a new flame (नवीयसी (*navīyasī*)) he goes (एति (*eti*)) to the sacrifice, the Pravargya. The होतारः (*hotāraḥ*), the Adhvaryu and the others who accomplish the oblation, anoint (परि अंजते (*pari aṃjate*)) with honey (मध्वा (*madhvā*)), that is, with ghee and the like. Or else: the flame of Agni, threefold, quick and swifter, goes around the Mahāvīra, and they anoint it with honey.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्रिधातुः (*tridhātuḥ*)—having red, white and black colours
- जूर्णिः (*jūrṇiḥ*)—swift
- नवीयसी (*navīyasī*)—new; Agni with a flame of this kind
- अध्वरं (*adhvaraṃ*)—to the sacrifice
- एति (*eti*)—comes
- होतारः (*hotāraḥ*)—the Hotṛs
- मध्वा (*madhvā*)—with sweet ghee and the like
- परि अंजते (*pari aṃjate*)—smear all around and adorn

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Agni, who has red, white and black colours and a swift and new flame, comes to the sacrifice. The Hotṛs smear and adorn Agni all around with sweet ghee and the like.

##### English translation
The three-hued fresh impetuous (blaze) goes swiftly round the sacrifice ; the priests anoint it with butter.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सिं॒चंति॒ नम॑साव॒तमु॒च्चाच॑क्रं॒ परि॑ज्मानम् ।  
> नी॒चीन॑बार॒मक्षि॑तम् ॥ १० ॥

### Printed p. 89

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सिंचंति । नमसा । अवतम् । उच्चाऽचक्रम् । परिऽज्मानम् ।  
> नीचीनऽबारम् । अक्षितम् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नमसा नमनेन अवतं महावीरम् उच्चाचक्रम् उपरिस्थितचक्रं परिज्मानं परितो व्याप्तं नीचीनबारं नीचीनद्वारम् अक्षितम् अक्षीणमीदृशं क्षीराद्यवशेषयुक्तमाहवनीयस्योपरि नमनेन सिंचंति जुह्वति । महावीरेण ह्याहवनीये हूयते ॥ ॥ १५ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With reverence (नमसा (*namasā*)), that is, with bowing, they sprinkle, that is, offer, over the Āhavanīya the अवतं (*avataṃ*), the Mahāvīra, उच्चाचक्रं (*uccācakraṃ*), with its wheel standing above, परिज्मानं (*parijmānaṃ*), pervading all around, नीचीनबारं (*nīcīnabāraṃ*), with its door below, अक्षितं (*akṣitaṃ*), undecayed, being such, together with the remnant of milk and the like. For with the Mahāvīra it is offered in the Āhavanīya.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अवतं (*avataṃ*)—that which bears the name Mahāvīra
- उच्चाचक्रं (*uccācakraṃ*)—having the shape of a wheel in the upper part
- परिज्मानं (*parijmānaṃ*)—pervading everywhere
- नीचीनबारं (*nīcīnabāraṃ*)—having a door in the lower part
- अक्षितं (*akṣitaṃ*)—free from decay; the flame of Agni (the Mahāvīra vessel)
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with reverence
- सिंचंति (*siṃcaṃti*)—they smear with ghee and the like and adorn

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

With reverence they smear with ghee and the like and adorn the flame of Agni (the Mahāvīra vessel), that which bears the name Mahāvīra, has the shape of a wheel in the upper part, pervades everywhere, has a door in the lower part and is free from decay.

##### English translation
They pour out with reverence the inexhaustible cauldron, as it goes round circular above and with an opening below.

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भ्यार॒मिदद्र॑यो॒ निषि॑क्तं॒ पुष्क॑रे॒ मधु॑ ।  
> अ॒व॒तस्य॑ वि॒सर्ज॑ने ॥ ११ ॥

### Printed p. 90

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभिऽआरम् । इत् । अद्रयः । निऽसिक्तम् । पुष्करे । मधु ।  
> अवतस्य । विऽसर्जने ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अद्रयः आद्रियमाणा अध्वर्य्वादयः अभ्यारमित् अभिगम्यैव निषिक्तम् अतिरिक्तं मधु पुष्करे वपुष्करे प्रवृद्ध उपयमनीपात्रे सिंचंति अग्निहोत्रार्थम् अवतस्य महावीरस्य विसर्जने विसर्जनसमये । होमानंतरं खलु महावीरमासंद्यामासादयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*), the Adhvaryu and the others who are honoured, having approached (अभ्यारमित् (*abhyāramit*)), pour the surplus honey (मधु (*madhu*)), poured out (निषिक्तं (*niṣiktaṃ*)), into the पुष्करे (*puṣkare*), the large Upayamanī vessel, for the Agnihotra, at the time of the setting down (विसर्जने (*visarjane*)) of the अवतस्य (*avatasya*), the Mahāvīra. For after the oblation they place the Mahāvīra on the seat.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अवतस्य (*avatasya*)—of Agni bearing the name Mahāvīra
- विसर्जने (*visarjane*)—(after the offering) at the time of setting down
- अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*)—the priests who are of reverent mind
- अभ्यारमित् (*abhyāramit*)—approaching
- निषिक्तं (*niṣiktaṃ*)—left over after the offering
- मधु (*madhu*)—the sweet ghee
- पुष्करे (*puṣkare*)—in the extended Upayamanī vessel (they pour)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

At the time of the setting down after the offering of the one that bears the name Mahāvīra, the priests of reverent mind, approaching Agni, pour the sweet ghee left over after the offering into the extended Upayamanī vessel.

##### English translation
The reverent priests drawing near pour the superfluous butter into the large (spoon), when they set the cauldron down.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गाव॒ उपा॑वताव॒तं म॒ही य॒ज्ञस्य॑ र॒प्सुदा॑ ।  
> उ॒भा कर्णा॑ हिर॒ण्यया॑ ॥ १२ ॥

### Printed p. 91

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गावः । उप । अवत । अवतम् । मही इति । यज्ञस्य । रप्सुदा ।  
> उभा । कर्णा । हिरण्यया ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे गावः घर्मदुघा यूयम् अवतं महावीरं प्रति उपावत उपागच्छत । यस्मात् यज्ञस्य घर्मयागस्य साधनभूते रप्सुदा। रप्सुदारप्सुदे आरिप्सोः फलप्रदे । लिप्स्वोरश्विनोर्दातव्ये वा। यद्वा रपणं शब्दनम् । रप् मंत्रः । तेन सुष्ठु दातव्ये । अथवा ‘ षूद क्षरणे '। रपा मंत्रेण क्षारणीये दोहनीये। ईदृशे गवाजयोः पयसी मही महती बहुले अपेक्षिते अत उपावतम् । गौरजाया अप्युपलक्षकः अजापयसोऽपि महावीरे सेचनीयत्वात्। अपि चास्य महावीरस्य उभा उभौ कर्णा कर्णस्थानीयौ द्वौ रुक्मौ हिरण्यया हिरण्मयौ सुवर्णरजतमयावित्यर्थः ॥
> प्रवर्ग्येऽजापयसि महावीर आनीयमाने ‘ आ सुते ' इत्येषा । सूत्रितं च - ‘ आ सुते सिंचत श्रियमित्याज आसिक्तयोः ' (आश्व. श्रौ. ४. ७) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O cows, you who yield the Gharma milk, come near (उपावत (*upāvata*)) to the अवतं (*avataṃ*), the Mahāvīra, because the two milks, serving the sacrifice of the Gharma, are रप्सुदा (*rapsudā*). He explains रप्सुदा (*rapsudā*) in several ways: fruit-giving to one who desires to obtain; or to be given to the two Aśvins who wish to obtain; or else रपणं (*rapaṇaṃ*) is sounding, रप् (*rap*) is a mantra, and so the milks are to be well given by it; or else, from the root षूद क्षरणे (*ṣūda kṣaraṇe*), they are to be made to flow by the mantra, that is, to be milked. Of such a kind are the milks of the cow and of the she-goat; they are मही (*mahī*), great, that is, plentiful, and they are required; therefore come near. The word cow also stands for the she-goat, since the milk of the she-goat too has to be poured into the Mahāvīra. Moreover, both (उभा (*ubhā*)) ears (कर्णा (*karṇā*)) of this Mahāvīra, that is, the two gold plates that stand in the place of ears, are golden (हिरण्यया (*hiraṇyayā*)), made of gold and silver. In the Pravargya, when the goat's milk is brought to the Mahāvīra, the Ṛk आ सुते (*ā sute*) is used. It is given in the sūtra: आ सुते सिंचत श्रियमित्याज आसिक्तयोः (*ā sute siṃcata śriyamityāja āsiktayoḥ*) (Āśv. Śrau. 4. 7).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—O she-goats and cows
- आवतं (*āvataṃ*)—to the Mahāvīra
- उपावत (*upāvata*)—come (your milks)
- यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*)—needed for the sacrifice
- रप्सुदा (*rapsudā*)—and fruit-giving
- मही (*mahī*)—are also of great nature
- (अस्य (*asya*))—of this Mahāvīra vessel
- उभा कर्णा (*ubhā karṇā*)—both the handles on the two sides, which are like ears
- हिरण्ययो (*hiraṇyayo*)—are made of gold and silver

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O she-goats and cows, come to the Mahāvīra. Your milks are needed for the sacrifice, are fruit-giving and are of great nature. Both the handles on the two sides of this Mahāvīra vessel, which are like ears, are made of gold and silver.

##### English translation
Draw nigh, you cows, to the cauldron ; (the two kinds of milk) in the sacrifice are plentiful and fruit-giving; both ears (of the vessel) are golden.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ सु॒ते सिं॑चत॒ श्रियं॒ रोद॑स्योरभि॒श्रिय॑म् ।  
> र॒सा द॑धीत वृष॒भम् ॥ १३ ॥

### Printed p. 92

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । सुते । सिंचत । श्रियम् । रोदस्योः । अभिऽश्रियम् ।  
> रसा । दधीत । वृषभम् ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुते दुग्धे गोपयसि श्रियं श्रयणमाजं पयः आ सिंचत । सिंचत हे अध्वर्यवः । कीदृशमाजम् । रोदस्योः । कर्मणि षष्ठ्येषा । द्यावापृथिव्यौ अभिश्रियम् अभिश्रयंतम् । अग्निसंयोगात्तावत्पर्यंतं प्रवृद्धमित्यर्थः । अथवा  ‘ तत्कावश्विनौ द्यावापृथिव्यावित्येके' (निरु. १२. १) इति निरुक्तत्वादश्विनोरभिश्रियमित्यर्थः । सेचनानंतरं रसा रस आजे पयसि वृषभं वर्षकमग्निं दधीत स्थापयत । अजाया आग्नेयीत्वात् क्षीरस्याप्यग्निसंयोजनमुचितम् ।  ‘ आग्नेयी वा एषा यदजा ' (तै. ब्रा. ३. ७. ३. १) इति ब्राह्मणम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Adhvaryus, pour (आ सिंचत (*ā siṃcata*)) the goat's milk, the श्रियं (*śriyaṃ*), that is, the admixture, into the milk of the cow that has been milked (सुते (*sute*)). What kind of goat's milk? रोदस्योः (*rodasyoḥ*) stands in the genitive of the object: heaven and earth; अभिश्रियं (*abhiśriyaṃ*) is that which reaches towards them; through contact with the fire it has grown so far, this is the meaning. Or else, since the Nirukta says तत्कावश्विनौ द्यावापृथिव्यावित्येके (*tatkāvaśvinau dyāvāpṛthivyāvityeke*) (Ni. 12. 1) **GLOSS** the meaning is the admixture that reaches the two Aśvins. After the pouring, in the sap (रसा (*rasā*)), that is, in the goat's milk, set (दधीत (*dadhīta*)), place, the bull (वृषभं (*vṛṣabhaṃ*)), Agni the rain-giver. Because the she-goat belongs to Agni, it is fitting to join even the milk with Agni. The Brāhmaṇa says: आग्नेयी वा एषा यदजा (*āgneyī vā eṣā yadajā*) (Tai. Brā. 3. 7. 3. 1) **GLOSS**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Adhvaryus) रोदस्योः (*rodasyoḥ*)—in both heaven and earth
- अभिश्रियं (*abhiśriyaṃ*)—which spreads, pervading
- श्रियं (*śriyaṃ*)—the goat's milk, which is the means of mixing
- सुते (*sute*)—with the milk of the cow that has been milked
- आ सिंचत (*ā siṃcata*)—pour and mix
- वृषभं (*vṛṣabhaṃ*)—Agni, the causer of rain and giver of desired objects
- रसा (*rasā*)—in the goat's milk
- दधीत (*dadhīta*)—establish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Adhvaryus, pour and mix the goat's milk, which spreads, pervading both heaven and earth and is the means of mixing, with the milk of the cow that has been milked. Establish Agni, the causer of rain and giver of desired objects, in the goat's milk.

##### English translation
Drop into the milked (stream) the admixture, which reaches, (as it boils), heaven and earth ; set the bull in the liquor.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Pravargyeṣṭi, when goat's milk is brought for the Mahāvīra, the Ṛk beginning आ सुते (*ā sute*) is to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, आ सुते सिंचत श्रियमित्याजे (*ā sute siṃcata śriyamityāje*) (Ā. 4-7).

### Printed p. 93

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ते जा॑नत॒ स्वमो॒क्यं१॒॑ सं व॒त्सासो॒ न मा॒तृभिः॑ ।  
> मि॒थो न॑संत जा॒मिभिः॑ ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ते । जानत । स्वम् । ओक्यम् । सम् । वत्सासः । न । मातृऽभिः ।  
> मिथः । नसंत । जामिऽभिः ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ते ता गावः जानत ज्ञातवत्यः । अथवा सामान्याकारेण त इति पुंनिर्देशः । किम् । स्वं स्वकीयम् ओक्यं निवासं महावीरम् । तत्र दोग्धुमगमन्नित्यर्थः । तदेवाह । वत्सासः वत्साः मातृभिः न जननीभिः सह यथा संगच्छंति तद्वत् जामिभिः बंधुभिः सहिता गावः मिथः प्रत्येकं सं नसंत संगच्छंते महावीरम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ते (*te*), those cows, knew (जानत (*jānata*)). Or else the word is in the masculine as a general form of reference. What did they know? Their own (स्वं (*svaṃ*)) dwelling (ओक्यं (*okyaṃ*)), the Mahāvīra; the meaning is that they went there to be milked. That is what he says: as calves (वत्सासः (*vatsāsaḥ*)) come together with their mothers, so the cows, accompanied by their kinswomen (जामिभिः (*jāmibhiḥ*)), each separately (मिथः (*mithaḥ*)), come together (सं नसंत (*saṃ nasaṃta*)) at the Mahāvīra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वत्सासः (*vatsāsaḥ*)—the calves
- मातृभिः न (*mātṛbhiḥ na*)—as they know their own place when they are with their mothers
- ते (*te*)—the cows that give milk for the Mahāvīra
- स्वं (*svaṃ*)—appointed for them for the sacrifice
- ओक्यं (*okyaṃ*)—the place
- जानत (*jānata*)—have known
- जामिभिः (*jāmibhiḥ*)—those cows, who have joined with their kinswomen
- मिथः (*mithaḥ*)—coming separately
- सं नसंत (*saṃ nasaṃta*)—unite

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As calves know their own place when they are with their mothers, so the cows that give milk for the Mahāvīra have known the place appointed for them for the sacrifice. Those cows, who have joined with their kinswomen, come separately and unite.

##### English translation
They know their own abode ; as calvs with their mothers, so they severally assemble with their cows.

### Printed p. 94

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उप॒ स्रक्वे॑षु॒ बप्स॑तः कृण्व॒ते ध॒रुणं॑ दि॒वि ।  
> इंद्रे॑ अ॒ग्ना नमः॒ स्वः॑ ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उप । स्रक्वेषु । बप्सतः । कृण्वते । धरुणम् । दिवि ।  
> इंद्रे । अग्ना । नमः । स्वः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> महावीरस्य स्रक्केषु बप्सतः ज्वालया भक्षयतोऽग्नेरन्नं धरुणम् इंद्रे अग्ना इति वक्ष्यमाणत्वादिंद्राग्न्योर्धारकं दिवि अंतरिक्षे उप कृण्वते उपकुर्वते । यदाग्निर्महावीरं दहति तदा तस्योपर्युभयविधं क्षीरमासेचयंतीत्यर्थः । एवं महावीर आसिच्य इंद्रे अग्ना अग्नौ च स्वः सर्वं गव्यमाजं च नमः अन्नम् । अथवा स्वरंतरिक्षे । योजयंतीति शेषः ॥ ॥ १६ ॥
> प्रवर्ग्ये घर्मदुहि दुग्धायाम् अधुक्षत् ' इत्येषा। सूत्रितं च – दुग्धायामधुक्षत्पिप्युषीम् ' (आश्व. श्रौ. ४. ७) इति आह्रियमाण । ग्रावस्तोत्रेऽप्येषा  ‘ अधुक्षत्पिप्युषीमिषमा कलशेषु धावति ' (आश्व. श्रौ. ५. १२) इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

They perform (उप कृण्वते (*upa kṛṇvate*)), that is, they offer, in the sky (दिवि (*divi*)), in the atmosphere, for the Agni of the Mahāvīra who devours (बप्सतः (*bapsataḥ*)) with his flame, the food (धरुणम् (*dharuṇam*)), the supporter of Indra and Agni, since इंद्रे अग्ना (*iṃdre agnā*) is to be said. The meaning is that when Agni burns the Mahāvīra, they then pour both kinds of milk over it. Thus, having poured on the Mahāvīra, they join all (स्वः (*svaḥ*)), the produce of the cow and of the goat, as food (नमः (*namaḥ*)), in Indra and in Agni. Or else स्वः (*svaḥ*) is the atmosphere. The words "they join" are to be supplied. The Ṛk अधुक्षत् (*adhukṣat*) is used in the Pravargya at the milking of the Gharma cow; the sūtra gives it: दुग्धायामधुक्षत्पिप्युषीम् (*dugdhāyāmadhukṣatpipyuṣīm*) (Āśv. Śrau. 4. 7). **NOTE** In the Grāvastotra also this Ṛk is used, because the sūtra gives it: अधुक्षत्पिप्युषीमिषमा कलशेषु धावति (*adhukṣatpipyuṣīmiṣamā kalaśeṣu dhāvati*) (Āśv. Śrau. 5. 12).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- स्रक्वेषु (*srakveṣu*)—with the flames
- बप्सतः (*bapsataḥ*)—to Agni who devours
- धरुणं (*dharuṇaṃ*)—the supporting food
- दिवि (*divi*)—in the atmosphere
- उप कृण्वते (*upa kṛṇvate*)—the Adhvaryus offer (thereafter)
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—all
- नमः (*namaḥ*)—the food also
- इंद्रे (*iṃdre*)—in Indra
- अग्ना (*agnā*)—and in Agni (they offer)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Adhvaryus offer in the atmosphere the supporting food to Agni, who devours with his flames; thereafter they offer all the food in Indra and in Agni.

##### English translation
(The priests) minister in the sky the supporting (milk) to (Agni) who devours with his jaws ; they minister all the food to Indra and Agni.

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अधु॑क्षत्पि॒प्युषी॒मिष॒मूर्जं॑ स॒प्तप॑दीम॒रिः ।  
> सूर्य॑स्य स॒प्त र॒श्मिभिः॑ ॥ १६ ॥

### Printed p. 95

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अधुक्षत् । पिप्युषीम् । इषम् । ऊर्जम् । सप्तऽपदीम् । अरिः ।  
> सूर्यस्य । सप्त । रश्मिऽभिः ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अरिः अरणशीलो वायुः सूर्यस्य सप्त रश्मिभिः साधनैः पिप्युषीम् आप्याययत् इषम् अन्नम् ऊर्जं रसं च सप्तपदीं सर्पणस्वभावपादां माध्यमिकां वाचं घर्मधुग्रूपेणावस्थिताम् अधुक्षत् दुग्धवान् । यद्यप्यध्वर्युः पात्रेण गां दुग्धे तथाप्येवंभावनया सांगं भवति । माध्यमिकाया वाचो मधुधुक्त्वं ' हिंकृण्वती, गौरमीमेत्' (ऋ. सं. १. १६४. २७, २८) इत्यादिषु प्रसिद्धम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The wind (अरिः (*ariḥ*)), which is of moving nature, with the seven rays of the sun as means, has milked (अधुक्षत् (*adhukṣat*)) the nourishing (पिप्युषीम् (*pipyuṣīm*)) food (इषम् (*iṣam*)) and sap (ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*)), that is, juice, and the seven-footed (सप्तपदीं (*saptapadīṃ*)), that is, having feet of creeping nature, speech of the middle region, standing in the form of a Gharma-milking cow. Although the Adhvaryu milks the cow with a vessel, yet by this way of conceiving it becomes complete in its parts. That the speech of the middle region yields honey is well known in such passages as हिंकृण्वती, गौरमीमेत् (*hiṃkṛṇvatī, gauramīmet*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 164. 27, 28) **GLOSS**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अरिः (*ariḥ*)—the wind, which is of moving nature
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the sun
- सप्त रश्मिभिः (*sapta raśmibhiḥ*)—by the seven rays
- पिप्युषीं (*pipyuṣīṃ*)—satisfying
- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—the food
- ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*)—and the juice
- सप्तपदीं (*saptapadīṃ*)—and the speech of the middle region, having seven feet
- अधुक्षत् (*adhukṣat*)—has milked

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The wind, which moves everywhere, has milked, by the seven rays of the sun, the satisfying food, the juice and the speech of the middle region, which has seven feet.

##### English translation
The wind by means of the sun's seven rays milks the nourishing food and drink from the seven-stepped one.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Pravargyeṣṭi, after the Gharma ..., the Ṛk beginning अधुक्षत् (*adhukṣat*) is to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, दुग्धायामधुक्षत्पिप्युषीं (*dugdhāyāmadhukṣatpipyuṣīṃ*) (Ā. 4-7).

### Printed p. 96

In the Grāvastuti also this Ṛk is to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, अधुक्षत्पिप्युषीमिषमा कलशेषु धावति (*adhukṣatpipyuṣīmiṣamā kalaśeṣu dhāvati*) (Ā. 5-12).

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सोम॑स्य मित्रावरु॒णोदि॑ता॒ सूर॒ आ द॑दे ।  
> तदातु॑रस्य भेष॒जम् ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सोमस्य । मित्रावरुणा । उत्ऽइता । सूरे । आ । ददे ।  
> तत् । आतुरस्य । भेषजम् ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मित्रावरुणौ सूरे सूर्ये उदिता उदिते सोमस्य सोमम् आ ददे स्वीकरोति । तत्र हेतुमाह। तत् स्वीकाररूपं कर्म आतुरस्य अस्मदादेः भेषजम् औषधम् । हितकरमित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Mitra and Varuṇa, when the sun (सूरे (*sūre*)) has risen (उदिता (*uditā*)), he takes, accepts (आ ददे (*ā dade*)), the Soma. He states the reason: that act, which consists of the taking, is the medicine (भेषजम् (*bheṣajam*)) of the afflicted (आतुरस्य (*āturasya*)), of us and others; the meaning is that it is beneficial.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रावरुणा (*mitrāvaruṇā*)—O deities Mitra and Varuṇa
- सूरे (*sūre*)—the sun
- उदिता (*uditā*)—when he has risen
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—the Soma
- आ ददे (*ā dade*)—I accept
- तत् (*tat*)—that
- आतुरस्य (*āturasya*)—for one afflicted by disease
- भेषजं (*bheṣajaṃ*)—is in the form of medicine

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O deities Mitra and Varuṇa, when the sun has risen I accept the Soma. That is in the form of medicine for one afflicted by disease.

##### English translation
Mitra and Varuna, I take the Soma when the sun is risen ; it is medicine to the sick ;

### Printed p. 97
#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒तो न्व॑स्य॒ यत्प॒दं ह॑र्य॒तस्य॑ निधा॒न्य॑म् ।  
> परि॒ द्यां जि॒ह्वया॑तनत् ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उतो इति । नु । अस्य । यत् । पदम् । हर्यतस्य । निऽधान्यम् ।  
> परि । द्याम् । जिह्वया । अतनत् ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पवमाने सोमे उतो अपि च अस्य सोमदातुः हर्यतस्य प्रदानं कामयमानस्य मम यत्पदं निधान्यं हविषां निधानार्हमुत्तरवेदिलक्षणं तत्र स्थित्वाग्निः द्यां परि परितः जिह्वया ज्वालया अतनत् व्याप्नोत् ॥ ॥ १७ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Soma that is being purified, "moreover" (उतो (*uto*)) of this giver of Soma, of me who desire to make the offering (हर्यतस्य (*haryatasya*)), whatever place is fit for laying down (निधान्यं (*nidhānyaṃ*)) the oblations, characterised as the northern altar (उत्तरवेदि (*uttaravedi*)), there Agni stands and with his tongue, that is his flame (ज्वालया (*jvālayā*)), pervades (अतनत् (*atanat*)) the sky all around (परितः (*paritaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उतो नु (*uto nu*)—and
- हर्यतस्य (*haryatasya*)—who desires to offer the oblation
- अस्य (*asya*)—to this sacrificer
- यत्पदं (*yatpadaṃ*)—the place which
- निधान्यं (*nidhānyaṃ*)—(for Agni) is fit for offering the oblation; Agni established on such a northern altar
- द्यां परि (*dyāṃ pari*)—all round the sky
- जिह्वया (*jihvayā*)—with his tongue of flame
- आतनत् (*ātanat*)—has pervaded

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For this sacrificer who desires to offer the oblation, Agni, established on the northern altar, the place fit for offering the oblation to Agni, has pervaded the sky all around with his tongue of flame.

##### English translation
Agni,—standing in the place which I, the eager offerer, choose as the spot for presenting the oblations,—fills the sky on every side with his blaze.

### Printed p. 98
## Sūkta 73 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘उदीराथाम्' इत्यष्टादशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तमात्रेयस्य गोपवनस्य सप्तवध्रेर्वार्ष गायत्रमाश्विनम्। तथा चानुक्रमणिका – उदीराथां गोपवन आत्रेयः सप्तवध्रिर्वाश्विनम्' इति । प्रातरनुवाक आश्विने क्रतौ गायत्रे छंदस्याश्विनशस्त्रे चेदं सूक्तम् ।
> उदीराथां ऎंब ई सूक्तवु ऎंटनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि नाल्कनॆय सूक्तवु. इदरल्लि हदिनॆंटु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ अत्रिगोत्रोद्भवनाद गोपवन अथवा सप्तवध्रि ऎंबुवनु ऋषियु; अश्विनीदेवतॆगळु देवतॆयु; गायत्रीछंदस्सु. अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि—उदीराथां गोपवन आत्रेयः सप्तवध्रिर्वाश्विनं ऎंदु हेळिरुवुदु. प्रातरनुवाकमंत्रपठन कालदल्लि आश्विनक्रतुसंबंधवाद गायत्रीछंदस्सिन ऋक्कुगळिगागियू, आश्विनशस्त्र मंत्रगळिगागियू ई सूक्तद विनियोगविरुवुदॆंदु आश्वलायनश्रौतसूत्रद—उदीराथामा मे हवमिति गायत्रं ऎंब सूत्रदिंद (आ. ४-१५) विवृतवागिरुवुदु.
> सूक्त—७३
> मंडल—८ ॥ अनुवाक—८ ॥ सूक्त—७३ ॥
> अष्टक—६ ॥ अध्याय—३ ॥ वर्ग—१८, १९, २० ॥
> सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यॆ—१८ ॥
> ऋषि—गोपवन आत्रेयः सप्तवध्रिर्वा ॥
> देवता—अश्विनौ ॥
> छंदः—गायत्री ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning उदीराथाम् (*udīrāthām*) has eighteen Ṛks and is the fourth sūkta of the eighth anuvāka. Its seer is Gopavana of the family of Atri, or Saptavadhri; its deity is the Aśvins; its metre is Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇikā says: उदीराथां गोपवन आत्रेयः सप्तवध्रिर्वाश्विनं (*udīrāthāṃ gopavana ātreyaḥ saptavadhrirvāśvinaṃ*). The sūkta is used at the morning recitation (prātaranuvāka), in the Āśvina rite for the Gāyatrī-metre Ṛks, and in the Āśvina-śastra. This use is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra उदीराथामा मे हवमिति गायत्रं (*udīrāthāmā me havamiti gāyatraṃ*) (Ā. 4-15).

Maṇḍala 8, Anuvāka 8, Sūkta 73; Aṣṭaka 6, Adhyāya 3, Vargas 18, 19, 20; number of Ṛks in the sūkta, 18; seer, Gopavana Ātreya or Saptavadhri; deity, the Aśvins; metre, Gāyatrī.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विना अश्विनौ ऋतायते यज्ञमिच्छते मह्यं मदर्थम् उदीराथाम् उद्गच्छतम् । तदर्थं हवमाह्वानं यज्ञं ता प्राप्तुं युंजाथां योजयतमश्वैः रथम् । वां युवयोः अवः रक्षणम् अंति अस्मदंतिके सत् वर्तमानं भूतु भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, for me who desire the sacrifice, rise up (उदीराथाम् (*udīrāthām*)) for my sake. To reach the sacrifice, the invocation made for it, yoke (युंजाथां (*yuṃjāthāṃ*)) your car with horses. Let your protection (अवः (*avaḥ*)) be near us (अंति (*aṃti*)), present (सत् (*sat*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—O Aśvins
- ऋतायुते (*ṛtāyute*)—to favour me who wish to perform the sacrifice
- उदीराथां (*udīrāthāṃ*)—rise and be ready to come to my sacrifice
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—your car
- युंजाथां (*yuṃjāthāṃ*)—join it with the horses
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—protection
- अंतिषत् (*aṃtiṣat*)—staying close by us
- भूत् (*bhūt*)—let it be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, be ready to come to my sacrifice, to favour me who wish to perform the sacrifice. Join your car with the horses. Grant that your protection may always be near us.

##### English translation
Rise, Ashwins, on my behalf, as I prepare to sacrifice; yoke your car ; let your protection abide near me.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

For the great seer Atri, who had been thrown into the fire by the Asuras, and for his benefit, you two spread over (उप स्तृणीतम् (*upa stṛṇītam*)) the burning (घर्मम् (*gharmam*)) fire with cold (हिमेन (*himena*)), that is with water. The Nigama is quoted: हिमेनाग्निं घ्रंसमवारयेथाम् (*himenāgniṃ ghraṃsamavārayethām*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 116. 8). **GLOSS**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ युवां कुह क्व स्थः भवथः । इदानीं कुह क्व कुत्र जग्मथुः गच्छथः स्वेच्छया । कुह क्व वा श्येनेव श्येनाविव शीघ्रपतनौ संतौ पेतथुः पतथः । एवमचिंत्यस्वभावौ कृपया संनिहितौ भवतमिति शेषः । तादृशयोः अवः अंतिके भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, where (कुह (*kuha*)) are you? Now, where do you go (जग्मथुः (*jagmathuḥ*)) at your own pleasure? Or where do you fly (पेतथुः (*petathuḥ*)) like two hawks (श्येनेव (*śyeneva*)), falling swiftly? Being of such inconceivable nature, be present near us out of compassion; this is the part to be supplied. Let the protection of such as you be near.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Aswins, you made a sheltering house for Atri let your protection abide near me.

### Printed p. 106

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सप्तवध्रिः महर्षिर्हे अश्विनौ युवयोः आशसा आशंसनेन स्तुत्या मंजूषाया निर्गत्य अग्नेः धारां तस्यां मंजूषायां प्र अशायत आशाययत् । स्वनिरोधिकां तां दग्धवानित्यर्थः । सप्तवध्रेः पेटिकांतःप्रवेशोऽश्विनोरनुग्रहान्निर्गमश्च ‘वि जिहीष्व वनस्पते' (ऋ. सं. ५. ७८.५) इत्यत्र स्पष्टमुक्तम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The great seer Saptavadhri, O Aśvins, by praise (आशसा (*āśasā*)) of you, came out of the chest and placed (प्र अशायत (*pra aśāyata*)) the stream (धारां (*dhārāṃ*)) of Agni in that chest; that is, he burnt the chest that confined him. Saptavadhri's entering the chest and coming out through the grace of the Aśvins is stated clearly in the passage वि जिहीष्व वनस्पते (*vi jihīṣva vanaspate*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5. 78.5). **GLOSS**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Aśvins) सप्तवध्रिः (*saptavadhriḥ*)—the seer named Saptavadhri
- आशसा (*āśasā*)—by the praise that extols you (coming out of the chest in which he had hidden himself)
- अग्नेः (*agneḥ*)—of Agni
- धारां (*dhārāṃ*)—the flame
- प्र अशायत (*pra aśāyata*)—placed it in that chest and made it burn it
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—protection
- अंतिषत् (*aṃtiṣat*)—staying very close to us
- भूतु (*bhūtu*)—let it be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, the seer named Saptavadhri praised you and, as a result of your help, came out of the chest in which he had hidden himself, and made that chest burn with the fire. May your protection always be very close to us.

##### English translation
Through his praise of you Saptavadhri let the fire's flame-point (to his basket) ; let your protection abide near me.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, who fulfil all our desires, come to this our sacrifice. Hear this prayer of mine. May your protection be very close to us.

##### English translation

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> किमि॒दं वां॑ पुराण॒वज्जर॑तोरिव शस्यते ।  
> अंति॒ षद्भू॑तु वा॒मवः॑ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> किम् । इदम् । वाम् । पुराणऽवत् । जरतोःऽइव । शस्यते ।  
> अंति । सत् । भूतु । वाम् । अवः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विनौ वां युवयोरर्थमागमनाय पुराणवत् पुराणयोरतिवृद्धयोरिव । तदेवाह । जरतोरिव शस्यते । पुनःपुनरागच्छतमिति शस्यते । किमिदम् । यथा लोके वृद्धो जीर्णो बहुवारमाहूतोऽपि नागच्छति तद्वद्युवामपीत्यर्थः । एवमनागमाद्ब्रवीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, for your coming, as if for two very old persons (पुराणवत् (*purāṇavat*)), as if for two aged ones (जरतोरिव (*jaratoriva*)), it is recited (शस्यते (*śasyate*)): "Come again and again." What is this? As in the world an old, decrepit man does not come though called many times, so you also do not; that is the meaning. Thus he speaks because of their not coming.

### Printed p. 108

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Aśvins) वां (*vāṃ*)—this praise addressed to you
- पुराणवत् (*purāṇavat*)—born in very ancient times
- जरतोरिव (*jaratoriva*)—as with old men, whose ears have become deaf, so that one has to say it again and again
- शस्यते (*śasyate*)—is being recited again and again
- किं इदं (*kiṃ idaṃ*)—what is the reason for this?
- वां (*vāṃ*)—your
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—protection
- अंतिषत् (*aṃtiṣat*)—staying very close
- भूतु (*bhūtu*)—let it be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvins, as with old men born in former times, who, if they are deaf, do not hear however many times one speaks to them, so I too offer my praise to you again and again, and yet it has not reached your ears. What is the reason for this? Grant that your protection may always be near us.

##### English translation
Why is this (repeated invocation) addresred to you as if you were decrepit like old men ? Let your protection abide near me.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> समानम् । वाम् । सऽजात्यम् । समानः । बंधुः । अश्विना ।

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अश्विना अश्विनौ वां युवयोः परस्परं सजात्यं समानजातित्वं समानम् एकमेव । उभयोरप्यश्व1रूपायाः सूर्यपत्न्या उत्पत्तेः सजात्यम् । तथा युवयोः बंधुः बंधकः स्रुवः समानः एक एव । अथवर्षिरहं समान एक एव बंधुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Aśvins, the kinship of birth (सजात्यं (*sajātyaṃ*)) between the two of you is common (समानम् (*samānam*)), one only; for both of you the common birth is from the wife of Sūrya in the form of a mare. Likewise the binder (बंधुः (*baṃdhuḥ*)) of you two is common, one only. **NOTE**
