##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- बृहंतः (*bṛhaṃtaḥ*)—great in strength
- वीळवः (*vīḷavaḥ*)—and firm in every way
- अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*)—mountains
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- न वरंते (*na varaṃte*)—cannot stop by the use of force
- स्तुवते (*stuvate*)—who praises you
- मावते (*māvate*)—to a man like me
- यत् वसु (*yat vasu*)—whatever wealth
- दित्ससि (*ditsasi*)—you wish to give
- तत् (*tat*)—that wealth, that is, that gift of wealth
- नकिः (*nakiḥ*)—no one
- आ मिनाति (*ā mināti*)—can injure, that is, can obstruct

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, even mountains that are great in size and exceedingly firm cannot stop you by the use of force. No one is able to prevent the gift of wealth that you are minded to give to a man like me, who praises you.

##### English translation
The vast firm mountains cannot stop you, Indra,—whatever wealth you would give to a worshipper such as I, none can hinder you therein.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the midday pressing, the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite the Ṛk न त्वा बृहंतः (*na tvā bṛhaṃtaḥ*) as the optional anurūpa mantra, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra: न त्वा बृहंतो अद्रयु उभयं शृणवच्च नः (*na tvā bṛhaṃto adrayu ubhayaṃ śṛṇavacca naḥ*) (Āśv. 6-4). **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> योद्धा॑सि॒ क्रत्वा॒ शव॑सो॒त दं॒सना॒ विश्वा॑ जा॒ताभि म॒ज्मना॑ ।  
> आ त्वा॒यम॒र्क ऊ॒तये॑ ववर्तति॒ यं गोत॑मा॒ अजी॑जनन् ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 288

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> योद्धा । असि । क्रत्वा । शवसा । उत । दंसना । विश्वा । जाता । अभि । मज्मना ।  
> आ । त्वा । अयम् । अर्कः । ऊतये । ववर्तति । यम् । गोतमाः । अजीजनन् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र क्रत्वा वृत्रहननादिकर्मणा अपि वा प्रज्ञानेन शवसा आत्मीयेन बलेन योद्धा शत्रूणां संप्रहारकः असि । उत अपि च त्वं दंसना स्वकीयेन कर्मणा मज्मना । मज मुजि शब्दार्थाः' । मजमुजी चेति मजतिः शब्दार्थः । शत्रूणामाक्रोशनसमर्थेन बलेन विश्वा जाता सर्वाणि भूतजातान्यभिभवसि । उक्तार्थस्य विश्वा जातान्यभ्यस्मि मह्ना' (ऋ. सं. ८. १००, ४ ) इत्यादिष्विंद्रेणैवोक्तत्वात् । एतादृशं त्वा त्वाम् अर्कः । ‘अर्च पूजायाम् । अर्चनीयः अयं मंत्रः यद्वार्को देवानामर्चकः पूजकोऽयं स्तोता ऊतये स्वरक्षणाय आ ववर्तति आवर्तयति । आत्माभिमुख्ये करोतीत्यर्थः । वर्ततेर्लेटि बहुलं श्लुरडागमश्च । यं त्वां गोतमाः गोतमपुत्रा नोधःप्रभृतयः अजीजनन् स्वयज्ञे प्रादुरबीभवन् । तं त्वामयं मंत्रः स्तोता वावर्तयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, by क्रत्वा (*kratvā*), that is, by the deeds beginning with the slaying of Vṛtra, or else by wisdom, and by शवसा (*śavasā*), your own strength, you are a योद्धा (*yoddhā*), a warrior, a striker of enemies. And you, by दंसना (*daṃsanā*), your own deed, and by मज्मना (*majmanā*), a strength able to make enemies cry out, overcome all beings (विश्वा जाता (*viśvā jātā*)). That this is the meaning is shown by Indra himself having said so in विश्वा जातान्यभ्यस्मि मह्ना' (*viśvā jātānyabhyasmi mahnā '*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8. 100, 4) and other places. Such as you are, this अर्कः (*arkaḥ*), the mantra to be worshipped, or else the worshipper of the gods, this praiser, turns hither (आ ववर्तति (*ā vavartati*)) for his protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*)), that is, makes you face himself. You, whom the Gotamas (गोतमाः (*gotamāḥ*)), the sons of Gotama, Nodhas and others, brought forth (अजीजनन् (*ajījanan*)), that is, made to appear at their sacrifice, you this mantra or praiser turns hither.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(O Indra, you)
- क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)—by your capacity, consisting in the slaying of Vṛtra and the like, or by your surpassing wisdom
- शवसा (*śavasā*)—and by your own power and strength
- योद्धा (*yoddhā*)—a soldier fighting with enemies
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- उत (*uta*)—and you
- दंसना (*daṃsanā*)—by your deed of valour
- मज्मना (*majmanā*)—and by your strength that chastises enemies
- विश्वा जाता (*viśvā jātā*)—defeat all beings (creatures)
- यं (*yaṃ*)—whom
- गोतमाः (*gotamāḥ*)—the sons of the seer Gotama, Nodhas and others
- अजीजनन् (*ajījanan*)—made manifest in their sacrifice
- त्वा (*tvā*)—such as you are
- अर्कः (*arkaḥ*)—worthy of worship
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this mantra
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for our protection
- आ ववर्तति (*ā vavartati*)—let it bring you towards us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, by your capacity, consisting in the slaying of Vṛtra and the like, or by your surpassing wisdom, and by your own strength, you are an excellent soldier fighting with enemies. And by your deed of valour and by a strength capable of chastising enemies,

### Printed p. 289

you are able to defeat all. May this mantra, worthy of worship, bring here towards us, for our protection, you whom the sons of the seer Gotama made manifest in their sacrifice.

##### English translation
By your exploits and might you are a warrior ; you overpower all beings by your deeds and prowess ; this hymn which the Gotamas have made, causes you to turn hither for their protection.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र हि रि॑रि॒क्ष ओज॑सा दि॒वो अंते॑भ्य॒स्परि॑ ।  
> न त्वा॑ विव्याच॒ रज॑ इंद्र॒ पार्थि॑व॒मनु॑ स्व॒धां व॑वक्षिथ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । हि । रिरिक्षे । ओजसा । दिवः । अंतेभ्यः । परि ।  
> न । त्वा । विव्याच । रजः । इंद्र । पार्थिवम् । अनु । स्वधाम् । ववक्षिथ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र दिवः द्युलोकस्य पर्यंतेभ्यः ओजसा । हिरवधारणे । स्वबलेनैव प्र रिरिक्षे प्रकर्षेणातिरिक्तो भवसि । रिचेर्लटि • बहुलं छंदसि' इति श्लुः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । किंच हे इंद्र पार्थिवं पृथिव्यां भवः रजः लोकः त्वा त्वां महता स्वशरीरेण न विव्याच न व्याप्नोति । द्यावापृथिवीभ्यामपि स्वतः स त्वं बलेन समर्थों भवसीत्यर्थः । एवंभूतः सन्नस्माकं स्वधाम् अन्नमुदकं वा अनु ववक्षिथ अनुवोढुमिच्छ । वहेः सनंतस्य छांदसे लिटि रूपम् । मंत्रत्वादामभावः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, by your ओजसा (*ojasā*), your own strength alone, you stand pre-eminently in excess (प्र रिरिक्षे (*pra ririkṣe*)) of the ends of heaven, the world of light. Further, O Indra, the terrestrial (पार्थिवं (*pārthivaṃ*)) world does not encompass (विव्याच (*vivyāca*)) you with its great body; the meaning is that you, even beyond heaven and earth, are capable of yourself by strength. Being such, desire to bring (ववक्षिथ (*vavakṣitha*)) our स्वधाम् (*svadhām*), food or water.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(O Indra, you)
- दिवः अंतेभ्यः परि (*divaḥ aṃtebhyaḥ pari*)—as far as the end of the world of heaven
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—by your own strength
- प्र रिरिक्षे (*pra ririkṣe*)—have surpassed everything
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- पार्थिवं रजः (*pārthivaṃ rajaḥ*)—this terrestrial world (even with its great form)
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- विव्याच (*vivyāca*)—is not able to encompass
- स्वधां (*svadhāṃ*)—food or water
- अनु ववक्षिथ (*anu vavakṣitha*)—desire to bring for me **NOTE**

### Printed p. 290

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, with your own strength you pervade everywhere up to the farthest end of the world of heaven and surpass everything. O Indra, this terrestrial world, even with its great form, is not able to encompass you. Be pleased to give us food or water.

##### English translation
Indra, by your might you extend beyond the limits of heaven, the region of the earth cannot contain you ; deign to bring us food.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नकिः॒ परि॑ष्टिर्मघवन्म॒घस्य॑ ते॒ यद्दा॒शुषे॑ दश॒स्यसि॑ ।  
> अ॒स्माकं॑ बोध्यु॒चथ॑स्य चोदि॒ता मंहि॑ष्ठो॒ वाज॑सातये ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नकिः । परिष्टिः । मघऽवन् । मघस्य । ते । यत् । दाशुषे । दशस्यसि ।  
> अस्माकम् । बोधि । उचथस्य । चोदिता । मंहिष्ठः । वाजऽसातये ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र ते तव मघस्य मंहनीयस्य धनस्य परिष्टिः परिबाधको निरोद्धा नकिः न कश्चिदस्ति । यत् यदा दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय दशस्यसि धनं प्रयच्छसि तदा तस्य निरोधको नास्तीत्यर्थः । तथा सति चोदिता धनानां चोदयिता स्तोतृभ्यः प्रेरयिता अत एव मंहिष्ठः दातृतमो मंहनीयो वा स त्वम् अस्माकं संबंधि उचथस्य स्तोत्रं वाजसातये अन्नलाभाय तदर्थं क्रियमाणमिति बोधि बुध्यस्व । स्तोत्रेण स्तुतः सन्नस्मभ्यमन्नादिकं प्रयच्छेति शेषः । बोधि ।  ‘ बुध अवबोधने । भौवादिकः । लोटि छांदसः शपो लुक् । ध्यादेशः ॥ ॥ ११ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, there is no one who obstructs, hinders or holds back your bountiful wealth. When you give wealth to the sacrificer who has offered the oblation, there is none to stop it. Such being the case, you are the urger of wealth, the one who sends it to the praisers, and for that very reason the most liberal giver, or the one most worthy of praise. Know and hear our praise, which is performed for the gaining of food. The sense to be supplied is: being praised with the hymn, give us food and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O Indra, the wealthy one
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- दशस्यसि (*daśasyasi*)—you give wealth, then
- ते (*te*)—your
- मघस्य (*maghasya*)—of the excellent wealth, the gift of it
- परिष्टिः (*pariṣṭiḥ*)—one who obstructs
- नकिः (*nakiḥ*)—there is no one
- चोदिता (*coditā*)—you who urge the praisers
- मंहिष्ठः (*maṃhiṣṭhaḥ*)—and who give wealth most abundantly
- वाजसातये (*vājasātaye*)—for the gaining of food, which we recite
- अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*)—related to us
- उचथस्य (*ucathasya*)—the praise
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—hear and know

### Printed p. 291

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when you wish to give wealth to the sacrificer who offers you the oblation, there is no one to forbid that gift of wealth; that is, no one is able to. You who urge the praisers and give them wealth abundantly, hear and know the praise that we recite for the gaining of food.

##### English translation
None can hinder your bounty, Maghavan, when you give wealth to your votary ; most liberal sender (of wealth), listen to our praise for the attainment of food.

## Sūkta 89 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहदिंद्राय' इति सप्तर्चं नवमं सूक्तम् । नृमेधपुरुमेधावृषी । तौ चानुक्तत्वादांगिरसौ । आदितो द्वौ प्रगाथौ पंचमीषष्ठ्यावनुष्टुभौ सप्तमी बृहती । इंद्रो देवता। तथा चानुक्रम्यते- बृहदिंद्राय सप्त नृमेधपुरूमेधौ द्व्यनुष्टुब्बृहत्यंतम्' इति । चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि मरुत्वतीये प्राकृतान्मरुत्वतीयात्प्रगाथादूर्ध्वं  द्वौ मरुत्वतीयौ प्रगाथौ शंसनीयौ। बृहदिंद्राय गायत' इत्ययमाद्यः प्रगाथः । पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवषडहयोः द्वितीयेऽहन्ययं प्रगाथः । सूत्रितं च - बृहदिंद्राय गायत नकिः सुदासो रथमिति मरुत्वतीया ऊर्ध्वं नित्यात्' (आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ३) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ninth sūkta, beginning बृहदिंद्राय (*bṛhadiṃdrāya*), has seven Ṛks. Its seers are Nṛmedha and Purumedha **NOTE**, and since nothing else is stated they are of the Āṅgirasa line. The first two are Pragāthas, the fifth and sixth are Anuṣṭubh, the seventh is Bṛhatī. The deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇī says accordingly that the sūkta is for Indra, with seven Ṛks, by Nṛmedha and Purumedha, two Anuṣṭubh verses and a Bṛhatī at the end. On the Chāturviṃśika day, in the Marutvatīya litany, after the regular Marutvatīya Pragātha, two Marutvatīya Pragāthas are to be recited; the one beginning बृहदिंद्राय गायत (*bṛhadiṃdrāya gāyata*) is the first of them. This Pragātha is also used on the second day of the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava ṣaḍahas. It is stated in the sūtra, बृहदिंद्राय गायत नकिः सुदासो रथमिति मरुत्वतीया ऊर्ध्वं नित्यात् (*bṛhadiṃdrāya gāyata nakiḥ sudāso rathamiti marutvatīyā ūrdhvaṃ nityāt*) (Āśv. Śrau. 7. 3).

The Anuvāda: this sūkta, बृहदिंद्राय (*bṛhadiṃdrāya*), is the ninth sūkta in the ninth anuvāka; it has seven Ṛks. Its seers are the two named Nṛmedha and Purumedha; they were born in the line of Aṅgiras. The deity is Indra. Of the first four Ṛks of this sūkta, the first and third are in the Bṛhatī metre and the second and fourth in the Satobṛhatī metre. The fifth and sixth Ṛks are in the Anuṣṭubh metre.

### Printed p. 292

The seventh Ṛk is in the Bṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: बृहदिंद्राय सप्त नृमेधपुरुमेधौ द्व्यनुष्टुब्बृहत्यंतं (*bṛhadiṃdrāya sapta nṛmedhapurumedhau dvyanuṣṭubbṛhatyaṃtaṃ*). On the day of the sacrifice called Chāturviṃśika, at the time of reciting the regular Marutvatīya litany, the Marutvatīya Pragātha mantras are to be recited; on that occasion this Pragātha mantra beginning बृहदिंद्राय गायत (*bṛhadiṃdrāya gāyata*) is to be recited. This Pragātha mantra is also to be recited on the second day of the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava ṣaḍaha; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra बृहदिंद्राय गायत नकिः सुदासो रथमिति मरुत्वतीया ऊर्ध्वं नित्यात् (*bṛhadiṃdrāya gāyata nakiḥ sudāso rathamiti marutvatīyā ūrdhvaṃ nityāt*) (Ā. Sū. 7-3).

Sūkta 89.
Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 9; Sūkta 89.
Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 6; Varga 12.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 7.
Ṛṣi: Nṛmedhapurumedhau.
Devatā: Indra.
Chandas: 1–4. प्रागाथं (*prāgāthaṃ*). 5, 6. अनुष्टुप् (*anuṣṭup*). 7. बृहती (*bṛhatī*).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> बृ॒हदिंद्रा॑य गायत॒ मरु॑तो वृत्र॒हंत॑मम् ।  
> येन॒ ज्योति॒रज॑नयन्नृता॒वृधो॑ दे॒वं दे॒वाय॒ जागृ॑वि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बृहत् । इंद्राय । गायत । मरुतः । वृत्रहम्ऽतमम् ।  
> येन । ज्योतिः । अजनयन् । ऋतऽवृधः । देवम् । देवाय । जागृवि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतः । ‘रु शब्दे'। मितं रुवंतीति मरुतः । हे मितभाषिणः स्तोतारः वृत्रहंतमम् अतिशयेन पापविनाशनं बृहत् साम इंद्राय इंद्रार्थं गायत अस्मदीययज्ञे गानं कुरुत । ऋतावृधः सत्यस्य यज्ञस्य वा वर्धका विश्वे देवाः देवाय द्योतमानायेंद्राय देवं देवनशीलं --- जागृवि सर्वेषां जागरणशीलं ज्योतिः सूर्यं येन साम्ना अजनयन् इंद्रार्थमुदपादयन् तत्साम गायतेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, so called because they speak in measured words (from the root meaning "to sound"); O praisers who speak in measured words, sing to Indra, in our sacrifice, the Bṛhat Sāman, which is the greatest destroyer of Vṛtra and of sin. The all-gods, who increase truth or the sacrifice, produced for Indra, the shining god, the luminary, the sun, who is divine, playful and ever awake to all; sing that Sāman by which they produced it. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 293

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- ऋतावृधः (*ṛtāvṛdhaḥ*)—all the gods who increase the sacrificial rite
- देवाय (*devāya*)—for Indra, whose self is divine
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—shining
- जागृवि (*jāgṛvi*)—and sleepless
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—the sun
- येन (*yena*)—by which Sāman mantra
- अजनयन् (*ajanayan*)—they produced, that
- वृत्रहंतमं (*vṛtrahaṃtamaṃ*)—greatly sin-destroying
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—Bṛhat Sāman mantra
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—addressed to Indra
- गायत (*gāyata*)—recite and sing

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, sing, reciting it, for the pleasure of Indra, that Bṛhat Sāman mantra, remover of sin, by the power of which the all-gods, who increase the sacrifice, produced for Indra, whose self is divine, the ever-vigilant sun.

##### English translation
Priests, sing to Indra the most sin-destroying Brihat-Saman, by which the upholders of truth produced the divine all-waking luminary for the god.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अपा॑धमद॒भिश॑स्तीरशस्ति॒हाथेंद्रो॑ द्यु॒म्न्याभ॑वत् ।  
> दे॒वास्त॑ इंद्र स॒ख्याय॑ येमिरे॒ बृह॑द्भानो॒ मरु॑द्गण ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अप । अधमत् । अभिऽशस्तीः । अशस्तिऽहा । अथ । इंद्रः । द्युम्नी । आ । अभवत् ।  
> देवाः । ते । इंद्र । सख्याय । येमिरे । बृहद्भानो इति बृहत्ऽभानो । मरुत्ऽगण ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अशस्तिहा स्तोत्रशंसनरहितानां शत्रूणां हंता इंद्रः अभिशस्तीः । ‘शसु हिंसायाम् । अभितो हिंसा येषां ते । तादृशान् । यद्वा । अभिशस्तीः शत्रुकृता हिंसाः । अपाधमत् अपागमयत् । अथ शत्रुहननानंतरम् इंद्रः द्युम्नी सर्वत्र द्योतमानयशोयुक्तः । यद्वा । तेषां धनापहरणेन धनादिमान् । आभवत् सर्वतः प्रसिद्धोऽभवत् । अथोत्तरार्धः प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे बृहद्भानो बृंहणशीलतेजस्क महादीप्ते वा मरुद्गण । मरुतां सप्त गणा यस्य संति स तथोक्तः । तादृश हे इंद्र देवाः द्योतमानाः सर्वे देवाः सख्याय आत्मनः सखिभावाय ते त्वां येमिरे नियच्छंति ।
> अग्निष्टोमे मरुत्वतीये ‘प्र व इंद्राय' इत्ययं मरुत्वतीयः प्रगाथः । सूत्रितं च- प्र व इंद्राय बृहत इति मरुत्वतीयः प्रगाथः' ( आश्व. श्रौ. ५. १४) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, the slayer of enemies who offer no praise, drove away the ill-wishers, those who inflict harm on all sides; or else the harms inflicted by enemies. After killing the enemies Indra became glorious, endowed with a fame that shines everywhere; or else, by taking away their wealth, he became a possessor of wealth, and became known on every side. The latter half is addressed directly: O Indra of great splendour, of vast brightness, lord of the seven troops of Maruts, all the shining gods hold you fast for friendship with themselves.

In the Agniṣṭoma, in the Marutvatīya litany, the Pragātha beginning प्र व इंद्राय (*pra va iṃdrāya*) is the Marutvatīya Pragātha, as stated in the sūtra (Āśv. Śrau. 5. 14).

### Printed p. 294

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अशस्तिहा (*aśastihā*)—Indra, who slays the enemies who do not praise
- अभिशस्तीः (*abhiśastīḥ*)—the harm done by enemies
- अपाधमत् (*apādhamat*)—will remove
- अथ (*atha*)—afterwards
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- द्युम्नी (*dyumnī*)—as one who has fame everywhere, or as one who has wealth
- आ अभवत् (*ā abhavat*)—became renowned
- बृहद्भानो (*bṛhadbhāno*)—shining with great splendour
- मरुद्गण (*marudgaṇa*)—O host of Maruts
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—all the gods
- सख्याय (*sakhyāya*)—for gaining friendship
- ते (*te*)—you
- येमिरॆ (*yemirè*)—desire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the destroyer of the enemies who do not offer praise, removes the harm done by enemies; afterwards that same Indra became known as shining and glorious. O host of Maruts shining with great splendour, and O Indra, all the gods are desiring your friendship.

##### English translation
Indra, the destroyer of those who offer not praise, has driven away the malevolent and has become glorious ; O Indra of mighty splendour, lord of the troops of Maruts, the gods press you for your friendship.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र व॒ इंद्रा॑य बृह॒ते मरु॑तो॒ ब्रह्मा॑र्चत ।  
> वृ॒त्रं ह॑नति वृत्र॒हा श॒तक्र॑तु॒र्वज्रे॑ण श॒तप॑र्वणा ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । वः । इंद्राय । बृहते । मरुतः । ब्रह्म । अर्चत ।  
> वृत्रम् । हनति । वृत्रऽहा । शतऽक्रतुः । वज्रेण । शतऽपर्वणा ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 295

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतः मितराविणः स्तोतारः बृहते महते वः स्तुत्यस्तोतृत्वलक्षणेन संबंधेन युष्मदीयाय इंद्राय ब्रह्म सामलक्षणं स्तोत्रं प्र अर्चत प्रोच्चारयत । ततः वृत्रहा वृत्रस्य पापस्य वा हंता शतक्रतुः शतविधकर्मा बहुविधप्रज्ञो वेंद्रः शतपर्वणा शतसंख्याकधारेण वज्रेण एतन्नामकेनायुधेन वृत्रम् अपामावरकं वृत्राख्यमसुरं हनति युष्माभिरभिष्टुतः सन् हंतु । हंतेर्लेट्यडागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, praisers who speak in measured words, by the bond of the praised and the praiser recite forth to your great Indra the hymn in the form of a Sāman. Then Indra, slayer of Vṛtra or of sin, of a hundred works or of manifold wisdom, with his hundred-edged thunderbolt, a weapon of that name, let him, praised by you, smite the asura called Vṛtra, who shuts in the waters.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- बृहते (*bṛhate*)—of great glory
- वः (*vaḥ*)—and related to you
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—addressed to Indra
- ब्रह्म (*brahma*)—the hymn in the form of a Sāman
- प्र अर्चत (*pra arcata*)—recite (and afterwards)
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—the slayer of Vṛtra
- शतक्रतुः (*śatakratuḥ*)—Indra, the doer of many deeds of valour
- शतपर्वणा (*śataparvaṇā*)—with hundreds of edges
- वज्रेण (*vajreṇa*)—with the thunderbolt
- वृत्रं (*vṛtraṃ*)—Vṛtra the asura, who has held back the rain waters
- हनति (*hanati*)—let him slay

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, recite the hymn in the form of Sāman chant to Indra, who is of great glory and related to you (as king to subjects); afterwards let Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra or of sin, the doer of many deeds of valour, praised by you, slay with his hundred-edged thunderbolt the asura Vṛtra, who has held back the rain waters.

##### English translation
Priests, utter forth the hymn to your great Indra; let Shatakratu, the slayer of Vritra, smite Vritra with his hundred-edged thunderbolt.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, among the mantras of the Marutvatīya litany, this Pragātha (Ṛks 3-4) beginning प्र व इंद्राय (*pra va iṃdrāya*) is to be recited as the Marutvatīya Pragātha, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra प्र व इंद्राय बृहत इति मरुत्वतीयः प्रगाथः (*pra va iṃdrāya bṛhata iti marutvatīyaḥ pragāthaḥ*) (Ā. Sū. 5-14).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि प्र भ॑र धृष॒ता धृ॑षन्मनः॒ श्रव॑श्चित्ते असद्बृ॒हत् ।  
> अर्षं॒त्वापो॒ जव॑सा॒ वि मा॒तरो॒ हनो॑ वृ॒त्रं जया॒ स्वः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । प्र । भर । धृषता । धृषत्ऽमनः । श्रवः । चित् । ते । असत् । बृहत् ।  
> अर्षंतु । आपः । जवसा । वि । मातरः । हनः । वृत्रम् । जय । स्वः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे धृषन्मनः शत्रूणां धर्षणशीलमनस्केंद्र ते तवैव बृहत् महत् अतिप्रभूतम् श्रवः अन्नम् असत् अस्ति । तदन्नं धृषता धृष्टेन मनसा युक्तः सन् अस्मभ्यम् अभि प्र भर आभिमुख्येन प्रकर्षेण संपादय । देहीत्यर्थः । हे इंद्र मातरः अस्माकमुत्पादनहेतुत्वान्मातृभूताः । कथमपां मातृत्वम् ।  ‘ अद्भ्यः पृथिवी पृथिव्या ओषधयः' (तै. उ. २. १) इत्यादिश्रुतेः । तादृश्यः आपः जवसा वेगेन वि अर्षंतु विविधं भूमिं प्रति गच्छंतु । कथमापो गच्छंतीति चेत्तदाह । वृत्रम् अपामावरितारं शत्रुं मेघं हनः जहि ताडय । ततो मेघभेदनेनोदकानि विगच्छंतु । पुनरपि स्वः सर्वं भूतजातं जय ॥
> प्रथमे स्वरसाम्नि निष्केवल्ये  यज्जायथा अपूर्व्य ' इति स्तोत्रियः । तथा च सूत्र्यते-- ‘ तेषां स्तोत्रिया यज्जायथा अपूर्व्य' ( आश्व. श्रौ. ८. ५) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, whose mind is given to overpowering enemies, yours alone is the great, the very abundant food. Being possessed of a bold mind, bring that food towards us, supply it in abundance; that is, give it. O Indra, the waters are our mothers, because they are the cause of our coming into being. How are the waters mothers? Because of the scriptural text अद्भ्यः पृथिवी पृथिव्या ओषधयः (*adbhyaḥ pṛthivī pṛthivyā oṣadhayaḥ*) (Tai. U. 2. 1) **NOTE**, and the like. Let such waters flow swiftly, going in various ways towards the earth. If it is asked how the waters are to go, he says: smite Vṛtra, the enemy who holds the waters back, that is, the cloud; then, the cloud being split, let the waters flow forth. And again conquer all that is born.

In the first Svara-Sāman of the Niṣkevalya litany the stotriya is यज्जायथा अपूर्व्य (*yajjāyathā apūrvya*), and so it is laid down in the sūtra तेषां स्तोत्रिया यज्जायथा अपूर्व्य (*teṣāṃ stotriyā yajjāyathā apūrvya*) (Āśv. Śrau. 8. 5).

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, whose mind is bent on crushing enemies, bring towards us with an excellent mind the abundant food that is with you. Let the waters, nourishing like mothers, in the form of

rain, spread over the earth. Strike the cloud that does not pour down rain, and satisfy all living beings.

> तत् । पृथिवीम् । अप्रथयः । तत् । अस्तभ्नाः । उत । द्याम् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अपूर्व्य त्वत्तो व्यतिरिक्तेन पूर्व्येण वर्जित हे मघवन् मंहनीयधनवन्निंद्र वृत्रहत्याय वृत्रासुरहननाय यत् यदा त्वं जायथाः उत्पन्नः प्रादुर्भूतोऽसि तत् तदानीमेव पृथिवीं प्रथमानाम् अप्रथयः प्रसिद्धां दृढामकरोः । उत अपि च तत् तदानीमेव द्यां द्युलोकमंतरिक्षेण अस्तभ्नाः निरुद्धामकार्षीः । एतादृशं वीर्यं त्वदन्यस्य न संभवतीत्यर्थं द्योतयितुमपूर्व्येति पदम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Apūrvya, one who has none before you, none other than you who is earlier; O Maghavan, Indra, possessor of praiseworthy wealth: when you were born, came into being, for the slaying of the asura Vṛtra, then and there you spread out the earth, making it known and firm. And then and there you propped up the world of heaven with the atmosphere, that is, you held it fast. The word अपूर्व्य (*apūrvya*) is used to show that such valour is not possible for anyone other than you.

- तत् (*tat*)—at that very time
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—heaven (by the atmosphere)
- अस्तभ्नाः (*astabhnāḥ*)—you have set it firmly so that it does not fall

> तद्विश्व॑मभि॒भूर॑सि॒ यज्जा॒तं यच्च॒ जंत्व॑म् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत् । ते । यज्ञः । अजायत । तत् । अर्कः । उत । हस्कृतिः ।  
> तत् । विश्वम् । अभिऽभूः । असि । यत् । जातम् । यत् । च । जंत्वम् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यद्यदा त्वमजायथाः तत् तदानीं ते त्वदर्थं यज्ञः अग्निष्टोमादिः अजायत सोमपानार्थमभूत् । उत अपि च तदानीं हस्कृतिः ।  ‘ हसे हसने । हासकारी प्रीत्यर्थं क्रियमाणो हर्षस्य सूचकः अर्कः अर्चनीयो मंत्रोऽप्यजायत । किंच तदा यज्जातं भूतजातं यच्च जंत्वम् । कृत्यार्थे त्वन्प्रत्ययः । जनितव्यं यत् विश्वम् अस्ति तत् सर्वम् अभिभूरसि स्वमहिम्नाभिभूतवानसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, when you were born, then for you the sacrifice, the Agniṣṭoma and the rest, came into being for the drinking of Soma. And then too the हस्कृतिः (*haskṛtiḥ*) **NOTE**, the arka, the adorable mantra, performed for pleasure and indicating joy, came into being. Further, whatever creatures were born then and whatever is yet to be born, all that you overcame by your own greatness.

O Indra, when you were born, the sacrifices, the Agniṣṭoma and the rest, were produced for you, that is, for your drinking of Soma, and so were the mantras by which they are performed. And you overcome by your own greatness all living creatures, those born before and those to be born hereafter.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ॒मासु॑ प॒क्वमैर॑य॒ आ सूर्यं॑ रोहयो दि॒वि ।  
> घ॒र्मं न सामं॑तपता सुवृ॒क्तिभि॒र्जुष्टं॒ गिर्व॑णसे बृ॒हत् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आमासु । पक्वम् । ऐरयः । आ । सूर्यम् । रोहयः । दिवि ।  
> घर्मम् । न । सामन् । तपत । सुवृक्तिऽभिः । जुष्टम् । गिर्वणसे । बृहत् ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र आमासु अपक्वासु गोषु पक्वं पयः ऐरयः प्रैरयश्च । तथा मंत्रः - ‘ आमासु चिद्दधिषे पक्वमंतः' (ऋ. सं. १. ६२. ९) इति । किंच दिवि द्युलोके सूर्यम् आ रोहयः च । पूर्वं पणयो नामासुरा अंगिरसां गा अपहृत्यांधकारावृते कस्मिंश्चित्पर्वते ताः स्थापितवंतः । ततोऽंगिरस इंद्रं स्तुत्वा गाः पुनरस्मभ्यमाहरेति तैरुक्त इंद्रो गवां स्थानं तमसावृतं दृष्ट्वा तत्र गोदर्शनाय द्युलोके सर्वप्रकाशकं सूर्यमारोहितवान् । स्थापितवानसि । 'चादिलोपे विभाषा' इति पूर्वस्यैरय इत्यस्य न निघातः । अथ परोक्षकृतोऽर्धर्चः । हे स्तोतारः सुवृक्तिभिः शोभनाभिः स्तुतिभिः तपत इंद्रं तीक्ष्णीकुरुत । इंद्रं स्तुतिभिः प्रवर्धयतेत्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । घर्मं न । यथा घर्मं दीपनशीलं प्रवर्ग्यं सामन् । 'सुपा सुलुक्°' इति तृतीयाया लुक् । सामभिर्यथा तपंति तद्वत् । ततः गिर्वणसे गीर्भिर्वननीयायेंद्राय जुष्टं प्रीतिकरं पर्याप्तं वा बृहत् साम गायत ॥ ॥ १२ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, in the unripe cows you impelled ripe milk; so the mantra says, आमासु चिद्दधिषे पक्वमंतः (*āmāsu ciddadhiṣe pakvamaṃtaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 62. 9). Further, you made the sun ascend in the world of heaven. Formerly the asuras called Paṇis stole the cows of the Aṅgirases and placed them on a certain mountain wrapped in darkness. Then the Aṅgirases praised Indra and, being told by them to bring the cows back to us, Indra saw the place of the cows covered with darkness and, in order to see the cows there, made the sun, the illuminator of all, ascend in the world of heaven. The second half-verse is in the third person: O praisers, with beautiful praises sharpen Indra, that is, make Indra grow strong by praises. An illustration is given: as they heat the blazing Gharma, the Pravargya, with Sāmans, so do you. Then sing the Bṛhat Sāman, pleasing or sufficient, for Indra, who is to be won by songs.

- ऐरयः (*airayaḥ*)—you impel to fill the udders

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you cause milk to fill the udders of cows that have not yet given milk and have only just calved. You have established the sun in the atmosphere and made it shine everywhere. O praisers, praise Indra with hymns and the like, and as the Gharma sacrifice is made to grow by Sāman chanting, sing and praise Indra, who is won by words of praise, with the Bṛhat Sāman, the Sāman mantra that is pleasing to him.

##### English translation
In the immature (cows) you produced the mature (milk), you caused the sun to arise in heaven (Priests), excite (Indra) with your praises as men heat the Gharma with Saman-hymns; (sing) the acceptable Brihat-Saman to him who is to be honoured by song.

### Printed p. 301

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

गिर्वणसे (*girvaṇase*)—Yāska gives this nirukta for this word: गिर्वणा देवो भवति गीर्भिरेनं वनयंति जुष्टं गिर्वणसे बृहत् इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*girvaṇā devo bhavati gīrbhirenaṃ vanayaṃti juṣṭaṃ girvaṇase bṛhat ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 6-14). Girvaṇāḥ means a god; they win this god by courting him with words of praise. That is, since he is pleased with praises, inclines to the praisers and fulfils their wishes, girvaṇāḥ means a god. In this matter the sentence जुष्टं गिर्वणसे बृहत् (*juṣṭaṃ girvaṇase bṛhat*) of the present Ṛk is the example, he says.

आमासु (*āmāsu*) **NOTE**—In cows that have not yet calved or have only just calved, he describes Indra's surpassing greatness as impelling ripe, that is drinkable, milk, which was not there until now, to fill them of itself. In this matter the bhāṣyakāra cites the verse आमासु पक्वमंतः (*āmāsu pakvamaṃtaḥ*) (Saṃ. 1-62-9) **NOTE**.

आ सूर्यमारोहयो दिवि (*ā sūryamārohayo divi*)—O Indra, you have established the sun in the atmosphere and made it shine. This too is your surpassing greatness. In this matter the bhāṣyakāra tells an ancient story:

पूर्वं पणयोमासुरा अंगिरसां गा अपहृत्यांधकारावृते कस्मिंश्चित्स्वर्वते ताः स्थापितवंतः । ततोऽङ्गिरस इंद्रं स्तुत्वा गाः पुनरस्म्यैवमाहरेति तैरुक्त इंद्रो गवां स्थानं तमसावृतं दृष्ट्वा तत्र गोदर्शनाय द्युलोके सर्वप्रकाशकं सूर्यमारोहितवान् । (*pūrvaṃ paṇayomāsurā aṃgirasāṃ gā apahṛtyāṃdhakārāvṛte kasmiṃścitsvarvate tāḥ sthāpitavaṃtaḥ | tato 'ṅgirasa iṃdraṃ stutvā gāḥ punarasmyaivamāhareti tairukta iṃdro gavāṃ sthānaṃ tamasāvṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra godarśanāya dyuloke sarvaprakāśakaṃ sūryamārohitavān |*)

In ancient times the asuras called Paṇis stole the cows of the Aṅgiras sages and hid them in a secret place of a mountain, that is, in a cave. Then, when those sages prayed to Indra to bring their cows back, Indra found the place where the cows were and, in order to free them and bring them out, established the sun in the atmosphere so that it shone and the thick darkness that had gathered there was dispelled. By the light of that sun the cave became bright, and he freed the cows that were there, brought them and gave them to the Aṅgiras sages. This is the ancient story in connection with which the words आ सूर्यमारोहयो दिवि (*ā sūryamārohayo divi*) are spoken in this Ṛk. The mention of this story is made here and there in many Ṛks of the Ṛgveda.

### Printed p. 302

## Sūkta 90 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘आ नो विश्वासु' इति षड़ृचं दशमं सूक्तम् । नृमेधपुरुमेधावृषी । विषमसंख्याका बृहत्यः समसंख्याकाः सतोबृहत्यः । इंद्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतम्-' आ नो विश्वासु षट्' इति । महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये बार्हततृचाशीतावेतत्सूक्तम् । सूत्र्यते हि पंचमारण्यके- ‘ आ नो विश्वासु हव्यो या इंद्र भुज आभरः' (ऐ. आ. ५. २. ४) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The tenth sūkta, beginning आ नो विश्वासु (*ā no viśvāsu*), has six Ṛks. Its seers are Nṛmedha and Purumedha. The odd-numbered verses are Bṛhatī and the even-numbered are Satobṛhatī. The deity is Indra. The Anukramaṇī says accordingly आ नो विश्वासु षट् (*ā no viśvāsu ṣaṭ*). In the Mahāvrata, in the Niṣkevalya litany, this sūkta is used for the Bārhata tṛca **NOTE**. It is stated in the Fifth Āraṇyaka: आ नो विश्वासु हव्यो या इंद्र भुज आभरः (*ā no viśvāsu havyo yā iṃdra bhuja ābharaḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 5. 2. 4).

The Anuvāda: this sūkta, आ नो विश्वासु (*ā no viśvāsu*), is the tenth sūkta in the ninth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Its seers are the two, Nṛmedha and Purumedha. The deity is Indra. The Ṛks of odd number in this sūkta are in the Bṛhatī metre, and the Ṛks of even number in the Satobṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: आ नो विश्वासु षट् (*ā no viśvāsu ṣaṭ*). In the Mahāvratesṭi, at the time of reciting the mantras of the Niṣkevalya litany, this sūkta is used for the Ṛks of the Bṛhatī metre, as is indicated in the Fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka by the sentence आ नो विश्वासु हव्यो या इंद्र भुज आभरः (*ā no viśvāsu havyo yā iṃdra bhuja ābharaḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-4).

Sūkta 90.
Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 9; Sūkta 90.
Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 6; Varga 13.
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 6.
Ṛṣi: Nṛmedhapurumedhau.
Devatā: Indra.
Chandas: प्रगाथं (*pragāthaṃ*) (odd Ṛks Bṛhatī, even Ṛks Satobṛhatī).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ नो॒ विश्वा॑सु॒ हव्य॒ इंद्रः॑ स॒मत्सु॑ भूषतु ।  
> उप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि॒ सव॑नानि वृत्र॒हा प॑रम॒ज्या ऋची॑षमः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । नः । विश्वासु । हव्यः । इंद्रः । समत्ऽसु । भूषतु ।  
> उप । ब्रह्माणि । सवनानि । वृत्रऽहा । परमऽज्याः । ऋचीषमः ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 303

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिरनयेंद्र एवं करोत्वित्याशास्ते । विश्वासु सर्वासु समत्सु असुरयुद्धेषु हव्यः सर्वैदैवैरात्मरक्षणार्थमाह्वातव्य एतादृशः इंद्रः नः अस्माकं ब्रह्माणि स्तोत्राणि हवीरूपाण्यन्नानि वा उप आ भूषतु अनुभवतु । सेवतामित्यर्थः । यद्वा । एतान्यलंकरोतु । तदागमनेन स्तोत्राणि हवींषि वालंकृतानि भवंति । तथा सवनानि प्रातःसवनादीनि त्रीणि सवनानि च भूषतु । कीदृश इंद्रः। वृत्रहा वृत्रस्यासुरस्य पापस्य वा हंता परमज्याः । युद्धेषु शत्रुहननार्थं परमाविनश्वरी ज्या मौर्वी यस्य स तथोक्तः । यद्वा । परमान् बलेन प्रकृष्टाञ्शत्रूंजिनाति हिनस्तीति परमज्याः । ऋचीषमः स्तुत्या समः स्तुतिभिरभिमुखीकरणीयः । एतादृगिंद्रः स्तोत्राणि भूषत्विति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

By this Ṛk the seer prays that Indra may do thus. In all battles, in the wars with asuras, being one who must be called upon by all the gods for the protection of themselves, such an Indra is to adorn, that is, to enjoy, our hymns, or our oblations in the form of food; let him partake of them. Or else, let him adorn these: by his coming the hymns or oblations become adorned. Likewise let him adorn the three savanas, the morning savana and the others. What sort of Indra is he? The slayer of Vṛtra, that is, of the asura Vṛtra, or of sin. परमज्याः (*paramajyāḥ*): one whose supreme, imperishable bowstring is for the slaying of enemies in battles; or else, one who overcomes or injures the foremost enemies, eminent in strength. ऋचीषमः (*ṛcīṣamaḥ*): one equal to praise, who must be turned towards us by praises. May such an Indra adorn our hymns.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्वासु (*viśvāsu*)—all
- समत्सु (*samatsu*)—in the battles waged with the asuras
- हव्यः (*havyaḥ*)—he who is prayed to and called for protection
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—the slayer of Vṛtra, or the remover of sin
- परमज्याः (*paramajyāḥ*)—he who has an imperishable bowstring
- ऋचीषमः (*ṛcīṣamaḥ*)—he who becomes manifest before us through praises
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—hymns or oblations in the form of food
- उप आभूषतु (*upa ābhūṣatu*)—let him partake of (or adorn)
- सवनानि (*savanāni*)—let him partake of the three savanas, the morning savana and the others

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, who is called upon with prayers for protection in all the battles fought with the asuras, who is the slayer of the asura Vṛtra, who has an imperishable bowstring, and who becomes manifest through praises, adorn, that is, partake of, our hymns and the three savanas.

##### English translation
May Indra, who is to be invoked in all battles, regard our hymns and our libations,—he, the slayer of Vritra, who crushes the mightiest (foes), who is worthy of his praise.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

उप आ भूषतु—एतान्यलंकरोतु । तदागमनेन स्तोत्राणि हवींषि वालंकृतानि भवंति । सेवतामित्यर्थः ॥ (*upa ā bhūṣatu—etānyalaṃkarotu | tadāgamanena stotrāṇi havīṃṣi vālaṃkṛtāni bhavaṃti | sevatāmityarthaḥ ‖*). When Indra comes to the sacrificial ground of the sacrificer, by his presence the hymns, the oblations, the three savanas and all the other ritual acts that are parts of the sacrifice acquire a kind of lustre, so that they appear adorned. That is, the seer expresses the wish that Indra may accept them with favour.

### Printed p. 304

परमज्याः—युद्धेषु शत्रुहननार्थं परमविनश्वरी ज्या मौर्वी यस्य स तथोक्तः यद्वा परमान् बलेन प्रकृष्टान् शत्रून् जिनाति हिनस्तीति परमज्याः । (*paramajyāḥ—yuddheṣu śatruhananārthaṃ paramavinaśvarī jyā maurvī yasya sa tathoktaḥ yadvā paramān balena prakṛṣṭān śatrūn jināti hinastīti paramajyāḥ |*). Two kinds of meaning are given for this word. The bowstring (the cord) of Indra's bow, which he uses in battles for slaying enemies, is imperishable, that is, it does not break and lasts a very long time; Indra possessing such a bowstring is one meaning. Or else Indra, by his excellent strength, injures powerful enemies; this is the other meaning.

ऋचीषमः (*ṛcīṣamaḥ*), स्तुत्या समः (*stutyā samaḥ*) (one who must be turned towards us by praises): if Indra is to be pleased, he will become manifest before the praisers only if he is praised with hymns and the like. This is the meaning intended: such an Indra.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं दा॒ता प्र॑थ॒मो राध॑साम॒स्यसि॑ स॒त्य ई॑शान॒कृत् ।  
> तु॒वि॒द्यु॒म्नस्य॒ युज्या वृ॑णीमहे पु॒त्रस्य॒ शव॑सो म॒हः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वम् । दाता । प्रथमः । राधसाम् । असि । असि । सत्यः । ईशानऽकृत् ।  
> तुविऽद्युम्नस्य । युज्या । आ । वृणीमहे । पुत्रस्य । शवसः । महः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र प्रथमः सर्वेषां मुख्यः त्वं राधसां धनानां दाता असि । यद्वा । धनदातॄणां  मध्ये त्वं प्रथम आदिमो भवसि । तथा ईशानकृत् तव स्तोतॄन् ईशानान् ऐश्वर्ययुक्तान् कुर्वंस्त्वं सत्यः  सत्यकर्मा असि । यथार्थकर्मा भवसीत्यर्थः । यस्मादेवं तस्माद्वयं तुविद्युम्नस्य बहुधनवतो बह्वन्नस्य वा शवसः बलस्य पुत्रस्य शत्रुवधार्थं बलकारणत्वेनोत्पन्नत्वात्तत्पुत्रस्य अत एव महः महतस्तव युज्या योग्यानि धनानि आ वृणीमहे संभजामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you, the foremost, the chief of all, are the giver of riches; or else, among the givers of wealth you are the first, the earliest. And making your praisers lords, that is, endowed with wealth, you are true, true in your deeds; the meaning is that you act in accordance with the fact. Since it is so, we choose and enjoy fitting riches from you, the son of strength, of him who has abundant wealth or abundant food, who was born as the cause of strength for the slaying of enemies, and therefore great.

### Printed p. 305

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—(O Indra) chief of all
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- राधसां (*rādhasāṃ*)—riches
- दाता असि (*dātā asi*)—you are the giver; or else
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- राधसां (*rādhasāṃ*)—among the givers of wealth
- प्रथमः दाता असि (*prathamaḥ dātā asi*)—you are the best giver; likewise
- ईशानकृत् (*īśānakṛt*)—you who make the people who praise you possessed of wealth
- सत्यः असि (*satyaḥ asi*)—you are a doer of true deeds (therefore we)
- तुविद्युम्नस्य (*tuvidyumnasya*)—of him who has abundant wealth
- शवसः पुत्रस्य (*śavasaḥ putrasya*)—who was born strong for the slaying of enemies
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—of you, who are of great nature, or from you
- युज्या (*yujyā*)—fitting riches
- आ वृणीमहे (*ā vṛṇīmahe*)—we ask for

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are the best giver among the givers of wealth; you who give wealth to the people who praise you and protect them do only true deeds. Therefore we ask from you, who have abundant wealth, who were born strong for the slaying of enemies and who are of great nature, for fitting riches, that is, riches fit to be enjoyed.

##### English translation
You are the chief giver of wealth, you are truthful and make your worshippers rulers ; we solicit (blessings) worthy of you, lord of vast riches, mighty son of strength.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ब्रह्मा॑ त इंद्र गिर्वणः क्रि॒यंते॒ अन॑तिद्भुता ।  
> इ॒मा जु॑षस्व हर्यश्व॒ योज॒नेंद्र॒ या ते॒ अम॑न्महि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ब्रह्म । ते । इंद्र । गिर्वणः । क्रियंते । अनतिद्भुता ।  
> इमा । जुषस्व । हरिऽअश्व । योजना । इंद्र । या । ते । अमन्महि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे गिर्वणः गीर्भिर्वननीय इंद्र अनतिद्भुता त्वद्गुणान् सर्वानतिक्रम्य न भवंति । इंद्रगुणव्यापकानि । यथार्थभूतानीत्यर्थः । तादृशानि यानि ब्रह्म ब्रह्माणि स्तोत्राणि ते त्वदर्थमस्माभिः क्रियंते हे हर्यश्व हरिताश्ववन् हे इंद्र योजनानि तव सम्यग्योजनशीलानि तानि इमा इमानि स्तोत्राणि जुषस्व सेवस्व । किंच हे इंद्र ते त्वदर्थं या यानि स्तोत्राणि अमन्महि वयमुच्चरामः तानि सर्वाणि सेवस्व ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, to be won by songs: the hymns that are not exceeded, that do not go beyond all your qualities, that pervade Indra's qualities, that is, are true to fact, such hymns are made by us for you. O Indra, lord of the bay horses, accept these hymns, which are well-fitted to you. Further, O Indra, whatever hymns we utter for you, accept them all.

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—accept

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, whose self is divine, hymns describing only your qualities are made by us for you. O Indra, who have the horses named Hari, accept those hymns, fitting to your dignity, which we recite for you.

##### English translation
Indra, who are the object of hymns, unexaggerated praises are offered by us ; lord of bay steeds, accept these fitting hymns, which we have meditated for you.

### Printed p. 307

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र सत्यः सत्यकर्मा त्वम् एव अनानतः केषामप्यप्रह्वः सन् भूरि भूरीणि वृत्राणि रक्षांसि न्यृंजसे तानि प्रह्वीभावयसि । न्यक्करोषीत्यर्थः । हिरवधारणे । हे शविष्ठ बलेन वृद्धतम हे वज्रहस्त । वज्रो हस्ते यस्य स तथोक्तः । हे इंद्र सः तादृशः त्वं दाशुषे तुभ्यं हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय रयिं धनादिकम् अर्वांचम् अवाचीनमभिमुखं यथा गच्छति तथा तम् आ कृधि समंतात्कुरु ॥
> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिशस्त्रे ‘त्वमिंद्र यशा असि' इति प्रगाथो वैकल्पिकोऽनुरूपः । सूत्र्यते च- ‘ त्वमिंद्र यशा असींद्र क्रतुं न आ भर' (आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ४) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, you alone, true in your deeds, unbowed before anyone, bring low many Vṛtras, that is, demons; you put them down. The word हि (*hi*) is for emphasis. O most mighty in strength, O thunderbolt-handed, one who has the thunderbolt in his hand: O Indra, such as you are, make wealth and the like come to the sacrificer who has given you the oblation, so that it goes facing him; do it all round.

On the Chāturviṃśika day, at the midday savana, in the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's śastra, the Pragātha त्वमिंद्र यशा असि (*tvamiṃdra yaśā asi*) is an optional anurūpa. It is stated in the sūtra: त्वमिंद्र यशा असींद्र क्रतुं न आ भर (*tvamiṃdra yaśā asīṃdra kratuṃ na ā bhara*) (Āśv. Śrau. 7. 4).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हे मघवन् (*he maghavan*)—O Indra, the wealthy
- सत्यः (*satyaḥ*)—who do true deeds
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अनानतः (*anānataḥ*)—although you are not bent, that is, not defeated, by anyone
- भूरि वृत्राणि (*bhūri vṛtrāṇi*)—many demons
- न्यृंजसे (*nyṛṃjase*)—you make them subject under your feet
- हे शविष्ठ (*he śaviṣṭha*)—O most mighty
- वज्रहस्त (*vajrahasta*)—O bearer of the thunderbolt, Indra
- सः त्वं (*saḥ tvaṃ*)—such as you are
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth and the like
- अर्वांचं (*arvāṃcaṃ*)—so that it reaches him, facing him
- आ कृधि (*ā kṛdhi*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, you who do true deeds, although you are not bent by anyone, you alone make many demons bend to you. O most mighty Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, such a mighty one as you, make wealth and the like go to and reach the sacrificer who offers you the oblation, facing him.

##### English translation
You are truthful, Maghavan; unhumbled yourself, you humble many enemies; most mighty thunderer, cause wealth to meet your worshipper.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वमिं॑द्र य॒शा अ॑स्यृजी॒षी श॑वसस्पते ।  
> त्वं वृ॒त्राणि॑ हंस्यप्र॒तीन्येक॒ इदनु॑त्ता चर्षणी॒धृता॑ ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 308

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वम् । इंद्र । यशाः । असि । ऋजीषी । शवसः । पते ।  
> त्वम् । वृत्राणि । हंसि । अप्रतीनि । एकः । इत् । अनुत्ता । चर्षणिऽधृता ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शवसस्पते बलस्य पालयितर्हे इंद्र ऋजीषी । ऋजीषोऽपार्जितोऽभिषुतः सोमः । तद्वान् त्वं यशाः यशस्वी असिः । कथमस्य यशस्वित्वं तदाह । अप्रतीनि बलिभिरप्यप्रतिगतानि अत एव अनुत्तानि अन्यैर्नोत्तुमशक्यानि वृत्राणि रक्षांसि त्वम् एक इत् असहाय एव चर्षणीधृता असुरादिहननद्वारेण मनुष्याणां धारकेण वज्रेण हंसि संप्रहरसि । अत एवास्य यशस्वित्वम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, lord of strength, protector of strength; ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*) means one who possesses the ṛjīṣa, that is, the Soma that has been obtained and pressed. Possessing it, you are यशाः (*yaśāḥ*), glorious. How is he glorious? Sāyaṇa answers: you, alone and unaided (एक इत् (*eka it*)), smite the Vṛtras, that is, the demons, who are अप्रतीनि (*apratīni*), not faced even by the mighty, and therefore अनुत्तानि (*anuttāni*), such as others cannot drive away. You smite them with the thunderbolt, which is चर्षणीधृता (*carṣaṇīdhṛtā*), the sustainer of men through the slaying of asuras and the like. Hence his glory.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शवसस्पते (*śavasaspate*)—protector of strength
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ऋजीषी (*ṛjīṣī*)—one who desires the Soma drawn again from the plants that were pressed once, called ṛjīṣa
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- यशाः असि (*yaśāḥ asi*)—you are renowned
- अप्रतीनि (*apratīni*)—those of unopposed strength
- अनुत्ता (*anuttā*)—and therefore those who cannot be defeated by others
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the demons who are enemies
- त्वं एक इत् (*tvaṃ eka it*)—you alone, without anyone's help
- चर्षणीधृता (*carṣaṇīdhṛtā*)—with the thunderbolt that sustains and protects men through the slaying of asuras and the like
- हंसि (*haṃsi*)—you destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, protector of strength and power, you who delight in the Soma juice drawn again from Soma plants pressed once, called ṛjīṣa, are renowned. For you alone, without anyone's help, destroy the demons who are enemies, whose strength is unopposed and whom others cannot subdue, with your thunderbolt that protects men through the slaying of enemies. This is the cause of your fame.

##### English translation
You, Indra, lord of strength, are the glorious possessor of the offered

### Printed p. 309

Soma; alone with (your thunderbolt), that protector of men, you smite the enemies that none else could oppose or drive away.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तमु॑ त्वा नू॒नम॑सुर॒ प्रचे॑तसं॒ राधो॑ भा॒गमि॑वेमहे ।  
> म॒हीव॒ कृत्तिः॑ शर॒णा त॑ इंद्र॒ प्र ते॑ सु॒म्ना नो॑ अश्नवन् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तम् । ऊं इति । त्वा । नूनम् । असुर । प्रऽचेतसम् । राधः । भागम्ऽइव । ईमहे ।  
> महीऽइव । कृत्तिः । शरणा । ते । इंद्र । प्र । ते । सुम्ना । नः । अश्नवन् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे असुर बलवन् प्राणवन् हे इंद्र य उक्तगुणोऽस्ति तं प्रचेतसं प्रकृष्टज्ञानं त्वा । उ इत्यवधारणे । पितृवत्पोषकं त्वामेव राधः धर्मादिसाधनं धनं नूनम् इदानीम् ईमहे वयं याचामहे । तत्र दृष्टांतः । भागमिव । यथा कश्चित्पितृभागभूतं धनं याचते तद्वदिंद्रो यजमानेभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यश्च धनं प्रयच्छत्येव । तस्माद्भागभूतं धनं यष्टारो वयं याचामहे । हे इंद्र महीव कृत्तिः । कृत्तिर्यशो वान्नं वा । ‘कृती छेदने । करणे क्तिन् । कृंतत्यनेनेति । ईदृशी कृत्तिरिव ते तव शरणा शरणं गृहमंतरिक्षे द्युलोके महद्वर्तते । अत्र यास्कः---‘कृत्तिः कृंततेर्यशो वान्नं वा महीव कृत्तिः शरणा त इंद्र सुमहत्त इंद्र शरणमंतरिक्षे कृत्तिरिव' (निरु. ५, २२ ) इति । किंच ते तव स्वभूतानि सुम्ना सुम्नानि पुत्रादिविषयसुखानि च नः अस्मान् प्र अश्नवन् । प्रकर्षेणाश्नुवतां व्याप्नुवंतु । अश्नोतेर्लेट्यडागमः ॥ ॥ १३ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O asura, one who has strength and vitality, O Indra, you who have the stated qualities, you who are प्रचेतसं (*pracetasaṃ*), of excellent knowledge and a nourisher like a father: of you alone we ask, now, for राधः (*rādhaḥ*), wealth that is the means to dharma and the like. The particle उ (*u*) is used for emphasis. An illustration is given: भागमिव (*bhāgamiva*), as someone asks for the wealth that is his share from his father, so Indra gives wealth to sacrificers and to praisers; therefore we, the sacrificers, ask for wealth as our share. O Indra, महीव कृत्तिः (*mahīva kṛttiḥ*): kṛtti is fame or food. Like such a kṛtti, your शरणा (*śaraṇā*), your abode, your house, is great in the sky, in the heavenly world. On this Yāska says: कृंततेर्यशो वान्नं वा महीव कृत्तिः शरणा त इंद्र सुमहत्त इंद्र शरणमंतरिक्षे कृत्तिरिव (*kṛṃtateryaśo vānnaṃ vā mahīva kṛttiḥ śaraṇā ta iṃdra sumahatta iṃdra śaraṇamaṃtarikṣe kṛttiriva*) (Ni. 5, 22). Moreover, may your own joys, सुम्ना (*sumnā*), the pleasures connected with sons and the like, pervade us abundantly.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- असुर (*asura*)—O mighty Indra
- भागमिव (*bhāgamiva*)—as a son asks his father for his share of the property
- तं (*taṃ*)—such a renowned one, and
- प्रचेतसं (*pracetasaṃ*)—the most excellent, the wise
- त्वा उ (*tvā u*)—you alone
- राधः (*rādhaḥ*)—for wealth
- नूनं (*nūnaṃ*)—now
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- महीव कृत्तिः (*mahīva kṛttiḥ*)—great like fame or like food
- ते (*te*)—your

### Printed p. 310

- शरणा (*śaraṇā*)—the abode is in the heavenly world
- ते (*te*)—connected with you
- सुम्ना (*sumnā*)—pleasures concerning sons and the like
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- प्र आश्नवत् (*pra āśnavat*)—may they come and reach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O mighty Indra, you who are the most excellent and wise, of you alone we now ask for wealth, as a son asks his father for the wealth that is his share. O Indra, your abode, great like fame, is in the heavenly world. May the pleasures connected with sons and the like that belong to you come and reach us.

##### English translation
Living one, who possess supreme knowledge, we verily ask you for wealth as though it were an inheritance ; your abode (in heaven), Indra, is vast like your glory ; may your blessings fill us.

## Sūkta 91 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘ कन्या वाः' इति सप्तर्चमेकादशं सूक्तम् । अत्रेः पुत्र्यपालाख्या त्वग्दोषपरिहारायानेन सूक्तेनेंद्रं स्तुतवती । अतः सैवर्षिः । प्रथमाद्वितीये पंक्ती शिष्टाः पंचानुष्टुभः । इंद्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं- कन्या वाः सप्तात्रेय्यपालेतिहास ऐंद्र आनुष्टुभं द्विपंक्त्यादि ' इति । विनियोगो लैंगिकः । अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । पुरा किलात्रिसुतापाला ब्रह्मवादिनी केनचित्कारणेन त्वग्दोषदुष्टा सत्यत एव दुर्भगेति भर्त्रा परित्यक्ता पितुराश्रमे त्वग्दोषपरिहाराय चिरकालमिंद्रमधिकृत्य तपस्तेपे । सा कदाचिदिंद्रस्य सोमः प्रियकरो भवति तमिंद्राय दास्यामीति बुद्ध्या नदीतीरं प्रत्यागमत् । सा तत्र स्नात्वा पथि सोममप्यलभत । तमादाय गृहं प्रत्यागच्छंती मार्ग एव तं चखाद । तद्भक्षणकाले दंतघर्षणजातं शब्दं ग्राव्णां सोमाभिषवध्वनिमिति मत्वा तदानीमेवेंद्रः समागमत् । आगत्य तमुवाच । किमत्र ग्रावाणोऽभिषुण्वंतीति । सा प्रत्यूचे । अत्र कन्या स्नानार्थमागत्य सोमं दृष्ट्वा तं भक्षयति तद्भक्षणजो ध्वनिरेव न तु ग्राव्णां सोमाभिषवध्वनिरिति । तथा प्रत्युक्त इंद्रः पराङावर्तत । गच्छंतमिंद्रं सा पुनरब्रवीत् । किमर्थं निवर्तसे त्वं तु सोमपानाय गृहं गृहं प्रति गच्छसि । इदानीमत्रापि मम दंष्ट्राभ्यामभिषुतं सोमं पिब धानादींश्च भक्षयेति । सैवेंद्रमनाद्रियमाणा सती पुनरप्याह । अत्रागतं त्वामिंद्र इति न जानामि त्वयि गृहमागते बहुमानं करिष्यामीतींद्रमुक्त्वात्र समागत इंद्र एव नान्य इति निश्चित्य स्वास्ये निहितं सोममाह । हे सोम त्वमागतायेंद्राय पूर्वं शनैस्ततः शनकैः क्षिप्रं परिस्रवेति । तत इंद्रस्तां कामयित्वा तस्या आस्य एव दंष्ट्राभिषुतं सोममपात् । तत इंद्रेण सोमे पीते सति त्वग्दोषादहं भर्त्रा परित्यक्ता सतीदानीमिंद्रेण संगतेत्यपालायामुक्तायामिंद्रस्तां व्याजहार । किं कामयसे तदहं करिष्यामीत्युक्ते सा वरमचीकमत । मम पितुः शिरो रोमवर्जितं तस्योषरं क्षेत्रं फलादिरहितं मम गुह्यस्थानमप्यरोमशमेतानि रोमफलादियुक्तं कुर्वित्युक्तायां तत्पितृशिरःस्थितं खलतिमपहाय क्षेत्रं च फलादियुक्तं कृत्वैतस्यास्त्वग्दोषपरिहाराय स्वकीयरथच्छिद्रे शकटस्य युगस्य च छिद्र एतां त्रिवारं निश्चकर्ष । तस्याः पूर्वापहता या त्वक् शल्यको द्वितीया गोधा तृतीया कृकलासोऽभूत् । तत इंद्रस्तामप्यपालां सूर्यसदृशत्वचमकरोदित्यैतिहासिकी कथा । एतच्च शाट्यायनब्राह्मणे स्पष्टमुक्तम् । तद्ब्राह्मणं तत्तदृग्व्याख्यानसमये दर्शयिष्यते । एषोऽर्थः ‘कन्या वाः' इत्यादिष्वृक्षु प्रतिपाद्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The eleventh sūkta, of seven Ṛks, beginning कन्या वाः (*kanyā vāḥ*). Apālā, the daughter of Atri, praised Indra with this sūkta for the removal of her skin disease; therefore she is the seer. The first two Ṛks are in the Paṅkti metre, and the remaining five are Anuṣṭubh. Indra is the deity. The Anukramaṇikā says accordingly: कन्या वाः सप्तात्रेय्यपालेतिहास ऐंद्र आनुष्टुभं द्विपंक्त्यादि (*kanyā vāḥ saptātreyyapāletihāsa aiṃdra ānuṣṭubhaṃ dvipaṃktyādi*). The application is by indication (laiṅgika). A story is told about it. Long ago Apālā, the daughter of Atri and a knower of Brahman, was afflicted for some reason with a skin disease and, as truly unfortunate, was abandoned by her husband. In her father's hermitage she practised austerity for a long time, directed at Indra, for the cure of the skin disease. Once, thinking that Soma is dear to Indra and that she would give it to him, she went to the riverbank. After bathing there she found Soma on the way. Carrying it home, she chewed it on the road itself. While she ate it, Indra took the sound produced by the grinding of her teeth for the sound of the pressing stones at a Soma pressing, and came to her at that moment. Coming, he asked: do pressing stones press Soma here? She replied: a maiden has come here to bathe, and seeing Soma she eats it; this sound is only the sound of that eating, not of stones pressing Soma. So answered, Indra turned away. As he went, she spoke again: why do you turn back? You go from house to house for the drinking of Soma; here too, now, drink the Soma pressed by my jaws and eat the grain and the rest. Though she had not yet shown him deference, she spoke again: I do not know that you who have come here are Indra; if you come to my house I shall do you honour. Having thus addressed him, and having concluded that the one who had come was Indra himself and no other, she spoke to the Soma placed in her mouth: O Soma, flow around for the Indra who has come, first gently, then quickly. Then Indra, desiring her, drank the Soma pressed by her teeth in her very mouth. When Indra had drunk the Soma, Apālā said that she, abandoned by her husband because of the skin disease, was now united with Indra. Indra said to her: what do you desire? I shall do it. She chose a boon: my father's head is without hair, his field is barren and without fruit, and my private part is without hair; make these furnished with hair and fruit. Having freed her father's head of its baldness and made the field fruitful, Indra, for the removal of this woman's skin disease, drew her three times through the hole of his chariot, the hole of the cart and the hole of the yoke. The skin shed the first time became a porcupine, the second a monitor lizard, the third a chameleon. Then Indra made Apālā's skin like that of the sun. This is the story. It is stated clearly in the Śāṭyāyana-brāhmaṇa; that Brāhmaṇa will be shown at the explanation of the respective Ṛks. This is the meaning set forth in the Ṛks beginning कन्या वाः (*kanyā vāḥ*).

### Printed p. 311

The Anuvāda: this sūkta, कन्या वाः (*kanyā vāḥ*), is the eleventh sūkta in the ninth anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. The woman named Apālā, the daughter of the seer Atri, praised Indra with this sūkta for the cure of her skin disease. Therefore the seer of this sūkta is the woman Apālā, the daughter of Atri; Indra is the deity; the first two Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Paṅkti metre, the remaining five Ṛks in the Anuṣṭubh metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: कन्या वाः सप्तात्रेय्यपालेतिहास ऐंद्र आनुष्टुभं द्विपंक्त्यादि (*kanyā vāḥ saptātreyyapāletihāsa aiṃdra ānuṣṭubhaṃ dvipaṃktyādi*). The application of the sūkta is laiṅgika.

There is an old story about this sūkta. Long ago a woman named Apālā, the daughter of the seer Atri and a knower of Brahman, was for some other reason attacked by a skin disease (leprosy) and suffered from it. For this reason her husband abandoned her. So this Apālā came to the hermitage of her father, the seer Atri, and practised austerity directed at Indra for the cure of the skin disease that had befallen her. Once that woman thought thus: the Soma juice is very dear to Indra; therefore I shall bring it and offer it to Indra. Thinking so, she went to the bank of the river that was there, bathed, and as she returned she saw Soma plants growing along the way, plucked them, and, as she was coming home with them, she walked along chewing the plant with her teeth (as one splits sugar cane). Then the sound of the chewing with the teeth reached Indra, and thinking: someone here, in a sacrifice, in my honour, is ritually pounding Soma with stones and extracting the juice,

### Printed p. 312

he took it to be the sound of those stones, and himself came to that woman and said: what is this? Here the sounds of Soma plants being pounded are heard. Then the woman said: O Indra, this is not the sound of Soma plants being pounded with stones. A maiden went to the river to bathe, and as she comes back she is chewing and eating a Soma plant that she found on the way; the sound that comes from it is this one. It is not the sound of pounding with stones. Hearing this, Indra began to turn back and go. The woman called him and said again: O man, why do you go back? Do you not go from house to house for the drinking of Soma? Now Soma juice is oozing from the plants that I have torn and am chewing with my teeth. Therefore drink this very Soma juice now, and eat the grains and the like that I give. Having said so, and having doubted whether this man was Indra or not, she said to him again: O man, I do not know that you who have come here are Indra. Still, if you come to our house I shall give you a reward. Having said this, and having decided in her mind that this man who had come here was Indra and no other, she spoke to the Soma juice that was in her mouth: O Soma juice, for Indra flow and drip, first a little at a time and afterwards abundantly. Then Indra cherished her and drank the Soma juice that she had chewed with her teeth and filled her mouth with. After Indra had drunk the Soma, the woman said to Indra: my husband has abandoned me, afflicted as I am with a skin disease; now I have met Indra. Then Indra said to her: O woman, what is your wish? Say it; I shall fulfil it. The woman said: then you must give me a boon. All the hair on my father's head has fallen out and his head is bald; the field that he cultivates has become barren land and nothing grows in it now; and my private part (the place of urination) is without hair, that is, hair does not grow in that part. Therefore now grant that hair grow on my father's head, that plants and the like grow in his field and become fruitful, and that hair grow in my private region. Hearing this, Indra said: let it be so. He made her father's head free of the disease **NOTE** and his field fruitful, and then, for the cure of that woman's skin disease, he made her pass three times through the hole of his chariot, the hole of the cart, and the hole of the yoke, these three holes. By this the skin of that woman became free of disease and bright like the radiance of the sun. This old story the commentator tells here, and he says that this account is clearly described in the Śāṭyāyana-brāhmaṇa, and that this matter will be described at the proper place in the respective Ṛks.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> क॒न्या॒३॒॑ वार॑वाय॒ती सोम॒मपि॑ स्रु॒तावि॑दत् ।  
> अस्तं॒ भरं॑त्यब्रवी॒दिंद्रा॑य सुनवै त्वा श॒क्राय॑ सुनवै त्वा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कन्या । वाः । अवऽयती । सोमम् । अपि । स्रुता । अविदत् ।  
> अस्तम् । भरंती । अब्रवीत् । इंद्राय । सुनवै । त्वा । शक्राय । सुनवै । त्वा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वाः उदकं प्रति अवायती स्नानार्थमभ्यवगच्छंती कन्या अपाला नाम स्त्री स्रुता स्रुतौ मार्गे सोममपि अविदत् अलभत ।  ‘ विद्लृ लाभे' । लतारूपं तं सोमम् अस्तं गृहं प्रति भरंती आहरंती सा सोमम् अब्रवीत् । हे सोम त्वा त्वाम् इंद्राय सुनवै मम दंतैरेवाभिषुणवै । पुनर्हे सोम त्वा त्वां शक्राय समर्थायेंद्राय सुनवै इदानीमेवाभिषवं करवै । सोमभक्षणकाले दंतध्वनिं ग्रावध्वनिमिति मत्वेंद्रस्तामगमत् । एषोऽर्थः शाट्यायनब्राह्मणे स्पष्टमभिहितः ‘ सा तीर्थमभ्यवयंती सोमांशुमविंदत्तं समखादत्तस्यै ह  ग्रावाण इव दंता ऊदुः। स इंद्र आद्रवत् ग्रावाणो वै वदंतीति । सा तमभिव्याजहार कन्या वारवायती सोममपि स्रुताविददित्यस्यै त इदं ग्रावाण इव दंता वदंतीति विदित्वेंद्रः पराङावर्तत । तमब्रवीदसौ य एषि वीरक इत्यादिना' इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वाः (*vāḥ*) is water; going down towards the water for bathing, the maiden, the woman named Apālā, on the way (स्रुता (*srutā*)) found Soma as well. Carrying that Soma, in the form of a plant, home (अस्तं (*astaṃ*)), she addressed the Soma: O Soma, I shall press you for Indra, with my own teeth; and again, O Soma, I shall press you for Śakra, the capable Indra, right now. At the time of eating the Soma, Indra, taking the sound of the teeth for the sound of pressing stones, came to her. This meaning is stated clearly in the Śāṭyāyana-brāhmaṇa: सा तीर्थमभ्यवयंती सोमांशुमविंदत्तं समखादत्तस्यै ह ग्रावाण इव दंता ऊदुः। स इंद्र आद्रवत् ग्रावाणो वै वदंतीति । सा तमभिव्याजहार कन्या वारवायती सोममपि स्रुताविददित्यस्यै त इदं ग्रावाण इव दंता वदंतीति विदित्वेंद्रः पराङावर्तत । तमब्रवीदसौ य एषि वीरक इत्यादिना (*sā tīrthamabhyavayaṃtī somāṃśumaviṃdattaṃ samakhādattasyai ha grāvāṇa iva daṃtā ūduḥ| sa iṃdra ādravat grāvāṇo vai vadaṃtīti | sā tamabhivyājahāra kanyā vāravāyatī somamapi srutāvidadityasyai ta idaṃ grāvāṇa iva daṃtā vadaṃtīti viditveṃdraḥ parāṅāvartata | tamabravīdasau ya eṣi vīraka ityādinā*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वाः (*vāḥ*)—to the water of the river
- अवायती (*avāyatī*)—going for bathing
- कन्या (*kanyā*)—the woman named Apālā
- स्रुता (*srutā*)—in the middle of the way
- सोमं अपि (*somaṃ api*)—the Soma plant
- अविदत् (*avidat*)—she saw

### Printed p. 314

- (the Soma plant came to her) afterwards
- अस्तं (*astaṃ*)—while coming towards her house
- भरंती (*bharaṃtī*)—bringing that Soma
- अब्रवीत् (*abravīt*)—she said thus (O Soma)
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra, that is, in order to offer to Indra
- सुनवै (*sunavai*)—I shall tear with my teeth (O) Soma
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- शक्राय (*śakrāya*)—for the capable Indra
- सुनवै (*sunavai*)—I shall tear with my teeth and make the juice flow out

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The woman named Apālā, who was going to the water of the river to bathe, saw on her way home after the bath the Soma plant that she found on the road, and said: O Soma, in order to offer you to Indra, I shall tear you with my teeth and bring out the juice. O Soma, for the capable Indra himself I shall tear you with my teeth and take out the juice.

##### English translation
A young woman going to the water found Soma in the path ; as she carried it home she said, I will press you for Indra, I will press you for Shakra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The woman Apālā spoken of in the present Ṛk, while returning from the river, was tearing with her teeth the Soma she had found on the road, and that sound was heard by Indra. Then Indra thought: here the sound of Soma being pounded with grāvas (stones) is being heard; therefore I shall go there; and he came there. The commentator cites here what is said of this account in the Śāṭyāyana-brāhmaṇa:

सा तीर्थमभ्यवयंती सोमांशुमविंदत्तं समुखादत्तस्यै ह ग्रावाण इव दंता ऊदुः । स इंद्र आप्रवत् ग्रावाणो वै वदंतीति । सा तमभिव्याजहार कन्या वारवायती सोममपि स्रुताविददित्यस्यै त इदं ग्रावाण इव दंता वदंतीति विदित्वेंद्रः पराजावर्तत । तमब्रवीदसौ य एषि वीरक इत्यादिना ॥ (*sā tīrthamabhyavayaṃtī somāṃśumaviṃdattaṃ samukhādattasyai ha grāvāṇa iva daṃtā ūduḥ | sa iṃdra āpravat grāvāṇo vai vadaṃtīti | sā tamabhivyājahāra kanyā vāravāyatī somamapi srutāvidadityasyai ta idaṃ grāvāṇa iva daṃtā vadaṃtīti viditveṃdraḥ parājāvartata | tamabravīdasau ya eṣi vīraka ityādinā ‖*) (Śā. Brā.) **NOTE**

When the woman named Apālā was returning from the river, she found there a Soma plant that had grown. She plucked it and came along tearing it with her teeth and eating it, and the sound of the tearing with the teeth was heard like the sound of Soma plants being pounded with a stone. Therefore Indra, thinking that this must be the sound of a Soma plant being pounded with a stone,

### Printed p. 315

came there quickly. Then the woman said to Indra: O man, you have run here on hearing this sound, have you not? This is only the sound that comes from my teeth. It is not the sound of Soma plants being pounded with stones. At this Indra, dejected in mind, made ready to go back. Seeing that, the woman questions Indra with the next Ṛk, असौ य एषि (*asau ya eṣi*).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒सौ य एषि॑ वीर॒को गृ॒हंगृ॑हं वि॒चाक॑शद् ।  
> इ॒मं जंभ॑सुतं पिब धा॒नावं॑तं करं॒भिण॑मपू॒पवं॑तमु॒क्थिन॑म् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असौ । यः । एषि । वीरकः । गृहम्ऽगृहम् । विऽचाकशत् ।  
> इमम् । जंभऽसुतम् । पिब । धानाऽवंतम् । करंभिणम् । अपूपऽवंतम् । उक्थिनम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सा शक्रमब्रवीत् । हे इंद्र वीरकः वीरः समर्थस्त्वं यः असौ त्वं विचाकशत् । ‘काशृ दीप्तौ' । यङ्लुकि शतरि रूपम् । धातोर्ह्रस्वश्छांदसः । अत्यर्थं दीप्यमानः सन् गृहंगृहं यजमानगृहं प्रति सोमपानाय त्वम् एषि गच्छसि । अतस्त्वमत्रापि जंभसुतं मम दंतैरभिषुतम् इमं सोमं पिब । कीदृशम् । धानावंतम् । धाना भृष्टयवाः । तद्वंतं करंभिणं सक्तुमंतम् अपूपवंतं पुरोडाशादिसहितम् उक्थिनं स्तोत्रादियुक्तमेतादृशं सोममत्रैव पिबेति । सा सोमेन सह धानादीनावेदयत् स्तोत्रं चाकार्षीदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

She said to Śakra: O Indra, you, वीरकः (*vīrakaḥ*), a hero, one who is capable, who असौ (*asau*), you, shining exceedingly (विचाकशत् (*vicākaśat*)), go गृहंगृहं (*gṛhaṃgṛhaṃ*), to each sacrificer's house, for the drinking of Soma. Therefore here too drink this Soma जंभसुतं (*jaṃbhasutaṃ*), pressed by my teeth. Of what kind? धानावंतं (*dhānāvaṃtaṃ*): धाना (*dhānā*) are parched barley grains, and it has them; करंभिणं (*karaṃbhiṇaṃ*), with barley meal; अपूपवंतं (*apūpavaṃtaṃ*), with the purodāśa and the like; उक्थिनं (*ukthinaṃ*), accompanied by hymns and the like. Drink such a Soma right here. Together with the Soma she presented grains and the rest, and she made a hymn; that is the meaning.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) वीरकः (*vīrakaḥ*)—mighty
- असौ (*asau*)—well known
- यः त्वं (*yaḥ tvaṃ*)—(जाप (*jāpa*)) you **NOTE**
- विचाकशत् (*vicākaśat*)—shining with your own radiance
- गृहंगृहं (*gṛhaṃgṛhaṃ*)—to the house of many sacrificers
- एषि (*eṣi*)—you go for the drinking of Soma; therefore you
- जंभसुतं (*jaṃbhasutaṃ*)—that which, chewed by my teeth, drips from it
- धानावंतं (*dhānāvaṃtaṃ*)—mixed with grains
- करंभिणं (*karaṃbhiṇaṃ*)—mixed with flour

### Printed p. 316

- आपूपवंतं (*āpūpavaṃtaṃ*)—accompanied by purodāśa and the like
- उक्थिनं (*ukthinaṃ*)—offered with the recitation of mantras
- इमं (*imaṃ*)—this Soma juice
- पिब (*piba*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you, the mighty one, shining in your greatness, go to the house of every sacrificer for the drinking of Soma. Therefore drink now this Soma juice, which drips from the Soma plants that I am chewing with my teeth, which is mixed with grains, flour and purodāśa and the like, and which is offered with mantras.

##### English translation
You, who goes from house to house, a hero bright in your splendour, drink this Soma pressed by my teeth, together with fried grains of barley, the karambha, cakes and hymns.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ च॒न त्वा॑ चिकित्सा॒मोऽधि॑ च॒न त्वा॒ नेम॑सि ।  
> शनै॑रिव शन॒कैरि॒वेंद्रा॑येंदो॒ परि॑ स्रव ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शनैःऽइव । शनकैःऽइव । इंद्राय । इंदो इति । परि । स्रव ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुनरपि सा तमनादृत्याह । हे इंद्र । चन इति निपातसमुदायोऽवधारणार्थे । त्वा त्वाम् आ चिकित्सामः ज्ञातुमिच्छाम एव । इह मार्ग एवागतं त्वा त्वां न अधि इमसि नाधिगच्छामः । अत्रापि चन इत्यवधारणे । मम गृहमागच्छंतं त्वामिंद्र इति न जानीम एवेत्यपाला तमिंद्रमुक्त्वा स्वास्ये स्थितं सोमं प्रत्याह । हे इंदो क्षरणशील सोम अस्मा आगताय इंद्राय तदर्थं पूर्वं शनैः मंदं मंदं ततः शनकैरिव । कुत्सितार्थेऽकच् । कुत्सितं शनैः शनकैः । क्षिप्रमित्यर्थः । क्षिप्रमेव त्वं परि स्रव मदीयदंष्ट्राभिरभिषूयमाणः सन् परितः क्षरेति । तथा यज्ञेष्वपि ग्रावभिरभिषूयमाणः सोमः प्रथमं शनैः परिस्रवति ततः शनकैः क्षिप्रमिति तदभिप्रायेणोक्तम् । तत इंद्र एतद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा तदानीमेवमभिषुतं सोमं यज्ञस्थानीयादपालामुखादेवाधासीत् । उक्तार्थः शाट्यायनकब्राह्मणे स्पष्टमभ्यधायि- ‘ अनाद्रियमाणैव तमब्रवीदा चन त्वा चिकित्सामोऽधि चन त्वा नेमसीति । पुरा मां सर्वयर्चापाला स्तौतीत्युपपर्यावर्तत शनैरिव शनकैरिवेंद्रायेंदो परि स्रवेति ह वा अस्यै मुखात्सोमं निरधयत्सोमपीथ इह वा अस्य भवति य एवं विद्वान् स्त्रीमुपजिघ्रति ' इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Again she, not respecting him, said: O Indra, चन (*cana*) is a combination of particles in the sense of emphasis. We do wish to know you (आ चिकित्सामः (*ā cikitsāmaḥ*)). You who have come here on the road itself, we do not recognise (न अधि इमसि (*na adhi imasi*)); here too चन (*cana*) is for emphasis. Having said to Indra, "I do not know that you who are coming to my house are Indra", Apālā then spoke to the Soma that was in her mouth: O Indu, flowing Soma, for this Indra who has come, first gently (शनैः (*śanaiḥ*)), slowly, slowly, then quickly (शनकैरिव (*śanakairiva*)), flow around, pressed by my teeth, all around. So also in sacrifices Soma pressed by the pressing stones flows first gently and then quickly; it was said with that in view. Then Indra, hearing this speech, at that very moment drank the Soma so pressed from Apālā's mouth, which stood in the place of the sacrifice. The meaning stated was clearly declared in the Śāṭyāyaka-brāhmaṇa: अनाद्रियमाणैव तमब्रवीदा चन त्वा चिकित्सामोऽधि चन त्वा नेमसीति । पुरा मां सर्वयर्चापाला स्तौतीत्युपपर्यावर्तत शनैरिव शनकैरिवेंद्रायेंदो परि स्रवेति ह वा अस्यै मुखात्सोमं निरधयत्सोमपीथ इह वा अस्य भवति य एवं विद्वान् स्त्रीमुपजिघ्रति (*anādriyamāṇaiva tamabravīdā cana tvā cikitsāmo 'dhi cana tvā nemasīti | purā māṃ sarvayarcāpālā stautītyupaparyāvartata śanairiva śanakairiveṃdrāyeṃdo pari sraveti ha vā asyai mukhātsomaṃ niradhayatsomapītha iha vā asya bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān strīmupajighrati*).

### Printed p. 317

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) त्वा चन (*tvā cana*)—you indeed
- आ चिकित्सानुः (*ā cikitsānuḥ*)—we wish to know **NOTE**
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you who are going on this road
- नॆ (*nè*)—now **NOTE**
- अधि इमसि चन (*adhi imasi cana*)—we are unable to know
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma, dripping (from my mouth)
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- शनैः (*śanaiḥ*)—(first) little by little, and (afterwards)
- शनकैः (*śanakaiḥ*)—very quickly
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow, trickling

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, we cannot know your great nature. Yet we wish to know it. O Soma juice dripping from my mouth, for Indra to drink, first trickle little by little and then gradually, flow quickly.

##### English translation
We wish to know you, but here we know you not. O Soma, flow forth for Indra first slowly, then quickly.

> कु॒विच्छक॑त्कु॒वित्कर॑त्कु॒विन्नो॒ वस्य॑स॒स्कर॑त् ।  
> कु॒वित्प॑ति॒द्विषो॑ य॒तीरिंद्रे॑ण सं॒गमा॑महै ॥ ४ ॥

> कुवित् । पतिऽद्विषः । यतीः । इंद्रेण । सम्ऽगमामहै ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 318

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सोमं पीतवानिंद्रोऽस्मानेवं करोत्वित्याह । स इंद्रः कुवित् बहुवारमस्मान् शकत् शक्तान् समर्थान् करोतु । किंच कुवित् बहु चास्मभ्यं करत् करोतु । किंच स एवेंद्रः नः अस्मान् कुवित् बहुकृत्वः वस्यसः वसीयसोऽतिशयेन वसुमतः करोतु । करोतेः शक्नोतेश्च लेट्यडागमः । इदानीमात्रेय्यहमेवं करिष्यामीति वदति । पूर्वं कुवित् बहु पतिद्विषः त्वग्दोषात्पतिभिर्भर्तृभिबहुवारं द्विष्टा अत एव यतीः पतिभ्यः सकाशादितो गच्छंत्यो वयं कैश्चिदप्यनूह्यमानाः सत्यः संप्रति इंद्रेण सह संगमामहै संगच्छामहै । सर्वत्र पूजार्थे बहुवचनम् । संगमशब्देनेंद्रोऽपालामचकमतेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra having drunk the Soma, she says: may he do so to us. May that Indra, कुवित् (*kuvit*), many times, make us शकत् (*śakat*), able, capable. Moreover, may he do much for us. And may that same Indra make us वस्यसः (*vasyasaḥ*), exceedingly wealthy. Now Apālā says that she will do thus: previously, पतिद्विषः (*patidviṣaḥ*), hated many times by husbands because of the skin disease, and therefore यतीः (*yatīḥ*), leaving the husbands and going from here, not carried off by anyone, we now unite, संगमामहै (*saṃgamāmahai*), with Indra. The plural is used everywhere in the sense of honour. By the word संगम (*saṃgama*) is meant that Indra desired Apālā.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (that Indra) कुवित् (*kuvit*)—in many ways
- शकत् (*śakat*)—let him make us capable
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—abundantly
- करत् (*karat*)—let him give to us
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—in many ways
- वस्यसः (*vasyasaḥ*)—endowed with wealth
- करत् (*karat*)—let him make
- कुवित् (*kuvit*)—greatly
- पतिद्विषः (*patidviṣaḥ*)—hated by the husband because of my skin disease
- यतीः (*yatīḥ*)—we (I), who have been sent away from the husband's side, now
- इंद्रेण (*iṃdreṇa*)—with Indra
- संगमामहै (*saṃgamāmahai*)—may be united

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra make us very capable and give us wealth and the like of many kinds; may I, who because of my skin disease was driven out of the house by my husband, be united with Indra.

##### English translation
May (Indra) repeatedly make us powerful, may he do abundantly for us, may he repeatedly make us very rich ; often hated by our husband and forced to leave him, may we be united to Indra.

> इ॒मानि॒ त्रीणि॑ वि॒ष्टपा॒ तानीं॑द्र॒ वि रो॑हय ।  
> शिर॑स्त॒तस्यो॒र्वरा॒मादि॒दं म॒ उपो॒दरे॑ ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 319

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमानि । त्रीणि । विष्टपा । तानि । इंद्र । वि । रोहय ।  
> शिरः । ततस्य । उर्वराम् । आत् । इदम् । मे । उप । उदरे ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रेण किं कामयसे तद्दास्यामीत्युक्ता सा वरमनया प्रार्थयते । हे इंद्र इमानि त्रीणि विष्टपानि स्थानानि संति । तानि त्रीणि स्थानानि वि रोहय उत्पादय । कानि तानि । ततस्य मम पितुः रोमवर्जितं शिरः । खलतिमित्यर्थः। तच्चापगमय । रोमशं कुर्वित्यर्थः । उर्वरां तस्योषर क्षेत्रं सर्वसस्याढ्यं कुरु । आत् अनंतरं मे मम उपोदरे उपोदरस्य समीपे यत् इदं स्थानम् । गुह्यमित्यर्थः। तच्च त्वग्दोषे सत्यसंजातरोमकम् । तदपि त्वग्दोषपरिहारेण रोमयुक्तं कुरु। एतानि त्रीणि स्थानानि । एषोऽर्थः शाट्यायनके प्रपंचेनोक्तः- ‘ तामब्रवीदपाले किं कामयसीति । साब्रवीदिमानि त्रीणि विष्टपेति खलतिर्हास्यै पिता स तं हाखलतिं चकारोर्वरा हास्य न जज्ञे सो ह जज्ञ उपस्थे हास्यै रोमाणि नासुस्तान्यु ह जज्ञिर इत्यस्योत्तरा भूयसे निर्वचनीयासौ च या नः' इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra having said, "What do you desire? I shall give it", she asks for a boon with this Ṛk. O Indra, there are these three places (विष्टपानि (*viṣṭapāni*)). Cause those three places to grow (वि रोहय (*vi rohaya*)), that is, produce them. Which are they? ततस्य (*tatasya*), my father's head devoid of hair, that is, bald; remove that, that is, make it hairy. उर्वरां (*urvarāṃ*), make his barren field rich in all crops. Then, मे (*me*) उप उदरे (*upa udare*), near my belly there is this place, that is, the private part; that too, in the skin disease, has not grown hair; make it furnished with hair by the cure of the skin disease. These are the three places. This meaning is told at length in the Śāṭyāyaka: तामब्रवीदपाले किं कामयसीति । साब्रवीदिमानि त्रीणि विष्टपेति खलतिर्हास्यै पिता स तं हाखलतिं चकारोर्वरा हास्य न जज्ञे सो ह जज्ञ उपस्थे हास्यै रोमाणि नासुस्तान्यु ह जज्ञिर इत्यस्योत्तरा भूयसे निर्वचनीयासौ च या नः (*tāmabravīdapāle kiṃ kāmayasīti | sābravīdimāni trīṇi viṣṭapeti khalatirhāsyai pitā sa taṃ hākhalatiṃ cakārorvarā hāsya na jajñe so ha jajña upasthe hāsyai romāṇi nāsustānyu ha jajñira ityasyottarā bhūyase nirvacanīyāsau ca yā naḥ*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- इमानि त्रीणि विष्टपा (*imāni trīṇi viṣṭapā*)—there are these three places
- तानि (*tāni*)—those, that is, in them
- वि रोहय (*vi rohaya*)—cause growth
- ततस्य शिरः (*tatasya śiraḥ*)—my father's bald head without hair, make it hairy
- उर्वरां (*urvarāṃ*)—make his father's barren land bear crops
- आत् (*āt*)—afterwards
- मे (*me*)—my
- उप उदरे (*upa udare*)—near the lower belly
- इदं (*idaṃ*)—make this private region hairy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, there are now three places that you must set right. Make hair grow again on my father's bald head, which has no hair; make the plants and the like grow and become fruitful in his field, which is barren land; and, because of the skin disease, set right the private region below my lower belly, where hair does not grow, and make hair grow again.

### Printed p. 320

##### English translation
These three places,—you cause them all to grow,—my father's (bald) head, his (barren) field, and my body.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒सौ च॒ या न॑ उ॒र्वरादि॒मां त॒न्वं१॒॑ मम॑ ।  
> अथो॑ त॒तस्य॒ यच्छिरः॒ सर्वा॒ ता रो॑म॒शा कृ॑धि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असौ । च । या । नः । उर्वरा । आत् । इमाम् । तन्वम् । मम ।  
> अथो इति । ततस्य । यत् । शिरः । सर्वा । ता । रोमशा । कृधि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उक्तमेवार्थमनया विवृणोति । नः अस्माकं पितुः या असौ उर्वरा यदिदमूषरं क्षेत्रमस्ति ॥ आत् अनंतरं मम इमां तन्वम् इदं त्वग्दोषदुष्टं गुह्यस्थानम् । अथो अथापि च ततस्य तातस्य यच्छिरः रोमवर्जितमस्ति एतानि सर्वा सर्वाणि तानीमानि त्रीणि स्थानानि रोमशा रोमशानि कृधि कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

With this Ṛk he explains the very meaning already stated. नः (*naḥ*): of us, that is, of my father, the उर्वरा (*urvarā*), the field that is this barren land; आत् (*āt*), then, my इमां तन्वम् (*imāṃ tanvam*), this place spoilt by the skin disease, the private part; अथो (*atho*), and also, my father's शिरः (*śiraḥ*), the head that is without hair: all these three places, make hairy and fruitful, कृधि (*kṛdhi*), do it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) नः (*naḥ*)—of our (father)
- उर्वरा (*urvarā*)—which is barren land
- या असौ (*yā asau*)—whatever field there is, that also
- आत् (*āt*)—afterwards
- मम (*mama*)—my
- इमां तन्वं (*imāṃ tanvaṃ*)—this body afflicted with the skin disease, that is, the private region
- अथो (*atho*)—afterwards
- ततस्य (*tatasya*)—of my father
- यत् शिरः (*yat śiraḥ*)—whatever bald head without hair there is, that also
- सर्वा (*sarvā*)—all these three regions
- रोमशा (*romaśā*)—make furnished with hair, that is, so that hair grows well
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—do

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, make plants and the like grow in my father's field, which is barren land; make hair grow again in my private region, where because of the skin disease hair does not grow; and make hair grow on my father's bald head as before.

### Printed p. 321

##### English translation
This field which is our (father's), and this my body and the head of my father,—you make all these bear a crop.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> खे रथ॑स्य॒ खेऽन॑सः॒ खे यु॒गस्य॑ शतक्रतो ।  
> अ॒पा॒लामिं॑द्र॒ त्रिष्पू॒त्व्यकृ॑णोः॒ सूर्य॑त्वचम् ॥ ७ ॥
