### Printed p. 361

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृत्रहन् वृत्रस्यापामावरकस्य मेघस्य हंतः हे सूर्य सूर्यात्मक इंद्र अद्य अस्मिन् दिने यत् कच्च यत्किंचित्पदार्थजातम् अभि अभिमुखीकृत्य उदगाः ।  ‘ इण् गतौ । उत्पूर्वः । तस्य लुङि गादेशः। स्वतेजसोद्गतः प्रादुर्भूतोऽसि तदा तत् सर्वं स्थावरजंगमात्मकं जगत् ते तव वशे भवति । त्वदधीनं भवति । उदिते सूर्ये त्वदर्थं प्राक्कर्म कुर्वंति जुह्वति च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O slayer of Vṛtra, the cloud that holds back the waters, O Sūrya, Indra of the nature of the sun: today, whatever thing of any kind you rise towards, facing it, having appeared by your own radiance (इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*), with the prefix उत् (*ut*)), then all that world, moving and unmoving, comes under your control, is dependent on you. When the sun has risen, men perform rites for you in the east and offer oblations.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहन् (*vṛtrahan*)—who strike the cloud that holds back the water without letting it flow
- सूर्य (*sūrya*)—of the nature of the sun
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अद्य (*adya*)—today
- यत् कच्च (*yat kacca*)—whatever particular thing
- अभि (*abhi*)—aiming at
- उदगाः (*udagāḥ*)—you rise
- तत् (*tat*)—then
- सर्वं (*sarvaṃ*)—this whole world, moving and unmoving
- ते (*te*)—your
- वशे (*vaśe*)—is under the control

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who strike the cloud that obstructs the waters and pour down rain, who are of the nature of the sun, whenever today you rise aiming at this particular world, then this whole world, moving and unmoving, is under your control.

##### English translation
Whatsoever, O sun, slayer of Vritra, you have risen upon to-day,— it is all, Indra, under your power.

> उतो इति । तत् । सत्यम् । इत् । तव ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 362

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वाशब्दः समुच्चये । अपि च हे प्रवृद्ध स्वबलेन प्रवर्धमान सत्पते सतां पते स्वप्रकाशाधिक्येन सतां  नक्षत्राणां पते हे इंद्र न मरै इति मनुष्यवद्वार्धक्येनाहं न म्रिय इति यत् यदि मन्ये युध्यसे। मृङ् प्राणत्यागे'। लेट्यडागमः।' वैतोऽन्यत्र' इत्यैकारः। उतो अपि च तव तत् न म्रिय इति मननं सत्यमित् यथार्थमेव । इंद्रो न म्रियत इत्यर्थे मंत्रांतरं-- न ह्यस्या अपरं चन जरसा मरते पतिः' (ऋ. सं. १०. ८६. ११) इति ॥ ॥ २१ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The word वाशब्दः (*vāśabdaḥ*) is used in the sense of "and also". O Indra, who grow forth by your own strength, lord of the good (or, by the abundance of your own radiance, lord of the good, that is, of the stars): if you think "like a man, I shall not die of old age", that thought of yours, that you do not die, is true indeed, exactly as it is. For the meaning that Indra does not die, another mantra is adduced: न ह्यस्या अपरं चन जरसा मरते पतिः (*na hyasyā aparaṃ cana jarasā marate patiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10. 86. 11).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वा (*vā*)—and
- प्रवृद्ध (*pravṛddha*)—who grow by your own strength
- सत्पते (*satpate*)—protector of the good (or protector of the stars)
- ऎल्लै इंद्रने (*èllai iṃdrane*)—O Indra
- न मर्य इति (*na marya iti*)—that I shall not die like men
- यत् मन्यसे (*yat manyase*)—if you think
- उतो (*uto*)—and
- तव तत् (*tava tat*)—that knowledge of yours that you will not die
- सत्यं इत् (*satyaṃ it*)—is indeed true

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

And, O Indra, who grow exceedingly by your own strength and are the protector of the good, if you think "Like men, I shall not die when I grow old", that knowledge of yours is true indeed.

##### English translation
When, swelling in your might, lord of the good, you think " I shall not die, " that thought of yours is indeed true.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the matter that Indra has no old age and death, the commentator has cited as an example the scriptural sentence न ह्यस्या अपरं चन जरसा मरते पतिः (*na hyasyā aparaṃ cana jarasā marate patiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-86-11).

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ये सोमा॑सः परा॒वति॒ ये अ॑र्वा॒वति॑ सुन्वि॒रे ।  
> सर्वाँ॒स्ताँ इं॑द्र गच्छसि ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 363

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ये । सोमासः । पराऽवति । ये । अर्वाऽवति । सुन्विरे ।  
> सर्वान् । तान् । इंद्र । गच्छसि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र ये सोमासः सोमाः परावति विप्रकृष्टेऽतिदूरदेशे ये सोमाः अर्वावति अंतिकतमे देशे च सुन्विरे । छंदसि द्विर्वचनस्य विकल्पितत्वादत्र द्विर्वचनाभावः। ये सोमा ऋत्विग्भिरभिषूयंते सर्वान् दूरे समीपे चाभिषूयमाणान् तान् सोमान् गच्छसि तत्पानार्थं युगपत्प्राप्नोषि । अनेनेंद्रस्य सर्वगतत्वं सूचितम् ॥
> अप्तोर्यामे ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनोऽतिरिक्तोक्थे ' तमिंद्रं वाजयामसि' इति स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च - तमिंद्रं वाजयामसि महाँ इंद्रो य ओजसा' ( आश्व. श्रौ. ९. ११ ) इति । व्यूळ्हस्य दशरात्रस्य पंचमेऽहनि निष्केवल्येऽयमेव तृचो निविद्धानीयः । सूत्रितं च व्यूळ्हश्चेदिति खंडे--  ‘ मरुत्वाँ इंद्र मीढ्वस्तमिंद्रं वाजयामसि' (आश्व. श्रौ. ८. ८) इति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the Soma-juices that are pressed far away in a very distant region, and the Soma-juices that are pressed in a very near region, all of those that the priests press, whether far or near, to all those Soma-juices you go, reaching them at one and the same time in order to drink them. By this the omnipresence of Indra is indicated. This verse is the Stotriya triplet of the Āptoryāma, in the Atirikta-uktha of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, beginning तमिंद्रं वाजयामसि (*tamiṃdraṃ vājayāmasi*); it is prescribed in the Sūtra: तमिंद्रं वाजयामसि महाँ इंद्रो य ओजसा (*tamiṃdraṃ vājayāmasi mahām̐ iṃdro ya ojasā*) (Āśva. Śrau. 9. 11) **NOTE**. On the fifth day of the Vyūḍha Daśarātra, in the Niṣkevalya, this very triplet is to be used as the Nividdhānīya. It is prescribed in the section beginning व्यूळ्हश्चेदिति (*vyūḷhaścediti*): मरुत्वाँ इंद्र मीढ्वस्तमिंद्रं वाजयामसि (*marutvām̐ iṃdra mīḍhvastamiṃdraṃ vājayāmasi*) (Āśva. Śrau. 8. 8).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- परावति (*parāvati*)—in a distant region
- यो सोमासः (*yo somāsaḥ*)—which Soma-juices
- सुन्विरे (*sunvire*)—are pressed by the priests
- अर्वावति (*arvāvati*)—in a near region
- यो सोमाः (*yo somāḥ*)—which Soma-juices are pressed
- सर्वान् तान् (*sarvān tān*)—aiming at both those kinds of Soma-juices
- गच्छसि (*gacchasi*)—you go

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, whether the priests and sacrificers press Soma-juices for you in a distant region or in a near region, wherever they press them, you go there, to all of them, at one and the same time in order to drink those Soma-juices.

##### English translation
You go at once, Indra, to all those Soma-libations which are effused afar or effused near.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यजमाना आहुः । तं पूर्वोक्तलक्षणम् इंद्रं वाजयामसि वाजयामः । सोमेन स्तुतिभिर्वा वाजवंतं बलवंतं कुर्मः । किमर्थम् । महे महते वृत्राय अपामावरकं वृत्रासुरं हंतवे हंतुम् । सोमपानेन मत्तः स्तुतिभिर्वा स्तुतः सन् वृषा धनानां सेक्ता दाता सः इंद्रः वृषभः अस्माकं स्तोतॄणां सोमस्य दातॄणां धनादिसेचको दाता भुवत् भवतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sacrificers speak. We invigorate that Indra, of the kind described before, with Soma or with praises; we make him strong. For what purpose: to slay the great Vṛtra, the asura Vṛtra, who obstructs the waters. Intoxicated by drinking Soma, or praised by praises, that Indra, the showerer, the giver, the pourer of wealth, may become for us, the praisers and givers of Soma, a bounteous giver, a pourer of wealth and the rest.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महे (*mahe*)—mighty
- वृत्राय (*vṛtrāya*)—Vṛtra, the asura
- हंतवे (*haṃtave*)—for slaying
- तं इंद्रं (*taṃ iṃdraṃ*)—that Indra
- वाजयामसि (*vājayāmasi*)—we praise with hymns and make him full of strength
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—the showerer of desires
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Indra
- वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*)—as a giver to us of wealth and the rest
- भुवत् (*bhuvat*)—may he be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We praise that Indra with hymns so that he may become strong to slay the asura Vṛtra. May that Indra, the showerer of desires and full of strength, become the giver to us of wealth and the rest.

##### English translation
We invigorate that (great) Indra for the slaying of mighty Vritra ; may he be a bounteous showerer (of wealth).

### Printed p. 365

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

It is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra तमिंद्रं वाजयामसि महा इंद्रो य ओजसा (*tamiṃdraṃ vājayāmasi mahā iṃdro ya ojasā*) (Ā. 9-11), that, among the Atirikta-uktha mantras to be recited in the sacrifice called Āptoryāma by the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the three Ṛks beginning तमिंद्रं वाजयामसि (*tamiṃdraṃ vājayāmasi*) are to be recited as the Stotriya triplet. It is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra मरुत्वा इंद्र मीढ्वस्तमिंद्रं वाजयामसि (*marutvā iṃdra mīḍhvastamiṃdraṃ vājayāmasi*) (Ā. 8-8) that, on the fifth day of the ten-night sacrifice called Vyūḍha, among the Niṣkevalya Śastra mantras, this triplet is to be recited as the Nividdhānīya triplet.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः॒ स दाम॑ने कृ॒त ओजि॑ष्ठः॒ स मदे॑ हि॒तः ।  
> द्यु॒म्नी श्लो॒की स सो॒म्यः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । सः । दामने । कृतः । ओजिष्ठः । सः । मदे । हितः ।  
> द्युम्नी । श्लोकी । सः । सोम्यः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सः इंद्रः दामने स्तोतृभ्यो धनादिदानायैव कृतः प्रजापतिना सृष्टः । किंच ओजिष्ठः ओजस्वितमः सः एवेंद्रः मदे। माद्यंत्यनेनेति मदः सोमः । तस्मिंश्च प्रजापतिना सृष्टिकाले हितः । सोमपानार्थं च निहित इत्यर्थः । द्युम्नी । 'द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वान्नं वा' इति । यशस्व्यन्नवान् वा अत एव श्लोकी । श्लोकः स्तुतिः । तद्वान् सः इंद्रः सोम्यः सोमार्हो भवति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Indra was created by Prajāpati for giving wealth and the rest to the praisers. Moreover that same Indra, the most mighty, was placed by Prajāpati at the time of creation in मदे (*made*), that is, in Soma (that by which they are exhilarated is मदः (*madaḥ*), Soma); that is, he was placed for the drinking of Soma. द्युम्नी (*dyumnī*): he cites द्युम्नं द्योततेर्यशो वान्नं वा (*dyumnaṃ dyotateryaśo vānnaṃ vā*), so the word means one possessed of fame or of food. For that very reason he is श्लोकी (*ślokī*): श्लोकः (*ślokaḥ*) is praise, and he possesses it. That Indra is सोम्यः (*somyaḥ*), worthy of Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सः इंद्रः (*saḥ iṃdraḥ*)—that same Indra
- दामने (*dāmane*)—for giving wealth and the rest to the people who praise
- कृतः (*kṛtaḥ*)—has been created by Brahmā
- ओजिष्ठः (*ojiṣṭhaḥ*)—mighty
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Indra
- मदे (*made*)—for the drinking of Soma
- हितः (*hitaḥ*)—has been appointed
- द्युम्नी (*dyumnī*)—possessed of fame or of food
- श्लोकी (*ślokī*)—worthy of praise
- सः (*saḥ*)—that Indra
- सोम्यः (*somyaḥ*)—is worthy to drink Soma

### Printed p. 366

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That Indra has been created by Prajāpati for giving wealth and the rest to the people who praise him. That mighty Indra has been appointed for the drinking of Soma. Therefore that Indra, possessed of fame, possessed of food and worthy of praise, is worthy of drinking Soma.

##### English translation
Indra was created for giving, he, the most mighty, was set over the texhilarating Soma ; he the glorious one, the lord of praise, is worthy of he Soma. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गि॒रा वज्रो॒ न संभृ॑तः॒ सब॑लो॒ अन॑पच्युतः ।  
> व॒व॒क्ष ऋ॒ष्वो अस्तृ॑तः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गिरा । वज्रः । न । सम्ऽभृतः । सऽबलः । अनपऽच्युतः ।  
> ववक्षे । ऋष्वः । अस्तृतः ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गिरा स्तुतिलक्षणया वाचा स्तोतृभिः संभृतः उत्पादितस्तीक्ष्णीकृतः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । वज्रो न । वज्र आयुधम् । तत्कर्तृभिर्निशितधारो यथा भवति तीक्ष्णीक्रियते तद्वत् स्तोतृभिः स्तुत्या संभृतोऽत एव सबलः बलसहितस्तस्मात् अनपच्युतः परैरप्रच्युतः । अनभिगत इत्यर्थः । तादृशः ऋष्वः महान् दीप्यमानो वा अस्तृतः युद्धे शत्रुभिरहिंसित इंद्रः ववक्षे स्तोतृभ्यो धनादिकं वोढुमिच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra is संभृतः (*saṃbhṛtaḥ*), brought forth, that is, sharpened, by the praisers through गिरा (*girā*), speech in the form of praise. An illustration: वज्रो न (*vajro na*); वज्र (*vajra*) is a weapon, and as its makers sharpen its edge, so by the praisers' praise he is made keen, and therefore is सबलः (*sabalaḥ*), possessed of strength, and for that reason अनपच्युतः (*anapacyutaḥ*), not dislodged by others, that is, not overcome. Being such, ऋष्वः (*ṛṣvaḥ*), great or shining, and अस्तृतः (*astṛtaḥ*), unharmed by enemies in battle, Indra ववक्षे (*vavakṣe*), desires to bring wealth and the rest to the praisers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रो न (*vajro na*)—as a weapon is sharpened
- गिरा (*girā*)—by speech in the form of praise
- संभृतः (*saṃbhṛtaḥ*)—he who is extolled by the praisers
- सबलः (*sabalaḥ*)—he who is possessed of strength
- अनपच्युतः (*anapacyutaḥ*)—he who is unobstructed by others
- ऋष्वः (*ṛṣvaḥ*)—he who is of great nature or shining
- अस्तृतः (*astṛtaḥ*)—he who cannot be harmed by enemies in battle, that Indra
- ववक्षे (*vavakṣe*)—brings and gives wealth and the rest to the praising people

### Printed p. 367

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a weapon is rubbed and sharpened, so that Indra, who is made worthy of worship by being praised with hymns and the like, who is exceedingly mighty, unharmed by others, and not yielding to the injury of enemies in battle, brings and gives wealth and the rest to those who praise him.

##### English translation
The mighty (Indra), unassailed by his foes, hastens to confer wealth on his worshippers,—rendered keen by their praises, as a weapon, full of strength and invincible.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दु॒र्गे चि॑न्नः सु॒गं कृ॑धि गृणा॒न इं॑द्र गिर्वणः ।  
> त्वं च॑ मघव॒न्वशः॑ ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दुःऽगे । चित् । नः । सुऽगम् । कृधि । गृणानः । इंद्र । गिर्वणः ।  
> त्वम् । च । मघऽवन् । वशः ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे गिर्वणः गीर्भिर्वननीय इंद्र गृणानः स्तोतृभिः स्तूयमानस्त्वं नः अस्माकं दुर्गे चित् दुर्गमेऽपि मार्गे सुगं सुगमं पंथानं कृधि तथा कुरु । हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र त्वम् । चशब्दश्चेदर्थे । यदि वशः सोमपानार्थं तत्प्रदातॄनस्मान् कामयेथाः तदा पंथानं शोभनगमनं कुरुष्व । वष्टेर्लेट्यडागमः । चशब्दयोगादनिघातः ॥ ॥ २२ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*), Indra, to be served with hymns, praised by the praisers, make for us an easy, comfortable path even in a difficult, hard-to-traverse way. O wealthy Indra, च (*ca*) is in the sense of "if": if you desire us, the givers of Soma for drinking, then make the path a good going.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—who are obtained by praises
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—you who are extolled by the praising people
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- दुर्गे चित् (*durge cit*)—even on a very difficult way
- सुगं (*sugaṃ*)—a comfortable path
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—O wealthy Indra
- त्वं च (*tvaṃ ca*)—you
- वशः (*vaśaḥ*)—desire to come near us who offer Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, worthy of praise, you who are extolled by the praising people, make for us a favourable path, so that we may go comfortably even in places that are very difficult to traverse. The wealthy

### Printed p. 368

O Indra, you are indeed the one who wishes to come, for the drinking of Soma, to our neighbourhood, we who are ready today to offer Soma.

##### English translation
Indra, worthy of our praise, hymned by us, make our path plain even in the midst of difficulties, (hear us), Maghavan, if you love us ;

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्य॑ ते॒ नू चि॑दा॒दिशं॒ न मि॒नंति॑ स्व॒राज्य॑म् ।  
> न दे॒वो नाध्रि॑गु॒र्जनः॑ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्य । ते । नु । चित् । आऽदिशम् । न । मिनंति । स्वऽराज्यम् ।  
> न । देवः । न । अध्रिऽगुः । जनः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यस्य ते तव आदिशम् । आदिशति नयति सर्वत्रानयेत्यादिग्बलम् । औणादिकः करणे प्रत्ययः । यद्वा । आदेश एवादिगाज्ञा । भावे क्विप् । त्वदीयामाज्ञां नू चित् इदानीं पुरा च न मिनंति केचिदपि न हिंसंति । किंच। स्वराज्यं तव स्वभूतं राज्यं च । यद्वा । स्वशब्देन स्वर्गोऽभिधीयते । स्वर्गस्वामित्वं च न हिंसंति । हिंसकानाह। न देवः त्वदन्यो देवोऽपि च तथापि अध्रिगुः अधृतगमनः संग्रामे त्वरमाणो वीरोऽपि न च जनः प्रादुर्भूतो मनुष्योऽपि । एते न मिनंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, of you whose command (आदिशम् (*ādiśam*) is explained as the power that leads everywhere, or else simply as command) no one, now or before, violates or harms. Moreover they do not harm your own kingdom स्वराज्यम् (*svarājyam*); or else, the word स्व (*sva*) denotes heaven, and they do not harm your lordship over heaven. He names those who might harm: no god other than you, nor any hero who is अध्रिगुः (*adhriguḥ*), of irresistible going, hastening in battle, nor any man who has come into being. These do not harm.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्य ते (*yasya te*)—(O Indra) of you whose
- आदिशं (*ādiśaṃ*)—command
- नू चित् (*nū cit*)—before or now, that is, always
- न मिनंति (*na minaṃti*)—none can transgress
- स्वराज्यं (*svarājyaṃ*)—none harms your lordship over heaven
- न देवः (*na devaḥ*)—no other god than you
- अध्रिगुः (*adhriguḥ*)—no hero of swift going
- जने (*jane*)—no human being, whoever has come into being so far
- न च (*na ca*)—can harm you or transgress your command

### Printed p. 369

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, no one is ever able to withstand your command or your power. No one can question your lordship over heaven. No god other than you, no hero and no human being can harm you or transgress your command.

##### English translation
You whose command and rightful empire neither god nor irresistible hero can harm.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अधा॑ ते॒ अप्र॑तिष्कुतं दे॒वी शुष्मं॑ सपर्यतः ।  
> उ॒भे सु॑शिप्र॒ रोद॑सी ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । ते । अप्रतिऽस्कुतम् । देवी इति । शुष्मम् । सपर्यतः ।  
> उभे इति । सुऽशिप्र । रोदसी इति ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सुशिप्र सुहनो शोभनशिरस्त्राणेंद्र अध अपि च देवी देव्यौ स्वतेजसा दीप्यमाने उभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ अप्रतिष्कुतम् । स्कु इति सौत्रो धातुः स्तंभने वर्तते । शत्रुभिरप्रतिरोधनीयं ते त्वदीयं शुष्मं परबलशोषकं बलं सपर्यतः पूजयतः । त्वदधीने एव भवतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, of the fine jaw (or of the fine helmet), moreover both heaven and earth, the two goddesses shining by their own radiance, worship your शुष्मम् (*śuṣmam*), your strength that dries up the strength of others, which enemies cannot obstruct (अप्रतिष्कुतम् (*apratiṣkutam*): the root स्कु (*sku*) is a sautra root in the sense of stopping). The two are under your control.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुशिप्र (*suśipra*)—O Indra of the attractive cheeks or of the helmet
- अध (*adha*)—and
- देवी (*devī*)—the two shining (or divine)
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- अप्रतिष्कुतं (*apratiṣkutaṃ*)—unobstructed, that is, impossible for anyone to withstand
- ते शुष्मं (*te śuṣmaṃ*)—your strength and power
- सपर्यतः (*saparyataḥ*)—honour

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra of the attractive cheeks, the shining heaven and earth, that is, the earth and the heavenly world, honour your great strength and power, which no one can withstand.

### Printed p. 370

##### English translation
Yes, deity of the handsome jaw, the two goddesses, heaven and earth both worship your resistless consuming might.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वमे॒तद॑धारयः कृ॒ष्णासु॒ रोहि॑णीषु च ।  
> परु॑ष्णीषु॒ रुश॒त्पयः॑ ॥ १३ ॥

> त्वम् । एतत् । अधारयः । कृष्णासु । रोहिणीषु । च ।  
> परुष्णीषु । रुशत् । पयः ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्य सामर्थ्यमेवोपपादयति । हे इंद्र कृष्णासु कृष्णवर्णासु गोषु तथा रोहिणीषु ।  ‘ वर्णादनुदात्तात्तोपधात्तो नः' (पा. सू. ४. १. ३९) इति ङीप् । रोहितवर्णासु च गोषु रुशत् । रोचतेर्दीप्तिकर्मणः । दीप्यमानं श्वेतम् एतत् परिदृश्यमानं पयः क्षीरं त्वम् अधारयः धारयसि । तस्मात्त्वद्बलं पूजयत इति समन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He establishes this very capacity of Indra. O Indra, in the black cows and in the red cows (cows of a ruddy colour), you hold this bright, white milk that is seen. Therefore they worship your strength: this is the connection.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—(O Indra) you
- कृष्णासु (*kṛṣṇāsu*)—in the black cows
- रोहिणीषु (*rohiṇīṣu*)—in the red cows
- परुष्णीषु च (*paruṣṇīṣu ca*)—and in the cows of mixed colour
- रुशत् (*ruśat*)—white in one and the same way
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—milk
- अधारयः (*adhārayaḥ*)—you fill

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you fill the black cows, the red cows, and also the cows mixed black and white or red and white, with milk that is white in one and the same way.

##### English translation
It is you that keep this bright milk in the black, red, and spotted cows.

### Printed p. 371

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

It is natural that a white cow gives white milk. But whether the cow is white, black, red or of mixed colour, the milk obtained from all these kinds of cows is white and of one and the same kind. The seer describes the greatness of Indra, saying that this is your majesty.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि यदहे॒रध॑ त्वि॒षो विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॒ अक्र॑मुः ।  
> वि॒दन्मृ॒गस्य॒ ताँ अमः॑ ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वि । यत् । अहेः । अध । त्विषः । विश्वे । देवासः । अक्रमुः ।  
> विदत् । मृगस्य । तान् । अमः ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अध अपि च अहेः अहंतव्यस्य वृत्रासुरस्य त्विषः तेजोरूपादुच्छ्वासाद्भीताः यद्वा तस्य प्रभावेन परिगमिताः विश्वे सर्वे देवासः देवाः यत् यदा वि अक्रमुः विविधं पादविहरणमकुर्वन् । स्वस्थानं परित्यज्यान्यं देशमगच्छन्नित्यर्थः । तदानीं मृगस्य । एवं तान् भीषयितुं वृत्रो मृगरूपोऽभवत् । तद्रूपस्य संबंधि अमः सर्वतो गमनशीलं बलं तज्जातं भयं वा तान् सर्वान् देवान् विदत् अविंदत् । प्राप्नोदित्यर्थः । तस्यासुरस्येंद्रो निवारको हंताभवदित्युत्तरेण संबंधः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Moreover, when all the gods, frightened by the breath, of the nature of splendour, of Ahi, the asura Vṛtra who is not to be slain, or else carried about by his power, strode apart, that is, took steps in various directions (they left their own place and went to another region), then, to frighten them, Vṛtra took the form of a deer. The strength belonging to that form, which moves everywhere, or the fear born of it, found all those gods, that is, reached them. Indra became the repeller and slayer of that asura: this is the connection with the following verse.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अथ (*atha*)—moreover
- अहेः (*aheḥ*)—of the Vṛtra asura who cannot be killed
- त्विषः (*tviṣaḥ*)—frightened by the breath, of the nature of splendour
- विश्वे देवासः (*viśve devāsaḥ*)—all the gods
- वि अक्रमुः (*vi akramuḥ*)—ran off in various directions (then)
- मृगस्य (*mṛgasya*)—of him who had taken the form of a deer
- अमुः (*amuḥ*)—the strength or the fear of that Vṛtra pervading everywhere
- तान् (*tān*)—those gods
- विदत् (*vidat*)—pervaded

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Moreover, seeing the breath and out-breath, of the nature of splendour, of that Vṛtra who cannot be killed by anyone, all the gods were frightened and ran off in various directions. The all-pervading strength or fear of that Vṛtra, who had taken the form of a deer (an antelope), enveloped those gods.

### Printed p. 372

##### English translation
When all the gods fled in various directions from the splendour of the demon Ahi, and when fear of the deer seized them.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आदु॑ मे निव॒रो भु॑वद्वृत्र॒हादि॑ष्ट॒ पौंस्य॑म् ।  
> अजा॑तशत्रु॒रस्तृ॑तः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आत् । ऊं इति । मे । निऽवरः । भुवत् । वृत्रऽहा । अदिष्ट । पौंस्यम् ।  
> अजातऽशत्रुः । अस्तृतः ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आदु इत्यवधारणे । देवानां भीत्या सर्वतो गमनानंतरमेव मे स्तोतृस्तुत्यलक्षणेन संबंधेन मम संबंध्ययमिंद्रः निवरः वृत्रासुरस्य निवारयिता हंता भुवत् अभवत् । ततः वृत्रहा वृत्रस्य हंतेंद्रः पौंस्यम् । पुंसः कर्म पौंस्यम् । यद्वा । स्त्रीपुंसाभ्याम् (पा. सू. ४. १. ८७ ) इति भवार्थे स्रञ्   । नकारस्य यकारो वर्णव्यत्ययेन । पुंसींद्रे भवम् । यद्वा । बलनामैतत् । स्वबलम् ॥ अदिष्ट तस्य राज्ये दिशति निदधाति । तद्राज्यं स्ववशमकरोदित्यर्थः । ततः प्रभृतींद्रः अजातशत्रुः अनुत्पन्नशत्रुः अस्तृतः संग्रामे परैरहिंसितश्चाभवत् ॥ ॥ २३ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

आदु (*ādu*) is in the sense of emphasis. Immediately after the gods had gone in all directions out of fear, this Indra, who belongs to me through the relation of praiser and praised, became निवरः (*nivaraḥ*), the repeller and slayer of the asura Vṛtra. Then Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, अदिष्ट (*adiṣṭa*), set his पौंस्यम् (*pauṃsyam*) in Vṛtra's kingdom: पौंस्यम् (*pauṃsyam*) is the work of a man; or else it is said to be (by Pā. Sū. 4. 1. 87) a derivative in the sense of "being in", meaning what is in Indra the man; or else this is a name for strength, his own strength. He made that kingdom his own. From then on Indra became अजातशत्रुः (*ajātaśatruḥ*), one whose enemy is not born, and अस्तृतः (*astṛtaḥ*), unharmed by others in battle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अत् उ (*at u*)—afterwards
- मे (*me*)—my (Indra, the object of my praise)
- निवरः (*nivaraḥ*)—as the destroyer of the asura Vṛtra
- भुवत् (*bhuvat*)—he has become
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra
- पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*)—his own strength
- अदिष्ट (*adiṣṭa*)—established in his kingdom (afterwards that Indra)
- अजातशत्रुः (*ajātaśatruḥ*)—became one for whom no enemies are born
- अस्तृतः (*astṛtaḥ*)—and one unharmed by enemies in battle

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Afterwards that Indra, the object of my praise, became the destroyer of the asura Vṛtra and established his own strength and power in his lordship, that is, in his kingdom. Afterwards Indra came to have no enemies at all. There was no one who could face him in battle and harm him.

### Printed p. 373

##### English translation
Then was my Indra the repeller; then did the smiter of Vritra put forth his might, he who has no existent enemies, the invincible.

#### Ṛk 16

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्रु॒तं वो॑ वृत्र॒हंत॑मं॒ प्र शर्धं॑ चर्षणी॒नाम् ।  
> आ शु॑षे॒ राध॑से म॒हे ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्रुतम् । वः । वृत्रहन्ऽतमम् । प्र । शर्धम् । चर्षणीनाम् ।  
> आ । शुषे । राधसे । महे ॥ १६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे ऋत्विग्यष्टारः श्रुतं बलवत्तया प्रसिद्धमत एव वृत्रहंतमम् अतिशयेन वृत्रहंतारं शर्धं  बलभूतं वेगवंतं वा एतादृशमिंद्रं चर्षणीनां मनुष्याणां वः युष्माकम् आशुषे । अश्नोतेर्लेट्युत्तम इटि सिप् । व्यत्ययेनोप्रत्ययः । ‘बहुलं छंदसि' इत्यडागमः । तमिंद्रं स्तुतिभिः प्रीणयित्वा युष्मभ्यं प्रकर्षेणाश्नवै । प्रयच्छामीत्यर्थः । किमर्थम्। महे महते राधसे धनाय धनं युष्मभ्यं दातुम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O priests and sacrificers, Indra is श्रुतम् (*śrutam*), renowned for his strength, and therefore वृत्रहंतमम् (*vṛtrahaṃtamam*), the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, शर्धम् (*śardham*), strength itself or swift. Having pleased such an Indra with praises, I would obtain him for you, men (चर्षणीनाम् (*carṣaṇīnām*) means of men), that is, I give him to you. For what purpose: महे (*mahe*) राधसे (*rādhase*), for great wealth, in order to give you wealth. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- श्रुतं (*śrutaṃ*)—(O priests and sacrificers) renowned as mighty
- वृत्रहंतमं (*vṛtrahaṃtamaṃ*)—who has slain Vṛtra most completely
- शर्धं (*śardhaṃ*)—Indra, extremely mighty or of swift going
- चर्षणीनां (*carṣaṇīnāṃ*)—of men
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- वहे (*vahe*)—abundant
- राधसे (*rādhase*)—for the attainment of wealth
- आशिषे (*āśiṣe*)—I pray and call

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O priests and sacrificers, I pray to and call Indra, renowned as mighty, the slayer of Vṛtra, extremely swift of going, in order to give you men abundant wealth.

### Printed p. 374

##### English translation
(Priests), I bring to you men, for great wealth, that renowned and mighty one who utterly destroyed Vritra.

#### Ṛk 17

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒या धि॒या च॑ गव्य॒या पुरु॑णाम॒न्पुरु॑ष्टुत ।  
> यत्सोमे॑सोम॒ आभ॑वः ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अया । धिया । च । गव्यऽया । पुरुऽनामन् । पुरुऽस्तुत ।  
> यत् । सोमेऽसोमे । आ । अभवः ॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पुरुनामन् बहुविधशक्रवृत्रहादिनामोपेत । यद्वा । बहुस्तुतिमन् । नामयंति स्तुत्यं देवं वशं नयंतीति नाम स्तोत्रम् । अत एव पुरुष्टुत बहुभिरभिष्टुतेंद्र सोमेसोमे अस्मदीयेषु सोमेषु त्वं यदा आभवः तेषां पानार्थं समंतादभवः तदा वयम् अया अनया । कीदृश्या । गव्यया गा आत्मन इच्छंत्या धिया अनया बुद्ध्या युक्ता भवेम । सोमं पीतवति त्वयि वयं गवादियुक्ता भवेमेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O पुरुनामन् (*purunāman*), you who have many names such as Śakra and Vṛtrahan; or else, O you of many praises (नाम (*nāma*) is praise, since they bend the praised god and bring him under their power). For that very reason you are पुरुष्टुत (*puruṣṭuta*), praised by many, Indra. When, at each of our Soma-libations, you come around, to drink them, then may we be endowed with this intelligence, which desires cows for itself. The meaning is: when you have drunk Soma, may we be endowed with cows and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुनामन् (*purunāman*)—you who have many names such as Śakra and Vṛtrahā, or who are praised with manifold praises
- पुरुष्टुत (*puruṣṭuta*)—O Indra, who are praised by many
- सोमे सोमे (*some some*)—at every Soma-pressing that we perform
- आ अभवः (*ā abhavaḥ*)—when you come for the drinking of Soma (we)
- अया (*ayā*)—by this
- गव्यया (*gavyayā*)—cows-desiring
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—we shall be endowed with intelligence

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, famed by many names such as Śakra and Vṛtrahā and praised by many, at each Soma-sacrifice in which we press Soma, when you come to us for the drinking of Soma, we shall be possessed of the mind that we should obtain cows from you.

### Printed p. 375

##### English translation
O you bearing many names and praised by many, when you are present at our various Soma-libations, may we be endowed with a cows-desiring mind.

#### Ṛk 18

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> बो॒धिन्म॑ना॒ इद॑स्तु नो वृत्र॒हा भूर्या॑सुतिः ।  
> शृ॒णोतु॑ श॒क्र आ॒शिष॑म् ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> बोधित्ऽमनाः । इत् । अस्तु । नः । वृत्रऽहा । भूरिऽआसुतिः ।  
> शृणोतु । शुक्रः । आऽशिषम् ॥ १८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं परोक्षकृतः । वृत्रहा वृत्रहंता भूर्यासुतिः । बहुषु देशेष्विंद्रार्थं सोम आसूयतेऽभिषूयत इति तादृशः । यद्वा । बहूनि सोमादिहवींषींद्रार्थमासूयंते हूयंत इति तादृशः । बोधिन्मनाः ।  ‘ बुध अवगमने' । औणादिक इतिप्रत्ययः । यस्य मनः स्तोतॄणामभिमतं बुध्यते जानातीति तथोक्तः । इत् अवधारणे। नः अस्माकं बोधिन्मना एव अस्तु । सर्वदास्मदभीप्सितानि जानात्वेवेत्यर्थः । यद्वा । एतादृश इंद्रो नोऽस्माकं यज्ञे भवत्विति । ततः शक्रः संग्रामे शत्रुहननसमर्थ इंद्रः आशिषम् अस्मदीयां स्तुतिमाशासनं वा शृणोतु ॥
> ज्योतिष्टोमे चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिने मैत्रावरुणस्य ‘कया त्वं न ऊत्या' इति तृचोऽनुरूपः। सूत्रितं च -- होत्रकाणां कया नश्चित्र आ भुवत् कया त्वं न ऊत्या' (आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ४) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This verse is in the third person. Vṛtrahan is the slayer of Vṛtra; भूर्यासुतिः (*bhūryāsutiḥ*) is one for whom Soma is pressed in many places for Indra; or else one for whom many oblations such as Soma are offered for Indra. बोधिन्मनाः (*bodhinmanāḥ*) is one whose mind knows the wish of the praisers. Let him, for us, have just such a mind: let him always know what we desire; or else let such an Indra be at our sacrifice. Then may Śakra, Indra, who is able to slay enemies in battle, hear our आशिषम् (*āśiṣam*), our praise or our request. In the Jyotiṣṭoma, on the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, the triplet beginning कया त्वं न ऊत्या (*kayā tvaṃ na ūtyā*) is the Anurūpa of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest. It is prescribed in the Sūtra concerning the Hotrakas: होत्रकाणां कया नश्चित्र आ भुवत् कया त्वं न ऊत्या (*hotrakāṇāṃ kayā naścitra ā bhuvat kayā tvaṃ na ūtyā*) (Āśva. Śrau. 7. 4).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—the slayer of the asura Vṛtra
- भूर्यासुती (*bhūryāsutī*)—he for whom Soma is pressed by many or in many regions
- बोधिन्मनः (*bodhinmanaḥ*)—Indra, who knows the mind and wish of the praisers
- नः (*naḥ*)—at our sacrifice
- अस्तु इत् (*astu it*)—may he be always
- शक्रः (*śakraḥ*)—that all-capable Indra
- आशिषं (*āśiṣaṃ*)—our prayer
- शृणोतु (*śṛṇotu*)—let him hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, the slayer of the asura Vṛtra, he for whom Soma is pressed in many regions or by many, knowing the wish of us who are praising, come to our sacrifice. And

### Printed p. 376

that Indra, who is able to slay enemies in battle, listen with kindness to our prayer that makes known what we desire.

##### English translation
May the slayer of Vritra, to whom many libations are offered, know our desires,—may Sakra hear our praises.

#### Ṛk 19

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कया॒ त्वं न॑ ऊ॒त्याभि प्र मं॑दसे वृषन् ।  
> कया॑ स्तो॒तृभ्य॒ आ भ॑र ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कया । त्वम् । नः । ऊत्या । अभि । प्र । मंदसे । वृषन् ।  
> कया । स्तोतृऽभ्यः । आ । भर ॥ १९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृषन् कामानां वर्षितरिंद्र कया केन ऊत्या । अव रक्षणादिषु गत्यर्थे । ऊतियूति' इत्यादिना निपातितः । केनाभिगमनेन नः अस्मान् अभि अभितः प्र मंदसे प्रकर्षेण मादयसि । अस्मदीयं यज्ञं प्रति सोमपानार्थमागमनेन वा त्वदीयस्तुतिश्रवणार्थमागमनेन वा कदास्मान् प्रमादयसीति । किंच कया केनाभिगमनेन स्तोतृभ्यः अस्मभ्यं धनम् आ भर आबिभर्षीतींद्रं स्तोता पृच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O showerer of desires, Indra, with what ऊत्या (*ūtyā*), what approach, do you gladden us greatly on every side? Is it by coming to our sacrifice to drink Soma, or by coming to hear your praise: when will you gladden us? And again, with what approach do you bring wealth to us, the praisers? In this way the praiser asks Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषन् (*vṛṣan*)—O Indra, showerer of what is desired
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- कया ऊत्या (*kayā ūtyā*)—by what kind of protection of yours
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- अभि (*abhi*)—in every way
- प्र मंदसे (*pra maṃdase*)—do you gladden?
- कया (*kayā*)—by what coming of yours
- स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*)—to us who are praising
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—do you bring and supply wealth?

### Printed p. 377

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, showerer of desires, by what kind of protection or going of yours do you especially gladden us? By what coming of yours do you bring and supply wealth to us, who are praising?

##### English translation
Showerer, (of blessings), with what coming of yours do you gladden us, with what coming you bring (wealth) to your worshippers ?

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

It is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the sūtra होत्रकाणां कया नश्चित्र आ भुवत् कया त्वं न ऊत्या (*hotrakāṇāṃ kayā naścitra ā bhuvat kayā tvaṃ na ūtyā*) (Ā. 7-4), that, among the Śastra mantras recited by the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa at the midday pressing on the day called Cāturviṃśika of the Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice, the three Ṛks beginning कया त्वं न ऊत्या (*kayā tvaṃ na ūtyā*) are to be recited as the Anurūpa triplet.

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कस्य॒ वृषा॑ सु॒ते सचा॑ नि॒युत्वा॑न्वृष॒भो र॑णत् ।  
> वृ॒त्र॒हा सोम॑पीतये ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कस्य । वृषा । सुते । सचा । नियुत्वान् । वृषभः । रणत् ।  
> वृत्रऽहा । सोमऽपीतये ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृषा इंद्रः कस्य यजमानस्य सचा सुते ऋग्भिः सहाभिषुते सोमे । अनेन तद्वान् यज्ञो लक्ष्यते । कस्य यज्ञे सोमपीतये सोमपानाय तदर्थं रणत् रमते । कीदृशः । नियुत्वान् । नितरां युवंति मिश्रयंति स्वबलेन शत्रूनिति नियुतो मरुतः । तद्वान् । यद्वा । नियुत इति वायोर्वाहनाश्वाः । स वायुः कदाचित् संग्राम इंद्राय स्वाश्वानदात् । तद्वान् । वृषभः धनानामपां वा वर्षकः वृत्रहा वृत्रस्य हंतेंद्रः कस्य यज्ञे रमते । इदानीं नोऽस्मदीयं यागं प्रत्यागच्छतु । यद्वा । कस्याध्वरे रमते । न कुत्रापि । किंत्वस्मद्यज्ञ एव सोमपानार्थं संक्रीडते ॥ ॥ २४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The showerer Indra, in the sacrifice of which sacrificer, at the Soma pressed together with Ṛks (by this the sacrifice that has them is indicated), delights for the drinking of Soma? Of what kind is he? नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*): नियुतो (*niyuto*) are the Maruts, who join (युवंति (*yuvaṃti*)) with enemies by their own strength; he is possessed of them. Or else नियुत (*niyuta*) are the horses that draw Vāyu; once, in a battle, that Vāyu gave his horses to Indra; he is possessed of them. He is the showerer, the pourer of wealth or of waters, the slayer of Vṛtra. In whose sacrifice does he delight? Let him now come to our sacrifice. Or else: in whose sacrifice does he delight? In none anywhere; he takes his pleasure only at our sacrifice, for the drinking of Soma.

### Printed p. 378

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*)—he who fights enemies in battle with his own strength, or who is accompanied by the horses of Vāyu called Niyut
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—he who pours out wealth or waters
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—the slayer of the asura Vṛtra
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—the showerer of desires, Indra
- कस्य (*kasya*)—of which sacrificer
- सुते सचा (*sute sacā*)—at the Soma-pressing accompanied by the priests, that is, in the sacrifice of which sacrificer
- सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)—for the drinking of Soma
- रणत् (*raṇat*)—is he delighting?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who fights enemies in battle, or who has the horses of the god Vāyu, who supplies wealth and the rest to the praising people, the slayer of the asura Vṛtra and the showerer of desires, in the sacrifice of which sacrificer, who performs the Soma-pressing rite together with the priests, is he delighting with the drinking of Soma?

##### English translation
At whose hymn-accompanied libations does the showerer, the lord of the Niyuts, the slayer of Vritra, rejoice to drink the Soma ?

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भी षु ण॒स्त्वं र॒यिं मं॑दसा॒नः स॑ह॒स्रिण॑म् ।  
> प्र॒यं॒ता बो॑धि दा॒शुषे॑ ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । सु । नः । त्वम् । रयिम् । मंदसानः । सहस्रिणम् ।  
> प्रऽयंता । बोधि । दाशुषे ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इन्र्ो त्वं मंदसानः अस्माभिर्दत्तेन सोमेन मोदमानः सन् सहस्रिणं सहस्रसंख्याकं धनं नः अस्मभ्यं सु सुष्ठु अभि आभर । तदेवाह । त्वं दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय प्रयंता धनादेः प्रदाता कर्मणो नियंता वा भवानीति बोधि बुध्यस्व । ‘बुध अवगमने'। भौवादिकः । लोटि छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् । हेर्धिः। धित्वे धकारलोपश्छांदसः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you who are rejoicing in the Soma given by us, bring well and on every side to us a thousandfold wealth, that is, wealth that is a thousand in number. He says this: know that to the sacrificer who has given the oblation you are the giver of wealth and the rest, or the controller of the rite.

### Printed p. 379

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—(O Indra) you
- मंदसानः (*maṃdasānaḥ*)—delighted with the Soma-drinking offered by us
- सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*)—a thousandfold, or immeasurable
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सु अभि (*su abhi*)—bring especially
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- प्रयंता (*prayaṃtā*)—that you must give wealth and the rest
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—know

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, satisfied with the Soma-drinking offered by us, bring to us a thousandfold, that is, immeasurable wealth. Know that it is you yourself who give wealth and the rest to the sacrificer who offers the oblation.

##### English translation
Rejoicing (in our oblations), bring us wealth a thousandfold; remember that you are the giver of your votary.

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पत्नी॑वंतः सु॒ता इ॒म उ॒शंतो॑ यंति वी॒तये॑ ।  
> अ॒पां जग्मि॑र्निचुंपु॒णः ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पत्नीऽवंतः । सुताः । इमे । उशंतः । यंति । वीतये ।  
> अपाम् । जग्मिः । निऽचुंपुणः ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पत्नीवंतः । सोमसेकार्थे पत्न्यः पालयित्र्य आपो वसतीवर्य एकधनाश्च । तद्वंतः सुताः अस्माभिरभिषुताः इमे ग्रहस्थाश्चमसस्थाश्च सोमाः उशंतः आत्मनः पानं कामयमानाः संतः यंति इंद्रं गच्छंति । किमर्थम् । वीतये आत्मनः पानाय । किंच निचुंपुणः ।  ‘ निचांतपृणः । (निरु. ५. १७) इति यास्कः । ‘चमु अदने'। निचांतो भक्षितः पृणः प्रीणयिता । यद्वा ।  ‘ निचमनेन प्रीणाति' इति भक्षणेन तर्पयतीति निचुंपुणः । अभिषुतस्य सोमस्याप्सु प्रक्षेपासंभवात् सामर्थ्यादृजीषरूपः सोमो गृह्यते । तादृशः सोमः अपां जग्मिः । अपामिति 'न लोकाव्यय इति षष्ठीप्रतिषेधाभावश्छांदसः । अप इत्यर्थः । यद्वा । अपां मध्यं वापः प्रति वा जग्मिर्गमनशीलः साधुगंता वा । सोमश्चेंद्रं गच्छति । स ह्यवभृथकाल ऋजीषमप्सु प्रास्यंतीति वचनादप्स्वृजीषरूपः प्रक्षिप्यते । तदाह अपां जग्मिरिति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

पत्नीवंतः (*patnīvaṃtaḥ*): for the sprinkling of Soma, the पत्न्यः (*patnyaḥ*) are the protecting waters, the dwelling waters वसतीवर्य (*vasatīvarya*) and the एकधना (*ekadhanā*) waters. These Soma-juices pressed by us, possessed of them, standing in the cups and in the ladles, desiring their own drinking, go to Indra; for what purpose: वीतये (*vītaye*), in order to be drunk. Moreover, निचुंपुणः (*nicuṃpuṇaḥ*): Yāska says निचांतपृणः (*nicāṃtapṛṇaḥ*) (Ni. 5. 17). The root चमु (*camu*) is in the sense of eating; निचांत (*nicāṃta*) is eaten, पृणः (*pṛṇaḥ*) is the one who satisfies; or else, निचमनेन प्रीणाति (*nicamanena prīṇāti*), that is, it satisfies by being eaten, hence निचुंपुणः (*nicuṃpuṇaḥ*). Since it is not possible to throw the pressed Soma into the waters, by implication the Soma in the form of the residue ऋजीष (*ṛjīṣa*) is meant. Such a Soma is अपां जग्मिः (*apāṃ jagmiḥ*), that is, it goes to the waters; or else it goes into the midst of the waters or towards the waters, going or well-going. And the Soma goes to Indra. At the time of the Avabhṛtha, they throw the residue into the waters, according to the text; therefore the Soma in the form of the residue is thrown into the waters. This is why he says अपां जग्मिः (*apāṃ jagmiḥ*).

### Printed p. 380

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पत्नीवंतः (*patnīvaṃtaḥ*)—mixed with the water that is in the vessels called Vasatīvarī and Ekadhanā
- सुताः (*sutāḥ*)—just pressed
- इमो (*imo*)—these Soma-juices filled in the Graha and Camasa vessels
- उशंत (*uśaṃta*)—desiring to be drunk by Indra
- वीतये (*vītaye*)—for the sake of drinking
- यंति (*yaṃti*)—they join Indra
- निचुंपुणः (*nicuṃpuṇaḥ*)—that which brings satisfaction by eating, that is, by drinking
- अपां जग्मिः (*apāṃ jagmiḥ*)—the Soma-juice that is pressed out again from the Ṛjīṣa soaked in water goes to Indra himself and joins him, for his drinking

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These Soma-juices, mixed with the water that stands in the vessels called Vasatīvarī and Ekadhanā and just pressed, are made ready for Indra's drinking and join him alone. That is, Indra drinks that very Soma. And the Soma-juice that brings satisfaction by being drunk, pressed out once more from the pressed Soma-stalks called Ṛjīṣa soaked in water, is likewise offered to Indra alone.

##### English translation
These Soma-libations with their wives proceed (to Indra) longing to be drunk ; the stale Soma, pleasing to the taste, goes to the waters.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

Explaining two or three kinds of meaning for the word निचुंपुणः (*nicuṃpuṇaḥ*) in this Ṛk, Yāska has given the etymology—
निचुंपुणः । निचुंपुणः सोमो निचांतपृणो निचमनेन प्रीणाति । (*nicuṃpuṇaḥ | nicuṃpuṇaḥ somo nicāṃtapṛṇo nicamanena prīṇāti |*)
पत्नीवंतः सुता इम उशंतो यंति वीतये । अपां जग्मिर्निचुंपुणः । (*patnīvaṃtaḥ sutā ima uśaṃto yaṃti vītaye | apāṃ jagmirnicuṃpuṇaḥ |*)
पत्नीवंतः सुता इमोऽद्भिः सोमाः कामयमाना यंति वीतये पानायापां गंता निचुंपुणः ॥ (*patnīvaṃtaḥ sutā imo 'dbhiḥ somāḥ kāmayamānā yaṃti vītaye pānāyāpāṃ gaṃtā nicuṃpuṇaḥ ‖*)
(Ni. 5-18)
Nicuṃpuṇa means Soma, an intoxicating food. For when this (Soma) is drunk mixed with water, intoxication or joy arises. Therefore the Soma has the name

### Printed p. 381

निचुंपुण (*nicuṃpuṇa*). These pressed Soma-juices, mixed with the water that helps them, approach with eagerness those who drink, in order to be drunk. That is, those who drink Soma drink with eagerness the Soma-juice mixed with water (the water of the vessel called Vasatīvarī). Here the word पत्नीवंतः (*patnīvaṃtaḥ*) means पत्नीभिः अद्भिः तद्वंतः (*patnībhiḥ adbhiḥ tadvaṃtaḥ*), that is, mixed with water. Therefore the Soma-juice mixed with water has the name निचुंपुण (*nicuṃpuṇa*).
समुद्रोऽपि निचुंपुण उच्यते । निचमनेन पूर्यते ॥ (*samudro 'pi nicuṃpuṇa ucyate | nicamanena pūryate ‖*)
निचुंपुण (*nicuṃpuṇa*) means also the ocean. For the ocean also is called निचुंपुण (*nicuṃpuṇa*) because it is filled with water.
अवभृथोऽपि निचुंपुण उच्यते नीचैरस्मिन् क्वणंति नीचैर्दधतीति वा । आवभृथ निचुंपुण इत्यपि निगमो भवति । निचुंपुण निचुंकुणेति ॥ (*avabhṛtho 'pi nicuṃpuṇa ucyate nīcairasmin kvaṇaṃti nīcairdadhatīti vā | āvabhṛtha nicuṃpuṇa ityapi nigamo bhavati | nicuṃpuṇa nicuṃkuṇeti ‖*)
(Ni. 5-18)
The Avabhṛtha, the rite of the last day of the sacrifice, is also called निचुंपुण (*nicuṃpuṇa*). For in the rite of that day they recite the mantras and the like नीचैरस्मिन् क्वणंति (*nīcairasmin kvaṇaṃti*), very softly, in a low voice; or नीचैर्दधतीति वा (*nīcairdadhatīti vā*), that is, the sacrificial vessels are carried away by lowly persons, that is, by servants, attendants and the like; therefore the Avabhṛtha has the name निचुंपुण (*nicuṃpuṇa*). In some places the word निचुंकुण (*nicuṃkuṇa*) is used. This word also has the same meaning; that is, these two words निचुंपुण (*nicuṃpuṇa*) and निचुंकुण (*nicuṃkuṇa*) are synonyms. अवभृथ निचुंपुण नीचेरुशसि निचुंकुण (*avabhṛtha nicuṃpuṇa nīceruśasi nicuṃkuṇa*) is the example of a Vedic sentence in this matter.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒ष्टा होत्रा॑ असृक्ष॒तेंद्रं॑ वृ॒धासो॑ अध्व॒रे ।

### Printed p. 382

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अपां जग्मिरिति सामर्थ्यादवभृथदिन एव ---- र - वि- जः कुर्वंतीत्युक्तम् । तत्प्रसंगादाह । अध्वरे अस्मदीये यज्ञे वृधासः हविर्भिरिंद्रं वर्धयंतः इष्टाः इष्टवंतो यागं कृतवंतः सप्तसंख्याकाः होत्राः होत्रकाः अवभृथम् अंत्यदिवसम् अच्छ प्रति ओजसा स्वतेजसा सहिताः इंद्रम् असृक्षत विसृजंति । यावदवभृथं सप्तहोत्रका यजंतीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Since अपां जग्मिः (*apāṃ jagmiḥ*) by implication points to the day of the Avabhṛtha itself, it has been said that the priests perform the rite on that day; the damaged words of the text at this place cannot be construed. **NOTE**. Taking up this topic he says: अध्वरे (*adhvare*), in our sacrifice, the होत्राः (*hotrāḥ*), that is, the Hotṛ priests, seven in number, who वृधासः (*vṛdhāsaḥ*), strengthen Indra with oblations, and who are इष्टाः (*iṣṭāḥ*), that is, have performed the sacrifice, accompanied by their own ओजसा (*ojasā*), that is, their own brilliance, असृक्षत (*asṛkṣata*), dismiss Indra, अवभृथम् (*avabhṛtham*), the Avabhṛtha, that is, अंत्यदिवसम् (*aṃtyadivasam*), the last day, अच्छ (*accha*), towards it. For the seven Hotṛ priests sacrifice until the Avabhṛtha.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वरे (*adhvare*)—in the sacrifice that we are performing
- वृधासः (*vṛdhāsaḥ*)—those who make Indra grow by oblations and the like
- इष्टाः (*iṣṭāḥ*)—who are carrying out the sacrificial work
- होत्राः (*hotrāḥ*)—the seven priests of the Hotṛ group
- अवभृथं (*avabhṛthaṃ*)—the Avabhṛtha rite to be performed on the last day of the sacrifice
- अच्छ (*accha*)—having in view
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—together with their brilliance
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- असृक्षत (*asṛkṣata*)—dismissed, to go to his own place

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In this sacrifice that we are performing, the seven priests of the Hotṛ group, who satisfy Indra by offering oblations and the like and who take part in the sacrificial work, together with their brilliance, dismissed Indra to his own place at the time of the Avabhṛtha, the last day of the sacrifice, that is, when the sacrifice was completed.

##### English translation
The sacrificing priests, invigorating (Indra) by their offerings at the sacrifice, have by their might dismissed him at the Avabritha.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषा व्याख्याता (ऋ. सं. ८. ३२. २९ ) । अत्रापि वाक्यार्थो विधीयते । सधमाद्या इंद्रेण सह हविर्भिस्तर्पयितव्यौ यद्वा संग्रामे सह माद्यंतौ हिरण्यकेश्या हिरण्मयस्कंधगतकेशवंतौ त्या तौ प्रसिद्धौ हरी हरितवर्णावेतन्नामकावश्वौ इह अस्मिन् यज्ञे हितं - - वादिषु निहितं हितकरं वा प्रयः हवीरूपमन्नमभिलक्ष्य वोळ्हाम् इंद्रं वहताम् । प्रापयतामिति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Ṛk has been explained (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8. 32. 29). Here too the sense of the sentence is set out. The two horses named Hari, of green colour, famous, सधमाद्या (*sadhamādyā*), to be satisfied with oblations together with Indra, or rejoicing together in battle, हिरण्यकेश्या (*hiraṇyakeśyā*), having manes on their shoulders that are of gold, are asked to carry Indra, that is, to bring him, इह (*iha*), to this sacrifice, अभि (*abhi*), with a view to the प्रयः (*prayaḥ*), the food in the form of the oblation, which is हितं (*hitaṃ*), beneficial, or placed (the text is broken at this place) **NOTE**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- त्या (*tyā*)—the famous ones
- सधमाद्या (*sadhamādyā*)—those that are always happy together
- हिरण्यकेश्या (*hiraṇyakeśyā*)—those that have a line of mane on the neck shining like gold
- हरी (*harī*)—Indra's horses called Hari
- हितं (*hitaṃ*)—beneficial
- प्रयः (*prayaḥ*)—the food in the form of Soma
- अभि (*abhi*)—with a view to
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- वोळ्हां (*voḷhāṃ*)—let them carry Indra and bring him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

In this sacrifice, may Indra's two horses called Hari, the famous ones that are always together and rejoicing, adorned with a line of mane shining like gold on the neck, carry Indra here and bring him, in order that he may drink the beneficial food in the form of Soma, that is, the Soma-juice.

##### English translation
May those two golden-maned steeds together exulting bring him to our wholesome offering.

#### Ṛk 25

> तुभ्यं॒ सोमाः॑ सु॒ता इ॒मे स्ती॒र्णं ब॒र्हिर्वि॑भावसो ।  
> स्तो॒तृभ्य॒ इंद्र॒मा व॑ह ॥ २५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तुभ्यम् । सोमाः । सुताः । इमे । स्तीर्णम् । बर्हिः । विभावसो इति विभाऽवसो ।  
> स्तोतृऽभ्यः । इंद्रम् । आ । वह ॥ २५ ॥

### Printed p. 384

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विभावसो विशेषेण भासमानवसुमन् । यद्वा । विशिष्टा भा विभाः प्रकृष्टदीप्तयः । ता निवसंत्यत्रेति विभावसुरग्निः । हे तादृशाग्ने तुभ्यं त्वदर्थम् इमे सोमाः सुताः अभिषुताः । तथा बर्हिः स्तीर्णम् । तस्मात् स्तोतृभ्यः अस्मभ्यमस्मदर्थम् इंद्रं सोमपानार्थम् आ वह आह्वय । यज्ञे प्रति प्रापयेत्यर्थः ॥ ॥ २५ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

विभावसो (*vibhāvaso*): O one possessed of wealth that shines in a special way; or else, विभाः (*vibhāḥ*) are excellent lights, supreme splendours, and they dwell in him, hence Vibhāvasu is Agni. O such Agni, these Soma-juices are सुताः (*sutāḥ*), pressed, for you, and the grass is spread. Therefore bring Indra for us, your praisers, for the drinking of Soma, call him, that is, make him reach the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विभावसो (*vibhāvaso*)—O Agni, whose very wealth is splendour
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- इमे सोमाः (*ime somāḥ*)—these Soma-juices
- सुताः (*sutāḥ*)—are pressed and ready (and)
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—the cut darbha grass
- स्तीर्णं (*stīrṇaṃ*)—is spread as a seat (therefore)
- स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*)—for us who are praising you
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- आ वह (*ā vaha*)—bring him for the drinking of Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, whose wealth is splendour, that is, extremely resplendent, these Soma-juices are pressed and made ready for you alone. Cut darbha grass has been spread as a seat. Therefore now bring Indra for the drinking of Soma, for us who are praising you.

##### English translation
Resplendent (Agni), these Soma-libations are effused for you, and the clipped grass is spread ; bring Indra hither for his worshippers.

#### Ṛk 26

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ ते॒ दक्षं॒ वि रो॑च॒ना दध॒द्रत्ना॒ वि दा॒शुषे॑ ।  
> स्तो॒तृभ्य॒ इंद्र॑मर्चत ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । ते । दक्षम् । वि । रोचना । दधत् । रत्ना । वि । दाशुषे ।  
> स्तोतृऽभ्यः । इंद्रम् । अर्चत ॥ २६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिर्ऋत्विग्यजमानान् प्रत्याह । हे यष्टः दाशुषे इंद्राय हविर्दत्तवते ते तुभ्यं रोचना रोचनं दीप्यमानं दक्षं बलम् आ आभिमुख्येन वि दधत् इंद्रो विदधातु । यद्वा । रोचनमिति स्वर्गः । देवतेजसा दीप्तं रोचननामानं लोकं विदधातु । तथा रत्ना रत्नानि च तुभ्यं करोतु ।' डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः'। लेटि ‘घोर्लोपो लेटि वा' (पा. सू. ७. ३. ७० ) इत्याकारलोपः । अडागमः । हे स्तोतारः स्तोतृभ्यः इंद्रविषयस्तोत्रकारिभ्यो युष्मभ्यं च बलरत्नादिकमिंद्रः कुरुताम्। तस्मात् तम् इंद्रं यूयम् अर्चत हविर्भिः स्तुतिभिश्च पूजयत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer addresses the priests and the sacrificers. O sacrificer, to you who have given oblations to Indra, may Indra bestow दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*), shining strength, with आ (*ā*) meaning "towards"; or else, रोचन (*rocana*) is heaven: may he bestow the world named Rocana, bright with the lustre of the gods; and may he also provide you with jewels. O praisers, may Indra bestow strength, jewels and the like on you, who are those that sing praise concerning Indra. Therefore worship that Indra, honour him with oblations and with praises.

### Printed p. 385

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O sacrificer) दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to you who have offered oblations to Indra
- ते (*te*)—for you
- रोचना (*rocanā*)—shining
- दक्षं (*dakṣaṃ*)—strength
- आ (*ā*)—abundantly
- वि दधत् (*vi dadhat*)—may Indra give; [or रोचना वि दधत् (*rocanā vi dadhat*)—may Indra give heaven]
- रत्ना (*ratnā*)—may he give you also delightful jewels (O praisers)
- स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*)—to you who praise Indra, may Indra give jewels and the like (therefore you)
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- अर्चत (*arcata*)—worship with oblations and the like

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sacrificer, to you who offer oblations to Indra, may Indra give shining strength or heaven. Likewise may he give jewels. O praisers, may Indra give jewels and the like to you also, who praise Indra. Therefore worship Indra with oblations and the like and satisfy him.

##### English translation
May he give strength and his brilliant heaven and precious things to you his worshipper, and to his praising priests ; worship Indra.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शतक्रतो इंद्र ते तव इंद्रियं वीर्यवंतं सोमं विश्वा उक्था सर्वाणि स्तोत्राणि आ दधामि संपादयामि । हे इंद्र त्वं स्तोतृभ्यः मृळय सुखय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*) Indra, I prepare for you, that is, bring about, the Soma full of इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*), that is, of vigour, and all the उक्था (*ukthā*), that is, all the hymns of praise. O Indra, make your praisers happy, मृळय (*mṛḷaya*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O Indra, the doer of many deeds of daring
- ते (*te*)—for you
- इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*)—the Soma that produces exhilaration
- विश्वा उक्थानि (*viśvā ukthāni*)—all the hymns of praise
- आ दधामि (*ā dadhāmi*)—I prepare and offer
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra, you
- स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*)—those who praise you
- मृळय (*mṛḷaya*)—make happy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who perform many deeds of daring, I prepare and offer to you the exhilarating Soma and many hymns of praise. O Indra, make happy those who praise you.

##### English translation
I prepare, Satakratu, your strong (Soma) and all your praises ; be gracious, Indra, to your hymners·

#### Ṛk 28

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> भ॒द्रंभ॑द्रं न॒ आ भ॒रेष॒मूर्जं॑ शतक्रतो ।  
> यदिं॑द्र मृ॒ळया॑सि नः ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> भद्रम्ऽभद्रम् । नः । आ । भर । इषम् । ऊर्जम् । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो ।  
> यत् । इंद्र । मृळयासि । नः ॥ २८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शतक्रतो शतविधकर्मन् शतप्रज्ञ वा इंद्र भद्रंभद्रं कल्याणतममथ सुखोत्पादकं वा धनं नः अस्मभ्यम् आ भर आसंपादय देहि । तथा इषम् अन्नम् ऊर्जम् अन्नरसं यद्वा बलवदन्नं  च देहि । नः अस्मान् यत् यदि मृळयासि सुखयसि तर्हि तद्धनादिकं देहीति । ‘मृड सुखने'। ण्यंतस्य लेट्याडागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*) Indra, doer of a hundred kinds of deeds, or possessed of a hundred kinds of wisdom, bring to us, that is, procure and give, भद्रंभद्रं (*bhadraṃbhadraṃ*), the most auspicious wealth or wealth that produces happiness. Give also इषम् (*iṣam*), food, and ऊर्जम् (*ūrjam*), the juice of food, or else strengthening food. If you make us happy, मृळयासि (*mṛḷayāsi*), then give us that wealth and the rest.

- शतकृतो (*śatakṛto*)—doer of many deeds of valour, or possessed of manifold knowledge
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—if
- नः (*naḥ*)—us

##### English translation
Bring us what is most auspicious, Satakratu, (bring us) food and strength, if you have favour to us, Indra.

#### Ṛk 29

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । नः । विश्वानि । आ । भर । सुवितानि । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो ।  
> यत् । इंद्र । मृळयासि । नः ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शतक्रतो इंद्र सः पूर्वोक्तलक्षणस्त्वं विश्वानि सर्वाणि सुवितानि । सुष्ठ्वीयते प्राप्यते येष्विति सुवितानि मंगलानि । सुपूर्वादेतेः क्ते प्रत्यये उवङादेशः । सर्वानभ्युदयान् नः अस्मभ्यमाहर । हे इंद्र यदि नः अस्मान् सुखयसि तर्हि धनादिसहितानभ्युदयान् देहीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*) Indra, you, of the kind spoken of before, bring to us all सुवितानि (*suvitāni*), auspicious things, that is, those in which one is well led or reached; all blessings. O Indra, if you make us happy, then give blessings together with wealth and the rest.

- यत् (*yat*)—if
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मृळयासि (*mṛḷayāsi*)—you have the wish to make happy
- सः (*saḥ*)—you, who are distinguished by the qualities spoken of before
