- विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)—all
- सुवितानि (*suvitāni*)—blessings, or welfare
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—bring about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, possessed of manifold wisdom, if you have the wish to make us happy, bring about for us all welfare.

##### English translation
Bring us all blessings, Satakratu, if you have favour to us, Indra.

#### Ṛk 30

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वामिद्वृ॑त्रहंतम सु॒तावं॑तो हवामहे ।  
> यदिं॑द्र मृ॒ळया॑सि नः ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वाम् । इत् । वृत्रहन्ऽतम । सुतऽवंतः । हवामहे ।  
> यत् । इंद्र । मृळयासि । नः ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृत्रहंतम अतिशयेन वृत्रस्यापामावरकस्य हंतरिंद्र सुतवंतः अभिषुतसोमवंतो वयम् । इदवधारणे' । त्वामित् त्वामेव हवामहे । अस्मद्यज्ञमागत्य सोमपानायाह्वयामः । हे इंद्र नः अस्मान् यदि सुखयसि तर्ह्याह्वयाम इति ॥ ॥ २६ ॥
> व्यूळ्हस्य दशरात्रस्य षष्ठेऽहनि निष्केवल्ये ‘उप नो हरिभिः' इति तृचो निविद्धानीयः । सूत्रितं च --- अयं ह येन वा इदमुप नो हरिभिः सुतम् ' ( आश्व. श्रौ. ८. ८) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O वृत्रहंतम (*vṛtrahaṃtama*) Indra, extreme slayer of Vṛtra, the enclosure of the waters, we who have pressed Soma, सुतवंतः (*sutavaṃtaḥ*), invoke you alone, हवामहे (*havāmahe*): we call you to come to our sacrifice and drink Soma. O Indra, if you make us happy, then we call you. Use: on the sixth day of the Daśarātra called Vyūḷha, in the Niṣkevalya, the triplet beginning उप नो हरिभिः (*upa no haribhiḥ*) is the Nividdhānīya; and it is stated in the Sūtra: अयं ह येन वा इदमुप नो हरिभिः सुतम् (*ayaṃ ha yena vā idamupa no haribhiḥ sutam*) (Āśv. Śrau. 8. 8). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहंतमु (*vṛtrahaṃtamu*)—O Indra, who slew the demon Vṛtra
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—if
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मृळयासि (*mṛḷayāsi*)—you make happy
- सुतवंते (*sutavaṃte*)—we who have pressed and made ready the Soma-juice
- त्वामित् (*tvāmit*)—you alone
- हवामुहे (*havāmuhe*)—we pray and invoke for the drinking of Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, slayer of the demon Vṛtra, if you have the wish to make us happy, then we, who have pressed and made ready the Soma-juice to offer to you, pray to you alone in our sacrifice and invoke you for the drinking of Soma.

### Printed p. 389

##### English translation
Bearing the effused libation, we invoke you, mighty slayer of Vritra if you have favour to us, Indra.

#### Ṛk 31

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उप॑ नो॒ हरि॑भिः सु॒तं या॒हि म॑दानां पते ।  
> उप॑ नो॒ हरि॑भिः सु॒तम् ॥ ३१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उप । नः । हरिऽभिः । सुतम् । याहि । मदानाम् । पते ।  
> उप । नः । हरिऽभिः । सुतम् ॥ ३१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मदानां पते । माद्यंतेऽनेनेति मदाः सोमाः। ‘मदोऽनुपसर्गे' इति करणेऽप्प्रत्ययः । सोमानां स्वामिन्निंद्र हरिभिः ‘आ शतेन हरिभिः' (ऋ. सं. २.१८.६ ) इत्यादिषु बहूनामश्वानां श्रुतेरत्रापि शतसहस्रसंख्याकैरश्वैः सह नः अस्माकं यज्ञे सुतम् अभिषुतं सोमम् उप याहि । तत्पानार्थं शीघ्रमायाहि । पुनः उप नः इत्यादरार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O मदानां पते (*madānāṃ pate*), lord of the Somas (the मदाः (*madāḥ*) are the Somas, because by them one is exhilarated), Indra: since many horses are heard of in passages such as आ शतेन हरिभिः (*ā śatena haribhiḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2.18.6), here also come with hundreds and thousands of हरिभिः (*haribhiḥ*), horses, to the Soma pressed at our sacrifice; come quickly to drink it. The repetition उप नः (*upa naḥ*) is for respect.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मदानां पते (*madānāṃ pate*)—O Indra, lord of the exhilarating Soma-juice
- हरिभिः (*haribhiḥ*)—accompanied by many horses
- नः (*naḥ*)—at our sacrifice
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—with a view to the pressed Soma
- उप याहि (*upa yāhi*)—be pleased to come
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—for the drinking of the pressed Soma-juice
- हरिभिः (*haribhiḥ*)—with your horses
- नः उप (*naḥ upa*)—be pleased to come to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, lord of the exhilarating Soma-juice, be pleased to come to us, together with your many horses, for the drinking of the Soma-juice pressed and made ready at our sacrifice.

### Printed p. 390

##### English translation
Come with your steeds to our effused libation, lord of the Soma,—come with your steeds to our effused libation.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the sixth day of the ten-day sacrifice called Vyūḷha, in the Niṣkevalya recitations, the three Ṛks beginning उप नो हरिभिः (*upa no haribhiḥ*) are to be recited as the निविद्धानीयतृच (*nividdhānīyatṛca*); this is explained by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अयं ह येन वा इदमुप नो हरिभिः सुतं (*ayaṃ ha yena vā idamupa no haribhiḥ sutaṃ*) (Ā. 8-5). **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 32

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> द्वि॒ता यो वृ॑त्र॒हंत॑मो वि॒द इंद्रः॑ श॒तक्र॑तुः ।  
> उप॑ नो॒ हरि॑भिः सु॒तम् ॥ ३२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> द्विता । यः । वृत्रहन्ऽतमः । विदे । इंद्रः । शतऽक्रतुः ।  
> उप । नः । हरिऽभिः । सुतम् ॥ ३२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वृत्रहंतमः अतिशयेन वृत्रस्य हंता शतक्रतुः नानाविधकर्मा यः इंद्रः द्विता द्विधा विदे वृत्रवधादावुग्रकर्मा जगद्रक्षणकाले शांतकर्मेति द्विप्रकारेण सर्वैर्ज्ञायते । विद ज्ञाने'। कर्मणि विहितस्य तप्रत्ययस्य लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेषु' इति तलोपः । स त्वं हरिभिः सह सुतं सोममुपयाहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra, extreme slayer of Vṛtra and doer of many kinds of deeds, is known in two ways, द्विता (*dvitā*), विदे (*vide*): by all he is known as fierce in action at the slaying of Vṛtra and the like, and as gentle in action at the time of protecting the world. Such as you are, come with your horses to the pressed Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहंतमः (*vṛtrahaṃtamaḥ*)—he who slew the demon Vṛtra
- शतक्रतुः (*śatakratuḥ*)—and the doer of many deeds of daring
- यः इंद्रः (*yaḥ iṃdraḥ*)—which Indra
- द्विता (*dvitā*)—of two kinds, that is, the fierce action at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra and the like and the gentle action at the time of the protection of the world, both kinds of action
- विदे (*vide*)—who has known (such an Indra)
- नः (*naḥ*)—that concerns us
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—looking to the pressed Soma
- हरिभिः (*haribhiḥ*)—with his horses
- उप (*upa*)—let him be pleased to come

### Printed p. 391

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May that Indra, the slayer of the demon Vṛtra and doer of many kinds of deeds of daring, who knows that he must do cruel action at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra and the like and gentle action at the time of the protection of the world, be pleased to come to us with his horses, to drink the Soma that we have prepared.

##### English translation
Indra, Satakratu, mighty slayer of Vritra, you whose power is known in a two-fold way, come with your steeds to our effused libation.

#### Ṛk 33

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं हि वृ॑त्रहन्नेषां पा॒ता सोमा॑ना॒मसि॑ ।  
> उप॑ नो॒ हरि॑भिः सु॒तम् ॥ ३३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वम् । हि । वृत्रऽहन् । एषाम् । पाता । सोमानाम् । असि ।  
> उप । नः । हरिऽभिः । सुतम् ॥ ३३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वृत्रहन् वृत्रस्य पापस्य वा हंतरिंद्र । हिशब्दो हेत्वर्थे। यस्मात् त्वम् एषाम् अस्मदीयानां सोमानां पाता पानकर्ता असि भवसि । एषाम् इति इदमोऽन्वादेशे अशोदेशोऽनुदात्तश्च । अतस्त्वम् अश्वैः सह सोमं पातुमुपयाहि आगच्छ ॥
> व्यूळ्हस्य दशरात्रस्य नवमेऽहनि वैश्वदेवे अभिप्लवतृचस्य ‘इंद्र इषे ददातु नस्ते नो रत्नानि धत्तन' इति द्वे ऋचावार्भव्यौ । सूत्रितं च- इंद्र इषे ददातु नस्ते नो रत्नानि धत्तनेत्येका द्वे व (आश्व. श्रौ. ८. ११ ) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, or of sin: the word हि (*hi*) has the sense of cause. Because you are the drinker of these our Somas, therefore come with your horses to drink Soma. Use: on the ninth day of the Daśarātra called Vyūḷha, in the Vaiśvadeva, of the Abhiplava triplet, the two Ṛks इंद्र इषे ददातु नस्ते नो रत्नानि धत्तन (*iṃdra iṣe dadātu naste no ratnāni dhattana*) are Ārbhava; and it is stated in the Sūtra: इंद्र इषे ददातु नस्ते नो रत्नानि धत्तनेत्येका द्वे व (*iṃdra iṣe dadātu naste no ratnāni dhattanetyekā dve va*) (Āśv. Śrau. 8. 11).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहन् (*vṛtrahan*)—O Indra, slayer of the demon Vṛtra, or remover of sin
- हि (*hi*)—for what reason
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- एषां (*eṣāṃ*)—which we have prepared
- सोमानां (*somānāṃ*)—the Soma-juices
- पाता (*pātā*)—as drinker
- असि (*asi*)—you are, for that reason
- नः सुतं (*naḥ sutaṃ*)—with a view to our Soma
- हरिभिः (*haribhiḥ*)—with your horses
- उप (*upa*)—be pleased to come to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, slayer of the demon Vṛtra or remover of sin, you are the drinker of the Soma-juices that we have prepared for you. Therefore be pleased to come to us with your horses to drink that Soma-juice of ours.

### Printed p. 392

##### English translation
Slayer of Vritra, you are the drinker of these Soma juices, come with your steeds to our effused libation.

#### Ṛk 34

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॑ इ॒षे द॑दातु न ऋभु॒क्षण॑मृ॒भुं र॒यिम् ।  
> वा॒जी द॑दातु वा॒जिन॑म् ॥ ३४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । इषे । ददातु । नः । ऋभुक्षणम् । ऋभुम् । रयिम् ।  
> वाजी । ददातु । वाजिनम् ॥ ३४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रः एवास्माभिः स्तुत इष्टः सन् ऋभुक्षणम् । ‘वा षपूर्वस्य' इति दीर्घाभावः । यागादिकर्मकरणेन महांतं सर्वेषां भ्रातॄणां श्रेष्ठं वा । अथवा तृतीयसवने प्रजापतिसवित्रोर्मध्ये सोमपातृत्वात् महांतम् । रयिं दातारम् ऋभुं सोमपानेनामर्त्यत्वं प्राप्तं तादृशमेतन्नामकं देवं नः अस्मभ्यम् इषे अन्नार्थं ददातु प्रयच्छतु । तथा वाजी बलवानिंद्रः वाजिनं बलवंतमन्नवंतं वा वाजनामानं कनीयांसं भ्रातरं च अस्माकमन्नलाभाय ददातु ॥ ॥ २७ ॥ ॥ ९ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indra himself, praised by us and pleased, is asked to give to us ऋभुक्षणम् (*ṛbhukṣaṇam*), who is great through the performance of sacrifices and the like, or the foremost of all the brothers; or else great because at the third pressing he is a drinker of Soma between Prajāpati and Savitṛ. रयिं (*rayiṃ*): the giver (of wealth), Ṛbhu, who attained immortality by drinking Soma, the god of this name; may Indra give him to us इषे (*iṣe*), for food. Likewise may Indra, वाजी (*vājī*), the mighty, give वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*), the mighty or the one possessed of food, the younger brother named Vāja, for the gaining of food for us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra, thus praised by us
- ऋभुक्षणं (*ṛbhukṣaṇaṃ*)—the great one, that is, the eldest of the three brothers Ṛbhu, Vibhu and Vāja
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—the giver of wealth
- ऋभुं (*ṛbhuṃ*)—the god named Ṛbhu
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- इषे (*iṣe*)—in order to provide food
- ददातु (*dadātu*)—let him bring (and likewise)
- वाजी (*vājī*)—Indra, who is possessed of strength
- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—also the youngest brother named Vāja, possessed of food, for the gaining of food
- ददातु (*dadātu*)—let him bring and give

### Printed p. 393

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, thus praised by us, send to us the Ṛbhu among the Ṛbhus, that is, the eldest brother named Ṛbhu, the giver of wealth, of the three brothers Ṛbhu, Vibhu and Vāja, in order to provide us with food. Likewise may that same mighty Indra send the youngest brother named Vāja, for the gaining of our food.

##### English translation
May Indra bring to us the bounteous Ribhu Ribhukshana to partake of our sacrificial viands; may he, the mighty, bring the mighty (Vaja).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the ninth day of the ten-day sacrifice called Vyūḷha, when the Vaiśvadeva recitations are recited, the two Ṛks इंद्र इषे ददातु नः (*iṃdra iṣe dadātu naḥ*) and ते नो रत्नानि धत्तने (*te no ratnāni dhattane*) in the Abhiplava triplet are to be added and recited as Ṛks with the Ṛbhus as deity; this is explained by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra इंद्र इषे ददातु नस्तेनो रत्नानि धत्तनेत्येका द्वे च (*iṃdra iṣe dadātu nasteno ratnāni dhattanetyekā dve ca*) (Ā. 8-11). **NOTE**
We have given some explanations about the Ṛbhus here and there as occasion arose. Still it is necessary to give some more details about them here.

**The description of the skill of the Ṛbhus**
Their skill in the arts is praised in the words "When made by Tvaṣṭṛ, the Camasa vessel, which was one, you made it into four times as many," as said in the Ṛk
उत त्वं चमुसं नवं त्वष्टुर्देवस्य निष्कृतं । अकर्त चतुरः पुनः । (*uta tvaṃ camusaṃ navaṃ tvaṣṭurdevasya niṣkṛtaṃ | akarta caturaḥ punaḥ |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-20-6)
and as this same account is said later in the Ṛks
ज्येष्ठ आह चमसा द्वा करेति कनीयान्त्रीन्कृणवानेत्याह । कनिष्ठ आह चतुरस्करेति त्वष्ट ऋभवस्तत्पनयद्वचो वः ॥ (*jyeṣṭha āha camasā dvā kareti kanīyāntrīnkṛṇavānetyāha | kaniṣṭha āha caturaskareti tvaṣṭa ṛbhavastatpanayadvaco vaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-33-5)
and the like: the fact that, by their skill in the arts, they made the one vessel into four is well known. It is also said in the Bṛhaddevatā that in this work too they obtained this power by the instruction of Tvaṣṭṛ and that they were disciples of Tvaṣṭṛ.

### Printed p. 394

(Bṛ. De. 3-96 to 99)
Formerly, the three sons of Sudhanvan, Ṛbhu, Vibhva and Vāja, became disciples of Tvaṣṭṛ. Tvaṣṭṛ, skilled in all the arts, taught them also all the arts. Then the Viśvedevas, who were expert in the arts, opposed them with hostility. Then they made weapons and vehicles for all the gods. After that they created the cow that gives immortality. For Bṛhaspati and the Aśvins they made chariots with three seats, for Indra horses, and for Agni, who was sent by the gods as messenger, what was stated, that is,
किमु श्रेष्ठः किं यविष्ठो न आजगन्निमीयते दूत्यं १ कद्यमूचिम । न निंदिम चमसं यो महाकुलोऽग्ने भ्रातर्द्रुण इद्भूतिमूदिम ॥ एकं चमसं चतुरः कृणोतन तद्वो देवा अब्रवन्तद्व आगमं । सौधन्वना यद्येवा करिष्यथ साकं देवैर्यज्ञियासो भविष्यथ ॥ अग्निं दूतं प्रति यदब्रवीतनाश्वः कर्त्वो रथ उतेह कर्त्वः । धेनुः कर्त्वा युवशा कर्त्वा प्वा तानि भ्रातरनु वः कृत्व्येमसि ॥ (*kimu śreṣṭhaḥ kiṃ yaviṣṭho na ājagannimīyate dūtyaṃ 1 kadyamūcima | na niṃdima camasaṃ yo mahākulo 'gne bhrātardruṇa idbhūtimūdima ‖ ekaṃ camasaṃ caturaḥ kṛṇotana tadvo devā abravantadva āgamaṃ | saudhanvanā yadyevā kariṣyatha sākaṃ devairyajñiyāso bhaviṣyatha ‖ agniṃ dūtaṃ prati yadabravītanāśvaḥ kartvo ratha uteha kartvaḥ | dhenuḥ kartvā yuvaśā kartvā pvā tāni bhrātaranu vaḥ kṛtvyemasi ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-161-1 to 3)

### Printed p. 395

As described in these Ṛks, Agni went as the messenger of the gods to the sons of Sudhanvan and said that if they made the one Camasa vessel into four and helped the gods, they would then obtain with them the right to drink Soma. They replied that this was not the only task for them: whether the making of a horse, the making of a chariot, or the making of a cow, or making aged mothers and fathers young again, all this was possible for them, and that in the same way now also they would make for them all that was desired; and they made it for them. Since this matter is indicated here, they helped Agni by such skilful work. Then Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ and Prajāpati, the god of gods, called all the gods and granted that immortality should be attained by the Ṛbhus. Then Indra too (who had rejected them before) drank Soma with them. This story is told in the Bṛhaddevatā.
A story told in Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya is as follows. पुरा कस्य चिदृषेर्धेनुर्मृता। स सुषिक्तस्या धेनोर्वत्सं दृष्ट्वा ऋभुं तुष्टान ऋभवस्तत्स पृषीमन्यां धेनुं कृत्वा तदीयेन चर्मणा संवीय तेन वत्सेन समयोजयन्निति । (*purā kasya cidṛṣerdhenurmṛtā| sa suṣiktasyā dhenorvatsaṃ dṛṣṭvā ṛbhuṃ tuṣṭāna ṛbhavastatsa pṛṣīmanyāṃ dhenuṃ kṛtvā tadīyena carmaṇā saṃvīya tena vatsena samayojayanniti |*) Formerly the cow of a certain seer died. Out of pity for her small calf he prayed to the Ṛbhus to help it. Then the Ṛbhus created another cow, covered her with the hide of the dead cow and joined her with that calf. This is their greatness. According to the explanation of Skandasvāmin,
ऋषेः कस्यचिदग्निहोत्रधेनुस्तरुणवत्सा ममार । तस्यां विकर्तितायां आरुवता वत्सेन उद्वेजितः ऋभून् स्वपितरौ वृद्धौ पुनर्युवानौ कुर्वतो पदर्श । तानुवाच । ममास्यग्निहोत्रधेनुं मृतां पुनर्जीवयतेति । तस्य स्वमाहात्म्येन तस्माच्चर्मणः तामेव गां अशेषावयवोपेतां चक्रुः इति । तदेतदिहोच्यते निश्चर्मण इति ॥ (*ṛṣeḥ kasyacidagnihotradhenustaruṇavatsā mamāra | tasyāṃ vikartitāyāṃ āruvatā vatsena udvejitaḥ ṛbhūn svapitarau vṛddhau punaryuvānau kurvato padarśa | tānuvāca | mamāsyagnihotradhenuṃ mṛtāṃ punarjīvayateti | tasya svamāhātmyena tasmāccarmaṇaḥ tāmeva gāṃ aśeṣāvayavopetāṃ cakruḥ iti | tadetadihocyate niścarmaṇa iti ‖*)
The Agnihotra cow of a certain seer died, leaving her young calf. While she was being cut up, the seer, hearing the piteous cry of the young calf, remembered the Ṛbhus. They used to make their aged mother and father young again. Seeing that power of theirs, he asked that his dead Agnihotra cow also be brought to life. They made that dead cow, with the covering of that same cut hide, complete in all her limbs, and so brought that cow to life, it is said.

**How the Ṛbhus received hospitality in Savitṛ's house**
This story has been explained by Skandasvāmin in one way and by Sāyaṇa in another. In this connection,

### Printed p. 396

ऋभवो यज्ञियत्वं प्रार्थयमानाः प्रजापतेः सकाशमगमन् । अथ प्रजापतिः सवितारमाहूयावोचत्। एतेऽपि यज्ञिया भवंत्विति । कथेति सविता प्रतिपद्य तान् स्वगृहं नीत्वा द्वादश दिनान्यातिथ्यमेषामकार्षीदिति । तदेतद्वामदेवो वक्ष्यति । (*ṛbhavo yajñiyatvaṃ prārthayamānāḥ prajāpateḥ sakāśamagaman | atha prajāpatiḥ savitāramāhūyāvocat| ete 'pi yajñiyā bhavaṃtviti | katheti savitā pratipadya tān svagṛhaṃ nītvā dvādaśa dinānyātithyameṣāmakārṣīditi | tadetadvāmadevo vakṣyati |*)
The Ṛbhus, wishing to obtain the right to take part in the sacrifice and to receive the oblation, went into the presence of Prajāpati. Then Prajāpati called Savitṛ and said: let these also be worthy of the sacrifice (help them in this). After that Savitṛ agreed, saying so be it, took them to his house and carried out the hospitality for them for twelve days. Thus Skandasvāmin tells the story briefly, and cites the Ṛk that points to this occasion,
द्वादश द्यून्यदगोह्यस्यातिथ्ये रणन्नृभवः ससंतः । सुक्षेत्राकृण्वन्ननयंत सिंधून्धन्वातिष्ठन्नोषधीर्निम्नमापः ॥ (*dvādaśa dyūnyadagohyasyātithye raṇannṛbhavaḥ sasaṃtaḥ | sukṣetrākṛṇvannanayaṃta siṃdhūndhanvātiṣṭhannoṣadhīrnimnamāpaḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-33-7)
On this same occasion Sāyaṇa has indicated the part that tells the reason why the Ṛbhus came to Savitṛ's house.
दाशुषः प्रातःसवनादिष्वग्न्यादिभिरपसारितेभ्य ऋभुभ्यः सोमपानं दत्तवतः सवितुः गृहं निवासस्थानं तृतीयसवनाख्यमागच्छत प्राप्ताः । (*dāśuṣaḥ prātaḥsavanādiṣvagnyādibhirapasāritebhya ṛbhubhyaḥ somapānaṃ dattavataḥ savituḥ gṛhaṃ nivāsasthānaṃ tṛtīyasavanākhyamāgacchata prāptāḥ |*)
You, the Ṛbhus, who were rejected and sent out by Agni and the other gods at the morning pressing and the others, entered the sacrificial house, in the form of the third pressing, of Savitṛ, who gave you the drinking of Soma; with this he also states the rejection that came from Agni and the others. This matter is told fully in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa.
ऋभवो वै देवेषु तपसा सोमपीथमभ्यजयंस्तेभ्यः प्रातःसवने वाचि कल्पयिषंस्तानग्निर्वसुभिः प्रातःसवनादनुदत तेभ्यो माध्यंदिने सवने वाचि कल्पयिषंस्तानिंद्रो रुद्रैर्माध्यंदिनात्सवनादनुदत तेभ्यस्तृतीयसवने वाचि कल्पयिषंस्तान्विश्वे देवा अनोनुद्यंत नेह पास्यंति नेहेति स प्रजापतिरब्रवीत्सवितारं तव वा इमे अंतेवास्त्वमेवैभिः संपिबस्वेति स तथेत्यब्रवीत्सविता तान्स्वैः त्वमुभयतः परिपिबेति तान्प्रजापतिरुभयतः पर्यपिबत् । (*ṛbhavo vai deveṣu tapasā somapīthamabhyajayaṃstebhyaḥ prātaḥsavane vāci kalpayiṣaṃstānagnirvasubhiḥ prātaḥsavanādanudata tebhyo mādhyaṃdine savane vāci kalpayiṣaṃstāniṃdro rudrairmādhyaṃdinātsavanādanudata tebhyastṛtīyasavane vāci kalpayiṣaṃstānviśve devā anonudyaṃta neha pāsyaṃti neheti sa prajāpatirabravītsavitāraṃ tava vā ime aṃtevāstvamevaibhiḥ saṃpibasveti sa tathetyabravītsavitā tānsvaiḥ tvamubhayataḥ paripibeti tānprajāpatirubhayataḥ paryapibat |*)
(Ai. Brā. 3-30)
The Ṛbhus obtained the drinking of Soma among the gods by their austerity and by their excellent wish. First, when they wished to obtain it at the morning pressing, Agni, together with the Vasus

### Printed p. 397

joined and rejected them and drove them away. Then, when they wished to obtain it at the midday pressing, Indra, joined with the Rudras, drove them away. Again, when they wished to obtain it at the third pressing, the Viśvedevas rejected them there too with the harsh words, "You are surely not worthy to drink Soma here; you must not do so." Then Prajāpati said to Savitṛ, "These Ṛbhus are your pupils. Drink Soma with them." After that Savitṛ agreed. Prajāpati too drank the Soma-juice on both sides of them. In this way Sāyaṇa has told briefly the circumstance that is told at length in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa.

**Who are the Ṛbhus?**
It is said in many places in the Ṛgveda that the Ṛbhus were formerly men and attained the state of gods by their excellent conduct and the performance of good works. Formerly the seer Aṅgiras had a son named Nītimañjarī. In his family the seer Sudhanvan had three sons, Ṛbhu, Vibhu and Vāja. It is traditionally held that by good works such as the performance of good deeds and helping the gods they obtained the birth of gods, or became gods. There is a custom of calling all three sons of Sudhanvan, Ṛbhu and the others, Ṛbhus. All three sons are called by the name of the eldest. Since they were disciples of Tvaṣṭṛ, they are also called the craftsmen of the gods. It is said here and there that they made the equipment needed by Indra and the other gods, that is, Indra's chariot and Agni's Camasa vessel. In this hymn there is a description of some works done by them. There are descriptions here and there that they have wonderful power and that they are capable of doing any kind of work. Since they have the same power and capacity as the gods, the seers, thinking of them as belonging to the company of the gods, have described them and the works done by them in many ways. It is traditionally held that they live in the orb of the sun and do their work through the rays of the sun.

## Sūkta 94 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दशमेऽनुवाके दश सूक्तानि । तत्र ‘गौर्धयति' इति द्वादशर्चमाद्यं सूक्तमांगिरसस्य बिंदुनाम्नः पूतदक्षनाम्नो वार्षं गायत्रं मरुद्देवताकम् । तथा चानुक्रम्यते- ‘ गौर्धयति द्वादश बिंदुः पूतदक्षो वा मारुतम्' इति । सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः । प्रातःसवने सोमातिरिक्त एकं शस्त्रमुपजायते । तत्राद्यस्तृचोऽनुरूपः । सूत्रितं च - ‘अस्ति सोमो अयं सुतो गौर्धयति मरुतामिति स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ' (आश्व. श्रौ. ६. ७) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The tenth anuvāka has ten sūktas. Of these the first, गौर्धयति (*gaurdhayati*), of twelve Ṛks, is of the seer Bindu or Pūtadakṣa, of the family of Aṅgiras; its metre is Gāyatra and its deity the Maruts. As the Anukramaṇī says: गौर्धयति द्वादश बिंदुः पूतदक्षो वा मारुतम् (*gaurdhayati dvādaśa biṃduḥ pūtadakṣo vā mārutam*). The use of the sūkta is by the Liṅga (indicative sign). At the morning pressing, one recitation (śastra) additional to Soma is performed. In it the first triplet is the Anurūpa. And it is stated in the Sūtra: अस्ति सोमो अयं सुतो गौर्धयति मरुतामिति स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*asti somo ayaṃ suto gaurdhayati marutāmiti stotriyānurūpau*) (Āśv. Śrau. 6. 7). **NOTE**

### Printed p. 398

In the tenth anuvāka of the eighth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā there are ten sūktas. Of these, the sūkta called गौर्धयति (*gaurdhayati*) is the first. It has twelve Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Bindu, the son of Aṅgiras, or Pūtadakṣa; the deity is the Maruts; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: गौर्धयति द्वादश बिंदुः पूतदक्षो वा मारुतं (*gaurdhayati dvādaśa biṃduḥ pūtadakṣo vā mārutaṃ*). The use of the sūkta is by the Liṅga. At the morning pressing, one śastra among the additional mantras recited with reference to the Soma deity is to be recited. On that occasion the first three Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited as the Anurūpa triplet; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra अस्ति सोमो आयं सुतो गौर्धयति मरुतामिति स्तोत्रियानुरूपौ (*asti somo āyaṃ suto gaurdhayati marutāmiti stotriyānurūpau*) (Ā. 6-2). **NOTE**

Sūkta—94
Maṇḍala—8 ‖ Anuvāka—10 ‖ Sūkta—94 ‖
Aṣṭaka—6 ‖ Adhyāya—6 ‖ Varga—28, 29 ‖
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—12 ‖
Ṛṣi—Binduḥ Pūtadakṣo vā ‖
Devatā—Marutaḥ ‖
Chandas—Gāyatrī ‖

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गौर्ध॑यति म॒रुतां॑ श्रव॒स्युर्मा॒ता म॒घोना॑म् ।  
> यु॒क्ता वह्नी॒ रथा॑नाम् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गौः । धयति । मरुताम् । श्रवस्युः । माता । मघोनाम् ।  
> युक्ता । वह्निः । रथानाम् ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 399

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मघोनां धनवतां मरुतां माता निर्मात्री गौः पृश्निरूपा । ‘पृश्नियै वै पयसो मरुतो जाताः' इति श्रुतेः। यद्वा । गौर्माध्यमिकी वाक् । तत्रैव मध्यमस्थाने मरुतामपि वर्तनात्तेषां तत्पुत्रत्वमुपचर्यते। धयति सोमं पिबति पाययति वा स्वपुत्रान् मरुतः । किमिच्छंती। श्रवस्युः अन्नं कामयमाना । कीदृशी। रथानां मारुतानां वह्निः पृषतीभिर्वडवाभिर्वोढ्री संयोजयित्री सा युक्ता सर्वत्र समंतात् पूज्या भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of the wealthy Maruts, the mother, the maker, is the cow, in the form of Pṛśni; for the Śruti says पृश्नियै वै पयसो मरुतो जाताः (*pṛśniyai vai payaso maruto jātāḥ*). Or else the cow is the speech of the middle region; since the Maruts too abide in that same middle region, sonship to her is ascribed to them figuratively. She drinks Soma, or makes her sons the Maruts drink it. What does she wish for? She is desirous of food. What is she like? She is the bearer of the chariots of the Maruts, the one who yokes them with the dappled mares; thus yoked, she becomes worthy of worship everywhere and on every side.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघोनां (*maghonāṃ*)—of the wealthy
- मरुतां (*marutāṃ*)—of the Marut gods
- माता (*mātā*)—the mother
- गौः (*gauḥ*)—the cow called Pṛśni, or the speech of the middle region
- धयति (*dhayati*)—drinks the Soma, or makes her sons the Maruts drink Soma
- श्रवस्युः (*śravasyuḥ*)—she who desires food
- रथानां (*rathānāṃ*)—for the chariots of the Marut gods
- वह्नीः (*vahnīḥ*)—the horses called Pṛṣatī
- युक्ता (*yuktā*)—she who yokes them

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Pṛśni, the mother of the wealthy Marut gods, drinks the Soma; or she makes her sons the Maruts drink it. She who desires food, and who yokes to the chariots of the Marut gods their horses, the vehicles called Pṛṣatī, the Mother of the Maruts in the form of a cow called Pṛśni, is worshipped by all.

##### English translation
The cow (Prishni), the food-desiring mother of the wealthy Maruts, drinks the (Soma), she is worthy of all honour who yokes (the mares) to their chariots.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यस्या॑ दे॒वा उ॒पस्थे॑ व्र॒ता विश्वे॑ धा॒रयं॑ते ।  
> सूर्या॒मासा॑ दृ॒शे कम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यस्याः । देवाः । उपऽस्थे । व्रता । विश्वे । धारयंते ।  
> सूर्यामासा । दृशे । कम् ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 400

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गौः सर्वदेवमयीत्याह । यस्याः मरुतां मातुर्गोः उपस्थे वर्तमानाः विश्वे सर्वे देवाः व्रता व्रतानि स्वस्वकर्माणि धारयंते बिभ्रति । इयमेवास्माकं स्वपयोमिश्रितस्य सोमस्य दात्रीति सर्वे तत्समीपे तिष्ठंतीत्यर्थः। किंच सूर्यामासा । माति स्वकलाभिस्तिथीनिति माश्चंद्रमाः ॥  ‘ देवताद्वंद्वे च ' इत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सूर्याचंद्रमसौ दृशे दर्शनाय सर्वलोकप्रकाशनाय च यस्या गोः समीपे कं सुखेन वर्तमानौ भवतः । सेयं गौः सोमं धयतीति पूर्वेण समन्वयः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He says that the cow is made up of all the gods. In the lap of her, the cow who is the mother of the Maruts, all the gods, abiding there, bear their व्रता (*vratā*), that is, their own several works. The meaning is: "She alone is the giver to us of the Soma mixed with her own milk", and so all stay near her. Moreover, as to सूर्यामासा (*sūryāmāsā*): मा (*mā*) is the moon, who measures the lunar days with his own phases. The sun and the moon, for the sake of seeing, that is, for lighting up all the worlds, abide happily, कं (*kaṃ*), near the cow. This cow drinks Soma: so the connection with the previous verse.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यस्याः (*yasyāḥ*)—of the mother of the Marut gods, who is in the form of a cow
- उपस्थे (*upasthe*)—in the neighbourhood
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods
- व्रता (*vratā*)—their several works
- धारयंते (*dhārayaṃte*)—they bear; that is, engaged in their several works, they abide near the Mother Cow
- सूर्यामासा (*sūryāmāsā*)—the sun and the moon
- दृशे (*dṛśe*)—in order to be seen by people
- कं (*kaṃ*)—abide happily near that cow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Near Pṛśni, the Mother Cow, the mother of the Marut gods, all the gods abide, engaged in their several works. In the same way the sun and the moon, appearing to the people of the world near that Mother Cow itself, abide happily.

##### English translation
She, in whose presence all the gods observe their functions, and the sun and moon move in peace to enlighten the world.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तत्सु नो॒ विश्वे॑ अ॒र्य आ सदा॑ गृणंति का॒रवः॑ ।  
> म॒रुतः॒ सोम॑पीतये ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत् । सु । नः । विश्वे । अर्यः । आ । सदा । गृणंति । कारवः ।  
> मरुतः । सोमऽपीतये ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 401

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अर्यः स्तोत्रकरणार्थमितस्ततो गंतारः नः अस्मदीयाः विश्वे सर्वे कारवः स्तोतारः तत् मरुतां बलं  सदा सर्वदा आ गृणंति । आभिमुख्येन स्तुतिभिः स्तुवंति । किमर्थम् । सोमपीतये अस्माभिर्दीयमानं  सोमं पातुम् । मरुतः एतन्नामका देवा अस्माभिराह्वातव्याः खलु । ततः पुरस्तात्तद्बलं स्तुवंतीत्यर्थः॥
> पूर्वाभिहित एव शस्त्रे 'अस्ति सोमः' इति स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । सूत्रं तु पूर्वेण सहोदाहृतम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The अर्यः (*aryaḥ*) are those who go hither and thither for the sake of praise. All our praisers, कारवः (*kāravaḥ*), always sing that strength of the Maruts; that is, they praise it facing them with hymns. For what purpose? In order to drink the Soma given by us. The Maruts, gods of this name, are indeed to be invoked by us; therefore they praise their strength beforehand. In the second paragraph: in the same śastra mentioned before, the triplet अस्ति सोमः (*asti somaḥ*) is the Stotriya triplet; the Sūtra has been quoted together with the preceding one.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)—those who go about
- नः (*naḥ*)—our own, belonging to us
- विश्वे कारवः (*viśve kāravaḥ*)—all the praisers
- तत् (*tat*)—the strength (greatness) of those Marut gods
- सदा (*sadā*)—at all times
- सु आ गृणाति (*su ā gṛṇāti*)—they praise well
- सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)—in order to drink the Soma offered by us
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—those Marut gods are invoked by us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

All the praisers, who go from here to there on the sacrificial altar in order to sing praises, and who belong to us, praise the great nature of the Marut gods well at all times; and the Marut gods, entreated by us, are invoked in order to drink the Soma that we offer.

##### English translation
Therefore all our priests in their worship always sing the Maruts that they may drink the Soma.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस्ति॒ सोमो॑ अ॒यं सु॒तः पिबं॑त्यस्य म॒रुतः॑ ।  
> उ॒त स्व॒राजो॑ अ॒श्विना॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्ति । सोमः । अयम् । सुतः । पिबंति । अस्य । मरुतः ।  
> उत । स्वऽराजः । अश्विना ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 402

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं पुरोवर्ती सोमः सुतः मरुदर्थमस्माभिरभिषुतः अस्ति विद्यते । तस्मात् अस्य । अन्वादेशे । एनं सुतं सोमं स्वराजः स्वयं दीप्यमानाः । स्वतेजसा नान्यदीयेनेत्यर्थः । तादृशाः मरुतः पिबंति । उत अपि च अश्विना अश्विनौ च सोमं पिबतः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma, present before us, has been pressed by us for the Maruts; it exists, अस्ति (*asti*). Therefore अस्य (*asya*), with reference to something already mentioned: this pressed Soma is drunk by the स्वराजः (*svarājaḥ*), those shining of themselves, by their own splendour and not by another's. Such Maruts drink it. Moreover, the Aśvins too drink the Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं सोमः (*ayaṃ somaḥ*)—this Soma before us
- सुतः अस्ति (*sutaḥ asti*)—has been pressed by us for the Marut gods (therefore)
- अस्य (*asya*)—this Soma
- स्वराजः (*svarājaḥ*)—shining with their own radiance
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—the Marut gods
- पिबंति (*pibaṃti*)—drink
- उत (*uta*)—and
- अश्विना (*aśvinā*)—the Aśvin gods also drink this Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Soma-juice, made ready before us, has been pressed by us for the Marut gods to drink. Therefore the Marut gods, who shine with their own radiance, and the Aśvin gods, drink this Soma.

##### English translation
This soma is effused (by us); the self-resplendent Maruts drink of it and the Aswins.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पिबं॑ति मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा तना॑ पू॒तस्य॒ वरु॑णः ।  
> त्रि॒ष॒ध॒स्थस्य॒ जाव॑तः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पिबंति । मित्रः । अर्यमा । तना । पूतस्य । वरुणः ।  
> त्रिऽसधस्थस्य । जाऽवतः ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 403

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> न केवलं मरुत एव सोमपातारः किंत्वेतेऽपीत्याह । मित्रः सर्वेषां स्वस्वकर्मणि प्रवर्तकत्वात् सखिभूतः अर्यमा च वरुणः दुःखादीनां शत्रूणां वा वरिता निवारकः । एतन्नामकास्त्रयो देवाः तना। ततमूर्णास्तुकेनेति तनं दशापवित्रम् । ‘सुपां सुलुक् ' इति तृतीयाया आलादेशः । तनाद्युदात्तः । तना पूतस्य शोधितं त्रिसधस्थस्य । सह तिष्ठन्यत्रेति सधस्थं स्थानम् । द्रोणकलशाधवनीयपूतभृदात्मनि त्रीणि स्थानानि यस्य तं तथोक्तं तादृशं जावतः स्तुत्यजनवंतमिमं सोमं पिबंति । द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठ्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Not only the Maruts are Soma-drinkers; he says that these also are. मित्रः (*mitraḥ*) is a friend, because he impels all to their own works. अर्यमा (*aryamā*), and वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*), the वरिता (*varitā*), the one who keeps off sorrows and the like, or enemies. These three gods of those names drink this Soma. तना (*tanā*): तनं (*tanaṃ*) is the ten-strand filter; the third case-ending is replaced by आ (*ā*). पूतस्य (*pūtasya*): purified by it. त्रिसधस्थस्य (*trisadhasthasya*): सधस्थं (*sadhasthaṃ*) is a place where things stand together; the Soma has three places, the Droṇakalaśa, the Ādhavanīya and the Pūtabhṛt, and is so described. जावतः (*jāvataḥ*): possessed of people who praise. They drink this Soma, the genitives standing in the sense of the accusative.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—the god Mitra, who is like a friend to all
- अर्यमा (*aryamā*)—the god Aryaman
- वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*)—the god Varuṇa, who removes the sorrow of all; these three gods
- तना (*tanā*)—by the ten-strand filter
- पूतस्य (*pūtasya*)—purified
- त्रिषधस्थस्य (*triṣadhasthasya*)—stored in three kinds of vessels, the Droṇakalaśa, the Ādhavanīya and the Pūtabhṛt
- जावतः (*jāvataḥ*)—the Soma offered with praise by the praisers
- पिबंति (*pibaṃti*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitra, who is as beneficial as a friend to all, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, who removes sorrow, these three gods drink this Soma-juice, purified by the ten-strand filter, filled into the three kinds of vessels, the Droṇakalaśa, the Ādhavanīya and the Pūtabhṛt, and offered by the praisers with mantras.

##### English translation
Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuna drink (the Soma), purified by the straining cloth, abiding in three places, and granting posterity.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒तो न्व॑स्य॒ जोष॒माँ इंद्रः॑ सु॒तस्य॒ गोम॑तः ।  
> प्रा॒तर्होते॑व मत्सति ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 404

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उतो इति । नु । अस्य । जोषम् । आ । इंद्रः । सुतस्य । गोऽमतः ।  
> प्रातः । होताऽइव । मत्सति ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उतो अपि च इंद्रः सुतस्य अस्माभिरभिषुतस्य गोमतः गव्यैर्मिश्रणवतः अस्य । अन्वादेशः । पूर्ववद्दशापवित्रेण पूतस्य सोमस्य जोषं पानरूपां सेवां प्रातः प्रातःसवने नु क्षिप्रम् आ मत्सति । मदि स्तुत्यादिषु । आभिमुख्येन स्तौति । यद्वा । सोमसेवां कामयते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । होतेव । यथा होता प्रातःसवने देवानभिष्टौति देवान् स्तोतुं वाभिवांछति ॥ ॥ २८ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

उतो (*uto*) means "moreover": Indra, of this Soma pressed by us and गोमतः (*gomataḥ*), that is, mixed with cow-products, and purified as before by the ten-strand filter, जोषं (*joṣaṃ*), the service in the form of drinking, प्रातः (*prātaḥ*), at the morning pressing, नु (*nu*), quickly, आ मत्सति (*ā matsati*): the root मदि (*madi*) is used in the sense of praise and the like; he praises, facing it. Or else, he desires the service of Soma. The illustration is होतेव (*hoteva*): as the Hotṛ at the morning pressing praises the gods, or wishes to praise the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उतो (*uto*)—moreover
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—pressed by us
- गोमतः (*gomataḥ*)—mixed with milk or curds, a product of the cow
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Soma-juice, purified by the ten-strand filter
- जोषं (*joṣaṃ*)—the service in the form of drinking
- होतेव (*hoteva*)—as the priest called the Hotṛ praises the gods at the morning pressing
- प्रातः (*prātaḥ*)—at the time of the morning pressing
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- आ मत्स्यति (*ā matsyati*)—praises, or desires the drinking of Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Moreover Indra too, at the time of the morning pressing, praises, as the Hotṛ praises the gods, the service of the Soma-juice that has been pressed by us, purified by the ten-strand filter and made ready mixed with milk or curds; or else he desires the drinking of the Soma.

##### English translation
Indra also is eager in the morning to drink this effused (Soma) mixed with milk, as a priest (to praise the gods).

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कद॑त्विषंत सू॒रय॑स्ति॒र आप॑ इव॒ स्रिधः॑ ।  
> अर्षं॑ति पू॒तद॑क्षसः ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 405

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कत् । अत्विषंत । सूरयः । तिरः । आपःऽइव । स्रिधः ।  
> अर्षंति । पूतऽदक्षसः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिर्मरुतो बहुवारं स्तुत्वेदानीमात्मानं वितर्कयति । सूरयः प्राज्ञाः आपइव उदकानीव तिरः यथोदकानि तिर्यग्गच्छंति तद्वत्तिरश्चीनगतयः संतः कत् कदा अत्विषंत । त्विष दीप्तौ । अंतरिक्षे कदा दीप्यंते । किंच स्रिग्धः शत्रूणां शोषका हंतारस्त इमे मरुतः पूतदक्षसः शुद्धबलाः संतः कदा वा अर्षंति । अस्मदीयं यज्ञं प्रत्यागच्छंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer, having praised the Maruts many times, now reflects on himself. The सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*) are the wise. आप इव (*āpa iva*), like waters, तिरः (*tiraḥ*): as waters flow sideways, so, moving obliquely, when, कत् (*kat*), do they shine, अत्विषंत (*atviṣaṃta*)? The root त्विष (*tviṣa*) is used in the sense of shining: when do they gleam in the sky? Moreover, स्रिग्धः (*srigdhaḥ*), they are the destroyers who dry up the enemies, these Maruts; being पूतदक्षसः (*pūtadakṣasaḥ*), of pure strength, when do they come? They come to our sacrifice. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*)—the wise ones (the Maruts)
- आप इव तिरः (*āpa iva tiraḥ*)—with their gaze turned downwards, as water flows down to a low region
- कत् (*kat*)—when
- अत्विषंत (*atviṣaṃta*)—they look down at us from the lofty sky
- स्निग्धः (*snigdhaḥ*)—these Maruts, who dry up their enemies
- पूतदक्षसः (*pūtadakṣasaḥ*)—being of pure strength
- अर्षंति (*arṣaṃti*)—when do they come towards our sacrifice?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As flowing water runs downward to a low region, the wise Maruts have their gaze turned downwards. Therefore when will the Marut gods, the driers-up of enemies, of pure strength, come downward from the sky where they are to our place of sacrifice?

##### English translation
When do the sages flash like waters across (the sky) ? when do the Maruts, pure in vigour, destroyers of enemies, come to our offering ?

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कद्वो॑ अ॒द्य म॒हानां॑ दे॒वाना॒मवो॑ वृणे ।  
> त्मना॑ च द॒स्मव॑र्चसाम् ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 406

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कत् । वः । अद्य । महानाम् । देवानाम् । अवः । वृणे ।  
> त्मना । च । दस्मऽवर्चसाम् ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतः महानां मंहनीयानां महतां वा त्मना च आत्मनैवालंकरणैर्विनापि दस्मवर्चसां दर्शनीयतेजस्कानामत एव देवानां द्योतमानानां वः युष्माकम् अवः पालनं कत् कदाहं वृणे संभजे । वृङ् संभक्तौ' । क्रैयादिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, of you who are महानां (*mahānāṃ*), honourable or great, त्मना (*tmanā*), by yourselves, even without ornaments, दस्मवर्चसां (*dasmavarcasāṃ*), of beautiful splendour, and therefore देवानां (*devānāṃ*), shining gods, अवः (*avaḥ*), your protection, कत् (*kat*), when shall I वृणे (*vṛṇe*), obtain? The root वृङ् (*vṛṅ*) is used in the sense of sharing.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महानां (*mahānāṃ*)—(O Marut gods) of you who are of great nature, or excellent
- त्मना च (*tmanā ca*)—by yourselves, without the help of any ornaments
- दस्मवर्चसां (*dasmavarcasāṃ*)—shining with exceeding brilliance
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—and shining
- वः (*vaḥ*)—your
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—protection
- कत् (*kat*)—when
- अद्य (*adya*)—in this sacrifice
- वृणे (*vṛṇe*)—shall I obtain?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Marut gods, when shall I obtain in this place of sacrifice the protection of you, who are of great nature, who shine by your own radiance alone without the help of ornaments or the like, and who are divine in nature?

##### English translation
O shall I to-day possess your protection, mighty deities, beautifully bright in yourselves (though unadorned) ?

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ ये विश्वा॒ पार्थि॑वानि प॒प्रथ॑न्रोच॒ना दि॒वः ।  
> म॒रुतः॒ सोम॑पीतये ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । ये । विश्वा । पार्थिवानि । पप्रथन् । रोचना । दिवः ।  
> मरुतः । सोमऽपीतये ॥ ९ ॥

### Printed p. 407

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये मरुतः विश्वा विश्वानि पार्थिवानि पृथिव्यां भवानि भूतजातानि दिवः द्युलोकस्य रोचना रोचमानानि ज्योतींषि च आ पप्रथन् सर्वत्र विस्तारितान्यकार्षुः । ‘प्रथ प्रख्याने'। ण्यंतस्य चङि अत्स्मृदॄत्वरप्रथम्रदस्तॄस्पशाम् ' ( पा. सू. ७. ४. ९५ ) इत्यभ्यासस्यादादेशः ।  ‘ चङन्यन्यतरस्याम् ' इति स्वरेण मध्योदात्तः । तादृशान् मरुतः देवान् सोमपीतये सोमपानायाहमाह्वयामि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts who आ पप्रथन् (*ā paprathan*), spread everywhere, all पार्थिवानि (*pārthivāni*), that is, born on the earth, all created beings, and रोचना (*rocanā*), the shining lights of दिवः (*divaḥ*), the world of heaven: such Maruts, gods, I invoke for the drinking of Soma. The root प्रथ (*pratha*) is used in the sense of making known.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये मरुतः (*ye marutaḥ*)—the Marut gods who
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- पार्थिवानि (*pārthivāni*)—belonging to the earth, that is, the multitude of creatures on the earth
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the world of heaven
- रोचना (*rocanā*)—with the light, or with the shining stars
- आ पप्रथन् (*ā paprathan*)—have made them pervaded and filled
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—such Marut gods
- सोमपीतये (*somapītaye*)—I entreat and invoke for the drinking of Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Marut gods who have made all the creatures in this world of earth shine, pervaded by the light of the sky or of heaven, such Marut gods I entreat and invoke for the drinking of Soma.

##### English translation
(We invoke) those Maruts to drink our Soma, who have spread out all the things of earth and the luminaries of heaven.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतः मितराविण एतन्नामका देवाः पूतदक्षसः परिशुद्धबलान् दिवः स्वतेजसा दीप्यमानान् । यद्वा । दिवो द्युलोकस्थितान् । त्यान् तान् प्रसिद्धान् वः युष्मान् नु क्षिप्रं हुवे आह्वयामि । किमर्थम् । अस्य अस्मदीयस्य सोमस्य पीतये पानाय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Maruts, gods of this name, मितराविण (*mitarāviṇa*), **NOTE** you, पूतदक्षसः (*pūtadakṣasaḥ*), of wholly pure strength, दिवः (*divaḥ*), shining with your own brilliance; or else दिवः (*divaḥ*) means those who stand in the world of heaven. त्यान् (*tyān*), those well-known you, नु (*nu*), quickly, I invoke, हुवे (*huve*). For what purpose? अस्य (*asya*), of this our Soma, पीतये (*pītaye*), for the drinking.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Marut gods
- पूतदक्षसः (*pūtadakṣasaḥ*)—of purified strength
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—shining by your own light, or
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—dwelling in the world of heaven
- त्यान् (*tyān*)—well-known
- वः (*vaḥ*)—you
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- अस्य सोमस्य (*asya somasya*)—this Soma
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—for drinking
- हुवे (*huve*)—I entreat and invoke

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Marut gods, you who are of pure strength, who shine by your own light, who dwell in the world of heaven and are well known, I entreat and invoke you for the drinking of this Soma.

##### English translation
O Maruts, I invoke you, resplendent of pure vigour, to drink this Soma.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ये मरुतः रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ वि तस्तभुः स्वबलेनैवात्यर्थं स्तब्धे चक्रुः । ते रोदसी स्वाधीने अकार्षुरित्यर्थः। त्यान् तान् सर्वतः प्रसिद्धान् नु क्षिप्रमहं हुवे आह्वयामि । किमर्थम् । अस्य इत्यादि ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Maruts who वि तस्तभुः (*vi tastabhuḥ*), by their own strength alone made रोदसी (*rodasī*), heaven and earth, exceedingly firm: the meaning is that they made heaven and earth subject to themselves. त्यान् (*tyān*), those, famed on every side, नु (*nu*), quickly I invoke, हुवे (*huve*). For what purpose? अस्य (*asya*) and so on.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ये मरुतः (*ye marutaḥ*)—the Marut gods who
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- वि तस्तभुः (*vi tastabhuḥ*)—have established by their own power, that is, have made subject to themselves
- त्यान् (*tyān*)—such famous Marut gods
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- अस्य सोमस्य (*asya somasya*)—this Soma
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—for drinking
- हुवे (*huve*)—I entreat and invoke

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Marut gods who by their own power have taken heaven and earth in hand and hold them in subjection to themselves, those famous Marut gods I quickly entreat and invoke to drink this Soma that I have made ready.

##### English translation
I invoke those Maruts to drink this Soma, who have established heaven and earth.

> त्यं नु मारु॑तं ग॒णं गि॑रि॒ष्ठां वृष॑णं हुवे ।

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्यम् । नु । मारुतम् । गणम् । गिरिऽस्थाम् । वृषणम् । हुवे ।  
> अस्य । सोमस्य । पीतये ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> त्यं तं सर्वत्र विश्रुतं गिरिष्ठां गिरिषु मेघेषु पर्वतेषु वा तिष्ठंतं वृषणम् उदकानां कामानां वा वर्षितारं मारुतं मरुत्संबंधिनं गणं संघं हुवे बिंदुरहमाह्वयामि । किं प्रयोजनम् । अस्य अस्मदीयस्य सोमस्य पीतये पानाय ॥ ॥ २९ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

त्यं (*tyaṃ*), that group renowned everywhere, गिरिष्ठां (*giriṣṭhāṃ*), abiding in the गिरिषु (*giriṣu*), in clouds or mountains, वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*), the rainer of waters or of wishes, the मारुतं (*mārutaṃ*) host of the Maruts, गणं (*gaṇaṃ*), the company, I, Bindu, invoke, हुवे (*huve*). For what purpose? अस्य (*asya*), of this our Soma, पीतये (*pītaye*), for the drinking.

- त्यं (*tyaṃ*)—the well-known
- गिरिष्ठां (*giriṣṭhāṃ*)—that moves in the mountain regions or among masses of cloud
- वृषणं (*vṛṣaṇaṃ*)—that rains desires or water **NOTE**
- मारुतं गणं (*mārutaṃ gaṇaṃ*)—the company of the Marut gods
- अस्य सोमस्य (*asya somasya*)—of this Soma that I have made ready

- सु (*su*)—quickly
- हुवे (*huve*)—I, the seer of this sūkta, named Bindu, entreat and invoke

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That well-known company of the Marut gods, which blows in the mountain regions or among masses of cloud, and which rains desires or water, I, the seer of this sūkta, named Bindu, quickly entreat and invoke for the drinking of this Soma-juice that I have made ready.

##### English translation
I invoke that band of the Maruts, abiding in the clouds, the showers, to drink this Soma.

## Sūkta 95 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘आ त्वा' इति नवर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तमानुष्टुभमैंद्रम् । तिरश्चीर्नामांगिरस ऋषिः । तथा चानुक्रम्यते- ‘ आ त्वा नव तिरश्चीरानुष्टुभम्' इति । आभिप्लविकेषूक्थ्येषु तृतीयसवनेऽच्छावाकस्य  ‘ आ त्वा गिरः' इति तृचो वैकल्पिकोऽनुरूपः । सूत्र्यते हि -- गायंति त्वा गायत्रिण आ त्वा गिरो रथीरिव' (आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ८) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning आ त्वा (*ā tvā*) has nine Ṛks; it is the second sūkta, in the Anuṣṭubh metre, addressed to Indra. The seer is Tiraścī of the family of Aṅgiras. So the Anukramaṇī says: आ त्वा नव तिरश्चीरानुष्टुभम् (*ā tvā nava tiraścīrānuṣṭubham*). In the Ābhiplavika Ukthya rites, at the third pressing, the triplet beginning आ त्वा गिरः (*ā tvā giraḥ*) is an optional Anurūpa of the Acchāvāka. For it is stated in the Sūtra: गायंति त्वा गायत्रिण आ त्वा गिरो रथीरिव (*gāyaṃti tvā gāyatriṇa ā tvā giro rathīriva*) (Āśv. Śrau. 7. 8).

In the Ṛgveda, the sūkta beginning आ त्वा गिरः (*ā tvā giraḥ*) is the second sūkta in the tenth maṇḍala. **NOTE** It has nine Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Tiraścī, the son of Aṅgiras; the deity is Indra; the metre is Anuṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: आ त्वा नव तिरश्चीरानुष्टुभं (*ā tvā nava tiraścīrānuṣṭubhaṃ*). In the Ukthya sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava, at the third pressing, the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite the three Ṛks beginning आ त्वा गिरः (*ā tvā giraḥ*) as the optional Anurūpa triplet; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra गायंति त्वा गायत्रिण आ त्वा गिरो रथीरिव (*gāyaṃti tvā gāyatriṇa ā tvā giro rathīriva*) (Ā. 7-8).

Sūkta—95
Maṇḍala—8 ‖ Anuvāka—10 ‖ Sūkta—95 ‖
Aṣṭaka—6 ‖ Adhyāya—6 ‖ Varga—30, 31 ‖
Number of Ṛks in the sūkta—9 ‖
Ṛṣi—Tiraścīḥ ‖
Devatā—Indraḥ ‖
Chandas—Anuṣṭup ‖

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ त्वा॒ गिरो॑ र॒थीरि॒वास्थुः॑ सु॒तेषु॑ गिर्वणः ।  
> अ॒भि त्वा॒ सम॑नूष॒तेंद्र॑ व॒त्सं न मा॒तरः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । त्वा । गिरः । रथीःऽइव । अस्थुः । सुतेषु । गिर्वणः ।  
> अभि । त्वा । सम् । अनूषत । इंद्र । वत्सम् । न । मातरः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे गिर्वणः गीर्भिर्वननीयेंद्र सुतेषु सोमेष्वभिषुतेषु सत्सु गिरः अस्माकं स्तुतिलक्षणा वाचः त्वा त्वाम् आ अस्थुः आभिमुख्येन शीघ्रं तिष्ठंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । रथीरिव । यथा रथवान् रथेन गच्छन् वीरः प्राप्यं देशं क्षिप्रं गच्छति तद्वदस्माभिरभिगंतव्यं त्वां स्तुतयोऽभिगच्छंति । किंच हे इंद्र अस्मदीया गिरः त्वा त्वामभिलक्ष्य समनूषत सम्यक् शब्दायंते । स्तुवंतीत्यर्थः । ‘नू स्तवने' । कुटादिः । तस्य लुङि रूपम् । तत्र दृष्टांतः । वत्सं न मातरः । यथा मातरो गावो वत्समभिलक्ष्य हंभारवादिशब्दं कुर्वंति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*), Indra, who are to be served with songs, when the Soma has been pressed, our songs, in the form of praise, आ अस्थुः (*ā asthuḥ*), stand quickly facing you. The illustration is रथीरिव (*rathīriva*): as a hero who has a chariot, going by chariot, quickly reaches the place he is to reach, so our praises go to you, whom we are to approach. Moreover, O Indra, our songs, aiming at you, समनूषत (*samanūṣata*), sound well, that is, they praise. The illustration is वत्सं न मातरः (*vatsaṃ na mātaraḥ*): as mother cows, aiming at the calf, make a sound such as lowing.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—O Indra, fond of praise
- रथीरिव (*rathīriva*)—as the master of a chariot goes to any region he likes
- सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)—at the time when Soma is pressed
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—our praises
- त्वा (*tvā*)—aiming at you
- आ अस्थुः (*ā asthuḥ*)—come and gather quickly
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- मातरः (*mātaraḥ*)—the cows who are mothers
- वत्सं न (*vatsaṃ na*)—as they call out lovingly when calling their calves
- त्वा अभि (*tvā abhi*)—towards you
- समनूषत (*samanūṣata*)—our words of praise resound

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, fond of praise, as the master of a chariot goes to any region he likes, so at the time when Soma is pressed our praises, aiming at you, come and gather quickly. O Indra, as the mother cows call out lovingly when they call their calves, so our words of praise resound towards you.

### Printed p. 412

##### English translation
O Indra worthy of praise, when the Soma is effused, our songs hasten to you as a charioteer (to his goal); they low towards you as cows towards their calves.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ त्वा॑ शु॒क्रा अ॑चुच्यवुः सु॒तास॑ इंद्र गिर्वणः ।  
> पिबा॒ त्व१॒॑स्यांध॑स॒ इंद्र॒ विश्वा॑सु ते हि॒तम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । त्वा । शुक्राः । अचुच्यवुः । सुतासः । इंद्र । गिर्वणः ।  
> पिब । तु । अस्य । अंधसः । इंद्र । विश्वासु । ते । हितम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे गिर्वणः गीर्भिर्वननीय हे इंद्र शुक्राः ग्रहेषु पात्रेषु च दीप्यमानाः सुतासः अस्माभिः अभिषुताः सोमाः त्वा त्वाम् आ अचुच्यवुः आगच्छंतु । ' च्युङ् प्लुङ् गती'। लङि ‘बहुलं छंदसि ' इति शपः  श्लुः । ततस्त्वमस्माभिर्दीयमानस्य अंधसः सोमस्य भवदीयं भाग तु क्षिप्रं पिब । तदेवोपपादयति । हे इंद्र विश्वासु सर्वासु दिक्षु ते त्वदर्थं सोमपुरोडाशादिहविः हितं निहितं भवति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*), Indra, to be served with songs, the Soma-juices शुक्राः (*śukrāḥ*), shining in the cups and vessels, सुतासः (*sutāsaḥ*), pressed by us, आ अचुच्यवुः (*ā acucyavuḥ*), may come to you. Then do you quickly drink your portion of the Soma, अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*), given by us. He confirms this: O Indra, in all directions, विश्वासु (*viśvāsu*), the oblations, Soma, the cake and the rest, are placed for you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—fond of praise
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- शुक्राः (*śukrāḥ*)—shining
- सुतासः (*sutāsaḥ*)—the Soma-juices pressed by us
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- आ अचुच्यवुः (*ā acucyavuḥ*)—may they come and join
- अस्य अंधसः (*asya aṃdhasaḥ*)—of this Soma-juice, your portion
- तु (*tu*)—quickly
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- विश्वासु (*viśvāsu*)—in all directions
- ते (*te*)—aiming at you
- हितं (*hitaṃ*)—oblations such as Soma have been offered

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, fond of praise, may the shining Soma-juices pressed by us come and join you. Drink quickly your portion of this Soma-juice. O Indra, in all directions oblations such as Soma have been offered to you.

### Printed p. 413

##### English translation
Indra worthy of praise, let the bright Soma-libations come to you ; drink your portion of the beveragr ; Indra, in all places it is fit for you.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पिबा॒ सोमं॒ मदा॑य॒ कमिंद्र॑ श्ये॒नाभृ॑तं सु॒तम् ।  
> त्वं हि शश्व॑तीनां॒ पती॒ राजा॑ वि॒शामसि॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पिब । सोमम् । मदाय । कम् । इंद्र । श्येनऽआभृतम् । सुतम् ।  
> त्वम् । हि । शश्वतीनाम् । पतिः । राजा । विशाम् । असि ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं श्येनाभृतम् । 'हृग्रहोर्भश्छंदसि ' इति हकारस्य भकारः । द्युलोकात् श्येनरूपया गायत्र्याहृतं सुतम् अभिषुतं सोमं मदाय हर्षाय पिब । कम् इति पूरणः सुखार्थो वा । सुखेन सोमं पिब । हिशब्दो हेतौ । हि यस्मात् त्वं शश्वतीनां बह्वीनां विशां मरुद्गणानां सर्वेषां देवगणानां च पतिः पालयिता स्वामी असि भवसि तथा राजा स्वतेजसा दीप्यमानश्चासि । अतस्त्वं पूर्वं सोमं पिबेति ॥
> आभिप्लविकेषूक्थ्येषु तृतीयसवनेऽच्छावाकस्य ‘श्रुधी हवं तिरश्च्या' इति वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रियः । सूत्रितं च -- श्रुधी हवं तिरश्च्या आश्रुत्कर्ण श्रुधी हवम् ' ( आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ८) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the pressed Soma, श्येनाभृतम् (*śyenābhṛtam*), brought from the world of heaven by the Gāyatrī in the form of a hawk, drink for exhilaration, मदाय (*madāya*). कम् (*kam*) is either an expletive or has the sense of pleasure: drink the Soma comfortably. The word हि (*hi*) has the sense of reason: because you are the lord and protector of the many शश्वतीनां (*śaśvatīnāṃ*) hosts, विशां (*viśāṃ*), of the Maruts and of all the hosts of the gods, and because you are a king shining by your own splendour, therefore drink the Soma first.

In the second paragraph: in the Ābhiplavika Ukthya rites, at the third pressing, the optional Stotriya of the Acchāvāka is श्रुधी हवं तिरश्च्या (*śrudhī havaṃ tiraścyā*). And it is stated in the Sūtra: श्रुधी हवं तिरश्च्या आश्रुत्कर्ण श्रुधी हवम् (*śrudhī havaṃ tiraścyā āśrutkarṇa śrudhī havam*) (Āśv. Śrau. 7. 8).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- श्येनाभृतं (*śyenābhṛtaṃ*)—brought by the Gāyatrī in the form of a hawk
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for your exhilaration
- पिब (*piba*)—drink
- हि (*hi*)—because
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- शश्वतीनां (*śaśvatīnāṃ*)—of the many
- विशां (*viśāṃ*)—of all the peoples, gods, men and the rest
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—as the protector
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- राजा (*rājā*)—you are self-resplendent

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are the lord and protector of the many peoples, gods, men and the rest, and you are self-resplendent. Therefore drink, for your exhilaration, the Soma pressed here, brought by the Gāyatrī in the form of a hawk.

### Printed p. 414

##### English translation
Drink to your fill, Indra, the effused Soma brought by the hawk, you are the lord of all the divine hosts, you are the self-resplendent.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्रु॒धी हवं॑ तिर॒श्च्या इंद्र॒ यस्त्वा॑ सप॒र्यति॑ ।  
> सु॒वीर्य॑स्य॒ गोम॑तो रा॒यस्पू॑र्धि म॒हाँ अ॑सि ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> श्रुधि । हवम् । तिरश्च्याः । इंद्र । यः । त्वा । सपर्यति ।  
> सुऽवीर्यस्य । गोऽमतः । रायः । पूर्धि । महान् । असि ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यस्त्वा त्वां सपर्यति । सपरशब्दः कंड्वादिः । हविर्भिः परिचरति तादृशस्य तिरश्च्याः एतन्नामकस्यर्षेः मम हवं स्तुतिभिस्त्वद्विषयमाह्वानं श्रुधि शृणु । श्रुत्वा च हे इंद्र त्वं सुवीर्यस्य शोभनवीर्योपेतस्य । यद्वा । वीरे पुत्रे भवं वीर्यम् । सुपुत्रवतः । गोमतः गवादिपशुमतः रायः धनस्य दानेन पूर्धि अस्मान् पूरय । एतत्सामर्थ्यं कुत इत्यत आह । त्वं महान् गुणाधिको देवानां श्रेष्ठश्च असि भवसि खलु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, he who serves you, सपर्यति (*saparyati*), that is, attends on you with oblations: of such a one, of me, the seer named तिरश्च्याः (*tiraścyāḥ*), hear the invocation, हवं (*havaṃ*), the call addressed to you with praises. Having heard, O Indra, fill us by the gift of wealth, रायः (*rāyaḥ*), सुवीर्यस्य (*suvīryasya*), endowed with excellent heroism; or else, that which is born in a son, a hero, is वीर्यम् (*vīryam*): so, wealth with good sons; and गोमतः (*gomataḥ*), with cattle such as cows. Whence this ability? He says: you are महान् (*mahān*), greater in qualities, and the best of the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- सपर्यति (*saparyati*)—worships; such
- तिरश्च्यः (*tiraścyaḥ*)—of the seer called Tiraścī
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—the praise
- श्रुधि (*śrudhi*)—hear
- सुवीर्यस्य (*suvīryasya*)—accompanied by heroic sons
- गोमतः (*gomataḥ*)—accompanied by cows
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—by the gift of wealth
- पूर्धि (*pūrdhi*)—fulfil our desires
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- महान् (*mahān*)—of great nature
- असि (*asi*)—you are

### Printed p. 415

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, hear the praise of the seer called Tiraścī, who worships you. By the gift of wealth that is accompanied by heroic sons and by cows, fulfil our desires. You are of great nature.

##### English translation
Hear, Indra, the prayer of Tirashchi who worships you, and satisfy him with wealth bringing gallant offspring and cattle,—for you are mighty.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Ukthya sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava, at the third pressing, the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite the three Ṛks beginning श्रुधी हवं तिरश्च्यः (*śrudhī havaṃ tiraścyaḥ*) as the optional Stotriya triplet; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra श्रुधी हवं तिरश्च्यः आश्रुत्कर्ण श्रुधी हवं (*śrudhī havaṃ tiraścyaḥ āśrutkarṇa śrudhī havaṃ*) (Ni. 6-8). **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॒ यस्ते॒ नवी॑यसीं॒ गिरं॑ मं॒द्रामजी॑जनत् ।  
> चि॒कि॒त्विन्म॑नसं॒ धियं॑ प्र॒त्नामृ॒तस्य॑ पि॒प्युषी॑म् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्र । यः । ते । नवीयसीम् । गिरम् । मंद्राम् । अजीजनत् ।  
> चिकित्वित्ऽमनसम् । धियम् । प्रत्नाम् । ऋतस्य । पिप्युषीम् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यः यजमानः नवीयसीं नवतरां पुनःपुनः क्रियमाणतया मंद्रां मदकरीं गिरं स्तुतिलक्षणां वाचं ते त्वदर्थम् अजीजनत् उदपीपदत् । अकार्षीदित्यर्थः। तस्मै स्तोत्रे त्वं प्रत्नां पुरातनम् ऋतस्य सत्यस्य संबंधि । यद्वा । तृतीयार्थे षष्ठी । सत्येन पिप्युषीं प्रवृद्धम् । लिड्यङोश्च' इति प्यायतेः पीभावः । तादृशं चिकित्विन्मनसम्। कित ज्ञाने' । क्वसौ रूपम् । अकारस्येकारश्छांदसः । चिकित्वांसि ज्ञातानि सर्वेषां हृदयानि ययेति । अमायया क्रियमाणं यत्तव रक्षणं सर्वेषां हृदयं प्रज्ञापयतीति तदतींद्रियार्थदर्शकं धियं त्वदीयं रक्षणाख्यं तस्मै कुरु ॥ ॥ ३० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the sacrificer who has produced for you, अजीजनत् (*ajījanat*), that is, made, a newer song, नवीयसीं (*navīyasīṃ*), because it is made again and again, मंद्रां (*maṃdrāṃ*), gladdening, a speech in the form of praise: for him, in this praise, you, प्रत्नां (*pratnāṃ*), ancient, ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*), connected with truth; or else the genitive stands in the sense of the instrumental, पिप्युषीं (*pipyuṣīṃ*), grown great through truth; such, चिकित्विन्मनसम् (*cikitvinmanasam*), that is, that by which the hearts of all are made known. Your protection, which is done without deceit, makes the heart of all known; that, a धियं (*dhiyaṃ*), your own, called protection, which shows things beyond the senses, do for him.

### Printed p. 416

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंप्र (*iṃpra*)—O Indra
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the sacrificer who
- नवीयसीं (*navīyasīṃ*)—new
- मंद्रां (*maṃdrāṃ*)—and joy-giving
- गिरं (*giraṃ*)—speech in the form of praise
- ते (*te*)—addressed to you
- आजीजनत् (*ājījanat*)—has made; for that praiser
- प्रत्नां (*pratnāṃ*)—ancient
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—by its own true nature
- पिप्युषीं (*pipyuṣīṃ*)—greatly grown
- चिकित्विन्मनसं (*cikitvinmanasaṃ*)—that which by its power knows the minds of all
- धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)—the act in the form of protection, accomplish

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, for that praiser, the sacrificer who makes for you a new and joy-giving speech in the form of praise, accomplish the act in the form of protection, which is ancient, greatly grown by its own true nature, and by its power knows the minds of all.

##### English translation
To him who has made for you this newest joy-giving hymn, Indra, (extend), your ancient truthful providence to which all hearts are known.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तमु॑ ष्टवाम॒ यं गिर॒ इंद्र॑मु॒क्थानि॑ वावृ॒धुः ।  
> पु॒रूण्य॑स्य॒ पौंस्या॒ सिषा॑संतो वनामहे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तम् । ऊं इति । स्तवाम । यम् । गिरः । इंद्रम् । उक्थानि । ववृधुः ।  
> पुरूणि । अस्य । पौंस्या । सिसासंतः । वनामहे ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषयः परस्परमाहुः । तं पूर्वोक्तलक्षणम् । उ इत्यवधारणे । तमेवेंद्रं स्तवाम स्तुतिभिः स्तुमः। यम् इंद्रं गिरः अस्माकं स्तुतयः उक्थानि शस्त्राणि च वावृधुः प्रावर्धयन् तं स्तुमः । ततो वयम् अस्य इंद्रस्य पुरूणि बहूनि पौंस्या वीर्याणि सिषासंतः । ‘षण संभक्तौ'। सनीडभावपक्ष आत्वे कृते ‘सनोतेरनः' इति सांहितिकं षत्वम् । तानि वीर्याणि संभक्तुमिच्छंतः संतः वनामहे । तमिंद्रं स्तुतिभिः संभजामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sages say to one another: that Indra, described before (the particle उ (*u*) is for emphasis), that very Indra we praise with praises. We praise the Indra whom our praises, गिरः (*giraḥ*), and our recited hymns, उक्थानि (*ukthāni*), that is, the śastras, have made grow. Therefore we, desiring to share in his many deeds of might, पौंस्या (*pauṃsyā*), that is, heroic deeds, वनामहे (*vanāmahe*): we serve and worship that Indra with praises.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यं इंद्रं (*yaṃ iṃdraṃ*)—the Indra whom
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—our words of praise
- उक्थानि (*ukthāni*)—our śastra-mantras
- वावृधुः (*vāvṛdhuḥ*)—have made to grow strong
- तमु (*tamu*)—that very Indra
- स्तवाम (*stavāma*)—let us praise
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)—of many kinds
- पौंस्य (*pauṃsya*)—heroic deeds
- सिषासंतः (*siṣāsaṃtaḥ*)—desiring to praise
- वनामहे (*vanāmahe*)—we honour this Indra

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let us praise that very Indra whom our words of praise and our śastra-mantras have made to grow strong. Desiring to praise the many kinds of heroic deeds of this Indra, we honour this Indra.

##### English translation
Let us praise that Indra whom our chants and hymns have magnified ; we worship him, desirous to honour his many deeds of might.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> एतो॒ न्विंद्रं॒ स्तवा॑म शु॒द्धं शु॒द्धेन॒ साम्ना॑ ।  
> शु॒द्धैरु॒क्थैर्वा॑वृ॒ध्वांसं॑ शु॒द्ध आ॒शीर्वा॑न्ममत्तु ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एतो इति । नु । इंद्रम् । स्तवाम । शुद्धम् । शुद्धेन । साम्ना ।  
> शुद्धैः । उक्थैः । ववृध्वांसम् । शुद्धः । आशीःऽवान् । ममत्तु ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । पुरा किलेंद्रो वृत्रादिकानसुरान् हत्वा ब्रह्महत्यादिदोषेणात्मानमपरिशुद्धमित्यमन्यत । ततस्तद्दोषपरिहारायेंद्र ऋषीनवोचत् । अपूतं मां युष्मदीयेन साम्ना शुद्धं कुरुतेति । ततस्ते च शुद्धयुत्पादकेन साम्ना शस्त्रैश्च परिशुद्धमकार्षुः । पश्चात्पूतायेंद्राय' यागादिकर्माणि सोमादीनि हवींषि प्रादुरिति । एषोऽर्थः शाट्यायनकब्राह्मणे प्रतिपादितः- ‘ इंद्रो वासुरान्हत्वापूत इवामेध्योऽमन्यत । सोऽकामयत शुद्धमेव मा संतं शुद्धेन साम्ना स्तुयुरिति । स ऋषीनब्रवीत् स्तुत मेति । ततः ऋषयः सामापश्यन् । तेनास्तुवन्नेतो न्विंद्रमिति । ततो वा इंद्रः पूतः शुद्धो मेध्योऽभवत्' इति । तथा चास्या ऋचोऽयमर्थः । ऋषयः परस्परं ब्रुवंति । नु क्षिप्रम् एतो आगच्छतैव । आगत्य च शुद्धेन शुद्ध्युत्पादकेन साम्ना तथा शुद्धैः शुद्धिहेतुभिः उक्थैः शस्त्रैश्च इंद्रं शुद्धम् अपापिनं कृत्वा स्तवाम स्तुयाम । ततः सामशस्त्रैश्च वावृध्वांसं पापरहित्येन वर्धमानं तमिममिंद्रं शुद्धः दशापवित्रेण आशीर्वान् आश्रयणवान् गव्यादिभिः ।  ‘ छंदसीरः ' इति मतुपो वत्वम् । तादृशः सोमः ममत्तु इंद्रं मादयतु । माद्यतेश्छांदसः श्लुः ॥
> xxv. 27

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Here they relate an old story. Once, it is said, Indra, having slain Vṛtra and other asuras, thought himself impure through the fault of brahmin-slaying and the like. To remove that fault Indra said to the sages: make me, who am unclean, pure with your Sāman. They then made him pure with a Sāman that produces purity and with śastras, and afterwards offered to the purified Indra sacrificial rites and oblations such as Soma. This meaning is set forth in the Śāṭyāyana-brāhmaṇa: Indra, having slain the asuras, thought himself as if unclean and unfit for the sacrifice. He desired: "Let them praise me, being pure, with a pure Sāman." He said to the sages: "Praise me." Then the sages saw a Sāman, and with it they praised him, न्विंद्रमिति (*nviṃdramiti*). Thereupon Indra became clean, pure and fit for the sacrifice. According to this the meaning of the Ṛk is as follows. The sages speak to one another: come quickly, all of you. Having come, with the pure Sāman that produces purity, and with pure recited hymns and śastras, the causes of purity, let us praise Indra, making him pure and without sin. Then the pure Soma, purified by the ten-stranded filter and furnished with admixtures of milk and the like, āśīrvān, is to gladden, ममत्तु (*mamattu*), this Indra, who grows through Sāman and śastras by being free from sin.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O sages) सु (*su*)—quickly
- एतो (*eto*)—come together
- शुद्धेन (*śuddhena*)—purifying
- साम्ना (*sāmnā*)—with the Sāman
- शुद्धैः (*śuddhaiḥ*)—the means of purification
- उक्थैः (*ukthaiḥ*)—with the śastra-mantras
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- शुष्ठं (*śuṣṭhaṃ*)—so that he becomes free from fault
- स्तवाम (*stavāma*)—let us praise (afterwards)
- शुद्धो (*śuddho*)—the Soma that has obtained purity through the ten-stranded filter
- आशीर्वान् (*āśīrvān*)—and is furnished with substances such as milk as its support
- वावृध्वांसं (*vāvṛdhvāṃsaṃ*)—Indra, grown strong by the Soma vessel
- ममत्तु (*mamattu*)—may it gladden

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sages, come together quickly. Let us praise Indra, so that he becomes free from fault, with the purifying Sāman and with the śastra-mantras that are the means of purification. Afterwards may the Soma, which has obtained purity through the ten-stranded filter and is furnished with substances such as milk as its support, gladden Indra, who has grown strong through freedom from fault.

##### English translation
Come, let us praise the purified Indra with a pure Saman and with pure recited hymns ; let the pure (Soma) mixed with milk gladden him waxing strong.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In regard to this Ṛk and the next two Ṛks the commentator has told an earlier story:
अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । पुरा किलेंद्रो वृत्रादिकानसुरान् हत्वा ब्रह्महत्या-दिदोषेणात्मानमपरिशुद्धमित्यमन्यत । ततस्तद्दोषपरिहारायेंद्र ऋषी- नवोचत् । अपूतं मां युष्मदीयेन साम्ना शुद्धं कुरुतेति । ततस्ते च शुद्ध्यृत्पादकेन साम्ना शस्त्रैश्च परिशुद्धमकार्षुः । पश्चात्पूतायें-द्राय यागादिकर्माणि सोमादीनि हवींषि प्रादुरिति । (*atretihāsamācakṣate | purā kileṃdro vṛtrādikānasurān hatvā brahmahatyā-didoṣeṇātmānamapariśuddhamityamanyata | tatastaddoṣaparihārāyeṃdra ṛṣī- navocat | apūtaṃ māṃ yuṣmadīyena sāmnā śuddhaṃ kuruteti | tataste ca śuddhyṛtpādakena sāmnā śastraiśca pariśuddhamakārṣuḥ | paścātpūtāyeṃ-drāya yāgādikarmāṇi somādīni havīṃṣi prāduriti |*)

### Printed p. 419

In former times Indra, having killed many asuras beginning with Vṛtra, thought that the fault of brahmin-slaying had come upon him. To remove that fault he addressed the sages: "O sages, you must make me, who am made impure by the fault of brahmin-slaying, perfectly pure. For this, praise me with fitting Sāma-mantras and make me pure." Thereupon those sages, to purify Indra, recited the Sāma-mantras and the śastra-mantras needed for it and made Indra perfectly pure as before. Afterwards they performed sacrifices and other rites for the purified Indra and offered Soma, oblations and the like. Such is the purport of this story. That this matter is stated in the Śāṭyāyana-brāhmaṇa (of the Sāmaveda) is why it is quoted here.
इंद्रो वासुरान् हत्वापूत इवामेध्योऽमन्यत । सोऽकामयत शुद्ध-मेव मा संतं शुद्धेन साम्ना स्तुयुरिति । स ऋषीनब्रवीत् स्तुत मेति । तत ऋषयः सामापश्यन् । तेनास्तुवन्नेतो न्विंद्रमिति । ततो वा इंद्रः पूतः शुद्धो मेध्योऽभवत् ॥ (*iṃdro vāsurān hatvāpūta ivāmedhyo 'manyata | so 'kāmayata śuddha-meva mā saṃtaṃ śuddhena sāmnā stuyuriti | sa ṛṣīnabravīt stuta meti | tata ṛṣayaḥ sāmāpaśyan | tenāstuvanneto nviṃdramiti | tato vā iṃdraḥ pūtaḥ śuddho medhyo 'bhavat ‖*)
The same meaning is stated here also. At Indra's command the sages, perceiving by their divine vision three mantras, एतोन्विंद्रः (*etonviṃdraḥ*) (Sāmaveda 350, 1402), इंद्र शुद्धो न आगहि (*iṃdra śuddho na āgahi*) (Sāmu. 1403) **NOTE** and इंद्र शुद्धो हि नो रयिं (*iṃdra śuddho hi no rayiṃ*) (Sāmu. 1404), praised Indra. Thereby Indra became pure. That this very matter is stated in these Ṛks is why the above story has been given as an introduction to the meaning of these Ṛks.

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्र॑ शु॒द्धो न॒ आ ग॑हि शु॒द्धः शु॒द्धाभि॑रू॒तिभिः॑ ।  
> शु॒द्धो र॒यिं नि धा॑रय शु॒द्धो म॑मद्धि सो॒म्यः ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्र । शुद्धः । नः । आ । गहि । शुद्धः । शुद्धाभिः । ऊतिऽभिः ।  
> शुद्धः । रयिम् । नि । धारय । शुद्धः । ममद्धि । सोम्यः ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 420

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र शुद्धः अस्मदीयैः सामभिः शस्त्रैश्च परिशुद्धस्त्वं नः अस्मान् आ गहि आगच्छ । शुद्धाभिरूतिभिः । ऊतयो मरुतः । अवंति सर्वत्र गच्छंतीति वा । तेऽपि सामभिः शस्त्रैः परिपूताः । तैर्मरुद्भिः सह शुद्धः पापरहितस्त्वमा गहि । आगत्य च शुद्धः त्वं रयिं धनमस्मासु नि धारय नितरां स्थापय । किंच शुद्धः त्वं सोम्यः सोमार्हो भूत्वा ममद्धि सोमेन माद्य । ‘मदी हर्षे' । लोटि ‘बहुलं छंदसि' इति शपः श्लुः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you, purified by our Sāmans and śastras, come to us. With pure ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*): the ūtis are the Maruts, or those who go everywhere, अवंति (*avaṃti*). They too are purified by Sāmans and śastras. With those Maruts, you who are pure and free from sin, come. Having come, being pure, establish wealth firmly in us. Moreover, being pure and having become worthy of Soma, rejoice with Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- शुद्धः (*śuddhaḥ*)—you, purified by our śastras and the like
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be gracious and come
- शुद्धाभिः (*śuddhābhiḥ*)—with the thoroughly purified
- ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)—Maruts, your protectors
- शुद्धः (*śuddhaḥ*)—you, free from fault, come
- शुद्धः (*śuddhaḥ*)—you, free from stain
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- नि धारय (*ni dhāraya*)—establish in us
- शुद्धः (*śuddhaḥ*)—you, thoroughly purified
- सोम्यः (*somyaḥ*)—having obtained the right to drink Soma
- ममद्धि (*mamaddhi*)—obtain joy from the drinking of Soma

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you, thoroughly purified by our śastra-mantras and the like, be gracious and come to us. Free from fault, come with the Maruts, who are thoroughly purified and are your protectors. Free from stain, establish wealth in us. Thoroughly purified, having obtained the right to drink Soma, obtain the joy that comes from drinking Soma.

##### English translation
Come to us, Indra, purified ; purified with your pure protecting hosts ; purified, establish wealth in us ; purified and now worthy of the Soma, rejoice.

> शुद्धः । वृत्राणि । जिघ्नसे । शुद्धः । वाजम् । सिसाससि ॥ ९ ॥

### Printed p. 421

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र शुद्धः । हिरवधारणे । शुद्ध एव त्वं रयिं धनं नः अस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छ । तथा शुद्धः त्वं दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय रत्नानि रमणीयानि धनादीनि च देहि । ततः शुद्धः पापरहितस्त्वं वृत्राणि अपामावरकान् कर्मविघ्कारिणः शत्रून् पापानि वा जिघ्नसे हंसि । ततः शुद्धः शत्रुहननदोषपरिहारायास्मदीयैः सामभिः शस्त्रैः परिशुद्धस्त्वं वाजम् अन्नमस्मभ्यं सिषाससि प्रदातुमिच्छसि । यदा यदा शत्रूनहं हन्यां तदा तदा शुद्ध्युत्पादकैः सामभिः शस्त्रैश्च यूयं मां परिशुद्धं कुरुतेत्यस्मभ्यमन्नं दातुमिच्छसीत्यर्थः ॥ ॥ ३१ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, being pure (हि (*hi*) is for emphasis), give us wealth. Likewise, being pure, give to the sacrificer who has given oblations, दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*), delightful treasures, रत्नानि (*ratnāni*), wealth and the like. Then, being pure and free from sin, you smite the वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*): the enemies who obstruct the waters and hinder the ritual, or else sins. Then, being pure, purified by our Sāmans and śastras for the removal of the fault of killing enemies, you desire to give us food, वाजम् (*vājam*). The sense is: whenever I kill enemies, then you purify me with Sāmans and śastras that produce purity; thus you wish to give us food.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- शुद्धः (*śuddhaḥ*)—you, thoroughly purified
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—give to us
- शुद्धः (*śuddhaḥ*)—you, free from stain
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who gives oblations
- रत्नानि (*ratnāni*)—delightful riches, give
- शुद्धः (*śuddhaḥ*)—you, free from sin
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the asura powers that cause obstruction
- जिघ्नसे (*jighnase*)—destroy
- शुद्धः (*śuddhaḥ*)—you, free from sin
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- सिषाससि (*siṣāsasi*)—be willing to give to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you, thoroughly purified, give us wealth. Free from stain, give delightful riches to the sacrificer who gives oblations. Free from sin, destroy the asura powers that cause obstruction. Free from sin, be willing to give us food.

##### English translation
Purified, Indra, give us wealth ; purified, give to your worshipper preceious things ; purified, you smite your enemies ; purified, you desire to give us food.

## Sūkta 96 (Maṇḍala 8)
**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘ अस्मै ' इत्येकविंशत्यृचं तृतीयं सूक्तम् । अत्रानुक्रम्यते- अस्मै सैका द्युतानो वा मारुतस्त्रैष्टुभं चतुर्थी विराळिष्यामीति मारुतः पादः परैंद्राबार्हस्पत्या' इति । [१]द्युतानाख्यो मरुतां पुत्र ऋषिस्तिरश्चीर्नामांगिरसो वा । चतुर्थी विराट् । शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः । इंद्रो देवता । इष्यामि वो मरुतः' इति पादो मरुद्देवत्यः। ‘अध द्रप्सः' इत्येषा त्विंद्राबृहस्पतिदेवताका । सूक्तविनियोगो लिंगादवगंतव्यः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning अस्मै (*asmai*), of twenty-one Ṛks, is the third. About it the Anukramaṇī says: अस्मै सैका द्युतानो वा मारुतस्त्रैष्टुभं चतुर्थी विराळिष्यामीति मारुतः पादः परैंद्राबार्हस्पत्या (*asmai saikā dyutāno vā mārutastraiṣṭubhaṃ caturthī virāḷiṣyāmīti mārutaḥ pādaḥ paraiṃdrābārhaspatyā*). The seer is Dyutāna, a son of the Maruts, or Tiraścī of the Aṅgirases. The fourth Ṛk is in the Virāṭ metre; the rest are in Triṣṭubh. The deity is Indra. The pāda beginning इष्यामि (*iṣyāmi*) has the Maruts as deity. The Ṛk beginning अध द्रप्सः (*adha drapsaḥ*) has Indra and Bṛhaspati as deity. The use of the sūkta in ritual is to be understood from the indication.

### Printed p. 422

The Anuvāda: this sūkta beginning अस्मै (*asmai*) is the third sūkta in the tenth anuvāka. It has twenty-one Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said—अस्मै सैका द्युतः नो वा मारुतस्त्रैष्टुभं चतुर्थी विराळिष्यामिति मारुतः पादः पर्यैंद्राबार्हस्पत्या (*asmai saikā dyutaḥ no vā mārutastraiṣṭubhaṃ caturthī virāḷiṣyāmiti mārutaḥ pādaḥ paryaiṃdrābārhaspatyā*). **NOTE** For this sūkta the seer is Dyutāna, a son of the Maruts, or Tiraścīḥ Āṅgirasaḥ; Indra is the deity; the fourth Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Virāṭ metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭup metre. The fourth pāda of the fourteenth Ṛk, इष्यामि वः (*iṣyāmi vaḥ*), has the Maruts as deity; the fifteenth Ṛk, अध दृप्सः (*adha dṛpsaḥ*), has Indra and Bṛhaspati as deities. The use of the sūkta is by the Liṅga.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒स्मा आपो॑ मा॒तरः॑ स॒प्त त॑स्थु॒र्नृभ्य॒स्तरा॑य॒ सिंध॑वः सुपा॒राः ॥ १ ॥
