##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋभुक्षाः महान् । यद्वा । ऋभुशब्देनर्भ्वादयस्त्रयो गृह्यंते । ऋभुभिः सह क्षियति निवसतीति तादृशः। वृत्रहा सः इंद्रः सद्यः तदानीमेव जज्ञानः प्रादुर्भवन् हव्यः सर्वैः स्तोतृभिः यष्टॄभिराह्वातव्यो बभूव । किंच नर्या नर्याणि । नरा मनुष्याः कर्मनेतारः । तेभ्यो हितानि पुरूणि बहूनि अपांसि कर्माणि कृण्वन् कुर्वन् सखिभ्यः हविष्प्रदानेनोपकारकत्वान्मित्रेभ्य ऋत्विग्भ्यः हव्यः आह्वातव्यो हवनयोग्यो वाभूत् । तत्र दृष्टांतः। सोमो न यथा पीतः सोमो यष्टृभ्यः स्वर्गादिफलानि कुर्वन् देवैराह्वातव्यो भवति तद्वत् ॥ ॥ ३५ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

*Ṛbhukṣāḥ* means "great"; or else, by the word *ṛbhu* the three, Ṛbhu and the others, are meant, and he is one who dwells (*kṣiyati*) with the Ṛbhus. That Indra, the slayer of Vritra, at the very moment he was born (*jajñānaḥ*, appearing) became *havyaḥ*, to be invoked by all the praisers and sacrificers. Further, *naryā* are the things beneficial to *narāḥ*, men, the leaders of the rite; performing (*kṛṇvan*) many (*purūṇi*) such deeds (*apāṃsi*), he became to be invoked, worthy of invocation, by his friends (*sakhibhyaḥ*), the priests, because he helps them by receiving their oblations. The illustration: as Soma, when drunk (*pītaḥ*), giving the sacrificers heaven and the other fruits, is to be invoked by the gods, so is he.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋभुक्षाः (*ṛbhukṣāḥ*)—dwelling with the Ṛbhus
- वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*)—and the slayer of Vritra
- सः इंद्रः (*saḥ iṃdraḥ*)—that same Indra
- जज्ञानः (*jajñānaḥ*)—having been born
- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—at that very moment
- हव्यः (*havyaḥ*)—became worthy of the praise of all
- बभूव (*babhūva*)—became
- पीतः (*pītaḥ*)—fit to be drunk by the gods
- सोमो न (*somo na*)—as Soma is worthy of their invocation
- नर्या (*naryā*)—beneficial to men
- पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)—and of many kinds
- अपांसि (*apāṃsi*)—deeds
- कृण्वन् (*kṛṇvan*)—performing
- सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)—to his friends, the priests
- हव्यः (*havyaḥ*)—he became worthy of invocation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, who dwells with the Ṛbhus and is the slayer of Vritra, became worthy of the praise of all as soon as he was born. As Soma, fit to be drunk by the gods, is worthy of their respectful invocation, so Indra too, performing deeds of many kinds that are beneficial to men, is worthy of the invocation of his friends the priests, and is worshipful.

##### English translation
As soon as he was born, he, Indra, the slayer of Vritra, the chief of the Ribhus, was worthy to be invoked ; he, performing many sacred acts for men, is worthy to be invoked for his frends like the quaffed Soma juice.

### Printed p. 455

## Sūkta 97 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> या इंद्र इति पंचदशर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं काश्यपस्य रेभस्यार्षमैंद्रम् । दशम्यतिजगती द्वापंचाशदक्षरा। एकादशीद्वादश्यावुपरिष्टाद्बृहत्यौ त्र्यष्टकांतद्वादशकवत्यौ। त्रयोदश्यतिजगती । चतुर्दशी त्रिष्टुप् । पंचदशी जगती । शिष्टा बृहत्यः । तथा चानुक्रम्यते- या इंद्र पंचोना रेभः काश्यपो बार्हतमतिजगत्युपरिष्टाद्बृहत्यावतिजगती त्रिष्टुब्जगतीत्यंततः' इति । सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः । महाव्रते निष्केवल्ये बार्हततृचाशीतौ ' या इंद्र' इत्यादिका नवर्चः । तथैव पंचमारण्यके सूत्र्यते ' या इंद्र भुज आभर इति नव सूददोहाः' (ऐ. आ. ५. २. ४) इति । चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनो वैकल्पिकानुरूपतृचस्य ' या इंद्र' इत्यादिके द्वे द्वितीयातृतीये । सूत्र्यते च--- तमिंद्रं जोहवीमि या इंद्र भुज आभर इत्येका द्वे च' (आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ४) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The hymn beginning या इंद्र (*yā iṃdra*) has fifteen verses and is the fourth hymn; its seer is Rebha Kāśyapa and its deity is Indra. The tenth verse is an atijagatī of fifty-two syllables; the eleventh and twelfth are upariṣṭādbṛhatī, with three octosyllabic quarters and the last of twelve syllables; the thirteenth is an atijagatī; the fourteenth is a triṣṭubh; the fifteenth is a jagatī; the rest are bṛhatī. So the Anukramaṇī says: या इंद्र पंचोना रेभः काश्यपो बार्हतमतिजगत्युपरिष्टाद्बृहत्यावतिजगती त्रिष्टुब्जगतीत्यंततः (*yā iṃdra paṃconā rebhaḥ kāśyapo bārhatamatijagatyupariṣṭādbṛhatyāvatijagatī triṣṭubjagatītyaṃtataḥ*). The application of the hymn is by indication (*laiṅgika*). In the Mahāvrata, in the Niṣkevalya, the nine verses of the Bārhata tṛca beginning या इंद्र (*yā iṃdra*) are used; so it is taught in the fifth Āraṇyaka: या इंद्र भुज आभर इति नव सूददोहाः (*yā iṃdra bhuja ābhara iti nava sūdadohāḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 5. 2. 4). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, the two verses beginning या इंद्र (*yā iṃdra*) are the second and third of the alternative Anurūpa tṛca of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; and it is taught: तमिंद्रं जोहवीमि या इंद्र भुज आभर इत्येका द्वे च (*tamiṃdraṃ johavīmi yā iṃdra bhuja ābhara ityekā dve ca*) (Āśva. Śrau. 7. 4).

##### Anuvāda

This hymn beginning *yā indra* is the fourth hymn in the tenth Anuvāka. It has fifteen verses. For this hymn the seer is Rebhaḥ Kāśyapaḥ; the deity is Indra; the tenth verse of this hymn is in the metre atijagatī of fifty-two syllables; the eleventh and twelfth verses are in the metre upariṣṭādbṛhatī. In this metre there are four quarters, of which the first three have eight syllables each and the last has twelve syllables; the thirteenth verse is in the atijagatī metre; the fourteenth is in triṣṭubh; the fifteenth is in jagatī; the remaining verses are in bṛhatī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: या इंद्र पंचोना रेभः काश्यपो बार्हतमतिजगत्युपरिष्टाद्बृहत्यावतिजगती त्रिष्टुब्जगतीत्यंततः (*yā iṃdra paṃconā rebhaḥ kāśyapo bārhatamatijagatyupariṣṭādbṛhatyāvatijagatī triṣṭubjagatītyaṃtataḥ*). The application of the hymn is by indication. In the Mahāvrata rite, when the Niṣkevalya recitation is made, the nine verses of this hymn beginning with *yā indra* are applied for the verses of the bṛhatī metre, as is set out in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka by the sentence या इंद्र भुज आभर इति नव सूददोहाः (*yā iṃdra bhuja ābhara iti nava sūdadohāḥ*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-4). And on the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the time of the midday pressing, in the Anurūpa tṛca recited by the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the two verses beginning with *yā indra* are to be recited as the second and third verses of the tṛca; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, तमिंद्रं जोहवीमि या इंद्र भुज आभर इत्येका द्वे च (*tamiṃdraṃ johavīmi yā iṃdra bhuja ābhara ityekā dve ca*) (Ā. 7-4).

##### Particulars

Sūkta 97. Maṇḍala 8. Anuvāka 10. Aṣṭaka 6. Adhyāya 6. Vargas 36, 37, 38. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 15. Seer: Rebhaḥ Kāśyapaḥ. Deity: Indraḥ. Metre: 1-9 Bṛhatī; 10, 13 Atijagatī; 11, 12 Upariṣṭādbṛhatī; 14 Triṣṭup; 15 Jagatī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> या इं॑द्र॒ भुज॒ आभ॑रः॒ स्व॑र्वाँ॒ असु॑रेभ्यः ।  
> स्तो॒तार॒मिन्म॑घवन्नस्य वर्धय॒ ये च॒ त्वे वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> याः । इंद्र । भुजः । आ । अभरः । स्वःऽवान् । असुरेभ्यः ।  
> स्तोतारम् । इत् । मघवन् । अस्य । वर्धय । ये । च । त्वे इति । वृक्तऽबर्हिषः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिरिंद्रं प्रार्थयते । हे इंद्र स्वर्वान् सुखवान् स्वर्गवान् वा । अथवा स्वःशब्दः सर्वपर्यायः । सर्वं भूतजातम् । आत्मन एवोत्पन्नत्वात्तद्वान् । एवंगुणस्त्वं याः यानि भुजः भोक्तव्यानि धनानि असुरेभ्यः बलवद्भ्यो राक्षसेभ्यः आभरः आहरः तान् हत्वाहृतवानसि। हग्रहोः' इति भकारादेशः । अत एव हे मघवन् धनवन्निंद्र अस्य । अन्वादेशेऽशादेशः । एतस्याहृतस्य धनस्य दानेन स्तोतारमित् तव स्तोत्रकारिणमेव वर्धय वृद्धिमंतं कुरु। ये च अन्ये यष्टारः त्वे त्वदर्थं वृक्तबर्हिषः स्तीर्णबर्हिषो भवंति अतस्तांश्च धनेन वर्धय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer prays to Indra. O Indra, *svarvān*: possessed of happiness, or of heaven; or else the word *svaḥ* is a synonym of "all", the whole host of beings, and he is *svarvān* because all that exists arose from himself. Such as you are, those enjoyable riches (*bhujaḥ*) which you carried off (*ābharaḥ*) from the Asuras, the mighty demons, you brought after slaying them. Therefore, O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, by giving this wealth that you have brought, make prosper (*vardhaya*) your praiser alone, the one who makes hymns to you. And those other sacrificers who for you have strewn the sacred grass (*vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*), make them also prosper with wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—wealthy
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- स्वर्वान् (*svarvān*)—you who embrace all beings
- याः (*yāḥ*)—which
- भुजः (*bhujaḥ*)—riches that are the means of enjoyment
- असुरेभ्यः (*asurebhyaḥ*)—from the Asuras
- आभरः (*ābharaḥ*)—you have carried off and brought
- अस्य (*asya*)—by the gift of that same wealth
- स्तोतारं इत् (*stotāraṃ it*)—your praisers alone
- वर्धय (*vardhaya*)—make prosper
- यो (*yo*)—which
- अन्ये च (*anye ca*)—other sacrificers also
- त्वे (*tve*)—for you
- वृक्तबर्हिषः (*vṛktabarhiṣaḥ*)—who prepare the seats of darbha grass, make those also prosper

### Printed p. 457

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O wealthy Indra, you who embrace all beings, make your praisers prosper through the gift of that same wealth, the riches that are the means of enjoyment which you have carried off from the Asuras and brought. Be the cause of prosperity also to the other sacrificers who have prepared and made ready, for your worship, the seats of darbha grass.

##### English translation
Indra, lord of heaven, with those good things which you have carried off from the Asuras you prosper, O Maghavan, your praiser and those who have spread for you the clipped grass.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यमिं॑द्र दधि॒षे त्वमश्वं॒ गां भा॒गमव्य॑यम् ।  
> यज॑माने सुन्व॒ति दक्षि॑णावति॒ तस्मिं॒तं धे॑हि॒ मा प॒णौ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यम् । इंद्र । दधिषे । त्वम् । अश्वम् । गाम् । भागम् । अव्ययम् ।  
> यजमाने । सुन्वति । दक्षिणाऽवति । तस्मिन् । तम् । धेहि । मा । पणौ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं यम् अश्वं गमनसाधनान् हरीन् गाम् अग्निहोत्रकर्मणि पयःप्रदानेनोपकारिका गाः अव्ययं व्ययरहितमविनश्वरं भाग भजनीयं धनम्। सर्वत्रैकत्वमविवक्षितम् । एतान् शत्रुभ्य आहृत्य दधिषे बिभर्षि तं सर्वं सुन्वति सोमाभिषवं कुर्वति दक्षिणावति यज्ञ ऋत्विग्भ्यो दक्षिणादेयत्वेन तद्वति यजमाने यागं कुर्वाणे तस्मिन् त्वं धेहि। सर्वत्र धनादिदानं मा कुर्वित्याह। मा पणौ ।' पण व्यवहारे'। द्रव्यव्यवहारादयष्टा जनः पणिः । तस्मिन्नेतत् सर्वं मा देहि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the horse (*aśvam*) that you hold (*dadhiṣe*) means the steeds, the means of going; the cow (*gām*) means the cows that are helpful in the Agnihotra rite by giving milk; *avyayam* is the undiminishing, imperishable share (*bhāgam*), the wealth to be enjoyed. The singular is not meant to be specific throughout. Having taken all these from your enemies you hold them; all that you place in the sacrificer who presses Soma (*sunvati*) and is *dakṣiṇāvat*, one who has to give fees to the priests at the sacrifice, who performs the sacrifice. He says: do not give wealth and the rest everywhere. *Mā paṇau*: the root पण (*paṇa*) is used of trade; a man who does not sacrifice and is given to trading in goods is a *paṇi*. Do not give all this to him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which
- अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—horses
- गां (*gāṃ*)—and cows
- अव्ययं (*avyayaṃ*)—and imperishable
- भागं (*bhāgaṃ*)—and worshipful wealth
- दधिषे (*dadhiṣe*)—you have carried off from the Asuras and brought
- तं (*taṃ*)—all of that
- सुन्वति (*sunvati*)—to him who presses Soma and offers it

### Printed p. 458

- दक्षिणावति (*dakṣiṇāvati*)—and liberal in giving fees to the priests
- तस्मिन् यजमाने (*tasmin yajamāne*)—in that same sacrificer
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—deposit
- पणौ (*paṇau*)—to the niggard who has fallen away from the rites
- मा (*mā*)—do not give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, whatever horses, cows and imperishable, worshipful riches you have carried off from the Asuras, deposit all of them in that same sacrificer who presses Soma and offers it, and who is liberal in giving fees to the priests. Do not give to the niggard who has fallen away from the rites.

##### English translation
Those horses, those cows, that imperishable wealth which you have seized (from your enemies),—bestow them on the sacrificer who offers the Soma and is liberal to the priests,—not on the niggard.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> य इं॑द्र॒ सस्त्य॑व्र॒तो॑ऽनु॒ष्वाप॒मदे॑वयुः ।  
> स्वैः ष एवै॑र्मुमुर॒त्पोष्यं॑ र॒यिं स॑नु॒तर्धे॑हि॒ तं ततः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । इंद्र । सस्ति । अव्रतः । अनुऽस्वापम् । अदेवऽयुः ।  
> स्वैः । सः । एवैः । मुमुरत् । पोष्यम् । रयिम् । सनुतः । धेहि। तम् । ततः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अदेवयुः देवान् युष्मानकामयमानः अव्रतः व्रतरहितः कर्मरहितो भूत्वा अनुस्वापम् अनुवृत्तस्वप्नं यथा भवति तथा यः सस्ति स्वपिति । ‘षस स्वापे'। आदादिकः । सः जनः स्वैः आत्मीयैः एवैः गमनैरेव पोष्यं पोषणयं रयिं स्वीयं धनं मुमुरत् मारयतु विनाशयतु । अमार्गैर्द्यूतादिभिस्तस्य धनं नश्यतु न तु देवानां हविष्प्रदानेनेति । ततः त्वं तम् अयष्टारं जनम् । सनुतरित्यंतर्हितनाम । सनुतः अंतर्हिते कर्मरहिते कस्मिश्चिद्देशे धेहि स्थापय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the man who is *adevayuḥ*, who does not desire you, the gods, and is *avrataḥ*, without vows, without rites, and who sleeps (*sasti*) in such a way that his sleep goes on without a break (*anusvāpam*): let that man destroy (*mumurat*), cause to perish, by his own (*svaiḥ*) courses (*evaiḥ*, his goings) the wealth he has to nourish (*poṣyam*), his own riches. Let his wealth perish by improper ways such as gambling and the like, and not by giving oblations to the gods. Then (*tataḥ*) you place that man who does not sacrifice, *sanutaḥ*, which is a word for "hidden" (*antarhita*), in some hidden place devoid of rites.
**NOTE**

### Printed p. 459

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अदेवयुः (*adevayuḥ*)—one without interest in the worship of the gods
- अव्रतः (*avrataḥ*)—and without rites
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which unbeliever
- अनःस्वापं (*anaḥsvāpaṃ*)—always idle
- सस्ति (*sasti*)—lies sleeping, unaware of himself
- सः (*saḥ*)—he
- स्वैः (*svaiḥ*)—his own
- एव्यैः (*evyaiḥ*)—as the fruit of evil courses
- पोष्यं (*poṣyaṃ*)—that has to be nourished by him
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- मुमुरत् (*mumurat*)—let him lose
- ततः (*tataḥ*)—as the fruit of that falling away from rites
- तं (*taṃ*)—that unbeliever
- सनुतः (*sanutaḥ*)—in deep darkness
- धेहि (*dhehi*)—push

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, let the unbeliever who, without interest in the worship of the gods and without rites, lies always idle, sleeping unaware of himself, lose, as the fruit of his evil courses, all the wealth that has to be nourished by him. As the fruit of that falling away from rites, push that unbeliever into deep darkness.

##### English translation
Let him, Indra, who sleeps away careless of the gods and offering no sacrifices,—let him lose his precious wealth by his own evil courses, and then you stow him away in some hidden place.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यच्छ॒क्रासि॑ परा॒वति॒ यद॑र्वा॒वति॑ वृत्रहन् ।  
> अत॑स्त्वा गी॒र्भिर्द्यु॒गदिं॑द्र के॒शिभिः॑ सु॒तावाँ॒ आ वि॑वासति ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । शक्र । असि । पराऽवति । यत् । अर्वाऽवति । वृत्रऽहन् ।  
> अतः । त्वा । गीःऽभिः । द्युऽगत् । इंद्र । केशिऽभिः । सुतऽवान्। आ । विवासति ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शक्र शत्रुहननसमर्थेंद्र यत् यदा परावति विप्रकृष्टेऽतिदूरे द्युलोके देशे असि विद्यसे हे वृत्रहन् वृत्रस्य हंतरिंद्र यत् यदि अर्वावति अर्वाचीने तस्मादधस्तात्स्थिते तदपेक्षया समीपे देशेऽंतरिक्षे भवसि तस्मादपि अतः अस्माद्भूलोकाद्वा द्युगत् ।' गम्लृ गतौ'। क्विपि 'गमः क्वौ' इत्यनुनासिकलोपः । तुक् ।' सुपां सुलुक्' इति लुक् । द्युलोकं प्रति गच्छद्भिः स्वभासा सर्वतो गच्छद्भिः केशिभिः केशवद्भिर्हरिभिरिव स्थिताभिः गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिः वा त्वां सुतवान् अभिषुतसोमवान् यजमानः आ विवासति । आत्मीयं यज्ञं प्रत्यागमयति त्वामेतैः स्तोत्रैः परिचरतीति वा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śakra, Indra, able to slay enemies, whether (*yat*) you are in *parāvati*, a distant place, very far away, in the world of heaven; or, O Vṛtrahan, slayer of Vritra, if you are *arvāvati*, in a nearer place, lower than that, in the firmament; from there (*ataḥ*), or from this earth, the sacrificer who has pressed Soma (*sutavān*) *ā vivāsati*, brings you back to his sacrifice, or serves you, with these hymns (*gīrbhiḥ*) which are *dyugat*, going toward the world of heaven, going everywhere by their own radiance, and are *keśin*, set like horses with manes.
**NOTE**

### Printed p. 460

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शक्र (*śakra*)—able to slay enemies
- वृत्रहन् (*vṛtrahan*)—and the slayer of Vritra
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—if perchance
- परावति (*parāvati*)—in the very distant world of heaven
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- यत् (*yat*)—or if perchance
- अर्वावति (*arvāvati*)—in the firmament, a region lower than that
- अतः (*ataḥ*)—from there itself
- द्युगत् (*dyugat*)—going through the firmament
- केशिभिः (*keśibhiḥ*)—like horses with fine manes
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with words of praise
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- सुतवान् (*sutavān*)—the sacrificer
- आ विवासति (*ā vivāsati*)—worships

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, able to slay enemies and slayer of Vritra, even if you are in the very distant world of heaven, or if you are in the firmament, a region lower than that, from there itself the sacrificer worships you with words of praise that go through the firmament and are like horses with fine manes.

##### English translation
Whether, Shakra, you are in the far-distant region, or whether, slayer of Vritra, you are in the lower,—the sacrificer longs to bring you, Indra, from thence by his hymns as by heaven-going steeds ;

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यद्वासि॑ रोच॒ने दि॒वः स॑मु॒द्रस्याधि॑ वि॒ष्टपि॑ ।  
> यत्पार्थि॑वे॒ सद॑ने वृत्रहंतम॒ यदं॒तरि॑क्ष॒ आ ग॑हि ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । वा। सि । रोचने । दिवः । समुद्रस्य । अधि । विष्टपि ।  
> यत् । पार्थिवे । सदने । वृत्रहन्ऽतम । यत् । अंतरिक्षे । आ । गहि ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 461

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र यद्वा यदि वा दिवः द्युलोकस्य रोचने दीपनशीले स्थाने भवसि । यद्वा समुद्रस्य मध्ये अधि अधिगते विष्टपि विष्टपे तत्संबद्धे कस्मिंश्चित् स्थाने भवसि । हे वृत्रहंतम अतिशयेन वृत्रस्यासुरस्य पापस्य वा हंतरिंद्र यत् यदि वा पार्थिवे पृथिव्यां भवे सदने स्थाने विद्यसे । यदि वा अंतरिक्षे तस्मिँल्लोके वर्तसे । यत्रकुत्र भवसि तथाप्यस्मदीयं यज्ञं प्रति आ गहि आगच्छ ॥ ॥ ३६ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, if you are in the *rocana* of heaven, the shining place of the world of heaven; or else if you are *adhi*, over, in the middle of the sea, at *viṣṭapi*, in some place connected with it. O Vṛtrahantama, Indra, in the highest degree the slayer of Vritra, the asura, or of sin; if you are known in an earthly abode, a place on the earth; or if you dwell in the firmament, in that world: wherever you may be, come (*ā gahi*) to our sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृत्रहंतम (*vṛtrahaṃtama*)—O Indra, who slay Vritra with great ease
- यद्वा (*yadvā*)—if perchance
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the world of heaven
- रोचने असि (*rocane asi*)—you are in the shining place, or
- समुद्रस्य अधि (*samudrasya adhi*)—in the middle of the sea
- विष्टपि (*viṣṭapi*)—in a region
- यत् (*yat*)—or if perchance
- पार्थिवे (*pārthive*)—connected with the earth
- सदने (*sadane*)—in some house of sacrifice
- अंतरिक्षे (*aṃtarikṣe*)—or in the region of the firmament, from there everywhere
- आ गहि (*ā gahi*)—be gracious and come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who slay Vritra with great ease, whether you are in the shining place of the world of heaven, or in a region in the middle of the sea, or in some house of sacrifice connected with the earth, or in the region of the firmament, from everywhere there be gracious and come.

##### English translation
Or whether you are in the bringhtness of heaven, or whether in some region in the midst of the sea, or whether, mightiest slayer of Vritra, in some abode in the earth, or whether in the firmament,—come to us.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स नः॒ सोमे॑षु सोमपाः सु॒तेषु॑ शवसस्पते ।  
> मा॒दय॑स्व॒ राध॑सा सू॒नृता॑व॒तेंद्र॑ रा॒या परी॑णसा ॥ ६ ॥

> मादयस्व । राधसा । सुनृताऽवता । इंद्र। राया। परीणसा ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 462

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोमपाः सोमस्य पातः हे शवसस्पते बलस्य पालयितः इंद्र सः पूर्वोक्तलक्षणस्त्वं सुतेषु अस्माभिरभिषुतेषु सोमेषु नः अस्मान् राधसा बलसाधनेनान्नेन सूनृतावता अनृतरहितत्वोपेतेन । यद्वा । सूनृतेति वाङ्नाम । शोभनवाक्ययुक्तेन । अनेन पुत्रादिकं लक्ष्यते । पुत्रोपेतेनान्नेन । परीणसा । बहुनामैतत् । बहुना राया धनेन च नोऽस्मान् मादयस्व मोदय । सोमस्य प्रदातृभ्योऽस्मभ्यमन्नपुत्रधनादिकं देहीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O *somapāḥ*, drinker of Soma, O *śavasaspati*, protector of strength, Indra, you of the character stated before: now that Soma has been pressed (*suteṣu*) by us, gladden (*mādayasva*) us with *rādhas*, food that is a means of strength, which is *sūnṛtāvat*, free from untruth; or else *sūnṛtā* is a name of speech, so: possessed of good speech; by this sons and the like are indicated, so: food together with sons. And with *parīṇas*, which is a word for "much": with much wealth (*rāyā*). The meaning is: give us, the givers of Soma, food, sons, wealth and the rest.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोमपाः (*somapāḥ*)—O drinker of Soma
- शवसस्पते (*śavasaspate*)—and protector of strength
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सः (*saḥ*)—you, the well-known
- सुतेषु (*suteṣu*)—pressed by us
- सोमेषु (*someṣu*)—now that the Soma juices are ready for you
- सः (*saḥ*)—us
- राधसा (*rādhasā*)—with food that brings strength
- सूनृतावता (*sūnṛtāvatā*)—with excellent encouraging words
- परीणसा (*parīṇasā*)—and with abundant
- रायू (*rāyū*)—gift of wealth
- मूदयस्व (*mūdayasva*)—satisfy us
**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, drinker of Soma and protector of strength, you the well-known, now that the Soma juices pressed by us are ready to be offered to you, satisfy us with food that brings strength, and with a gift of wealth that has excellent encouraging words and is abundant.

##### English translation
Indra, drinker of the Soma, lord of strength, now that our Soma-libations have been effused, gladden us with wholesome food and ample wealth.

> त्वम् । नः । ऊती । त्वम् । इत् । नः । आप्यम् । मा। नः । इंद्र। परा। वृणक् ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 463

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र नः हविषां प्रदातॄनस्मान् मा परा वृणक् मा परित्याक्षीः । 'वृजी वर्जने'। रौधादिकः । लङि रूपम् । तदेवाह । त्वं नः अस्माकं सोमेन सधमाद्यः सधमादनशीलः भव। किंच हे इंद्र नः अस्मान् त्वम् एव ऊती ऊत्यां स्थापथ । यद्वा । ऊती। व्यत्ययेन कर्तरि क्तिचि वा निपातितः । त्वमेवास्माकं रक्षिता खलु । तथा त्वमित् । इदवधारणे । त्वमेव अस्माकम् आप्यं ज्ञातेयम् । त्वमेव बंधुरित्यर्थः । अत एव मा न इंद्र परा वृणक् इत्येष गतार्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, do not abandon (*parā vṛṇak*), do not forsake us, the givers of oblations. Then he says: be *sadhamādyaḥ*, one who rejoices together with us over the Soma. Further, O Indra, you alone place us in *ūtī*, in protection; or else *ūtī* is formed irregularly as an agent word, by the affix *ktic*: you alone are our protector. Likewise *tvam it*, *it* being a word of emphasis: you alone are our *āpya*, our kinsman; the meaning is that you alone are our friend. Therefore the phrase "do not abandon us, Indra" is explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—us, the sacrificers
- मा परा वृणक् (*mā parā vṛṇak*)—do not forsake
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- सधमाद्यः (*sadhamādyaḥ*)—sharing our joys together with us
- भव (*bhava*)—be
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- ऊती (*ūtī*)—keep together with protection
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वमित् (*tvamit*)—you alone
- आप्यं (*āpyaṃ*)—are a kinsman to me
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- मा परा वृणक् (*mā parā vṛṇak*)—do not by any means forsake

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, do not forsake us, the sacrificers. Together with us, share our joys. Keep us together with your protection. O Indra, you alone are a kinsman to us. Do not by any means forsake us.

##### English translation
Leave us not, Indra, but share our joy ; you are our protection, you are our kindred ; Indra, leave us not.

### Printed p. 464

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अस्मे अस्माभिः.सचा सह सुते अभिषुते सोमे नि षद अस्मदीये यज्ञे निषीद । किमर्थम् । मधु पीतये मधुनः । ‘सुपां सुलुक्' इति ङसो लुक् । मदकरस्य सोमस्य पीतये पानाय । किंच हे मघवन् धनवन् इंद्र महत् अवः रक्षणं जरित्रे कृधि कुरु। कस्मिन् सति । अस्मे इंद्र सचा सुते इति व्याख्यातः पादः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, sit down (*ni ṣada*) at our sacrifice, together with us (*asme*), when the Soma has been pressed (*sute*). For what purpose? *Madhu pītaye*: to drink the intoxicating Soma, the sweet one. Further, O Maghavan, wealthy Indra, make (*kṛdhi*) great protection (*avaḥ*) for the praiser (*jaritre*). When is this? When Soma has been pressed together with us (*asme indra sacā sute*): thus the quarter has been explained.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अस्मे (*asme*)—with us
- सचा (*sacā*)—together
- सुते (*sute*)—when the pressed Soma is ready
- मधु (*madhu*)—the sweet Soma
- पीतये (*pītaye*)—to drink
- नि षद (*ni ṣada*)—sit down in our place of sacrifice
- मघवन् (*maghavan*)—wealthy
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सुते (*sute*)—when the Soma is pressed and ready
- अस्मे सचा (*asme sacā*)—together with us
- जरित्रे (*jaritre*)—for the praiser
- महत् (*mahat*)—abundant
- अवः (*avaḥ*)—protection
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—bring about

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when the pressed Soma is ready, sit down together with us in our place of sacrifice to drink the sweet Soma. O wealthy Indra, when the Soma is pressed and ready, bring about abundant protection for the praiser, together with us.

##### English translation
Sit with us, Indra, at the oblation to drink the Soma ; Maghavan, perform a mighty protection for your worshipper, (seated) with us at the oblation.

> विश्वा॑ जा॒तानि॒ शव॑साभि॒भूर॑सि॒ न त्वा॑ दे॒वास॑ आशत ॥ ९ ॥

> विश्वा । जातानि । शवसा । अभिऽभूः । असि । न । त्वा । देवासः । आशत ॥ ९ ॥

### Printed p. 465

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अद्रिवः वज्रवन्निंद्र त्वा त्वां देवासः त्वदन्ये सर्वे देवाः न आशत । स्वकर्मणा स्वबलेन वा न व्याप्नुवंति । न मर्त्यासः मर्त्या मनुष्याश्च न व्याप्नुवंति । कुत एतदवसीयते तदाह । विश्वा विश्वानि सर्वाणि जातानि भूतजातानि शवसा स्वबलेनैव अभिभूरसि । अभिभावुकोऽसि भवसि । तस्मात् न त्वा देवास आशत इति गतार्थः ॥
> चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः ‘विश्वाः पृतनाः' इति वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रियः । सूत्रितं च--- विश्वाः पृतना अभिभूतरं नरं तमिंद्रं जोहवीमि' (आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ४) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O *adrivaḥ*, Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, the gods (*devāsaḥ*), all the gods other than you, do not attain (*na āśata*) you, do not reach you by their own act or their own strength; nor do mortals, men, reach you. From what is this concluded? He says: you overcome (*abhibhūḥ asi*) all (*viśvā*) beings (*jātāni*) by your strength (*śavasā*), by your own might. Therefore "the gods do not attain you" is explained. Further: on the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, विश्वाः पृतनाः (*viśvāḥ pṛtanāḥ*) is the alternative Stotriya of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin; and it is taught: विश्वाः पृतना अभिभूतरं नरं तमिंद्रं जोहवीमि (*viśvāḥ pṛtanā abhibhūtaraṃ naraṃ tamiṃdraṃ johavīmi*) (Āśva. Śrau. 7. 4).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—none of the gods
- न आशत (*na āśata*)—can surpass
- न मर्त्यासः (*na martyāsaḥ*)—none among men can be greater than you
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- जातानि (*jātāni*)—created things
- शवसा (*śavasā*)—by your own strength
- अभिभूः असि (*abhibhūḥ asi*)—you alone surpass and are greater than all
- देवासः (*devāsaḥ*)—none among the gods
- त्वा (*tvā*)—than you
- न आशत (*na āśata*)—can be greater

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, neither among the gods nor among men is there anyone equal to you or possessed of strength surpassing yours. You alone, by your own strength, stand surpassing all created beings.

##### English translation
Thunderer, neither gods nor mortals equal you by their acts; you surpass all beings by your might, the gods equal you not.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> विश्वाः॒ पृत॑ना अभि॒भूत॑रं॒ नरं॑ स॒जूस्त॑तक्षु॒रिंद्रं॑ जज॒नुश्च॑ रा॒जसे॑ ।  
> क्रत्वा॒ वरि॑ष्ठं॒ वर॑ आ॒मुरि॑मु॒तोग्रमोजि॑ष्ठं त॒वसं॑ तर॒स्विन॑म् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विश्वा: । पृतनाः । अभिऽभूतरम् । नरम् । सऽजूः । ततक्षुः । इंद्रम् । जजनुः । च । राजसे।  
> क्रत्वा । वरिष्ठम् । वरे । आऽमुरिम् । उत । उग्रम् । ओजिष्ठम्। तवसम्। तरस्विनम् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

### Printed p. 466

> विश्वाः सर्वा व्याप्ता वा पृतनाः । 'पृङ् व्यायामे'। व्याप्रियंत इति पृतनाः सेनाः । सजू परस्परं संगताः सत्यः अभिभूतरं शत्रूणामत्यर्थमभिभवितारं नरं सर्वस्य नेतारम् इंद्रं ततक्षुः । आयुधादिभिस्तीक्ष्णीकुर्वंति । आयुधवंतमश्ववंतं च चक्रुरित्यर्थः । यद्वा पृतना इति संग्रामनाम । व्याप्रियंतेऽत्रेति पृतनाः संग्रामाः । सर्वानेव संग्रामानभिभावुकमिंद्रं स्तोतारोऽन्योन्यं संगताः स्तुतिभिस्तीक्ष्णमकुर्वन् । स्तुते सति बलवान् भवतीति । यद्वा । यष्टारो हविष्प्रदानेन वीर्यवंतं कुर्वंतीति । किंच स्तोतारः राजसे । राजतेस्तुमर्थेऽसेप्रत्ययः । आत्मनो विराजनार्थं प्रकाशनार्थं सूर्यात्मानम् इंद्रं जजनुः जनयामासुः । स्तोत्रं यज्ञे प्रादुरभावयन्नित्यर्थः । उत अपि च क्रत्वा स्वीयवृत्रवधादिकर्मणैव वरिष्ठम् उरुतरम् आमुरिं शत्रूणामाभिमुख्येन मारयितारमिंद्रं वरे वरणीये धने स्तोतारश्चक्रुः । आत्मनां धनलाभार्थं स्तुवंतीत्यर्थः । कीदृशम् । उग्रम् उद्गूर्णबलमत एव ओजिष्ठम् ओजस्वितमं तवसं प्रवृद्धं तरस्विनं संग्रामे शत्रुवधार्थं वेगवंतमिंद्रं धनार्थं स्तुवंति ॥ ॥ ३७ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

*Viśvāḥ*, all, *pṛtanāḥ*, armies, so called because they are engaged in action (from the root पृङ् (*pṛṅ*), "to be engaged"); assembled together (*sajūḥ*), they sharpen (*tatakṣuḥ*) Indra, *abhibhūtara*, who greatly overcomes enemies, *nara*, the leader of all, with weapons and the like; the meaning is that they made him possessed of weapons and horses. Or else, *pṛtanā* is a name for battle, because men are engaged in it: the praisers, assembled together, sharpened with their hymns Indra, who overcomes all battles; for when praised he becomes strong. Or else, the sacrificers make him vigorous by giving oblations. Further, the praisers *jajanuḥ*, brought forth Indra, whose nature is the sun, *rājase*, to shine (that is, to make himself manifest); the meaning is that they made the hymn appear at the sacrifice. Moreover, *kratvā*, by his own deeds such as the slaying of Vritra, they made Indra *variṣṭha*, the widest, *āmuri*, the one who slays enemies by facing them, *vare*, for desirable wealth; the meaning is that the praisers praise him to gain wealth for themselves. Of what kind is he? *Ugra*, of uplifted strength, and therefore *ojiṣṭha*, most vigorous, *tavasa*, grown great, *tarasvin*, swift in battle for the slaying of enemies: such an Indra they praise for wealth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राजसे (*rājase*)—for his own shining
- जजनुः (*jajanuḥ*)—they have caused him to become manifest

**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

All the priests and the rest, gathered together, made Indra, who defeats enemies and is the leader, vigorous by giving oblations and the like. For his own shining they have caused him to become manifest. By their excellent rites, the most excellent one, who confronts the enemies and

### Printed p. 467

destroys them, who has exceeding vigour, who is mighty and swift, Indra, they have made an excellent object of praise.

##### English translation
The assembled (priests) have roused Indra, the leader, the conqueror in all battles ; they have created him ( by their hymns ) to shine,—him the mightiest in his acts, the smiter of enemies for spoil, the terrible, the most powerful, the stalwart, the furious.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the time of the midday pressing, the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite the three verses beginning with विश्वाः पृतनाः (*viśvāḥ pṛtanāḥ*) as the alternative Stotriya tṛca; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, विश्वाः पृतना अभिभूतरं नरं तमिंद्रं जोहुवीमि (*viśvāḥ pṛtanā abhibhūtaraṃ naraṃ tamiṃdraṃ johuvīmi*) (Ā. 7-4).

#### Ṛk 11

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> समीं॑ रे॒भासो॑ अस्वर॒न्निंद्रं॒ सोम॑स्य पी॒तये॑ ।  
> स्व॑र्पतिं॒ यदीं॑ वृ॒धे धृ॒तव्र॑तो॒ ह्योज॑सा॒ समू॒तिभिः॑ ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सम् । ईम् । रेभासः । अस्वरन् । इंद्रम् । सोमस्य । पीतये ।  
> स्वःऽपतिम् । यत् । ईम् । वृधे । धृतऽव्रतः । हि । ओजसा । सम् । ऊतिऽभिः ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> रेभासः । ‘रेभृ शब्दे' । शब्दयितारः स्तोतारः । यद्वा । रेभासः कश्यपपुत्रा रेभा एतन्नामका ऋषयः । ईम् एनम् इंद्रं सम् अस्वरन् सम्यगशब्दयन् समस्तुवन् । किमर्थम् । सोमस्य पीतये सोमपानाय । किंच स्वर्पतिं स्वर्गस्य पालयितारं धनस्य स्वामिनं वा ईम् एनमिंद्रं यत् यदा वृधे हविर्भिर्वर्धनाय संस्तुवंति तदा धृतव्रतः धृतकर्मेंद्रः ओजसा बलेन स्तोतृभिः ऊतिभिः मरुद्भिः पालनैश्च सह संगच्छते। स्तुतिभिर्बलं मरुद्भिः पालनं चेंद्रस्य भवतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

*Rebhāsaḥ* (from the root रेभृ (*rebhṛ*), "to sound") are the praisers who raise their voices; or else, *rebhāsaḥ* are the seers named Rebha, sons of Kaśyapa. They together (*sam asvaran*) praised this (*īm*) Indra. For what purpose? *Somasya pītaye*, to drink Soma. Further, when they praise this Indra, *svarpati*, the protector of heaven or the lord of wealth, for his growth (*vṛdhe*) with oblations, then Indra, *dhṛtavrata*, who upholds rites, with his strength (*ojasā*), given by the praisers, and with protections (*ūtibhiḥ*), that is, the Maruts, is united. The meaning is that Indra gets strength by praises and protection by the Maruts.

- पीतये (*pītaye*)—for the drinking

- वृधे (*vṛdhe*)—they praise for his growth, then

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The praisers (or the seers called Rebha) gathered together and praised this Indra for the drinking of the Soma juice. When they praise this Indra, the protector of heaven, for his growth, then Indra, who upholds his rules, is united with his strength and with the protecting Maruts.
**NOTE**

##### English translation
The Rebhas have together praised Indra that he may drink the Soma ; when (they praise) the lord of heaven that he may wax strong (by the oblations), then he, observant of pious rites, is united to his strength and his protecting guards.

#### Ṛk 12

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ने॒मिं न॑मंति॒ चक्ष॑सा मे॒षं विप्रा॑ अभि॒स्वरा॑ ।  
> सु॒दी॒तयो॑ वो अ॒द्रुहोऽपि॒ कर्णे॑ तर॒स्विनः॒ समृक्व॑भिः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नेमिम् । नमंति । चक्षसा । मेषम् । विप्राः । अभिऽस्वरा ।  
> सुऽदीतयः । वः । अद्रुहः । अपि । कर्णे। तरस्विनः । सम् । ऋक्वऽभिः ॥ १२ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नेमिम् । अरान् यथा नेमिर्व्याप्नोति तद्वत् सर्वं व्याप्नुते । तादृशं नमनशीलमिंद्रं चक्षसा दर्शनमात्रेणैव नमंति। काश्यप रेभाः स्तोतारो वा नमस्कुर्वंति । ततः विप्राः मेधाविनः मेषम् । इंद्रो मेषो भूत्वा मेधातिथिं स्वर्गमनयत् । तस्मात् मेधातिथेर्मेषभूतमिंद्रम् अभिस्वरा अभिस्वरणेन स्तोत्रेण प्रणमंति। इदानीं यजमानः स्तोतॄनाह । अपि च सुदीतयः शोभनदीप्तयः अद्रुहः कस्याप्यद्रोग्धारः वः यूयम्। छंदसो वसादेशः । तरस्विनः कर्मसु स्तोत्रेषु वा त्वरायुक्ताः संत इंद्रस्य कर्णे श्रोत्रसमीपे ऋक्वभिः अर्चनायुक्तैर्मंत्रैः। यद्वा । ऋचो बह्व्यो येषु संति तैः शस्त्रादिभिः । संस्तुत । इंद्रो यथा युष्मदीयानि स्तोत्रशस्त्रादीनि शृणोति तथा सम्यगभिष्टुतेत्यर्थः ॥
> पूर्वोक्त एव शस्त्रे वैकल्पिकस्यानुरूपतृचस्य  'तमिंद्रम्' इत्याद्या । सूत्रमुदाहृतम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

*Nemim*: as the felly encloses the spokes, so Indra pervades everything; such an Indra, ever bowing, they bow to *cakṣasā*, at the mere sight of him: the Rebhas of Kaśyapa's line, or the praisers, do homage. Then the *viprāḥ*, the wise, bow *meṣam*: Indra became a ram and led Medhātithi to heaven; therefore they bow with *abhisvara*, a hymn of praise, to Indra, who became the ram of Medhātithi. Now the sacrificer addresses the praisers: and you, *sudītayaḥ*, of fair radiance, *adruhaḥ*, harming no one, *tarasvinaḥ*, hasty in rites or in hymns, in Indra's ear (*karṇe*), with *ṛkvabhiḥ*, mantras accompanied by worship; or else with the śastras and the like in which there are many Ṛks: praise well (*saṃstuta*), so that Indra hears your hymns and śastras. Further: in the same śastra stated before, तमिंद्रम् (*tamiṃdram*) is the first verse of the alternative Anurūpa tṛca; the sūtra has been quoted.

- चक्षसा (*cakṣasā*)—at the mere sight

- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—the wise praisers
- मेषं (*meṣaṃ*)—Indra in the form of a ram
- अभिस्वरा (*abhisvarā*)—bow with praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The praisers bow, at the mere sight, to Indra, who encloses all beings as the rim of a wheel encloses the spokes. They bow with praise to Indra in the form of a ram. O praisers, of excellent radiance and free from malice, being skilled in rites, praise Indra near his ear with worshipful mantras.

##### English translation
At the first sight (the Rebhas) bow to him who is the circumference of the wheel, the priests (worship) with their praise (Indra) the ram ; radiant and unharming, you also, full of earnestness, sing in his ear with your hymns.

#### Ṛk 13

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तमिंद्रं॑ जोहवीमि म॒घवा॑नमु॒ग्रं स॒त्रा दधा॑न॒मप्र॑तिष्कुतं॒ शवां॑सि ।  
> मंहि॑ष्ठो गी॒र्भिरा च॑ य॒ज्ञियो॑ व॒वर्त॑द्रा॒ये नो॒ विश्वा॑ सु॒पथा॑ कृणोतु व॒ज्री ॥ १३ ॥

### Printed p. 470

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तम् । इंद्रम् । जोहवीमि । मघऽवानम् । उग्रम् । सत्रा । दधानम् । अप्रतिऽस्कुतम् । शवांसि ।  
> मंहिष्ठः । गी:ऽभिः । आ। च । यज्ञियः । ववर्तत् । राये । नः । विश्वा । सुऽपथा । कृणोतु । वज्री ॥ १३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तं पूर्वोक्तगुणोपेतम् इंद्रं जोहवीमि । यष्टाहं पुनःपुनराह्वयामि । ह्वयतेः  अभ्यस्तस्य च इति संप्रसारणम् । कीदृशम् । मघवानं मंहनीयधनवंतम् उग्रम् उद्गूर्णबलं सत्रा सत्यं यथार्थमेव शवांसि बलानि दधानम् अत एव अप्रतिष्कुतं शत्रुभिरप्रतिरोधनीयमाह्वयामि । किंच मंहिष्ठः पूज्यतमो दातृतमो वा यज्ञियः यज्ञार्ह इंद्रः गीर्भिः अस्मदीयाभिः स्तुतिभिः आ ववर्तत् च यज्ञेष्वाभिमुख्येन वर्ततां च । वर्ततेर्ण्यंतस्य चङि रूपम्। 'चवायोगे प्रथमा' इति न निघातः । ‘चङयन्यतरस्याम्' इति स्वरः । ततः वज्री वज्रवानिंद्रः नः अस्माकं राये धनाय विश्वा विश्वानि सर्वाण्येव सुपथा सुमार्गाणि कृणोतु च करोतु । धनं सर्वदिक्स्थमस्मान् प्राप्नोत्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa explains: I, the sacrificer, call again and again (जोहवीमि (*johavīmi*)) that Indra who has the qualities stated before. What kind of Indra? मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*): possessed of praiseworthy wealth; उग्रम् (*ugram*): of surging strength; he who truly, in very fact, bears powers (शवांसि (*śavāṃsi*)), and therefore is not to be resisted by enemies (अप्रतिष्कुतं (*apratiṣkutaṃ*)). Further, मंहिष्ठः (*maṃhiṣṭhaḥ*) means the most worshipful or the most bountiful; Indra, who is worthy of sacrifice (यज्ञियः (*yajñiyaḥ*)), may turn towards us (आ ववर्तत् (*ā vavartat*)) at the sacrifices, drawn by our praises. Then may the thunderer (वज्री (*vajrī*)) Indra make all paths good (सुपथा (*supathā*)) for our wealth (राये (*rāye*)); that is, may wealth lying in every direction reach us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*)—the wealthy one
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—the one of exceeding strength
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—real, truthful
- शवांसि (*śavāṃsi*)—powers
- दधानं (*dadhānaṃ*)—the one who possesses
- अप्रतिष्कुतं (*apratiṣkutaṃ*)—the unstruck one
- तं इंद्रं (*taṃ iṃdraṃ*)—that Indra himself
- जोहवीमि (*johavīmi*)—I pray and call again and again
- मंहिष्ठः (*maṃhiṣṭhaḥ*)—the most worshipful
- यज्ञियः (*yajñiyaḥ*)—Indra, who is worthy of sacrifice
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—pleased by praises
- आ ववर्तत् च (*ā vavartat ca*)—may he come towards the sacrifice
- वज्री (*vajrī*)—Indra, the bearer of the thunderbolt
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- राये (*rāye*)—for the gaining of wealth
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- सुपथा (*supathā*)—good paths
- कृणोतु (*kṛṇotu*)—may he make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I again and again pray and call that Indra, who is wealthy, of exceeding strength, who possesses real powers, and who is unstruck. May Indra, the most worshipful and worthy of sacrifice, pleased by praises, come towards the sacrifice. May Indra, the bearer of the thunderbolt, make all good paths for us for the gaining of wealth.

### Printed p. 471

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Among the Śastra mantras that have been mentioned (the 10th Ṛk of this sūkta), when the optional anurūpa tṛca is recited, this Ṛk beginning तमिंद्रं (*tamiṃdraṃ*) is to be recited as the first Ṛk of the tṛca; this has been exemplified in the sūtra mentioned before.

##### English translation
Again and again I invoke the strong Indra, Maghavan, who alone really possess might, the irresistible ; may he draw nigh through our songs most bounteous and worthy of sacrifice ; may he, the thunderer, make all things prosperous for our wealth.

#### Ṛk 14

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं पुर॑ इंद्र चि॒किदे॑ना॒ व्योज॑सा शविष्ठ शक्र नाश॒यध्यै॑ ।  
> त्वद्विश्वा॑नि॒ भुव॑नानि वज्रिं॒द्यावा॑ रेजेते पृथि॒वी च॑ भी॒षा ॥ १४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वम् । पुरः । इंद्र । चिकित् । एनाः । वि । ओजसा । शविष्ठ । शक्र । नाशयध्यै ।  
> त्वत् । विश्वानि । भुवनानि । वज्रिन् । द्यावा । रेजेते इति । पृथिवी इति । च । भीषा ॥१४॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शविष्ठ बलवत्तम अत एव हे शक्र शत्रुहननसमर्थ हे इंद्र त्वम् एनाः । अन्वादेशे । एतानि पुरः शंबरस्य पुराणि ओजसा स्वीयेनैव तेजसा वि नाशयध्य विनाशयितुं चिकित् ज्ञाता भवसि । नशेर्ण्यंताच्छध्यैप्रत्ययः । पुनरपि सामर्थ्यं प्रशंसति । हे वज्रिन् वज्रवन्निंद्र विश्वानि सर्वाणि भुवनानि भूतजातानि त्वत् त्वत्तो भीत्या कंपंते । तथा द्यावापृथिवी । 'दिवो द्यावा' इति द्यावादेशः । आद्युदात्तश्च । पृथिवी ङीषंतत्वेनांतोदात्तः । 'देवताद्वंद्वे च' इत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । विप्रकर्षस्तु छांदसः । द्यावापृथिवी च भीषा त्वत्तो भीत्या रेजेते कंपेते । ' अरेजेतां रोदसी' (ऋ. सं. १. ३१. ३ ) इति निगमः । सर्वे त्वदधीना इत्यर्थः ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śaviṣṭha, most mighty, and therefore O Śakra, able to slay enemies, O Indra: you are known (चिकित् (*cikit*)) to be able to destroy by your own splendour (ओजसा (*ojasā*)) these (एनाः (*enāḥ*), an anvādeśa form) cities (पुरः (*puraḥ*)) of Śambara. Again he praises Indra's power: O thunderer (वज्रिन् (*vajrin*)), all beings (भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*)) tremble from fear of you; likewise heaven and earth (द्यावापृथिवी (*dyāvāpṛthivī*)) tremble (रेजेते (*rejete*)) with fear (भीषा (*bhīṣā*)) of you. The Nigama is अरेजेतां रोदसी (*arejetāṃ rodasī*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1. 31. 3). The meaning is that all depend on you.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, of exceedingly great strength and destroyer of enemies, you know the means to destroy by your strength the well-known cities of Śambara. O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, all beings tremble for you. Heaven and earth also tremble from fear of you alone.

##### English translation
Indra, mighty Sakra, you know how to destroy those cities (of (Sambhara) by your strength at you all worlds tremble, thunderer,—heaven and earth (tremble) with fear.

#### Ṛk 15

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तन्म॑ ऋ॒तमिं॑द्र शूर चित्र पात्व॒पो न व॑ज्रिंदुरि॒ताति॑ पर्षि॒ भूरि॑ ।  
> क॒दा न॑ इंद्र रा॒य आ द॑शस्येर्वि॒श्वप्स्न्य॑स्य स्पृह॒याय्य॑स्य राजन् ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत् । मा । ऋतम् । इंद्र। शूर । चित्र । पातु। अपः । न । वज्रिन्। दुःऽइता । अति । पर्षि भूरि ।  
> कदा । नः । इंद्र। रायः । । दशस्येः । विश्वऽप्स्न्यस्य । स्पृहयाय्यस्य । राजन् ॥ १५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शूर बलवन् चित्र चायनीय विविधरूप वा। ‘इंद्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते' (ऋ. सं. ६. ४७. १८) इत्यादिषु दृष्टत्वात् । बहुविधरूप हे इंद्र तत् प्रशस्तं त्वदीयम् ऋतं सत्यं मा मां पातु सर्वतो रक्षतु । किंच हे वज्रिन् वज्रवन्निंद्र भूरि । सुपो लुक् । भूरीणि बहूनि दुरिता दुरितानि पापानि अति पर्षि अतीत्य पारय । तत्र दृष्टांतः । अपो न यथा नाविक उदकानि मनुष्यान् पारयति तद्वदस्मान् पापानि पारय । हे राजन् दीप्यमान हे इंद्र विश्वप्स्न्यस्य । प्स इति रूपनाम । रूपे साधु प्स्यम् । नकारोपजनश्छांदसः । बहुरूपं तत् स्पृहयाय्यस्य सर्वैः स्पृहणीयं रायः । 'क्रियाग्रहणम्' इति संप्रदानसंज्ञा । ‘चतुर्थ्यर्थे बहुलम्' इति षष्ठी । तद्धनं नः अस्मभ्यम् आ आभिमुख्येन कदा दशस्येः कस्मिन् काले प्रयच्छेः । तदा तव स्वभूतं सत्यं मा रक्षतु । मह्यं धनं दत्वा कर्माणि च मयानुष्ठाप्य मां पापरहितं कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥ ॥ ३८ ॥
> वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् ।
> पुमर्थांश्चतुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥
> इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराजपरमेश्वरवैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तकश्रीवीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये षष्ठाष्टके षष्ठोऽध्यायः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O hero, O mighty one, O Citra: this means worthy of being perceived, or of many forms, because he is seen as such in passages like इंद्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते (*iṃdro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6. 47. 18). O Indra of many forms, may that excellent truth of yours (ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)) protect me (पातु (*pātu*)) on every side. Further, O thunderer, carry us across (अति पर्षि (*ati parṣi*)) our many sins (दुरिता (*duritā*)). The illustration is अपो न (*apo na*): as a boatman takes men across the waters, so take us across our sins. O shining king Indra: प्स (*psa*) is a word for form; what is good in form is प्स्यम् (*psyam*); the wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)) here is of many forms and desirable to all (स्पृहयाय्यस्य (*spṛhayāyyasya*)). When will you give (दशस्येः (*daśasyeḥ*)) that wealth to us, directly before us? At that time may your truth protect me. The meaning is: having given me wealth and having had rites performed by me, make me free from sin.

Then follows a closing verse and the colophon: dispelling the darkness of the heart by the light of the meaning of the Veda, may Vidyātīrtha Maheśvara grant the four aims of man; thus ends the sixth chapter of the sixth Aṣṭaka in the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā commentary, the Vedārthaprakāśa of the Mādhavīya, composed by Sāyaṇācārya, who bore the burden of the empire of the illustrious king Vīra Bukka, founder of the Vedic path.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O valiant Indra, of attractive form, may your praiseworthy true nature protect me. O Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, as a boatman takes men across the waters and brings them to the shore, take us across our exceedingly many sins and bring us to the shore. O shining Indra, when will you send towards us the wealth that is of many forms and very attractive?

##### English translation
Indra, hero assuming many forms, may that truthfulness of yours protect me ; bear us, thunderer, over our many sins as over waters ; when, radiant Indra, will you give us some wealth, desirable to all, manifold in its kinds ?

Dispelling the darkness of the heart by the light of the meaning of the Veda, may Vidyātīrtha Maheśvara grant the four aims of man. Thus ends the sixth chapter of the sixth Aṣṭaka in the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā commentary, the Vedārthaprakāśa of the Mādhavīya, composed by Sāyaṇācārya, bearer of the burden of the empire of the illustrious king Vīra Bukka.

Om, that is the truth. Here, in the sixth Aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, which has Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya and a Kannada translation, the sixth chapter is concluded.

॥ श्री ॥ (*‖ śrī ‖*)

॥ श्री महागणाधिपतये नमः ॥ (*‖ śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ ‖*)

वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*)

यस्य निश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*yasya niśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*)

## Sūkta 98 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ॥ श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
> यस्य निःश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् ।
> निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरम् ॥
> अथ षष्ठस्य सप्तमोऽध्याय आरभ्यते । तत्र ' इंद्राय ' इति द्वादशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तमांगिरसस्य नृमेधाख्यस्यार्षमैंद्रम् । सप्तमी दशम्येकादश्यौ च तिस्रः ककुभो मध्यमपादस्य द्वादशाक्षरत्वात् ।  ‘ मध्यमश्चेत्ककुप् ' ( अनु. ५. ३ ) इति हि तल्लक्षणम् । नवमीद्वादश्यौ पुरउष्णिहौ। प्रथमपादस्य द्वादशाक्षरत्वात्। ' आद्यश्चेत् पुरउष्णिक् ' ( अनु० ५. २ ) इति हि तल्लक्षणम् । शिष्टा उष्णिहः । तथा चानुक्रम्यते - ‘इंद्राय द्वादश नृमेध औष्णिहं सप्तम्युपांत्ये च ककुभोऽंत्यानवम्यौ पुरउष्णिहौ ' इति । महाव्रते औष्णिहतृचाशीताविदं सूक्तम् । तथैव पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितम् - ‘इंद्राय साम गायत सखाय आ शिषामहि' (ऐ. आ. ५. २.५ ) इति । आभिप्लविकेषूक्थ्येषु तृतीयसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः  ‘ इंद्राय साम गायत' इति वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च- ‘ इंद्राय सोम गायत सखाय आ शिषामहि' (आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ८) इति । पूर्वोक्तस्यैव ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन आभिप्लविकेषूक्थ्येषु ‘एंद्र नो गधि' इति वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रियः । सूत्रितं च - ‘ एंद्र नो गध्येदु मध्वो मदिंतरम्' (आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ८) इति । उक्थ्ये तृतीयसवनेऽच्छावाकस्य अधा हींद्र' इति स्तोत्रियस्तृचः । सूत्रितं च -- ‘अधा हींद्र गिर्वण इयं त इंद्र गिर्वणः ' ( आश्व. श्रौ. ६. १ ) इति । पूर्वोक्त एव शस्त्रे  ‘ त्वं न इंद्रा भर ' इति तृचो वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रियः । सूत्रितं च - ‘ त्वं न इंद्रा भर वयमु त्वामपूर्व्य यो न इदमिदं पुरा' (आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ८) इति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

After the salutation to Gaṇeśa and the verse in which Sāyaṇa bows to Vidyātīrtha Maheśvara, whose breath is the Vedas and who made the whole world out of the Vedas, he says: now the seventh chapter of the sixth Aṣṭaka begins. In it, the fifth sūkta, इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*), of twelve Ṛks, has as seer Nṛmedha of the Āṅgirasa line, and Indra as deity. The seventh, tenth and eleventh Ṛks are Kakubh, because the middle pāda has twelve syllables, for the definition is मध्यमश्चेत्ककुप् (*madhyamaścetkakup*) (Anu. 5. 3). The ninth and twelfth are Puraūṣṇih, because the first pāda has twelve syllables; the definition is आद्यश्चेत् पुरउष्णिक् (*ādyaścet purauṣṇik*) (Anu. 5. 2). The rest are Uṣṇih. So the Anukramaṇī says: इंद्राय द्वादश नृमेध औष्णिहं सप्तम्युपांत्ये च ककुभोऽंत्यानवम्यौ पुरउष्णिहौ (*iṃdrāya dvādaśa nṛmedha auṣṇihaṃ saptamyupāṃtye ca kakubho 'ṃtyānavamyau purauṣṇihau*). In the Mahāvrata this sūkta serves for the Auṣṇiha tṛca; so it is laid down in the fifth Āraṇyaka: इंद्राय साम गायत सखाय आ शिषामहि (*iṃdrāya sāma gāyata sakhāya ā śiṣāmahi*) (Ai. Ā. 5. 2. 5). In the Ābhiplavika Ukthya rites, at the third pressing, इंद्राय साम गायत (*iṃdrāya sāma gāyata*) is the optional Stotriya tṛca of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and the sūtra says इंद्राय सोम गायत सखाय आ शिषामहि (*iṃdrāya soma gāyata sakhāya ā śiṣāmahi*) (Āśv. Śrau. 7. 8). In the same rites the optional Stotriya of the same Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is एंद्र नो गधि (*eṃdra no gadhi*), and the sūtra says एंद्र नो गध्येदु मध्वो मदिंतरम् (*eṃdra no gadhyedu madhvo madiṃtaram*) (Āśv. Śrau. 7. 8). In the Ukthya, at the third pressing, the Stotriya tṛca of the Acchāvāka is अधा हींद्र (*adhā hīṃdra*), and the sūtra says अधा हींद्र गिर्वण इयं त इंद्र गिर्वणः (*adhā hīṃdra girvaṇa iyaṃ ta iṃdra girvaṇaḥ*) (Āśv. Śrau. 6. 1). In the same Śastra the optional Stotriya is the tṛca त्वं न इंद्रा भर (*tvaṃ na iṃdrā bhara*), and the sūtra says त्वं न इंद्रा भर वयमु त्वामपूर्व्य यो न इदमिदं पुरा (*tvaṃ na iṃdrā bhara vayamu tvāmapūrvya yo na idamidaṃ purā*) (Āśv. Śrau. 7. 8).

### Printed p. 476

Anuvāda: Now the commentary on the seventh chapter of the sixth Aṣṭaka is begun. At the beginning of this chapter stands the sūkta इंद्राय सामु गायत (*iṃdrāya sāmu gāyata*). This is the fifth sūkta in the tenth Anuvāka of the eighth Maṇḍala. It has twelve Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Nṛmedha Aṅgirasa; the deity is Indra. Since the middle pāda of the seventh, tenth and eleventh Ṛks of this sūkta has twelve syllables, these three Ṛks have the Kakubh metre. Its definition is मध्यमश्चेत्ककुप् (*madhyamaścetkakup*) (Anu. 5-2). The ninth and twelfth Ṛks are in the Puraūṣṇih metre. Since the first pādas of these Ṛks have twelve syllables, according to the Anukramaṇī sentence आद्यश्चेत्पुर उष्णिक् (*ādyaścetpura uṣṇik*) (Anu. 5-2) these Ṛks are named Puraūṣṇih. The remaining Ṛks of this sūkta are in the Uṣṇih metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: इंद्राय द्वादश नृमेध औष्णिहं सप्तम्युपांत्ये च ककुभोऽन्त्यानवम्यौ पुरउष्णिहौ (*iṃdrāya dvādaśa nṛmedha auṣṇihaṃ saptamyupāṃtye ca kakubho 'ntyānavamyau purauṣṇihau*). That this sūkta is applied in the Mahāvrata rite to the Ṛks in the Uṣṇih metre is indicated in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka by the sentence इंद्राय सामुगायत सखायु आ शिषामहि (*iṃdrāya sāmugāyata sakhāyu ā śiṣāmahi*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-5). In the Ukthya sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava, at the time of the third pressing, among the Śastra mantras recited by the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the tṛca इंद्राय सामु गायत (*iṃdrāya sāmu gāyata*) is to be recited as the optional Stotriya tṛca; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra इंद्राय सामुगायतॆ सखायु आ शिषामहि (*iṃdrāya sāmugāyatè sakhāyu ā śiṣāmahi*) (Ā. 7 8). In the Ukthya sacrifices connected with the Abhiplava mentioned before, the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite the Ṛks 4-6 of this sūkta, beginning इंद्र नो गधि (*iṃdra no gadhi*), as the optional Stotriya tṛca; this is by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra इंद्र नो गध्येदु माध्वो मुदीतरं (*iṃdra no gadhyedu mādhvo mudītaraṃ*), the sūtra

### Printed p. 477

(Ā. 7-8) it is explained. And the priest called Acchāvāka, at the time of the third pressing of the Ukthya sacrifice, is to recite as the Stotriya tṛca the Ṛks 7-9 of this sūkta, beginning अथा हींद्र (*athā hīṃdra*); this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अथा हींद्र गिर्वण इयं त इंद्र गिर्वणः (*athā hīṃdra girvaṇa iyaṃ ta iṃdra girvaṇaḥ*) (Ā. 7-8). In the same Śastra mantras mentioned before, the Ṛks 10-12 of this sūkta, beginning त्वं न इंद्रा भर (*tvaṃ na iṃdrā bhara*), are to be recited as the optional Stotriya tṛca; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra त्वं न इंद्रा भर वयुनु त्वानुपूर्व्य यो न इदमिदं पुरा (*tvaṃ na iṃdrā bhara vayunu tvānupūrvya yo na idamidaṃ purā*) (Ā. 7-8).

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 10; Sūkta 98. Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 7; Varga 1, 2. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 12.

Seer: Nṛmedhaḥ.

Deity: Indraḥ.

Metre: 1-6 and 8, Uṣṇih; 7, 10 and 11, Kakubh; 9 and 12, Puraūṣṇih.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रा॑य॒ साम॑ गायत॒ विप्रा॑य बृह॒ते बृ॒हत् ।  
> ध॒र्म॒कृते॑ विप॒श्चिते॑ पन॒स्यवे॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्राय । साम । गायत । विप्राय । बृहते । बृहत् ।  
> धर्मऽकृते । विपःऽचिते । पनस्यवे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे उद्गातारः विप्राय मेधाविने बृहते महते धर्मकृते कर्मणः कर्त्रे विपश्चिते विदुषे पनस्यवे स्तुतिमिच्छते इंद्राय बृहत् बृहन्नामकं साम गायत पठत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa addresses the Udgātṛs: sing (गायत (*gāyata*)), that is, recite, the Sāman called Bṛhat (बृहत् (*bṛhat*)) to Indra, who is wise (विप्राय (*viprāya*)), great (बृहते (*bṛhate*)), the maker of rites (धर्मकृते (*dharmakṛte*), the doer of the sacrificial act), learned (विपश्चिते (*vipaścite*)), and desirous of praise (पनस्यवे (*panasyave*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विप्राय (*viprāya*)—(O Udgātṛs) to the wise one
- बृहते (*bṛhate*)—to the one of great nature
- धर्मकृते (*dharmakṛte*)—to the performer of extraordinary rites
- विपश्चिते (*vipaścite*)—to the learned one
- पनस्यवे (*panasyave*)—to the one fond of praise

### Printed p. 478

- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—addressed to Indra
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—called Bṛhat
- साम (*sāma*)—the Sāman
- गायत (*gāyata*)—recite in the form of song

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Udgātṛs, recite in the form of song the Bṛhat Sāman, addressed to Indra, who is wise, of great nature, a performer of extraordinary rites, learned, and fond of praise.

##### English translation
Sing a Saman to Indra, a Brihat to the mighty sage, to the performer of religious rites, the all-knowing one who longs for praise.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वमिं॑द्राभि॒भूर॑सि॒ त्वं सूर्य॑मरोचयः ।  
> वि॒श्वक॑र्मा वि॒श्वदे॑वो म॒हाँ अ॑सि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वम् । इंद्र । अभिऽभूः । असि । त्वम् । सूर्यम् । अरोचयः ।  
> विश्वऽकर्मा । विश्वऽदेवः । महान् । असि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वम् अभिभूः शत्रूणामभिभविता असि भवसि । किंच त्वं सूर्यम् आदित्यम् अरोचयः तेजोभिरदीपयः । किंच विश्वकर्मा विश्वस्य कर्ता असि विश्वदेवः सर्वदेवश्चासि । तथा च यजुर्ब्राह्मणम्- अग्निं वा अन्वन्या देवता इंद्रमन्वन्याः ' (तै. ब्रा. ३. ७. १. ८) इति । अतो महान् सर्वाधिकोऽसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you are the overcomer (अभिभूः (*abhibhūḥ*)) of enemies. Further, you made the sun, Āditya, shine (अरोचयः (*arocayaḥ*)) with your splendour. Further, you are the maker of the whole world (विश्वकर्मा (*viśvakarmā*)) and the All-god (विश्वदेवः (*viśvadevaḥ*)). So the Yajur-brāhmaṇa says: अग्निं वा अन्वन्या देवता इंद्रमन्वन्याः (*agniṃ vā anvanyā devatā iṃdramanvanyāḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 3. 7. 1. 8) **GLOSS**. Therefore you are great (महान् (*mahān*)), higher than all.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- अभिभूः (*abhibhūḥ*)—the overpowerer of enemies
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the sun
- आरोचयः (*ārocayaḥ*)—made to shine
- विश्वकर्मा (*viśvakarmā*)—the maker of all worlds
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- विश्वदेवः (*viśvadevaḥ*)—the embodiment of all the gods
- महान् (*mahān*)—you are the great one

### Printed p. 479

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are the one who crushes and defeats all enemies. You yourself made the sun shine. You are the maker of all worlds. You yourself are the embodiment of all the gods and the great one.

##### English translation
You are the conqueror, Indra ; you have lighted up the sun ; you are the maker of all, the lord of all the gods, the mighty.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि॒भ्राजं॒ज्योति॑षा॒ स्व१॒॑रग॑च्छो रोच॒नं दि॒वः ।  
> दे॒वास्त॑ इंद्र स॒ख्याय॑ येमिरे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विऽभ्राजन् । ज्योतिषा । स्वः । अगच्छः । रोचनम् । दिवः ।  
> देवाः । ते । इंद्र । सख्याय । येमिरे ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं ज्योतिषा तेजसा दिवः आदित्यस्य रोचनं प्रकाशकमधिकरणत्वेन स्वः स्वर्गं विभ्राजन् प्रकाशयन् अगच्छः प्राप्नोः । किंच देवाः सर्वे ते तव सख्याय मित्रत्वाय येमिरे स्वं स्वमात्मानं नियमितवंतः । अस्माकमिंद्रः सखा यथा स्यादिति सर्वे देवाः प्रयत्नमकार्षुरित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, by your splendour (ज्योतिषा (*jyotiṣā*)) you came (अगच्छः (*agacchaḥ*)) to heaven (स्वः (*svaḥ*)), the seat of the light of the sun (रोचनं (*rocanaṃ*)), illuminating it (विभ्राजन् (*vibhrājan*)). Further, all the gods have restrained (येमिरे (*yemire*)) each his own self for the sake of your friendship (सख्याय (*sakhyāya*)). The meaning is that all the gods made an effort so that Indra might be a friend to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ज्योतिषा (*jyotiṣā*)—by splendour
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the sun
- रोचनं (*rocanaṃ*)—the basis of the light
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—heaven
- विभ्राजन् (*vibhrājan*)—shining
- आगच्छः (*āgacchaḥ*)—you pervade and move about
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—all the gods
- ते (*te*)—with you
- सख्याय (*sakhyāya*)—to win friendship
- येमिरे (*yemire*)—strive humbly

### Printed p. 480

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, by your splendour you move about, pervading all the space between, shining on heaven, the basis of the light of the sun. All the gods strive humbly to win friendship with you.

##### English translation
You have pervaded the light of the sky, illumining heaven by your splendour ; the gods, Indra, submissively solicit your friendship.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> एंद्र॑ नो गधि प्रि॒यः स॑त्रा॒जिदगो॑ह्यः ।  
> गि॒रिर्न वि॒श्वत॑स्पृ॒थुः पति॑र्दि॒वः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । इंद्र । नः । गधि । प्रियः । सत्राऽजित् । अगोह्यः ।  
> गिरिः । न । विश्वतः । पृथुः । पतिः । दिवः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र प्रियः प्रियतमः सत्राजित् महतां जेता अगोह्यः केनापि गूहितुमशक्यः गिरिर्न पर्वत इव विश्वतः सर्वतः पृथुः पृथुतमः दिवः स्वर्गस्य पतिः ईश्वरस्त्वं नः अस्मान् आ गधि आगच्छ ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you who are dearest (प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)), the conqueror of the mighty (सत्राजित् (*satrājit*)), who cannot be hidden by anyone (अगोह्यः (*agohyaḥ*)), broad on all sides like a mountain (गिरिर्न (*girirna*)), the lord (पतिः (*patiḥ*)) of heaven (दिवः (*divaḥ*)): come (आ गधि (*ā gadhi*)) to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)—the one needed by all
- सत्राजित् (*satrājit*)—the conqueror of the mighty
- अगोह्यः (*agohyaḥ*)—the one who cannot be concealed by anyone
- गिरिर्न (*girirna*)—like a mountain
- विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)—everywhere
- पृथुः (*pṛthuḥ*)—the one who extends and pervades widely
- दिव (*diva*)—of heaven
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—the lord, such as you are
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- आ गधि (*ā gadhi*)—come towards us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you are the one needed by all, the conqueror of the exceedingly mighty, the one who cannot be concealed by anyone, extending and pervading everywhere widely like a mountain, and the lord of heaven; come towards us.

### Printed p. 481

##### English translation
Come to us Indra, beloved one, triumphant, and whom none can conceal—lord of heaven, vast on all sides as a mountain.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि हि स॑त्य सोमपा उ॒भे ब॒भूथ॒ रोद॑सी ।  
> इंद्रासि॑ सुन्व॒तो वृ॒धः पति॑र्दि॒वः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । हि । सत्य । सोमऽपाः । उभे इति । बभूथ । रोदसी इति ।  
> इंद्र । असि । सुन्वतः । वृधः । पतिः । दिवः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सत्य सोमपाः सोमस्य पातः इंद्र यस्त्वम् उभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ अभि बभूथ सामर्थ्येनाभिभवसि स त्वं सुन्वतः सोमाभिषवं कुर्वतो यजमानस्य वृधः वर्धकः असि । दिवः स्वर्गस्यापि पतिः ईश्वरः असि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O true one (सत्य (*satya*)), drinker of Soma (सोमपाः (*somapāḥ*)), Indra: you who overcome (अभि बभूथ (*abhi babhūtha*)) both heaven and earth (उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)) by your power, you are the increaser (वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)) of the sacrificer who presses the Soma (सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*)). You are also the lord (पतिः (*patiḥ*)) of heaven (दिवः (*divaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सत्य (*satya*)—of true nature
- सोमपाः (*somapāḥ*)—the drinker of Soma
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- इभूथ हि (*ibhūtha hi*)—you have overcome and pervaded
- सुन्वतः (*sunvataḥ*)—to the sacrificer who presses and offers Soma
- वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)—you are the increaser
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of heaven
- पतिः असि (*patiḥ asi*)—you are also the lord

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, of true nature and drinker of Soma, you have overcome and pervaded both heaven and earth. You are the increaser of the sacrificer who presses and offers Soma, and the lord of heaven too.

##### English translation
Truthful drinker of the Soma, you surpass heaven and earth ; O Indra, you are the fosterer of him who prepares the libation, you are the lord of heaven.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं हि शश्व॑तीना॒मिंद्र॑ द॒र्ता पु॒रामसि॑ ।  
> हं॒ता दस्यो॒र्मनो॑र्वृ॒धः पति॑र्दि॒वः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वम् । हि । शश्वतीनाम् । इंद्र । दर्ता । पुराम् । असि ।  
> हंता । दस्योः । मनोः । वृधः । पतिः । दिवः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वं शश्वतीनां बह्वीनां पुरां शत्रुनगरीणां दर्ता असि दारयिता भवसि । किंच दस्योः उपक्षपयितुरसुरस्य हंता असि घातको भवसि । मनोः मनुष्यस्य यागादिकं कुर्वतः वृधः वर्धकश्चासि । दिवः स्वर्गस्यापि पतिः ईश्वरोऽसि ॥ ॥ १ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, you are the breaker (दर्ता (*dartā*)), the one who splits, of the many (शश्वतीनां (*śaśvatīnāṃ*)) cities (पुरां (*purāṃ*)) of the enemy. Further, you are the slayer (हंता (*haṃtā*)) of the Dasyu (दस्योः (*dasyoḥ*)), the asura who wastes away others. You are also the increaser (वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)) of man (मनोः (*manoḥ*)) who performs sacrifices and the like. You are the lord (पतिः (*patiḥ*)) of heaven (दिवः (*divaḥ*)) as well.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं हि (*tvaṃ hi*)—you alone
- शश्वतीनां (*śaśvatīnāṃ*)—of the many
- पुरां (*purāṃ*)—enemy cities
- दर्ता (*dartā*)—the one who splits and destroys
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- दस्योः (*dasyoḥ*)—of the violent asura
- हंता (*haṃtā*)—you are also the destroyer
- मनोः (*manoḥ*)—of the man who performs sacrifice
- वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)—you are also the increaser
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of heaven
- पतिः (*patiḥ*)—you are also the lord

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you alone are the one who splits and destroys the many cities of the enemy. You are also the destroyer of the violent asura. You are the increaser of the man who performs sacrifice, and the lord of heaven.

##### English translation
You, Indra, are the stormer of many hostile cities, the slayer of the Dasyu, the fosterer of man, the lord of heaven.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अधा॒ हीं॑द्र गिर्वण॒ उप॑ त्वा॒ कामा॑न्म॒हः स॑सृ॒ज्महे॑ ।  
> उ॒देव॒ यंत॑ उ॒दभिः॑ ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 483

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध । हि । इंद्र । गिर्वणः । उप । त्वा । कामान् । महः । ससृज्महे ।  
> उदाऽइव । यंतः । उदऽभिः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे गिर्वणः गीर्भिर्वननीय इंद्र अधा हि संप्रति हि त्वा त्वां महः महतः कामान् कमनीयान् स्तोमान् उप ससृज्महे उपसृजामः । प्रापयाम इत्यर्थः। तत्र दृष्टांतमाह। उदेव यथोदकेन यंतः गच्छंतः उदभिः अंजलिना उत्क्षिप्य उदकैः समीपस्थान् पुरुषान् क्रीडार्थं संसृजंति तद्वदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Girvaṇas, Indra, who are to be served with praises: now (अधा हि (*adhā hi*)) we send up (उप ससृज्महे (*upa sasṛjmahe*)) to you great (महः (*mahaḥ*)), lovable (कामान् (*kāmān*)) praises; that is, we make them reach you. He gives the illustration: उदेव (*udeva*), as men going (यंतः (*yaṃtaḥ*)) through water, raising water in the joined hands (उदभिः (*udabhiḥ*)), splash those who stand near them in sport; so it is here.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—one who is to be worshipped with praises
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- उदेव (*udeva*)—in water
- यंतः (*yaṃtaḥ*)—men who move about (play)
- उदभिः (*udabhiḥ*)—as they splash their friends in play with water taken up in the joined hands
- अधा हि (*adhā hi*)—right now
- त्वा (*tvā*)—addressed to you
- महः (*mahaḥ*)—great
- कामान् (*kāmān*)—and attractive hymns of praise
- उप ससृज्महे (*upa sasṛjmahe*)—we offer to you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, who are to be worshipped with praises, as men who move about in water for sport splash their friends in play with water filled in their joined hands, right now we compose great and attractive hymns of praise addressed to you and offer them to you.

##### English translation
Indra, worthy of hymns, we send our earnest praises to you as men going by water (splash their friends) with handfuls

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वार्ण त्वा॑ य॒व्याभि॒र्वर्धं॑ति शूर॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि ।  
> वा॒वृ॒ध्वांसं॑ चिदद्रिवो दि॒वेदि॑वे ॥ ८ ॥

### Printed p. 484

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वाः । न । त्वा । यव्याभिः । वर्धंति । शूर । ब्रह्माणि ।  
> ववृध्वांसम् । चित् । अद्रिऽवः । दिवेऽदिवे ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अद्रिवः वज्रिन् शूर इंद्र वार्ण यथोदकमुदकस्थानं यव्याभिः नदीभिः ।  ‘ अवनयो यव्याः' इति नदीनामसु पाठात् । वर्धंति वर्धयंति तथा ब्रह्माणि स्तोत्रैः ववृध्वाँसं चित् यथा निरुदकं देशं नदीभिस्तथा न किंतु प्रवृद्धमेव त्वां दिवेदिवे अन्वहं वर्धंति । स्तोतारो वर्धयंति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Adrivat, thunderer, hero Indra: as a water-place (a place of water) is made to increase by rivers (यव्याभिः (*yavyābhiḥ*)), the word यव्याः (*yavyāḥ*) being read among the names of rivers, so (ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)) hymns of praise make you increase (वर्धंति (*vardhaṃti*)). Not as a waterless region is increased by rivers, but you, who are already grown (ववृध्वांसं (*vavṛdhvāṃsaṃ*)), the praisers make increase day after day (दिवेदिवे (*divedive*)).

**NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O bearer of the thunderbolt
- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant Indra
- यव्याभिः (*yavyābhiḥ*)—by rivers
- वार्णि (*vārṇi*)—as the sea grows
- दिवेदिवे (*divedive*)—every day
- ववृध्वांसं चित् (*vavṛdhvāṃsaṃ cit*)—you who grow by your own nature
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—hymns of praise
- वर्धंति (*vardhaṃti*)—make you grow still more

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O valiant Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt, as the sea is made to grow more by the rivers, our hymns of praise make you, who grow by your own nature every day, grow still more.

##### English translation
As the lake (swells) with the rivers, so our praises, O hero, O thunderer, augment you as you grow more and more day by day.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इं॒द्र॒वाहा॑ वचो॒युजा॑ ॥ ९ ॥

> इंद्रऽवाहा । वचःऽयुजा ॥ ९ ॥

### Printed p. 485

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इषिरस्य गमनशीलस्येंद्रस्य उरुयुगे महायुगे उरौ महति रथे इंद्रवाहा इंद्रस्य वाहनभूतौ वचोयुजा वचनमात्रेणैव युज्यमानौ हरी अश्वौ गाथया स्तोत्रेण स्तोतारः युंजंति योजयंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The praisers (स्तोतारः (*stotāraḥ*)) yoke (युंजंति (*yuṃjaṃti*)) by a song of praise (गाथया (*gāthayā*)) the two bay horses (हरी (*harī*)) of the swift-moving (इषिरस्य (*iṣirasya*)) Indra to his great chariot (रथे (*rathe*)) with a great yoke (उरुयुगे (*uruyuge*)): horses which are Indra's bearers (इंद्रवाहा (*iṃdravāhā*)) and are yoked by a mere word (वचोयुजा (*vacoyujā*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इषिरस्य (*iṣirasya*)—of Indra, who moves about
- उरुयुगे (*uruyuge*)—having a long yoke
- उरौ (*urau*)—and great
- रथेः (*ratheḥ*)—to the chariot
- इंद्रवाहा (*iṃdravāhā*)—fit to carry Indra
- वचोयुजा (*vacoyujā*)—yoked by mere speech
- हरी (*harī*)—the horses
- गाथया (*gāthayā*)—with praise
- युंजंति (*yuṃjaṃti*)—the praisers join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The praisers, with praise, join to the great chariot with a long yoke of Indra, who moves about, the horses that are fit to carry Indra and are yoked by mere speech.

##### English translation
(The priests) by their hymn yoke in the swift deity's huge broad-yoked chariot the two Indra-bearing steeds yoked at a word.

#### Ṛk 10

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं न॑ इं॒द्रा भ॑रँ॒ ओजो॑ नृ॒म्णं श॑तक्रतो विचर्षणे ।  
> आ वी॒रं पृ॑तना॒षह॑म् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वम् । नः । इंद्र । आ । भर । ओजः । नृम्णम् । शतक्रतो इति शतऽक्रतो । विऽचर्षणे ।  
> आ । वीरम् । पृतनाऽसहम् ॥ १० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे शतक्रतो बहुकर्मन् विचर्षणे विद्रष्टः इंद्र त्वं नः अस्मभ्यम् ओजः बलं नृम्णं धनम् । ‘गयो नृम्णम्' इति धननामसु पाठात् । आ भर आहर । वीरं वीर्योपितं पृतनाषहं सेनासहं सेनामभिभवितारं त्वाम् आ याचामह इति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Śatakratu, of many works, O Vicarṣaṇi, far-seeing Indra: bring (आ भर (*ā bhara*)) to us strength (ओजः (*ojaḥ*)) and wealth (नृम्णं (*nṛmṇaṃ*)), the word नृम्ण (*nṛmṇa*) being read among the names of wealth. We beg you, who are heroic (वीरं (*vīraṃ*)), the conqueror of armies (पृतनाषहं (*pṛtanāṣahaṃ*)), who overcomes the army; the words "we beg" (आ याचामह (*ā yācāmaha*)) are the remainder to be supplied.

- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O doer of many works
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you

- आ (*ā*)—(we beg) we ask for

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

> अधा॑ ते सु॒म्नमी॑महे ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वसो वासयितः शतक्रतो बहुकर्मन्निंद्र त्वं नः अस्माकं पिता पितृवत्पालकः बभूविथ भव। त्वं माता मातृवद्धारकश्च बभूविथ। अध अथ च वयं ते तव स्वभूतं सुम्नं सुखम् ईमहे याचामहे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vasu, giver of dwelling, Śatakratu, of many works, Indra: you have become (बभूविथ (*babhūvitha*)) our father (पिता (*pitā*)), our protector like a father, and you have become our mother (माता (*mātā*)), who bears us like a mother. And so (अध (*adha*)) we beg (ईमहे (*īmahe*)) your own happiness (सुम्नं (*sumnaṃ*)).

- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O doer of many works
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वं हि (*tvaṃ hi*)—you yourself
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- पिता (*pitā*)—in the form of a protecting father
- बभूविथ (*babhūvitha*)—you have become

### Printed p. 487

- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you yourself
- माता (*mātā*)—in the form of a mother also
- अध (*adha*)—therefore
- ते (*te*)—coming from you
- सुम्नं (*sumnaṃ*)—happiness
- ईमहे (*īmahe*)—we ask

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, giver of dwelling, doer of many works, you yourself are the protecting father for us and you yourself are the supporting mother. Therefore we ask for the happiness that comes from you.

- पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—worthy of the invocation of many
- शतक्रतो (*śatakrato*)—O doer of many works
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वाजयंतं (*vājayaṃtaṃ*)—you who desire strength

- उप ब्रुवे (*upa bruve*)—I praise

- नः (*naḥ*)—to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, powerful, worthy of the invocation of many, doer of many works, I praise you who desire strength.

The ninety-ninth sūkta.

## Sūkta 99 (Maṇḍala 8)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘ त्वामिदा ह्यः' इत्यष्टर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं नृमेधस्यार्षमैंद्रम् । अयुजो बृहत्यो युजः सतोवृहत्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं - त्वामिदाष्टौ प्रागाथम्' इति । चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि मध्यंदिनसवनेऽच्छावाकस्य ‘त्वामिदा ह्यः' इति (आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ४ )। महाव्रतेऽपि निष्केवल्ये बार्हततृचाशीतावयं प्रगाथः । तथैव पंचमारण्यके सूत्रितं- त्वामिदा ह्यो नर इत्येतं प्रगाथं प्रत्यवदधाति' (ऐ. आ. ५, २. ४ ) इति । चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिनसवने ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनः  ‘ श्रायंतइव ' इति वैकल्पिकः स्तोत्रियः प्रगाथः । सूत्रितं च - ‘ श्रायंतइव सूर्यं बण्महाँ असि सूर्य' (आश्व. श्रौ. ७, ४) इति । चातुर्विंशिकेऽहनि माध्यंदिने ‘त्वमिंद्र प्रतूर्तिषु त्वमिंद्र यशा असि ( आश्व. श्रौ. ७. ४) इति । तस्मिन्नेवाहनि निष्केवल्ये वैराजयोनिभूतोऽयं प्रगाथः शंसनीयः । [सूत्रितं च–' तयोरक्रियमाणस्य योनिं शंसेद्वैरूपवैराजशाक्कररैवतानां च ' (आश्व, श्रौ. ७. ३) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta त्वामिदा ह्यः (*tvāmidā hyaḥ*) of eight Ṛks is the sixth sūkta, of the seer Nṛmedha, to Indra. The odd Ṛks are Bṛhatī and the even ones Satobṛhatī. So the Anukramaṇī says त्वामिदाष्टौ प्रागाथम् (*tvāmidāṣṭau prāgātham*). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, it is the Acchāvāka's त्वामिदा ह्यः (*tvāmidā hyaḥ*) (Āśv. Śrau. 7. 4). In the Mahāvrata also, at the Niṣkevalya, this Pragātha belongs to the Bārhata tṛca. So it is laid down in the fifth Āraṇyaka: त्वामिदा ह्यो नर इत्येतं प्रगाथं प्रत्यवदधाति (*tvāmidā hyo nara ityetaṃ pragāthaṃ pratyavadadhāti*) (Ai. Ā. 5, 2. 4). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, the optional Stotriya Pragātha of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is श्रायंतइव (*śrāyaṃtaiva*); and the sūtra says श्रायंतइव सूर्यं बण्महाँ असि सूर्य (*śrāyaṃtaiva sūryaṃ baṇmahām̐ asi sūrya*) (Āśv. Śrau. 7, 4). On the Cāturviṃśika day, at the midday pressing, there is त्वमिंद्र प्रतूर्तिषु त्वमिंद्र यशा असि (*tvamiṃdra pratūrtiṣu tvamiṃdra yaśā asi*) (Āśv. Śrau. 7. 4). On the same day, at the Niṣkevalya, this Pragātha, which is the source of the Vairāja, is to be recited; and the sūtra says तयोरक्रियमाणस्य योनिं शंसेद्वैरूपवैराजशाक्कररैवतानां च (*tayorakriyamāṇasya yoniṃ śaṃsedvairūpavairājaśākkararaivatānāṃ ca*) (Āśv. Śrau. 7. 3).

Anuvāda: This sūkta त्वामिदा ह्यः (*tvāmidā hyaḥ*) is the sixth sūkta in the tenth Anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Nṛmedha; the deity is Indra. In this sūkta the Ṛks of odd number have the Bṛhatī metre; the Ṛks of even number have the Satobṛhatī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said त्वामिदाष्टौ प्रागाथं (*tvāmidāṣṭau prāgāthaṃ*). That on the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the time of the midday pressing, the priest called Acchāvāka is to recite the Pragātha (two Ṛks) त्वामिदा ह्यः (*tvāmidā hyaḥ*) is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 7-4). In the Mahāvrata rite also, when reciting the Niṣkevalya Śastra mantras, this Pragātha is to be recited among the Ṛks of the Bṛhatī metre; this is indicated in the fifth Āraṇyaka of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka by the sentence त्वामिदा ह्यो नर इत्येतं प्रगाथं प्रत्यवदधाति (*tvāmidā hyo nara ityetaṃ pragāthaṃ pratyavadadhāti*) (Ai. Ā. 5-2-4). On the day of the sacrifice called Cāturviṃśika, at the time of the midday pressing, the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite the Pragātha त्रायंत इव (*trāyaṃta iva*) (Ṛks 3-4) as the optional Stotriya Pragātha; this is by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, the त्रायंत इव (*trāyaṃta iva*)

### Printed p. 489

सूर्यं बण्महा असि सूर्य (*sūryaṃ baṇmahā asi sūrya*) (Ā. 7-4) it is explained. Further, on the day called Cāturviṃśika, at the time of the midday pressing, the priest called Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite the Pragātha त्वमिंद्र प्रतूर्तिषु (*tvamiṃdra pratūrtiṣu*) (Ṛks 5-6); this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra त्वमिंद्र प्रतूर्तिषु त्वमिंद्र यशा असि (*tvamiṃdra pratūrtiṣu tvamiṃdra yaśā asi*) (Ā. 7-4). On the same day of the sacrifice, when the Niṣkevalya Śastra mantras are recited, this same Pragātha, which is the source of the Vairāja, is to be recited; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra तयोरक्रियमाणस्य योनिं शंसेद्वैरूपवैराजशाक्वरैवतानां च (*tayorakriyamāṇasya yoniṃ śaṃsedvairūpavairājaśākvaraivatānāṃ ca*) (Ā. 7-3).

##### Particulars

Maṇḍala 8; Anuvāka 10; Sūkta 99. Aṣṭaka 6; Adhyāya 7; Varga 3. Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8.

Seer: Nṛmedhaḥ.

Deity: Indraḥ.

Metre: Prāgātha (the odd Ṛks Bṛhatī; the even Ṛks Satobṛhatī).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वामि॒दा ह्यो नरोऽपी॑प्यन्वज्रि॒न्भूर्ण॑यः ।  
> स इं॑द्र॒ स्तोम॑वाहसामि॒ह श्रु॒ध्युप॒ स्वस॑र॒मा ग॑हि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वाम् । इदा । ह्यः । नरः । अपीप्यन् । वज्रिन् । भूर्णयः ।  
> सः । इंद्र । स्तोमऽवाहसाम् । इह । श्रुधि । उप । स्वसरम् । आ । गहि ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे वज्रिन् इंद्र यं त्वां भूर्णयः हविर्भिर्भरणशीलाः नरः कर्मणां नेतारो यजमानाः इदा अद्य ह्यः च अपीप्यन् सोममपाययन् सः त्वं स्तोमवाहसां स्तोत्रवाहकानामस्माकं स्तोत्रम् इह यज्ञे श्रुधि शृणु। स्वसरं गृहं च । 'दुर्याः स्वसराणि' इति गृहनामसु पाठात् । उप आ गहि उपागच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Vajrin, Indra: the leaders of rites (नरः (*naraḥ*)), the sacrificers, who bear oblations (भूर्णयः (*bhūrṇayaḥ*)), have today (इदा (*idā*)) and yesterday (ह्यः (*hyaḥ*)) made you drink the Soma (अपीप्यन् (*apīpyan*)). You, such as you are, listen (श्रुधि (*śrudhi*)) here, at this sacrifice, to the praise of us who are bearers of praise (स्तोमवाहसां (*stomavāhasāṃ*)). स्वसरं (*svasaraṃ*) also means house, since दुर्याः स्वसराणि (*duryāḥ svasarāṇi*) is read among the names of the house. Come (उप आ गहि (*upa ā gahi*)) near to it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वज्रिन् (*vajrin*)—O wielder of the thunderbolt
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- त्वा (*tvā*)—to you
- भूर्णयः (*bhūrṇayaḥ*)—having vessels filled with oblations
- नरः (*naraḥ*)—the sacrificers
- इदा (*idā*)—now
- ह्यः (*hyaḥ*)—and yesterday
